Int.ModEq.add_right.code: Int.ModEq.add_right {n a b : ℤ} (c : ℤ) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) : a + c ≡ b + c [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.add_right.description: This theorem asserts that adding the same integer to two congruent integers preserves their equivalence under a specified modulus.

Int.ModEq.add_left_cancel.code: Int.ModEq.add_left_cancel {n a b c d : ℤ} (h₁ : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) (h₂ : a + c ≡ b + d [ZMOD n]) : c ≡ d [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.add_left_cancel.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent modulo a specified integer and their sums with two other integers are also congruent, then the two other integers are congruent under the same modulus.

Int.ModEq.add_left_cancel'.code: Int.ModEq.add_left_cancel' {n a b : ℤ} (c : ℤ) (h : c + a ≡ c + b [ZMOD n]) : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.add_left_cancel'.description: This theorem asserts that if two integers become congruent modulo a specified integer after adding the same integer to both, then the original integers are also congruent under the same modulus.

Int.ModEq.add_right_cancel.code: Int.ModEq.add_right_cancel {n a b c d : ℤ} (h₁ : c ≡ d [ZMOD n]) (h₂ : a + c ≡ b + d [ZMOD n]) : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.add_right_cancel.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent under modulo arithmetic and the sums of these integers with another pair of integers are also congruent, then the two other integers must be congruent as well.

Int.ModEq.add_right_cancel'.code: Int.ModEq.add_right_cancel' {n a b : ℤ} (c : ℤ) (h : a + c ≡ b + c [ZMOD n]) : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.add_right_cancel'.description: This theorem asserts that if adding the same integer to two congruent integers results in equivalent sums, then the original integers are also congruent under the specified modulus.

Int.ModEq.neg.code: Int.ModEq.neg {n a b : ℤ} (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) : -a ≡ -b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.neg.description: This theorem demonstrates that if two integers are congruent modulo a specified integer, then their negations are also congruent under the same modulo.

Int.ModEq.sub.code: Int.ModEq.sub {n a b c d : ℤ} (h₁ : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) (h₂ : c ≡ d [ZMOD n]) : a - c ≡ b - d [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.sub.description: This theorem indicates that if two pairs of integers are congruent under a specific modulus, then the difference of the first pair is also congruent to the difference of the second pair under the same modulus.

Int.ModEq.sub_left.code: Int.ModEq.sub_left {n a b : ℤ} (c : ℤ) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) : c - a ≡ c - b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.sub_left.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent under modulo arithmetic, then subtracting the same integer from both will preserve their congruence.

Int.ModEq.sub_right.code: Int.ModEq.sub_right {n a b : ℤ} (c : ℤ) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) : a - c ≡ b - c [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.sub_right.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent under a specified modulus, then subtracting the same integer from each of them maintains their congruence under that modulus.

Int.ModEq.mul_left.code: Int.ModEq.mul_left {n a b : ℤ} (c : ℤ) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) : c * a ≡ c * b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.mul_left.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent under a specified modulus, then multiplying each of them by the same integer preserves their congruence under that modulus.

Int.ModEq.mul_right.code: Int.ModEq.mul_right {n a b : ℤ} (c : ℤ) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) : a * c ≡ b * c [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.mul_right.description: This theorem asserts that if two integers are congruent modulo a given integer, then their products with any other integer also remain congruent under the same modulus.

Int.ModEq.mul.code: Int.ModEq.mul {n a b c d : ℤ} (h₁ : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) (h₂ : c ≡ d [ZMOD n]) : a * c ≡ b * d [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.mul.description: This theorem establishes that if two pairs of integers are congruent under modulo arithmetic, then the product of the first pair is also congruent to the product of the second pair under the same modulo.

Int.ModEq.pow.code: Int.ModEq.pow {n a b : ℤ} (m : ℕ) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]) : a ^ m ≡ b ^ m [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.pow.description: This theorem asserts that if two integers are congruent under a certain modulus, then their powers are also congruent under the same modulus.

Int.ModEq.of_mul_left.code: Int.ModEq.of_mul_left {n a b : ℤ} (m : ℤ) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD m * n]) : a ≡ b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.of_mul_left.description: This theorem asserts that if two integers are congruent modulo the product of two specified integers, then they are also congruent modulo the second integer alone.

Int.ModEq.of_mul_right.code: Int.ModEq.of_mul_right {n a b : ℤ} (m : ℤ) : a ≡ b [ZMOD n * m] → a ≡ b [ZMOD n]
Int.ModEq.of_mul_right.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent modulo the product of two integers, then they are also congruent modulo the first integer.

Int.ModEq.cancel_left_div_gcd.code: Int.ModEq.cancel_left_div_gcd {m a b c : ℤ} (hm : 0 < m) (h : c * a ≡ c * b [ZMOD m]) : a ≡ b [ZMOD m / ↑(m.gcd c)]

Int.ModEq.cancel_left_div_gcd.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent modulo a positive integer and share a common factor, then they remain congruent when the modulus is adjusted by dividing it by the greatest common divisor of that factor.

Int.modEq_one.description: This theorem establishes that any two integers are congruent modulo one.

Int.add_modEq_left.description: This theorem shows that adding a specified integer to another integer does not change the congruence class of the second integer when considered modulo the first integer.

Int.add_modEq_right.code: Int.add_modEq_right {n a : ℤ} : a + n ≡ a [ZMOD n]

Int.modEq_add_fac.description: This theorem states that if two integers are congruent modulo a specified integer, then adding a multiple of that integer to one of them results in the same congruence.

Int.exists_unique_equiv.description: This theorem claims that for any integer, there exists a unique non-negative integer that is congruent to it modulo a positive integer.

Int.image_Ico_emod.code: Int.image_Ico_emod (n a : ℤ) (h : 0 ≤ a) : image (fun x => x % a) (Ico n (n + a)) = Ico 0 a

Int.image_Ico_emod.description: This theorem demonstrates that the image of the integers in the interval from a specified integer to the sum of that integer and a non-negative integer, when taken modulo the non-negative integer, is equivalent to the interval from zero to that non-negative integer.

Int.Ico_filter_dvd_eq.code:
Int.Ico_filter_dvd_eq (a b : ℤ) {r : ℤ} (hr : 0 < r) :
  filter (fun x => r ∣ x) (Ico a b) = map { toFun := fun x => x * r, inj' := ⋯ } (Ico ⌈↑a / ↑r⌉ ⌈↑b / ↑r⌉)

Int.Ico_filter_dvd_eq.description: This theorem demonstrates that the filter of integers divisible by a positive integer within a specified interval can be expressed as a mapped interval of the ceiling values of the endpoints divided by that integer.

Int.Ioc_filter_dvd_eq.code:
Int.Ioc_filter_dvd_eq (a b : ℤ) {r : ℤ} (hr : 0 < r) :

Int.Ioc_filter_dvd_eq.description: This theorem establishes that the filter of integers divisible by a positive integer within a specified open interval can be written as a mapped interval of the floor values of the endpoints divided by that integer.

Int.Ico_filter_modEq_eq.code:
Int.Ico_filter_modEq_eq (a b : ℤ) {r : ℤ} (v : ℤ) :
  filter (fun x => x ≡ v [ZMOD r]) (Ico a b) =
    map { toFun := fun x => x + v, inj' := ⋯ } (filter (fun x => r ∣ x) (Ico (a - v) (b - v)))

Int.Ioc_filter_modEq_eq (a b : ℤ) {r : ℤ} (v : ℤ) :

Nat.Ico_filter_modEq_cast.code:
Nat.Ico_filter_modEq_cast (a b : ℕ) {r v : ℕ} :
  map castEmbedding (filter (fun x => x ≡ v [MOD r]) (Ico a b)) = filter (fun x => x ≡ ↑v [ZMOD ↑r]) (Ico ↑a ↑b)

Int.Ico_filter_modEq_card.code:

  ↑(filter (fun x => x ≡ v [ZMOD r]) (Ico a b)).card = max (⌈(↑b - ↑v) / ↑r⌉ - ⌈(↑a - ↑v) / ↑r⌉) 0
Int.Ico_filter_modEq_card.comment:
There are `⌈(b - v) / r⌉ - ⌈(a - v) / r⌉` numbers congruent to `v` mod `r` in `[a, b)`,
if `a ≤ b`.

Nat.count_modEq_card_eq_ceil.code:
Nat.count_modEq_card_eq_ceil (b : ℕ) {r : ℕ} (hr : 0 < r) (v : ℕ) :
  ↑(count (fun x => x ≡ v [MOD r]) b) = ⌈(↑b - ↑(v % r)) / ↑r⌉
Nat.count_modEq_card_eq_ceil.comment: There are `⌈(b - v % r) / r⌉` numbers in `[0, b)` congruent to `v` mod `r`.

Set.Elem.fullDefinition: @[coe, reducible] def Elem (s : Set α) : Type u := {x // x ∈ s}

Set.prod.code: Set.prod.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Set (α × β)
Set.prod.comment: The cartesian product `Set.prod s t` is the set of `(a, b)` such that `a ∈ s` and `b ∈ t`.
Set.prod.fullDefinition: def prod (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Set (α × β) := {p | p.1 ∈ s ∧ p.2 ∈ t}
Set.prod.description: The Cartesian product of two sets consists of all ordered pairs formed by taking one element from each set.

Set.offDiag.code: Set.offDiag.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : Set (α × α)
Set.offDiag.comment: The off-diagonal of a set `s` is the set of pairs `(a, b)` with `a, b ∈ s` and `a ≠ b`.
Set.offDiag.fullDefinition: def offDiag (s : Set α) : Set (α × α) := {x | x.1 ∈ s ∧ x.2 ∈ s ∧ x.1 ≠ x.2}
Set.offDiag.description: The off-diagonal of a set consists of all pairs of distinct elements from that set.

Set.pi.code: Set.pi.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} (s : Set ι) (t : (i : ι) → Set (α i)) : Set ((i : ι) → α i)
Set.pi.comment:
Given an index set `ι` and a family of sets `t : Π i, Set (α i)`, `pi s t`
is the set of dependent functions `f : Πa, π a` such that `f a` belongs to `t a`
whenever `a ∈ s`.
Set.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (s : Set ι) (t : ∀ i, Set (α i)) : Set (∀ i, α i) := {f | ∀ i ∈ s, f i ∈ t i}
Set.pi.description: The set of dependent functions can be defined for a given index set and a family of sets, where each function's values belong to the corresponding set whenever the index is part of the specified set.

explanatories.Set.pi: The set of dependent functions can be defined for a given index set and a family of sets, where each function's values belong to the corresponding set whenever the index is part of the specified set.

Set.EqOn.code: Set.EqOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f₁ f₂ : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop
Set.EqOn.comment: Two functions `f₁ f₂ : α → β` are equal on `s` if `f₁ x = f₂ x` for all `x ∈ s`.
Set.EqOn.fullDefinition: def EqOn (f₁ f₂ : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop := ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → f₁ x = f₂ x
Set.EqOn.description: Two functions are considered equal on a specified set if they produce the same output for every input from that set.

Set.MapsTo.code: Set.MapsTo.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop
Set.MapsTo.comment: `MapsTo f a b` means that the image of `a` is contained in `b`.
Set.MapsTo.fullDefinition: def MapsTo (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop := ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → f x ∈ t
Set.MapsTo.description: A function maps to a set if the image of that set is contained within another specified set.

Set.mapsTo_image.code: Set.mapsTo_image.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : MapsTo f s (f '' s)

Set.mapsTo_image.description: A function maps a set to its image if the function's output for every element in the set is included in that image.

Set.mapsTo_preimage.code: Set.mapsTo_preimage.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (t : Set β) : MapsTo f (f ⁻¹' t) t

Set.mapsTo_preimage.description: The preimage of a set under a function is guaranteed to map to that set through the function.

Set.MapsTo.restrict.code: Set.MapsTo.restrict.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) (h : MapsTo f s t) : ↑s → ↑t
Set.MapsTo.restrict.comment:
Given a map `f` sending `s : Set α` into `t : Set β`, restrict domain of `f` to `s`
and the codomain to `t`. Same as `Subtype.map`.
Set.MapsTo.restrict.fullDefinition: def MapsTo.restrict (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) (h : MapsTo f s t) : s → t :=   Subtype.map f h
Set.MapsTo.restrict.description: The restriction of a function to a specific domain and codomain produces a new function that only maps elements from the restricted input set to those in the restricted output set.

Set.restrictPreimage.code: Set.restrictPreimage.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (t : Set β) (f : α → β) : ↑(f ⁻¹' t) → ↑t
Set.restrictPreimage.comment: The restriction of a function onto the preimage of a set.

Set.restrictPreimage.fullDefinition: def restrictPreimage (t : Set β) (f : α → β) : f ⁻¹' t → t :=   (Set.mapsTo_preimage f t).restrict _ _ _

Set.InjOn.code: Set.InjOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop
Set.InjOn.comment: `f` is injective on `a` if the restriction of `f` to `a` is injective.
Set.InjOn.fullDefinition: def InjOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃x₁ : α⦄, x₁ ∈ s → ∀ ⦃x₂ : α⦄, x₂ ∈ s → f x₁ = f x₂ → x₁ = x₂
Set.InjOn.description: A function is considered injective on a set if it maps distinct elements of that set to distinct elements in the codomain.

Set.SurjOn.code: Set.SurjOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop
Set.SurjOn.comment: `f` is surjective from `a` to `b` if `b` is contained in the image of `a`.
Set.SurjOn.fullDefinition: def SurjOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop := t ⊆ f '' s
Set.SurjOn.description: A function is surjective from one set to another if the second set is entirely contained within the image of the first set under that function.

Set.BijOn.code: Set.BijOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop
Set.BijOn.comment: `f` is bijective from `s` to `t` if `f` is injective on `s` and `f '' s = t`.

explanatories.Set.MapsTo: A function maps to a set if the image of that set is contained within another specified set.
explanatories.Set.InjOn: A function is considered injective on a set if it maps distinct elements of that set to distinct elements in the codomain.

Set.BijOn.fullDefinition: def BijOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop := MapsTo f s t ∧ InjOn f s ∧ SurjOn f s t
Set.BijOn.description: A function is bijective from one set to another if it is both injective on the first set and its image under the function is exactly the second set.

Set.LeftInvOn.code: Set.LeftInvOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f' : β → α) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop
Set.LeftInvOn.comment: `g` is a left inverse to `f` on `a` means that `g (f x) = x` for all `x ∈ a`.
Set.LeftInvOn.fullDefinition: def LeftInvOn (f' : β → α) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop := ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → f' (f x) = x
Set.LeftInvOn.description: A function is said to have a left inverse on a set if applying the left inverse to the result of the function returns the original element for all elements in that set.

Set.RightInvOn.code: Set.RightInvOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (f' : β → α) (f : α → β) (t : Set β) : Prop
Set.RightInvOn.comment: `g` is a right inverse to `f` on `b` if `f (g x) = x` for all `x ∈ b`.

explanatories.Set.LeftInvOn: A function is said to have a left inverse on a set if applying the left inverse to the result of the function returns the original element for all elements in that set.

Set.RightInvOn.fullDefinition: abbrev RightInvOn (f' : β → α) (f : α → β) (t : Set β) : Prop := LeftInvOn f f' t
Set.RightInvOn.description: A function is said to have a right inverse on a set if applying the inverse function to any element in that set followed by the original function returns that element.

Set.InvOn.code: Set.InvOn.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (g : β → α) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop

Set.InvOn.fullDefinition: def InvOn (g : β → α) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop :=   LeftInvOn g f s ∧ RightInvOn g f t
Set.InvOn.description: An inverse of a function with respect to two sets signifies that one function can retrieve the original input for every element in the second set based on the output from the first function.

Set.image2.code: Set.image2.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type w} (f : α → β → γ) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Set γ
Set.image2.comment:
The image of a binary function `f : α → β → γ` as a function `Set α → Set β → Set γ`.
Mathematically this should be thought of as the image of the corresponding function `α × β → γ`.
Set.image2.fullDefinition: def image2 (f : α → β → γ) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Set γ := {c | ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ t, f a b = c}

Set.Notation.«term_↓∩_».comment:
Given two sets `A` and `B`, `A ↓∩ B` denotes the intersection of `A` and `B` as a set in `Set A`.

The notation is short for `((↑) ⁻¹' B : Set A)`, while giving hints to the elaborator
that both `A` and `B` are terms of `Set α` for the same `α`.
This set is the same as `{x : ↑A | ↑x ∈ B}`.

Set.le_eq_subset.code: Set.le_eq_subset.{u} {α : Type u} : (fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1) = fun x x_1 => x ⊆ x_1
Set.le_eq_subset.description: The relation of being less than or equal to in a lattice is equivalent to being a subset in set theory.

Set.lt_eq_ssubset.code: Set.lt_eq_ssubset.{u} {α : Type u} : (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) = fun x x_1 => x ⊂ x_1
Set.lt_eq_ssubset.description: The less-than relation in a poset corresponds to the proper subset relation between sets.

Set.le_iff_subset.code: Set.le_iff_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ≤ t ↔ s ⊆ t
Set.le_iff_subset.description: The relation of being less than or equal to for sets is equivalent to the subset relation.

Set.lt_iff_ssubset.code: Set.lt_iff_ssubset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s < t ↔ s ⊂ t
Set.lt_iff_ssubset.description: The relation of being strictly less than between two sets is equivalent to the proper subset relation.

HasSubset.Subset.le.code: HasSubset.Subset.le.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊆ t → s ≤ t
HasSubset.Subset.le.description: A set being a subset of another set implies that the first set is less than or equal to the second set in terms of inclusion.

HasSSubset.SSubset.lt.code: HasSSubset.SSubset.lt.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊂ t → s < t
HasSSubset.SSubset.lt.description: The proper subset relation implies the less-than relation in the context of ordered sets.

Set.PiSetCoe.canLift.code:
Set.PiSetCoe.canLift.{u, v} (ι : Type u) (α : ι → Type v) [∀ (i : ι), Nonempty (α i)] (s : Set ι) :
  CanLift ((i : ↑s) → α ↑i) ((i : ι) → α i) (fun f i => f ↑i) fun x => True
Set.PiSetCoe.canLift.fullDefinition: instance PiSetCoe.canLift (ι : Type u) (α : ι → Type v) [∀ i, Nonempty (α i)] (s : Set ι) :     CanLift (∀ i : s, α i) (∀ i, α i) (fun f i => f i) fun _ => True :=   PiSubtype.canLift ι α s
Set.PiSetCoe.canLift.description: The ability to lift functions from a set to a family of types is established when each type in the family is nonempty.

Set.PiSetCoe.canLift'.code:
Set.PiSetCoe.canLift'.{u, v} (ι : Type u) (α : Type v) [Nonempty α] (s : Set ι) :
  CanLift (↑s → α) (ι → α) (fun f i => f ↑i) fun x => True
Set.PiSetCoe.canLift'.fullDefinition: instance PiSetCoe.canLift' (ι : Type u) (α : Type v) [Nonempty α] (s : Set ι) :     CanLift (s → α) (ι → α) (fun f i => f i) fun _ => True :=   PiSetCoe.canLift ι (fun _ => α) s
Set.PiSetCoe.canLift'.description: The ability to lift functions from a set to a single type is established when that type is nonempty.

Set.coe_eq_subtype.code: Set.coe_eq_subtype.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : ↑s = { x // x ∈ s }
Set.coe_eq_subtype.description: The equality between the set of elements represented as a subtype and their original set is established through the coercion process.

Set.coe_setOf.code: Set.coe_setOf.{u} {α : Type u} (p : α → Prop) : ↑{x | p x} = { x // p x }
Set.coe_setOf.description: The set of elements satisfying a property is equal to the subtype of those elements that meet the property.

SetCoe.forall.code: SetCoe.forall.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : ↑s → Prop} : (∀ (x : ↑s), p x) ↔ ∀ (x : α) (h : x ∈ s), p ⟨x, h⟩
SetCoe.forall.description: The universal quantification over elements of a coerced subset is equivalent to universal quantification over the original set with membership constraints.

SetCoe.exists.code: SetCoe.exists.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : ↑s → Prop} : (∃ x, p x) ↔ ∃ x, ∃ (h : x ∈ s), p ⟨x, h⟩
SetCoe.exists.description: The existence of an element satisfying a property in a set is equivalent to the existence of an element in that set whose image under a coercion also satisfies the property.

SetCoe.exists'.code: SetCoe.exists'.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : (x : α) → x ∈ s → Prop} : (∃ x, ∃ (h : x ∈ s), p x h) ↔ ∃ x, p ↑x ⋯
SetCoe.exists'.description: The existence of an element in a set that satisfies a property is equivalent to the existence of that property being satisfied by a corresponding element in the set's type.

SetCoe.forall'.code:
SetCoe.forall'.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : (x : α) → x ∈ s → Prop} :
  (∀ (x : α) (h : x ∈ s), p x h) ↔ ∀ (x : ↑s), p ↑x ⋯
SetCoe.forall'.description: The universal quantification over elements of a set with membership conditions is equivalent to universal quantification over the coerced version of that set.

set_coe_cast.code: set_coe_cast.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (H' : s = t) (H : ↑s = ↑t) (x : ↑s) : cast H x = ⟨↑x, ⋯⟩
set_coe_cast.description: When two sets are equal and their corresponding types are equal, an element from one set can be cast to a subtype of that element in the other set.

SetCoe.ext.code: SetCoe.ext.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {a b : ↑s} : ↑a = ↑b → a = b
SetCoe.ext.description: The equality of lifted elements from a set implies the equality of their corresponding original elements.

SetCoe.ext_iff.code: SetCoe.ext_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {a b : ↑s} : ↑a = ↑b ↔ a = b
SetCoe.ext_iff.description: The equality of two elements in a coerced set is equivalent to the equality of the original elements.

Subtype.mem.code: Subtype.mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} (p : ↑s) : ↑p ∈ s
Subtype.mem.description: An element of a subtype is a member of the original set from which the subtype is derived.

Eq.subset.code: Eq.subset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} : s = t → s ⊆ t
Eq.subset.comment: Duplicate of `Eq.subset'`, which currently has elaboration problems.
Eq.subset.description: Equality of two sets implies that one set is a subset of the other.

Set.ext_iff.code: Set.ext_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s = t ↔ ∀ (x : α), x ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t

explanatories.SetCoe.ext_iff: The equality of two elements in a coerced set is equivalent to the equality of the original elements.

Set.ext_iff.description: Two sets are equal if and only if each element belongs to one set if and only if it belongs to the other.

Set.mem_of_mem_of_subset.code: Set.mem_of_mem_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {s t : Set α} (hx : x ∈ s) (h : s ⊆ t) : x ∈ t
Set.mem_of_mem_of_subset.description: If an element belongs to a set and that set is a subset of another, then the element also belongs to the second set.

Set.forall_in_swap.code:
Set.forall_in_swap.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} {p : α → β → Prop} :
  (∀ a ∈ s, ∀ (b : β), p a b) ↔ ∀ (b : β), ∀ a ∈ s, p a b
Set.forall_in_swap.description: The statement that for every element in a set, a property involving that element and another can be expressed in two equivalent ways depending on the order of quantification.

Set.mem_setOf.code: Set.mem_setOf.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {p : α → Prop} : a ∈ {x | p x} ↔ p a
Set.mem_setOf.description: An element is in the set of all elements satisfying a property if and only if that property holds for the element.

Membership.mem.out.code: Membership.mem.out.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {a : α} (h : a ∈ {x | p x}) : p a
Membership.mem.out.comment:
If `h : a ∈ {x | p x}` then `h.out : p x`. These are definitionally equal, but this can
nevertheless be useful for various reasons, e.g. to apply further projection notation or in an
argument to `simp`.

explanatories.Subtype.mem: An element of a subtype is a member of the original set from which the subtype is derived.

Membership.mem.out.description: If an element belongs to a set defined by a property, then that property holds for the element itself.

Set.nmem_setOf_iff.code: Set.nmem_setOf_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {p : α → Prop} : a ∉ {x | p x} ↔ ¬p a
Set.nmem_setOf_iff.description: An element is not a member of a set defined by a property if and only if that property does not hold for the element.

Set.setOf_mem_eq.code: Set.setOf_mem_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : {x | x ∈ s} = s
Set.setOf_mem_eq.description: The set of elements that belong to a set is equal to the original set itself.

Set.setOf_set.code: Set.setOf_set.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : setOf s = s
Set.setOf_set.description: The set of elements defined by a set is equal to the set itself.

Set.setOf_app_iff.code: Set.setOf_app_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} {x : α} : {x | p x} x ↔ p x
Set.setOf_app_iff.description: The statement that a specific element satisfies a property is equivalent to asserting that the property holds for that element.

Set.mem_def.code: Set.mem_def.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : a ∈ s ↔ s a
Set.mem_def.description: The membership of an element in a set is equivalent to the assertion that the set includes that element.

Set.setOf_bijective.description: The mapping from a set to its collection of elements is a bijective function.

Set.setOf_subset_setOf.code: Set.setOf_subset_setOf.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} : {a | p a} ⊆ {a | q a} ↔ ∀ (a : α), p a → q a
Set.setOf_subset_setOf.description: The inclusion of the set of elements satisfying one property in the set of elements satisfying another property is equivalent to stating that whenever an element satisfies the first property, it must also satisfy the second property.

Set.setOf_and.code: Set.setOf_and.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} : {a | p a ∧ q a} = {a | p a} ∩ {a | q a}
Set.setOf_and.description: The set of elements satisfying both properties is equal to the intersection of the sets defined by each property individually.

Set.setOf_or.code: Set.setOf_or.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} : {a | p a ∨ q a} = {a | p a} ∪ {a | q a}
Set.setOf_or.description: The set of elements satisfying either of two properties is equal to the union of the sets of elements satisfying each property individually.

Set.subset_def.code: Set.subset_def.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ⊆ t) = ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ t
Set.subset_def.description: A set is a subset of another set if and only if every element of the first set is also an element of the second set.

Set.ssubset_def.code: Set.ssubset_def.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ⊂ t) = (s ⊆ t ∧ ¬t ⊆ s)
Set.ssubset_def.description: A set is a proper subset of another set if and only if it is a subset of the second set and the second set is not a subset of the first set.

Set.Subset.refl.code: Set.Subset.refl.{u} {α : Type u} (a : Set α) : a ⊆ a
Set.Subset.refl.description: A set is always a subset of itself.

Set.Subset.rfl.code: Set.Subset.rfl.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s ⊆ s

explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.

Set.Subset.rfl.description: Every set is a subset of itself.

Set.Subset.trans.code: Set.Subset.trans.{u} {α : Type u} {a b c : Set α} (ab : a ⊆ b) (bc : b ⊆ c) : a ⊆ c

explanatories.Iff.trans: The theorem demonstrates that if two propositions are equivalent to a third proposition, then the first and the third propositions are also equivalent.
explanatories.Eq.trans: This theorem asserts that equality is transitive, meaning if one value equals a second value and that second value equals a third value, then the first value must equal the third value.

Set.Subset.trans.description: The transitive property of set inclusion states that if one set is included in a second set, and that second set is included in a third set, then the first set is also included in the third set.

Set.mem_of_eq_of_mem.code: Set.mem_of_eq_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} {s : Set α} (hx : x = y) (h : y ∈ s) : x ∈ s
Set.mem_of_eq_of_mem.description: If two elements are equal and one is a member of a set, then the other element is also a member of that set.

Set.Subset.antisymm.code: Set.Subset.antisymm.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : Set α} (h₁ : a ⊆ b) (h₂ : b ⊆ a) : a = b
Set.Subset.antisymm.description: Two sets are equal if each is a subset of the other.

Set.Subset.antisymm_iff.code: Set.Subset.antisymm_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : Set α} : a = b ↔ a ⊆ b ∧ b ⊆ a
Set.Subset.antisymm_iff.description: Two sets are equal if and only if each set is a subset of the other.

Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset.code: Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : Set α} : a ⊆ b → b ⊆ a → a = b
Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset.description: Two sets are equal if one is a subset of the other and vice versa.

Set.mem_of_subset_of_mem.code: Set.mem_of_subset_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} {a : α} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) : a ∈ s₁ → a ∈ s₂
Set.mem_of_subset_of_mem.description: If one set is a subset of another set, then any element belonging to the first set also belongs to the second set.

Set.not_mem_subset.code: Set.not_mem_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : a ∉ t → a ∉ s
Set.not_mem_subset.description: If an element is not a member of a superset, then it cannot be a member of the subset of that superset.

Set.not_subset.code: Set.not_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : ¬s ⊆ t ↔ ∃ a ∈ s, a ∉ t
Set.not_subset.description: The assertion that a set is not a subset of another is equivalent to the existence of at least one element in the first set that is not contained in the second set.

Set.eq_or_ssubset_of_subset.code: Set.eq_or_ssubset_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : s = t ∨ s ⊂ t
Set.eq_or_ssubset_of_subset.description: If one set is a subset of another, then either the two sets are equal or the first set is a proper subset of the second.

Set.exists_of_ssubset.code: Set.exists_of_ssubset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊂ t) : ∃ x ∈ t, x ∉ s
Set.exists_of_ssubset.description: If one set is a proper subset of another, then there exists at least one element in the larger set that is not contained in the smaller set.

Set.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.code: Set.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊂ t ↔ s ⊆ t ∧ s ≠ t
Set.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.description: The strict inclusion of one set in another is equivalent to asserting that the first set is a subset of the second set and that the two sets are not equal.

Set.ssubset_iff_of_subset.code: Set.ssubset_iff_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : s ⊂ t ↔ ∃ x ∈ t, x ∉ s
Set.ssubset_iff_of_subset.description: A proper subset relation between two sets is equivalent to the existence of an element in the larger set that is not in the smaller set, given that the smaller set is a subset of the larger one.

Set.ssubset_of_ssubset_of_subset.code: Set.ssubset_of_ssubset_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : Set α} (hs₁s₂ : s₁ ⊂ s₂) (hs₂s₃ : s₂ ⊆ s₃) : s₁ ⊂ s₃
Set.ssubset_of_ssubset_of_subset.description: If one set is a strict subset of a second set, and the second set is a subset of a third set, then the first set is also a strict subset of the third set.

Set.ssubset_of_subset_of_ssubset.code: Set.ssubset_of_subset_of_ssubset.{u} {α : Type u} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : Set α} (hs₁s₂ : s₁ ⊆ s₂) (hs₂s₃ : s₂ ⊂ s₃) : s₁ ⊂ s₃
Set.ssubset_of_subset_of_ssubset.description: If one set is a subset of a second and that second set is a proper subset of a third, then the first set is also a proper subset of the third.

Set.not_mem_empty.description: Any element cannot be a member of the empty set.

Set.not_not_mem.code: Set.not_not_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : ¬a ∉ s ↔ a ∈ s
Set.not_not_mem.description: The negation of an element not being in a set is equivalent to the element being in the set.

Set.nonempty_coe_sort.code: Set.nonempty_coe_sort.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : Nonempty ↑s ↔ s.Nonempty
Set.nonempty_coe_sort.description: A non-empty subtype of a set is equivalent to the original set being non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.coe_sort.code: Set.Nonempty.coe_sort.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty → Nonempty ↑s
Set.Nonempty.coe_sort.description: If a set is non-empty, then the sum of its elements is also a non-empty set.

Set.nonempty_def.code: Set.nonempty_def.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty ↔ ∃ x, x ∈ s
Set.nonempty_def.description: A set is nonempty if and only if there exists at least one element belonging to it.

Set.nonempty_of_mem.code: Set.nonempty_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} (h : x ∈ s) : s.Nonempty
Set.nonempty_of_mem.description: If an element is a member of a set, then that set is non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.not_subset_empty.code: Set.Nonempty.not_subset_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty → ¬s ⊆ ∅
Set.Nonempty.not_subset_empty.description: A nonempty set cannot be a subset of the empty set.

Set.Nonempty.some.code: Set.Nonempty.some.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (h : s.Nonempty) : α
Set.Nonempty.some.comment:
Extract a witness from `s.Nonempty`. This function might be used instead of case analysis
on the argument. Note that it makes a proof depend on the `Classical.choice` axiom.

explanatories.Classical.choose: The operation returns an element that satisfies a given property when it is known that such an element exists.

Set.Nonempty.some.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def Nonempty.some (h : s.Nonempty) : α :=   Classical.choose h
Set.Nonempty.some.description: The function provides a way to extract an element from a non-empty set, relying on the axiom of choice.

Set.Nonempty.some_mem.code: Set.Nonempty.some_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (h : s.Nonempty) : h.some ∈ s
Set.Nonempty.some_mem.description: If a set is nonempty, then there exists at least one element in that set.

Set.Nonempty.mono.code: Set.Nonempty.mono.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (ht : s ⊆ t) (hs : s.Nonempty) : t.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.mono.description: If a non-empty set is a subset of another set, then the larger set is also non-empty.

Set.nonempty_of_not_subset.code: Set.nonempty_of_not_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : ¬s ⊆ t) : (s \ t).Nonempty
Set.nonempty_of_not_subset.description: If a set is not a subset of another, then the difference between the two sets contains at least one element.

Set.nonempty_of_ssubset.code: Set.nonempty_of_ssubset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (ht : s ⊂ t) : (t \ s).Nonempty
Set.nonempty_of_ssubset.description: If one set is a proper subset of another, then the difference between the two sets is non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.of_diff.code: Set.Nonempty.of_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : (s \ t).Nonempty) : s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_diff.description: If the difference of two sets is nonempty, then at least one of those sets must also be nonempty.

Set.nonempty_of_ssubset'.code: Set.nonempty_of_ssubset'.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (ht : s ⊂ t) : t.Nonempty
Set.nonempty_of_ssubset'.description: If one set is a proper subset of another, then the larger set is non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.inl.code: Set.Nonempty.inl.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (hs : s.Nonempty) : (s ∪ t).Nonempty

explanatories.Or.inl: The left injection into a disjunction allows a proven statement to be included as a true proposition within either of the options of an "or" logical construction.

Set.Nonempty.inl.description: If one set is non-empty, then the union of that set with any other set is also non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.inr.code: Set.Nonempty.inr.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (ht : t.Nonempty) : (s ∪ t).Nonempty

explanatories.Or.inr: The right injection operation allows one to obtain a disjunction by confirming the truth of a specific proposition.

Set.Nonempty.inr.description: If one set is non-empty, then the union of that set with any other set is also non-empty.

Set.union_nonempty.code: Set.union_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∪ t).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty ∨ t.Nonempty
Set.union_nonempty.description: The union of two sets is non-empty if and only if at least one of the sets is non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.left.code: Set.Nonempty.left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : (s ∩ t).Nonempty) : s.Nonempty

explanatories.And.left: The left conjunct of a conjunction provides a proof of the first statement in the combined assertion.

Set.Nonempty.left.description: If the intersection of two sets is nonempty, then at least one of those sets must also be nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.right.code: Set.Nonempty.right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : (s ∩ t).Nonempty) : t.Nonempty

explanatories.And.right: The theorem allows one to derive the second component of a conjunction from a given statement that asserts both components are true.

Set.Nonempty.right.description: If the intersection of two sets is non-empty, then at least one of those sets must also be non-empty.

Set.inter_nonempty.code: Set.inter_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∩ t).Nonempty ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, x ∈ t
Set.inter_nonempty.description: The intersection of two sets is non-empty if and only if there exists at least one element that is a member of both sets.

Set.inter_nonempty_iff_exists_left.code: Set.inter_nonempty_iff_exists_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∩ t).Nonempty ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, x ∈ t
Set.inter_nonempty_iff_exists_left.description: The intersection of two sets is non-empty if and only if there exists at least one element in the first set that is also in the second set.

Set.inter_nonempty_iff_exists_right.code: Set.inter_nonempty_iff_exists_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∩ t).Nonempty ↔ ∃ x ∈ t, x ∈ s
Set.inter_nonempty_iff_exists_right.description: The intersection of two sets is non-empty if and only if there exists an element in one set that is also in the other set.

Set.nonempty_iff_univ_nonempty.code: Set.nonempty_iff_univ_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} : Nonempty α ↔ univ.Nonempty
Set.nonempty_iff_univ_nonempty.description: A type is nonempty if and only if its universe is nonempty.

Set.univ_nonempty.description: The universal set is nonempty if the underlying type is nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.to_subtype.code: Set.Nonempty.to_subtype.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty → Nonempty ↑s
Set.Nonempty.to_subtype.description: If a set is non-empty, then there exists at least one element in that set when considered as a subtype.

Set.Nonempty.to_type.code: Set.Nonempty.to_type.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty → Nonempty α
Set.Nonempty.to_type.description: If a set is non-empty, then its underlying type is also non-empty.

explanatories.Set.univ_nonempty: The universal set is nonempty if the underlying type is nonempty.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.to_subtype: If a set is non-empty, then there exists at least one element in that set when considered as a subtype.

Set.univ.nonempty.fullDefinition: instance univ.nonempty [Nonempty α] : Nonempty (↥(Set.univ : Set α)) :=   Set.univ_nonempty.to_subtype
Set.univ.nonempty.description: The universal set of a nonempty type is itself nonempty.

Set.nonempty_of_nonempty_subtype.code: Set.nonempty_of_nonempty_subtype.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} [Nonempty ↑s] : s.Nonempty
Set.nonempty_of_nonempty_subtype.description: If a subtype of a set is non-empty, then the original set is also non-empty.

Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_not_mem.description: A set is empty if and only if no element belongs to it.

Set.eq_empty_of_forall_not_mem.description: If no element belongs to a set, then that set is empty.

Set.eq_empty_of_subset_empty.description: If a set is a subset of the empty set, then that set must also be empty.

Set.eq_empty_of_isEmpty.description: Any set consisting of elements from an empty type is itself empty.

Set.uniqueEmpty.description: There is a unique set corresponding to any type that is empty.

Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.code: Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : ¬s.Nonempty ↔ s = ∅
Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.description: A set is not nonempty if and only if it is equal to the empty set.

Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.description: A set is non-empty if and only if it is not equal to the empty set.

Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty'.description: A set is empty if and only if it is not nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.ne_empty.description: If a set is non-empty, then it is not equal to the empty set.

Set.not_nonempty_empty.description: The empty set is not non-empty.

Set.isEmpty_coe_sort.code: Set.isEmpty_coe_sort.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : IsEmpty ↑s ↔ s = ∅
Set.isEmpty_coe_sort.description: The set is empty if and only if the set’s canonical representation corresponds to the empty set.

Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty.description: A set is either empty or contains at least one element.

Set.subset_eq_empty.description: A subset of an empty set must also be empty.

Set.forall_mem_empty.code: Set.forall_mem_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} : (∀ x ∈ ∅, p x) ↔ True
Set.forall_mem_empty.description: A property is vacuously true for all elements in the empty set, which is equivalent to stating that any statement is true.

Set.empty_ssubset.description: The empty set is a proper subset of a set if and only if that set is non-empty.

Set.setOf_true.description: The set of all elements for which a given statement is always true is equal to the universal set.

Set.subset_univ.code: Set.subset_univ.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : s ⊆ univ
Set.subset_univ.description: Every set is a subset of the universal set.

Set.univ_subset_iff.code: Set.univ_subset_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : univ ⊆ s ↔ s = univ
Set.univ_subset_iff.description: A set is a superset of the universal set if and only if it is equal to the universal set itself.

Set.eq_univ_of_univ_subset.code: Set.eq_univ_of_univ_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : univ ⊆ s → s = univ
Set.eq_univ_of_univ_subset.description: If the universal set is a subset of another set, then that set must be equal to the universal set.

Set.eq_univ_of_forall.description: A set is equal to the universal set if every element in the underlying type belongs to that set.

Set.Nonempty.eq_univ.description: If a set is non-empty and all of its elements are identical, then that set must be equal to the universal set.

Set.ssubset_univ_iff.description: A set is a proper subset of the universal set if and only if it is not equal to the universal set.

Set.inter_right_comm.code: Set.inter_right_comm.{u} {α : Type u} (s₁ s₂ s₃ : Set α) : s₁ ∩ s₂ ∩ s₃ = s₁ ∩ s₃ ∩ s₂
Set.inter_right_comm.description: The intersection of three sets is commutative in the sense that the order of the last two sets does not affect the result.

Set.inter_subset_left.code: Set.inter_subset_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ∩ t ⊆ s
Set.inter_subset_left.description: The intersection of two sets is a subset of the first set.

Set.inter_subset_right.code: Set.inter_subset_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ∩ t ⊆ t
Set.inter_subset_right.description: The intersection of two sets is a subset of the second set.

Set.subset_inter.code: Set.subset_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t r : Set α} (rs : r ⊆ s) (rt : r ⊆ t) : r ⊆ s ∩ t
Set.subset_inter.description: If a set is a subset of two other sets, then it is also a subset of their intersection.

Set.subset_inter_iff.code: Set.subset_inter_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t r : Set α} : r ⊆ s ∩ t ↔ r ⊆ s ∧ r ⊆ t
Set.subset_inter_iff.description: A set is a subset of the intersection of two other sets if and only if it is a subset of each of those sets individually.

Set.inter_eq_left.code: Set.inter_eq_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ∩ t = s ↔ s ⊆ t
Set.inter_eq_left.description: The intersection of two sets is equal to the first set if and only if the first set is a subset of the second set.

Set.inter_eq_right.code: Set.inter_eq_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ∩ t = t ↔ t ⊆ s
Set.inter_eq_right.description: The intersection of two sets equals one of the sets if and only if the second set is a subset of the first set.

Set.inter_eq_self_of_subset_left.code: Set.inter_eq_self_of_subset_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊆ t → s ∩ t = s
Set.inter_eq_self_of_subset_left.description: The intersection of a set with another set that it is a subset of is equal to the original set.

Set.inter_eq_self_of_subset_right.code: Set.inter_eq_self_of_subset_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : t ⊆ s → s ∩ t = t
Set.inter_eq_self_of_subset_right.description: If one set is a subset of another, then the intersection of the two sets with the larger set yields the smaller set.

Set.inter_congr_left.code: Set.inter_congr_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (ht : s ∩ u ⊆ t) (hu : s ∩ t ⊆ u) : s ∩ t = s ∩ u
Set.inter_congr_left.description: The intersection of two sets with a shared first set is equal if the first set's intersection with one is contained in the other and vice versa.

Set.inter_congr_right.code: Set.inter_congr_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (hs : t ∩ u ⊆ s) (ht : s ∩ u ⊆ t) : s ∩ u = t ∩ u
Set.inter_congr_right.description: The intersections of two sets with a common third set are equal if each set is a subset of the intersection with the third set.

Set.inter_eq_inter_iff_left.code: Set.inter_eq_inter_iff_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s ∩ t = s ∩ u ↔ s ∩ u ⊆ t ∧ s ∩ t ⊆ u
Set.inter_eq_inter_iff_left.description: The intersection of one set with two others is the same if and only if the intersection of that set with one is a subset of the other, and vice versa.

Set.inter_eq_inter_iff_right.code: Set.inter_eq_inter_iff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s ∩ u = t ∩ u ↔ t ∩ u ⊆ s ∧ s ∩ u ⊆ t
Set.inter_eq_inter_iff_right.description: The intersection of two sets with a third set is equal if and only if each intersection is a subset of the other.

Set.inter_univ.code: Set.inter_univ.{u} {α : Type u} (a : Set α) : a ∩ univ = a
Set.inter_univ.description: The intersection of any set with the universal set is equal to that set.

Set.univ_inter.code: Set.univ_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (a : Set α) : univ ∩ a = a
Set.univ_inter.description: The intersection of the universal set with any set is equal to that set.

Set.inter_subset_inter.code: Set.inter_subset_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} (h₁ : s₁ ⊆ t₁) (h₂ : s₂ ⊆ t₂) : s₁ ∩ s₂ ⊆ t₁ ∩ t₂
Set.inter_subset_inter.description: The intersection of two sets is a subset of the intersection of two other sets if each of the first sets is a subset of the corresponding second set.

Set.inter_subset_inter_left.code: Set.inter_subset_inter_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (u : Set α) (H : s ⊆ t) : s ∩ u ⊆ t ∩ u
Set.inter_subset_inter_left.description: The intersection of a set with another set is a subset of the intersection of the second set with the same set if the first set is a subset of the second.

Set.inter_subset_inter_right.code: Set.inter_subset_inter_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (u : Set α) (H : s ⊆ t) : u ∩ s ⊆ u ∩ t
Set.inter_subset_inter_right.description: The intersection of a set with two overlapping sets maintains the subset relationship if one of the sets is a subset of the other.

Set.union_inter_cancel_left.code: Set.union_inter_cancel_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∪ t) ∩ s = s
Set.union_inter_cancel_left.description: The intersection of a set with the union of itself and another set is equal to the original set.

Set.union_inter_cancel_right.code: Set.union_inter_cancel_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∪ t) ∩ t = t
Set.union_inter_cancel_right.description: The intersection of the union of two sets with one of those sets equals that set.

Set.inter_setOf_eq_sep.code: Set.inter_setOf_eq_sep.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) (p : α → Prop) : s ∩ {a | p a} = {a | a ∈ s ∧ p a}
Set.inter_setOf_eq_sep.description: The intersection of a set with the set of elements satisfying a property is equal to the set of elements from the first set that also satisfy that property.

Set.setOf_inter_eq_sep.code: Set.setOf_inter_eq_sep.{u} {α : Type u} (p : α → Prop) (s : Set α) : {a | p a} ∩ s = {a | a ∈ s ∧ p a}
Set.setOf_inter_eq_sep.description: The intersection of the set of elements satisfying a property with another set is equal to the set of elements that belong to the second set and satisfy that property.

Set.inter_union_distrib_left.code: Set.inter_union_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∩ (t ∪ u) = s ∩ t ∪ s ∩ u
Set.inter_union_distrib_left.description: The intersection of a set with the union of two other sets is equal to the union of the intersections of the first set with each of the two other sets.

Set.union_inter_distrib_right.code: Set.union_inter_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : (s ∪ t) ∩ u = s ∩ u ∪ t ∩ u
Set.union_inter_distrib_right.description: The intersection of the union of two sets with a third set is equal to the union of the intersections of each of the first two sets with the third set.

Set.union_inter_distrib_left.code: Set.union_inter_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∪ t ∩ u = (s ∪ t) ∩ (s ∪ u)
Set.union_inter_distrib_left.description: The union of a set with the intersection of two other sets is equal to the intersection of the union of the first set with each of the other two sets.

Set.inter_union_distrib_right.code: Set.inter_union_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∩ t ∪ u = (s ∪ u) ∩ (t ∪ u)
Set.inter_union_distrib_right.description: The intersection of a set with the union of two others is equal to the intersection of the first set with each of the others unioned with the third set.

Set.union_union_distrib_left.code: Set.union_union_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∪ (t ∪ u) = s ∪ t ∪ (s ∪ u)
Set.union_union_distrib_left.description: The union of a set with the union of two other sets is equal to the union of the first set with each of the other sets combined with the first set again.

Set.union_union_distrib_right.code: Set.union_union_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∪ t ∪ u = s ∪ u ∪ (t ∪ u)
Set.union_union_distrib_right.description: The union of three sets can be rearranged such that the first set is combined with the third set and then the union of the second set with the third set follows.

Set.inter_inter_distrib_left.code: Set.inter_inter_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∩ (t ∩ u) = s ∩ t ∩ (s ∩ u)
Set.inter_inter_distrib_left.description: The intersection of a set with the intersection of two other sets is equal to the intersection of the first set with each of the other sets.

Set.inter_inter_distrib_right.code: Set.inter_inter_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∩ t ∩ u = s ∩ u ∩ (t ∩ u)
Set.inter_inter_distrib_right.description: The intersection of three sets can be rearranged such that the first set intersects with the third set and the second set intersects with the third set without changing the overall set.

Set.union_union_union_comm.code: Set.union_union_union_comm.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u v : Set α) : s ∪ t ∪ (u ∪ v) = s ∪ u ∪ (t ∪ v)
Set.union_union_union_comm.description: The union of two sets combined with a union of two other sets can be rearranged without changing the overall result.

Set.inter_inter_inter_comm.code: Set.inter_inter_inter_comm.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u v : Set α) : s ∩ t ∩ (u ∩ v) = s ∩ u ∩ (t ∩ v)
Set.inter_inter_inter_comm.description: The equality of the intersection of four sets is commutative with respect to the grouping of the sets involved.

Set.insert_def.code: Set.insert_def.{u} {α : Type u} (x : α) (s : Set α) : insert x s = {y | y = x ∨ y ∈ s}

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_def.description: Inserting an element into a set is defined as the set of elements that are either the inserted element or belong to the original set.

Set.subset_insert.code: Set.subset_insert.{u} {α : Type u} (x : α) (s : Set α) : s ⊆ insert x s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.subset_insert.description: Any set is a subset of the set formed by adding an element to it.

Set.mem_insert.code: Set.mem_insert.{u} {α : Type u} (x : α) (s : Set α) : x ∈ insert x s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.mem_insert.description: An element is a member of the set formed by inserting that element into another set.

Set.mem_insert_of_mem.code: Set.mem_insert_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {s : Set α} (y : α) : x ∈ s → x ∈ insert y s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.mem_insert_of_mem.description: If an element belongs to a set, it also belongs to the set formed by adding another element to that set.

Set.eq_or_mem_of_mem_insert.code: Set.eq_or_mem_of_mem_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {x a : α} {s : Set α} : x ∈ insert a s → x = a ∨ x ∈ s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.eq_or_mem_of_mem_insert.description: An element is either equal to the inserted element or belongs to the remainder of the set if it is a member of the set formed by inserting that element into another set.

Set.mem_of_mem_insert_of_ne.code: Set.mem_of_mem_insert_of_ne.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} {s : Set α} : b ∈ insert a s → b ≠ a → b ∈ s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.mem_of_mem_insert_of_ne.description: If an element belongs to the insertion of a set but is different from the inserted element, then it must belong to the original set.

Set.eq_of_not_mem_of_mem_insert.code: Set.eq_of_not_mem_of_mem_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} {s : Set α} : b ∈ insert a s → b ∉ s → b = a

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.eq_of_not_mem_of_mem_insert.description: If an element is in a set that contains another element and is not in the original set, then the two elements must be equal.

Set.mem_insert_iff.code: Set.mem_insert_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {x a : α} {s : Set α} : x ∈ insert a s ↔ x = a ∨ x ∈ s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.mem_insert_iff.description: An element belongs to the insertion of an element into a set if and only if it is either that element or an element of the original set.

Set.insert_eq_of_mem.code: Set.insert_eq_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} (h : a ∈ s) : insert a s = s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_eq_of_mem.description: Inserting an element into a set that already contains that element does not change the set.

Set.ne_insert_of_not_mem.code: Set.ne_insert_of_not_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (t : Set α) {a : α} : a ∉ s → s ≠ insert a t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.ne_insert_of_not_mem.description: If an element is not a member of a set, then that set cannot be equal to the result of inserting that element into another set.

Set.insert_eq_self.code: Set.insert_eq_self.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : insert a s = s ↔ a ∈ s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_eq_self.description: The insertion of an element into a set results in the same set if and only if the element is already a member of that set.

Set.insert_ne_self.code: Set.insert_ne_self.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : insert a s ≠ s ↔ a ∉ s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_ne_self.description: Inserting an element into a set results in a different set if and only if that element is not already in the original set.

Set.insert_subset_iff.code: Set.insert_subset_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} : insert a s ⊆ t ↔ a ∈ t ∧ s ⊆ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_subset_iff.description: The inclusion of a set that contains an element and another set is equivalent to the condition that the element is in the second set and the first set is a subset of the second set.

Set.insert_subset_insert.code: Set.insert_subset_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : insert a s ⊆ insert a t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_subset_insert.description: If one set is a subset of another, then inserting an additional element into both sets still maintains the subset relationship.

Set.insert_subset_insert_iff.code: Set.insert_subset_insert_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (ha : a ∉ s) : insert a s ⊆ insert a t ↔ s ⊆ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_subset_insert_iff.description: The insertion of an element into one set is a subset of the insertion into another set if and only if the original sets are related as a subset.

Set.subset_insert_iff_of_not_mem.code: Set.subset_insert_iff_of_not_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (ha : a ∉ s) : s ⊆ insert a t ↔ s ⊆ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.subset_insert_iff_of_not_mem.description: If an element is not a member of a set, then that set is a subset of the result of inserting that element into another set if and only if it is a subset of the second set.

Set.ssubset_iff_insert.code: Set.ssubset_iff_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊂ t ↔ ∃ a ∉ s, insert a s ⊆ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.ssubset_iff_insert.description: A set is a proper subset of another set if and only if there exists an element not in the first set that can be added to it, resulting in a set that is contained within the second set.

Set.ssubset_insert.code: Set.ssubset_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {a : α} (h : a ∉ s) : s ⊂ insert a s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.ssubset_insert.description: A set is a proper subset of the set formed by inserting an element into it if that element is not already a member of the original set.

Set.insert_comm.code: Set.insert_comm.{u} {α : Type u} (a b : α) (s : Set α) : insert a (insert b s) = insert b (insert a s)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_comm.description: Inserting two elements into a set in either order results in the same set.

Set.insert_idem.code: Set.insert_idem.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) (s : Set α) : insert a (insert a s) = insert a s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_idem.description: Inserting the same element into a set multiple times does not change the set.

Set.insert_union.code: Set.insert_union.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} : insert a s ∪ t = insert a (s ∪ t)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_union.description: The union of a set with an element inserted into another set is equivalent to inserting that element into the union of both sets.

Set.union_insert.code: Set.union_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} : s ∪ insert a t = insert a (s ∪ t)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.union_insert.description: The union of a set with the insertion of an element into another set is equal to the insertion of that element into the union of both sets.

Set.insert_nonempty.code: Set.insert_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) (s : Set α) : (insert a s).Nonempty

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_nonempty.description: Inserting an element into a set always results in a non-empty set.

Set.insert_inter_distrib.code: Set.insert_inter_distrib.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) (s t : Set α) : insert a (s ∩ t) = insert a s ∩ insert a t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_inter_distrib.description: Inserting an element into the intersection of two sets results in a set that is equivalent to the intersection of the sets formed by inserting that element into each set individually.

Set.insert_union_distrib.code: Set.insert_union_distrib.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) (s t : Set α) : insert a (s ∪ t) = insert a s ∪ insert a t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_union_distrib.description: The insertion of an element into the union of two sets is equal to the union of the insertion of that element into each set individually.

Set.insert_inj.code: Set.insert_inj.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} {s : Set α} (ha : a ∉ s) : insert a s = insert b s ↔ a = b

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_inj.description: If an element is not a member of a set, then inserting two different elements into that set results in the same set if and only if the two elements are equal.

Set.forall_of_forall_insert.code:
Set.forall_of_forall_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {P : α → Prop} {a : α} {s : Set α} (H : ∀ x ∈ insert a s, P x) (x : α)
  (h : x ∈ s) : P x

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.forall_of_forall_insert.description: If a property holds for every element in a set when one specific element is added to that set, then the property must also hold for any element that is already in the original set.

Set.forall_insert_of_forall.code:
Set.forall_insert_of_forall.{u} {α : Type u} {P : α → Prop} {a : α} {s : Set α} (H : ∀ x ∈ s, P x) (ha : P a) (x : α)
  (h : x ∈ insert a s) : P x

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.forall_insert_of_forall.description: If a property holds for all elements in a set and also for an additional element, then it must hold for any element that is in the union of that element with the set.

Set.exists_mem_insert.code: Set.exists_mem_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {P : α → Prop} {a : α} {s : Set α} : (∃ x ∈ insert a s, P x) ↔ P a ∨ ∃ x ∈ s, P x

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.exists_mem_insert.description: An element in the insert of a set satisfies a property if and only if either the inserted element satisfies the property or an element in the original set satisfies it.

Set.forall_mem_insert.code: Set.forall_mem_insert.{u} {α : Type u} {P : α → Prop} {a : α} {s : Set α} : (∀ x ∈ insert a s, P x) ↔ P a ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, P x

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.forall_mem_insert.description: A property holds for all elements in an inserted set if and only if it holds for the newly added element and for all elements in the previous set.

Set.singleton_def.code: Set.singleton_def.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) : {a} = insert a ∅

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.singleton_def.description: The singleton set containing an element is equal to the set obtained by inserting that element into the empty set.

Set.mem_singleton_iff.code: Set.mem_singleton_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} : a ∈ {b} ↔ a = b
Set.mem_singleton_iff.description: An element belongs to a singleton set if and only if it is equal to the unique element in that set.

Set.setOf_eq_eq_singleton.code: Set.setOf_eq_eq_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} : {n | n = a} = {a}
Set.setOf_eq_eq_singleton.description: The set of elements equal to a specific element is identical to the singleton set containing that element.

Set.setOf_eq_eq_singleton'.code: Set.setOf_eq_eq_singleton'.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} : {x | a = x} = {a}
Set.setOf_eq_eq_singleton'.description: The set of elements equal to a specified element is exactly the singleton set containing that element.

Set.mem_singleton.description: An element is a member of the singleton set that contains only that element.

Set.eq_of_mem_singleton.code: Set.eq_of_mem_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} (h : x ∈ {y}) : x = y
Set.eq_of_mem_singleton.description: If an element belongs to a singleton set, then it must be equal to the element contained in that set.

Set.singleton_eq_singleton_iff.code: Set.singleton_eq_singleton_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} : {x} = {y} ↔ x = y
Set.singleton_eq_singleton_iff.description: Two singleton sets are equal if and only if their contained elements are equal.

Set.singleton_injective.description: The singleton function is injective, meaning that different elements produce different single-element sets.

Set.mem_singleton_of_eq.code: Set.mem_singleton_of_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} (H : x = y) : x ∈ {y}
Set.mem_singleton_of_eq.description: If two elements are equal, then one of them belongs to the singleton set containing the other.

Set.insert_eq.code: Set.insert_eq.{u} {α : Type u} (x : α) (s : Set α) : insert x s = {x} ∪ s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_eq.description: Inserting an element into a set results in a new set that is equivalent to the union of the singleton set containing that element and the original set.

Set.singleton_nonempty.description: A singleton set containing an element is non-empty.

Set.singleton_ne_empty.description: A singleton set containing an element is not empty.

Set.empty_ssubset_singleton.description: The empty set is a proper subset of any singleton set containing an element.

Set.singleton_subset_iff.code: Set.singleton_subset_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : {a} ⊆ s ↔ a ∈ s
Set.singleton_subset_iff.description: A singleton set is a subset of another set if and only if its single element is an element of that set.

Set.singleton_subset_singleton.code: Set.singleton_subset_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} : {a} ⊆ {b} ↔ a = b
Set.singleton_subset_singleton.description: The inclusion of one singleton set in another is true if and only if the elements of both singleton sets are equal.

Set.set_compr_eq_eq_singleton.code: Set.set_compr_eq_eq_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} : {b | b = a} = {a}
Set.set_compr_eq_eq_singleton.description: The set of elements equal to a specific element is identical to the singleton set containing just that element.

Set.singleton_union.code: Set.singleton_union.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : {a} ∪ s = insert a s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.singleton_union.description: The union of a singleton set with another set is equivalent to inserting the element of the singleton into the other set.

Set.union_singleton.code: Set.union_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∪ {a} = insert a s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.union_singleton.description: The union of a set with a singleton containing an element is equal to the insertion of that element into the set.

Set.singleton_inter_nonempty.code: Set.singleton_inter_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : ({a} ∩ s).Nonempty ↔ a ∈ s
Set.singleton_inter_nonempty.description: The intersection of a singleton set containing an element with another set is nonempty if and only if the element is a member of that other set.

Set.inter_singleton_nonempty.code: Set.inter_singleton_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : (s ∩ {a}).Nonempty ↔ a ∈ s
Set.inter_singleton_nonempty.description: The intersection of a set with a singleton set is nonempty if and only if the element of the singleton set belongs to the original set.

Set.singleton_inter_eq_empty.code: Set.singleton_inter_eq_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : {a} ∩ s = ∅ ↔ a ∉ s
Set.singleton_inter_eq_empty.description: The intersection of a singleton set with another set is empty if and only if the element is not in that set.

Set.inter_singleton_eq_empty.code: Set.inter_singleton_eq_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ∩ {a} = ∅ ↔ a ∉ s
Set.inter_singleton_eq_empty.description: The intersection of a set with a singleton is empty if and only if the element of the singleton is not in the set.

Set.nmem_singleton_empty.code: Set.nmem_singleton_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s ∉ {∅} ↔ s.Nonempty
Set.nmem_singleton_empty.description: A set is not a member of the singleton containing the empty set if and only if it is nonempty.

explanatories.Subtype.eq: This theorem states that if two subtypes of a type are equal as sets, then the underlying elements of those subtypes are also equal.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.
explanatories.Set.mem_singleton: An element is a member of the singleton set that contains only that element.

Set.uniqueSingleton.fullDefinition: instance uniqueSingleton (a : α) : Unique (↥({a} : Set α)) :=   ⟨⟨⟨a, mem_singleton a⟩⟩, fun ⟨_, h⟩ => Subtype.eq h⟩
Set.uniqueSingleton.description: A unique singleton set containing a specific element is characterized by having exactly one element.

Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.code: Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : s = {a} ↔ a ∈ s ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, x = a
Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.description: A set is equal to a singleton set if and only if it contains that element and every other element in the set is equal to that element.

Set.eq_singleton_iff_nonempty_unique_mem.code: Set.eq_singleton_iff_nonempty_unique_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : s = {a} ↔ s.Nonempty ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, x = a
Set.eq_singleton_iff_nonempty_unique_mem.description: A set is equal to a singleton set if and only if it is nonempty and contains only that single element.

explanatories.Inhabited.default: A default function provides a standard element from any inhabited type, which typically represents a general or neutral value.

Set.default_coe_singleton.description: The default element of a singleton set is equal to the singleton itself, represented by the inserted element.

Set.mem_sep.code: Set.mem_sep.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} {x : α} (xs : x ∈ s) (px : p x) : x ∈ {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x}
Set.mem_sep.description: An element that belongs to a set and satisfies a property also belongs to the set of elements that are members of the original set and meet that property.

Set.sep_mem_eq.code: Set.sep_mem_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : {x | x ∈ s ∧ x ∈ t} = s ∩ t
Set.sep_mem_eq.description: The set of elements that belong to both of two sets is equal to the intersection of those sets.

Set.mem_sep_iff.code: Set.mem_sep_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} {x : α} : x ∈ {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} ↔ x ∈ s ∧ p x
Set.mem_sep_iff.description: An element belongs to a set defined by a property if and only if it is a member of the original set and satisfies that property.

Set.sep_ext_iff.code:
Set.sep_ext_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p q : α → Prop} :
  {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} = {x | x ∈ s ∧ q x} ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, p x ↔ q x
Set.sep_ext_iff.description: The equality of two subsets defined by different predicates within a set holds true if and only if the predicates are equivalent for every element in that set.

Set.sep_eq_of_subset.code: Set.sep_eq_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : {x | x ∈ t ∧ x ∈ s} = s
Set.sep_eq_of_subset.description: The intersection of a set with a superset is equal to the original set itself.

Set.sep_subset.code: Set.sep_subset.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) (p : α → Prop) : {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} ⊆ s
Set.sep_subset.description: The subset formed by selecting elements from a set that satisfy a certain property is contained within the original set.

Set.sep_eq_self_iff_mem_true.code: Set.sep_eq_self_iff_mem_true.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} = s ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, p x
Set.sep_eq_self_iff_mem_true.description: The subset defined by a property within a set is equal to the entire set if and only if every element of the set satisfies that property.

Set.sep_eq_empty_iff_mem_false.code: Set.sep_eq_empty_iff_mem_false.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : α → Prop} : {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} = ∅ ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ¬p x
Set.sep_eq_empty_iff_mem_false.description: The set of elements satisfying a property is empty if and only if no element in the original set satisfies that property.

Set.sep_true.code: Set.sep_true.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : {x | x ∈ s ∧ True} = s
Set.sep_true.description: The set of elements in another set that also satisfy a trivial true condition is identical to the original set.

Set.sep_false.code: Set.sep_false.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : {x | x ∈ s ∧ False} = ∅
Set.sep_false.description: The set of elements that belong to a given set and simultaneously satisfy a false condition is empty.

Set.sep_empty.code: Set.sep_empty.{u} {α : Type u} (p : α → Prop) : {x | x ∈ ∅ ∧ p x} = ∅
Set.sep_empty.description: The set of elements that belong to the empty set and satisfy a property is itself the empty set.

Set.sep_univ.code: Set.sep_univ.{u} {α : Type u} {p : α → Prop} : {x | x ∈ univ ∧ p x} = {x | p x}
Set.sep_univ.description: The set of elements satisfying a property within the universal set is the same as the set of elements that satisfy that property.

Set.sep_union.code:
Set.sep_union.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {p : α → Prop} :
  {x | (x ∈ s ∨ x ∈ t) ∧ p x} = {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} ∪ {x | x ∈ t ∧ p x}
Set.sep_union.description: The set of elements that belong to either of two sets and also satisfy a given property is equal to the union of the sets of elements from each set that satisfy that property.

Set.sep_inter.code:
Set.sep_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {p : α → Prop} :
  {x | (x ∈ s ∧ x ∈ t) ∧ p x} = {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} ∩ {x | x ∈ t ∧ p x}
Set.sep_inter.description: The set of elements that belong to both of two sets and satisfy a given property is equal to the intersection of the sets of elements that belong to each set individually and satisfy the property.

Set.sep_and.code:
Set.sep_and.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p q : α → Prop} :
  {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x ∧ q x} = {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} ∩ {x | x ∈ s ∧ q x}
Set.sep_and.description: The set of elements satisfying two properties simultaneously within a given set is equal to the intersection of the sets of elements satisfying each property individually.

Set.sep_or.code:
Set.sep_or.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p q : α → Prop} :
  {x | x ∈ s ∧ (p x ∨ q x)} = {x | x ∈ s ∧ p x} ∪ {x | x ∈ s ∧ q x}
Set.sep_or.description: The set of elements that satisfy either of two properties from a given set is equal to the union of the sets of elements that satisfy each property independently.

Set.sep_setOf.code: Set.sep_setOf.{u} {α : Type u} {p q : α → Prop} : {x | x ∈ {y | p y} ∧ q x} = {x | p x ∧ q x}
Set.sep_setOf.description: The set of elements satisfying a property and another condition is equivalent to the set of elements satisfying both conditions.

Set.subset_singleton_iff.code: Set.subset_singleton_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} {x : α} : s ⊆ {x} ↔ ∀ y ∈ s, y = x
Set.subset_singleton_iff.description: A set is a subset of a singleton set if and only if every element in the set is equal to the single element in the singleton.

Set.subset_singleton_iff_eq.code: Set.subset_singleton_iff_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} : s ⊆ {x} ↔ s = ∅ ∨ s = {x}
Set.subset_singleton_iff_eq.description: A set is a subset of a singleton if and only if it is either empty or equal to that singleton.

Set.Nonempty.subset_singleton_iff.code: Set.Nonempty.subset_singleton_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} (h : s.Nonempty) : s ⊆ {a} ↔ s = {a}

explanatories.Set.subset_singleton_iff: A set is a subset of a singleton set if and only if every element in the set is equal to the single element in the singleton.

Set.Nonempty.subset_singleton_iff.description: A non-empty set is contained within a single element set if and only if it is equal to that single element set.

Set.ssubset_singleton_iff.code: Set.ssubset_singleton_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} : s ⊂ {x} ↔ s = ∅
Set.ssubset_singleton_iff.description: A proper subset of a singleton set is equivalent to the empty set.

Set.eq_empty_of_ssubset_singleton.code: Set.eq_empty_of_ssubset_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} (hs : s ⊂ {x}) : s = ∅
Set.eq_empty_of_ssubset_singleton.description: A set is empty if it is a strict subset of a singleton set.

Set.eq_of_nonempty_of_subsingleton.code:
Set.eq_of_nonempty_of_subsingleton.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Subsingleton α] (s t : Set α) [Nonempty ↑s] [Nonempty ↑t] :
  s = t

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.eq_of_nonempty_of_subsingleton.description: If two non-empty sets consist of the same elements due to each having a single unique element, then the two sets are equal.

Set.eq_of_nonempty_of_subsingleton'.code:
Set.eq_of_nonempty_of_subsingleton'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Subsingleton α] {s : Set α} (t : Set α) (hs : s.Nonempty)
  [Nonempty ↑t] : s = t

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.eq_of_nonempty_of_subsingleton'.description: If a set is nonempty and its elements belong to a subsingleton set, then it is equal to any other nonempty set of the same type.

Set.disjoint_iff.code: Set.disjoint_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t ↔ s ∩ t ⊆ ∅
Set.disjoint_iff.description: Two sets are disjoint if and only if their intersection is a subset of the empty set.

Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.code: Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t ↔ s ∩ t = ∅
Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.description: Two sets are disjoint if and only if their intersection is empty.

Disjoint.inter_eq.code: Disjoint.inter_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t → s ∩ t = ∅
Disjoint.inter_eq.description: If two sets are disjoint, then their intersection is empty.

Set.disjoint_left.code: Set.disjoint_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t ↔ ∀ ⦃a : α⦄, a ∈ s → a ∉ t
Set.disjoint_left.description: Two sets are disjoint if and only if every element of the first set is not an element of the second set.

Set.disjoint_right.code: Set.disjoint_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t ↔ ∀ ⦃a : α⦄, a ∈ t → a ∉ s
Set.disjoint_right.description: Two sets are disjoint if and only if no element from one set is contained in the other set.

Set.not_disjoint_iff.code: Set.not_disjoint_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : ¬Disjoint s t ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, x ∈ t
Set.not_disjoint_iff.description: Two sets are not disjoint if and only if there exists at least one element that belongs to both sets.

Set.not_disjoint_iff_nonempty_inter.code: Set.not_disjoint_iff_nonempty_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : ¬Disjoint s t ↔ (s ∩ t).Nonempty
Set.not_disjoint_iff_nonempty_inter.description: Two sets are not disjoint if and only if their intersection is nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.not_disjoint.code: Set.Nonempty.not_disjoint.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∩ t).Nonempty → ¬Disjoint s t
Set.Nonempty.not_disjoint.description: If the intersection of two sets contains at least one element, then the two sets cannot be disjoint.

Set.disjoint_or_nonempty_inter.code: Set.disjoint_or_nonempty_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : Disjoint s t ∨ (s ∩ t).Nonempty
Set.disjoint_or_nonempty_inter.description: Either two sets are disjoint or their intersection contains at least one element.
