Set.disjoint_iff_forall_ne.code: Set.disjoint_iff_forall_ne.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t ↔ ∀ ⦃a : α⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b : α⦄, b ∈ t → a ≠ b
Set.disjoint_iff_forall_ne.description: Two sets are disjoint if and only if no element from one set is equal to any element from the other set.

Disjoint.ne_of_mem.code: Disjoint.ne_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t → ∀ ⦃a : α⦄, a ∈ s → ∀ ⦃b : α⦄, b ∈ t → a ≠ b
Disjoint.ne_of_mem.description: If two sets are disjoint, then any element from one set differs from any element in the other set.

Set.disjoint_of_subset_left.code: Set.disjoint_of_subset_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (h : s ⊆ u) (d : Disjoint u t) : Disjoint s t
Set.disjoint_of_subset_left.description: If one set is a subset of another set that is disjoint from a third set, then the first set is also disjoint from the third set.

Set.disjoint_of_subset_right.code: Set.disjoint_of_subset_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (h : t ⊆ u) (d : Disjoint s u) : Disjoint s t
Set.disjoint_of_subset_right.description: If one set is a subset of another and the first set is disjoint from a third set, then the first set is also disjoint from the second set.

Set.disjoint_of_subset.code:
Set.disjoint_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} (hs : s₁ ⊆ s₂) (ht : t₁ ⊆ t₂) (h : Disjoint s₂ t₂) :
  Disjoint s₁ t₁
Set.disjoint_of_subset.description: If one set is a subset of another and the latter is disjoint from a third set, then the first set is also disjoint from the corresponding subset of the third set.

Set.disjoint_union_left.code: Set.disjoint_union_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : Disjoint (s ∪ t) u ↔ Disjoint s u ∧ Disjoint t u
Set.disjoint_union_left.description: The union of two sets is disjoint from a third set if and only if each of the two sets is disjoint from the third set individually.

Set.disjoint_union_right.code: Set.disjoint_union_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : Disjoint s (t ∪ u) ↔ Disjoint s t ∧ Disjoint s u
Set.disjoint_union_right.description: A set is disjoint from the union of two other sets if and only if it is disjoint from each of those sets individually.

Set.disjoint_empty.code: Set.disjoint_empty.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : Disjoint s ∅
Set.disjoint_empty.description: Any set is disjoint from the empty set.

Set.empty_disjoint.code: Set.empty_disjoint.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : Disjoint ∅ s
Set.empty_disjoint.description: The empty set is disjoint from any set.

Set.univ_disjoint.code: Set.univ_disjoint.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : Disjoint univ s ↔ s = ∅
Set.univ_disjoint.description: A set is disjoint from the universal set if and only if it is empty.

Set.disjoint_univ.code: Set.disjoint_univ.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : Disjoint s univ ↔ s = ∅
Set.disjoint_univ.description: A set is disjoint from the universal set if and only if it is the empty set.

Set.disjoint_sdiff_left.code: Set.disjoint_sdiff_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint (t \ s) s
Set.disjoint_sdiff_left.description: The difference of a set and another disjoint set does not intersect with the first set.

Set.disjoint_sdiff_right.code: Set.disjoint_sdiff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s (t \ s)
Set.disjoint_sdiff_right.description: A set is disjoint from the difference of another set and itself.

Set.disjoint_sdiff_inter.code: Set.disjoint_sdiff_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint (s \ t) (s ∩ t)
Set.disjoint_sdiff_inter.description: The difference between two sets and their intersection are disjoint from each other.

Set.diff_union_diff_cancel.code: Set.diff_union_diff_cancel.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (hts : t ⊆ s) (hut : u ⊆ t) : s \ t ∪ t \ u = s \ u
Set.diff_union_diff_cancel.description: The union of the difference between two sets is equal to the difference of the first set and a third set when the second set is a subset of the first and the third set is a subset of the second.

Set.diff_diff_eq_sdiff_union.code: Set.diff_diff_eq_sdiff_union.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (h : u ⊆ s) : s \ (t \ u) = s \ t ∪ u
Set.diff_diff_eq_sdiff_union.description: The difference between a set and the difference of two other sets is equal to the difference of the first set and the second set combined with the elements of the third set if the third set is contained within the first set.

Set.disjoint_singleton_left.code: Set.disjoint_singleton_left.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : Disjoint {a} s ↔ a ∉ s
Set.disjoint_singleton_left.description: A singleton set is disjoint from another set if and only if the element of the singleton is not in the other set.

Set.disjoint_singleton_right.code: Set.disjoint_singleton_right.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : Disjoint s {a} ↔ a ∉ s
Set.disjoint_singleton_right.description: A set is disjoint from a singleton containing an element if and only if that element is not in the set.

Set.disjoint_singleton.code: Set.disjoint_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} : Disjoint {a} {b} ↔ a ≠ b
Set.disjoint_singleton.description: Two singleton sets are disjoint if and only if their contained elements are not equal.

Set.subset_diff.code: Set.subset_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s ⊆ t \ u ↔ s ⊆ t ∧ Disjoint s u
Set.subset_diff.description: A set is a subset of the difference between two other sets if and only if it is a subset of the first set and has no elements in common with the second set.

Set.inter_diff_distrib_left.code: Set.inter_diff_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∩ (t \ u) = (s ∩ t) \ (s ∩ u)
Set.inter_diff_distrib_left.description: The intersection of a set with the difference of two other sets is equal to the difference of the intersection of the first set with the second and the intersection of the first set with the third.

Set.inter_diff_distrib_right.code: Set.inter_diff_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s \ t ∩ u = (s ∩ u) \ (t ∩ u)
Set.inter_diff_distrib_right.description: The intersection of the difference of a set and another set with a third set is equal to the difference of the intersection of the first set with the third set and the intersection of the second set with the third set.

Set.compl_def.code: Set.compl_def.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : sᶜ = {x | x ∉ s}
Set.compl_def.description: The complement of a set consists of all elements that do not belong to that set.

Set.mem_compl.code: Set.mem_compl.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} (h : x ∉ s) : x ∈ sᶜ
Set.mem_compl.description: If an element is not a member of a set, then it belongs to the complement of that set.

Set.compl_setOf.code: Set.compl_setOf.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (p : α → Prop) : {a | p a}ᶜ = {a | ¬p a}
Set.compl_setOf.description: The complement of the set of elements satisfying a property is equal to the set of elements not satisfying that property.

Set.not_mem_of_mem_compl.code: Set.not_mem_of_mem_compl.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} (h : x ∈ sᶜ) : x ∉ s
Set.not_mem_of_mem_compl.description: If an element is in the complement of a set, then it is not in the original set.

Set.not_mem_compl_iff.code: Set.not_mem_compl_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} : x ∉ sᶜ ↔ x ∈ s
Set.not_mem_compl_iff.description: An element is not in the complement of a set if and only if it is in the set itself.

Set.inter_compl_self.code: Set.inter_compl_self.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : s ∩ sᶜ = ∅
Set.inter_compl_self.description: The intersection of any set and its complement is the empty set.

Set.compl_inter_self.code: Set.compl_inter_self.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : sᶜ ∩ s = ∅
Set.compl_inter_self.description: The intersection of a set and its complement is always empty.

Set.compl_empty.description: The complement of the empty set is the universal set.

Set.compl_union.code: Set.compl_union.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : (s ∪ t)ᶜ = sᶜ ∩ tᶜ
Set.compl_union.description: The complement of the union of two sets is equal to the intersection of their complements.

Set.compl_inter.code: Set.compl_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : (s ∩ t)ᶜ = sᶜ ∪ tᶜ
Set.compl_inter.description: The complement of the intersection of two sets is equal to the union of their complements.

Set.compl_univ.description: The complement of the universal set is the empty set.

Set.compl_empty_iff.code: Set.compl_empty_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : sᶜ = ∅ ↔ s = univ
Set.compl_empty_iff.description: A set is empty if and only if its complement is the universal set.

Set.compl_univ_iff.code: Set.compl_univ_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : sᶜ = univ ↔ s = ∅
Set.compl_univ_iff.description: The complement of a set equals the universal set if and only if the set is empty.

Set.compl_ne_univ.code: Set.compl_ne_univ.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : sᶜ ≠ univ ↔ s.Nonempty
Set.compl_ne_univ.description: The complement of a set is not equal to the universal set if and only if the original set is non-empty.

Set.nonempty_compl.code: Set.nonempty_compl.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : sᶜ.Nonempty ↔ s ≠ univ
Set.nonempty_compl.description: The complement of a set is nonempty if and only if the set is not equal to the universal set.

Set.mem_compl_singleton_iff.code: Set.mem_compl_singleton_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a x : α} : x ∈ {a}ᶜ ↔ x ≠ a
Set.mem_compl_singleton_iff.description: An element is in the complement of a singleton set if and only if it is not equal to the element contained in that singleton.

Set.compl_singleton_eq.code: Set.compl_singleton_eq.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) : {a}ᶜ = {x | x ≠ a}
Set.compl_singleton_eq.description: The complement of a singleton set is the set of all elements that are not equal to the element in the singleton.

Set.compl_ne_eq_singleton.code: Set.compl_ne_eq_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) : {x | x ≠ a}ᶜ = {a}
Set.compl_ne_eq_singleton.description: The complement of the set of all elements not equal to a given element is the singleton set containing that element.

Set.union_eq_compl_compl_inter_compl.code: Set.union_eq_compl_compl_inter_compl.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s ∪ t = (sᶜ ∩ tᶜ)ᶜ
Set.union_eq_compl_compl_inter_compl.description: The union of two sets is equal to the complement of the intersection of their complements.

Set.inter_eq_compl_compl_union_compl.code: Set.inter_eq_compl_compl_union_compl.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s ∩ t = (sᶜ ∪ tᶜ)ᶜ
Set.inter_eq_compl_compl_union_compl.description: The intersection of two sets is equal to the complement of the union of their complements.

Set.union_compl_self.code: Set.union_compl_self.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : s ∪ sᶜ = univ
Set.union_compl_self.description: The union of any set with its complement equals the universal set.

Set.compl_union_self.code: Set.compl_union_self.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : sᶜ ∪ s = univ
Set.compl_union_self.description: The union of a set and its complement equals the universal set.

Set.compl_subset_comm.code: Set.compl_subset_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : sᶜ ⊆ t ↔ tᶜ ⊆ s
Set.compl_subset_comm.description: The complement of one set being a subset of another is equivalent to the complement of the latter set being a subset of the former.

Set.subset_compl_comm.code: Set.subset_compl_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊆ tᶜ ↔ t ⊆ sᶜ
Set.subset_compl_comm.description: The subset relation of a set to the complement of another set is equivalent to the complement of the first set being a subset of the second set.

Set.compl_subset_compl.code: Set.compl_subset_compl.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : sᶜ ⊆ tᶜ ↔ t ⊆ s
Set.compl_subset_compl.description: The complement of one set is contained within the complement of another if and only if the second set is contained within the first set.

Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_left.code: Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊆ tᶜ ↔ Disjoint t s
Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_left.description: One set is a subset of the complement of another set if and only if the two sets are disjoint.

Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_right.code: Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊆ tᶜ ↔ Disjoint s t
Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_right.description: A set is a subset of the complement of another set if and only if the two sets are disjoint.

Set.disjoint_compl_left_iff_subset.code: Set.disjoint_compl_left_iff_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint sᶜ t ↔ t ⊆ s
Set.disjoint_compl_left_iff_subset.description: The disjointness of the complement of a set with another set is equivalent to the inclusion of the second set within the first set.

Set.disjoint_compl_right_iff_subset.code: Set.disjoint_compl_right_iff_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s tᶜ ↔ s ⊆ t
Set.disjoint_compl_right_iff_subset.description: Two sets are disjoint if and only if one set is a subset of the complement of the other set.

Disjoint.subset_compl_right.code: Disjoint.subset_compl_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint s t → s ⊆ tᶜ
Disjoint.subset_compl_right.description: If two sets are disjoint, then the first set is a subset of the complement of the second set.

Disjoint.subset_compl_left.code: Disjoint.subset_compl_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : Disjoint t s → s ⊆ tᶜ
Disjoint.subset_compl_left.description: If two sets are disjoint, then the first set is contained within the complement of the second set.

HasSubset.Subset.disjoint_compl_left.code: HasSubset.Subset.disjoint_compl_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : t ⊆ s → Disjoint sᶜ t
HasSubset.Subset.disjoint_compl_left.description: If one set is a subset of another, then the first set is disjoint from the complement of the second set.

HasSubset.Subset.disjoint_compl_right.code: HasSubset.Subset.disjoint_compl_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ⊆ t → Disjoint s tᶜ
HasSubset.Subset.disjoint_compl_right.description: If one set is a subset of another set, then it is disjoint from the complement of that second set.

Set.subset_union_compl_iff_inter_subset.code: Set.subset_union_compl_iff_inter_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s ⊆ t ∪ uᶜ ↔ s ∩ u ⊆ t
Set.subset_union_compl_iff_inter_subset.description: A set is a subset of the union of another set and the complement of a third set if and only if its intersection with the third set is a subset of the second set.

Set.compl_subset_iff_union.code: Set.compl_subset_iff_union.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : sᶜ ⊆ t ↔ s ∪ t = univ
Set.compl_subset_iff_union.description: A set is a subset of another set if and only if their union equals the universal set.

Set.subset_compl_singleton_iff.code: Set.subset_compl_singleton_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : s ⊆ {a}ᶜ ↔ a ∉ s
Set.subset_compl_singleton_iff.description: A set is a subset of the complement of a singleton containing a specific element if and only if that element is not a member of the set.

Set.inter_subset.code: Set.inter_subset.{u} {α : Type u} (a b c : Set α) : a ∩ b ⊆ c ↔ a ⊆ bᶜ ∪ c
Set.inter_subset.description: The intersection of two sets is a subset of a third set if and only if one of the sets is a subset of the union of the complement of the other set and the third set.

Set.inter_compl_nonempty_iff.code: Set.inter_compl_nonempty_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∩ tᶜ).Nonempty ↔ ¬s ⊆ t
Set.inter_compl_nonempty_iff.description: The intersection of a set with the complement of another set is nonempty if and only if the first set is not a subset of the second set.

Set.not_mem_diff_of_mem.code: Set.not_mem_diff_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {x : α} (hx : x ∈ t) : x ∉ s \ t
Set.not_mem_diff_of_mem.description: If an element is in one set, it cannot be an element of the set difference between another set and the first set.

Set.mem_of_mem_diff.code: Set.mem_of_mem_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {x : α} (h : x ∈ s \ t) : x ∈ s
Set.mem_of_mem_diff.description: If an element belongs to the difference between two sets, it must also belong to the first set.

Set.not_mem_of_mem_diff.code: Set.not_mem_of_mem_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {x : α} (h : x ∈ s \ t) : x ∉ t
Set.not_mem_of_mem_diff.description: If an element belongs to the difference of two sets, then it cannot belong to the second set.

Set.diff_eq_compl_inter.code: Set.diff_eq_compl_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s \ t = tᶜ ∩ s
Set.diff_eq_compl_inter.description: The difference between two sets is equal to the intersection of the complement of one set with the other set.

Set.nonempty_diff.code: Set.nonempty_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s \ t).Nonempty ↔ ¬s ⊆ t
Set.nonempty_diff.description: The difference between two sets is nonempty if and only if the first set is not a subset of the second set.

Set.diff_subset.code: Set.diff_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s \ t ⊆ s
Set.diff_subset.description: The difference of two sets is a subset of the original set.

Set.union_diff_cancel'.code: Set.union_diff_cancel'.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (h₁ : s ⊆ t) (h₂ : t ⊆ u) : t ∪ u \ s = u
Set.union_diff_cancel'.description: The union of a set and another set minus a third set, under certain subset conditions, equals the larger set.

Set.union_diff_cancel.code: Set.union_diff_cancel.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : s ∪ t \ s = t
Set.union_diff_cancel.description: The union of a set with the difference of two sets is equal to the second set if the first set is a subset of the second.

Set.union_diff_cancel_left.code: Set.union_diff_cancel_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ∩ t ⊆ ∅) : (s ∪ t) \ s = t
Set.union_diff_cancel_left.description: If a set is disjoint from another set, the union of the two sets minus the first set equals the second set.

Set.union_diff_cancel_right.code: Set.union_diff_cancel_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ∩ t ⊆ ∅) : (s ∪ t) \ t = s
Set.union_diff_cancel_right.description: If the intersection of two sets is empty, then the union of the first set with the second set minus the second set is equal to the first set.

Set.union_diff_left.code: Set.union_diff_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∪ t) \ s = t \ s
Set.union_diff_left.description: The difference between the union of two sets and one of those sets is equal to the difference between the second set and the first set.

Set.union_diff_right.code: Set.union_diff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∪ t) \ t = s \ t
Set.union_diff_right.description: The difference between the union of two sets and one of those sets is equal to the difference between the first set and the second set.

Set.union_diff_distrib.code: Set.union_diff_distrib.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : (s ∪ t) \ u = s \ u ∪ t \ u
Set.union_diff_distrib.description: The difference of the union of two sets and a third set is equal to the union of the differences of each of the two sets with the third set.

Set.inter_diff_assoc.code: Set.inter_diff_assoc.{u} {α : Type u} (a b c : Set α) : (a ∩ b) \ c = a ∩ (b \ c)
Set.inter_diff_assoc.description: The difference between the intersection of two sets and a third set is equal to the intersection of the first set with the difference of the second set and the third set.

Set.inter_diff_self.code: Set.inter_diff_self.{u} {α : Type u} (a b : Set α) : a ∩ (b \ a) = ∅
Set.inter_diff_self.description: The intersection of a set with the difference of another set and itself is empty.

Set.inter_union_diff.code: Set.inter_union_diff.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s ∩ t ∪ s \ t = s
Set.inter_union_diff.description: The intersection of two sets combined with the difference of one set from the other equals the first set.

Set.diff_union_inter.code: Set.diff_union_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s \ t ∪ s ∩ t = s
Set.diff_union_inter.description: The union of the difference of one set from another and the intersection of the two sets equals the original set.

Set.inter_union_compl.code: Set.inter_union_compl.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s ∩ t ∪ s ∩ tᶜ = s
Set.inter_union_compl.description: The union of the intersection of a set with another set and the intersection of that set with the complement of the other set equals the original set.

Set.diff_subset_diff.code: Set.diff_subset_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ s₂ → t₂ ⊆ t₁ → s₁ \ t₁ ⊆ s₂ \ t₂
Set.diff_subset_diff.description: The difference of two sets is a subset of the difference of another two sets if the first set is contained in the second set and the second difference is contained in the first difference.

Set.diff_subset_diff_left.code: Set.diff_subset_diff_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) : s₁ \ t ⊆ s₂ \ t
Set.diff_subset_diff_left.description: The difference of a subset and a set is itself a subset of the difference of the original set and that set.

Set.diff_subset_diff_right.code: Set.diff_subset_diff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (h : t ⊆ u) : s \ u ⊆ s \ t
Set.diff_subset_diff_right.description: If one set is a subset of another, then the difference between a third set and the second set is also a subset of the difference between the third set and the first set.

Set.compl_eq_univ_diff.code: Set.compl_eq_univ_diff.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : sᶜ = univ \ s
Set.compl_eq_univ_diff.description: The complement of a set is equal to the universal set minus that set.

Set.empty_diff.code: Set.empty_diff.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : ∅ \ s = ∅
Set.empty_diff.description: The difference between the empty set and any set is still the empty set.

Set.diff_eq_empty.code: Set.diff_eq_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s \ t = ∅ ↔ s ⊆ t
Set.diff_eq_empty.description: A set minus another set is empty if and only if the first set is a subset of the second set.

Set.diff_empty.code: Set.diff_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s \ ∅ = s
Set.diff_empty.description: The difference between any set and the empty set is equal to the original set.

Set.diff_univ.code: Set.diff_univ.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : s \ univ = ∅
Set.diff_univ.description: The difference between any set and the universal set is always empty.

Set.diff_diff.code: Set.diff_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : (s \ t) \ u = s \ (t ∪ u)
Set.diff_diff.description: The difference between one set and a second set followed by a third set is equal to the difference between the first set and the union of the second and third sets.

Set.diff_diff_comm.code: Set.diff_diff_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : (s \ t) \ u = (s \ u) \ t
Set.diff_diff_comm.description: The difference between two sets is commutative with respect to the subtraction of a third set.

Set.diff_subset_iff.code: Set.diff_subset_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s \ t ⊆ u ↔ s ⊆ t ∪ u
Set.diff_subset_iff.description: The difference of two sets being a subset of a third set is equivalent to the original set being a subset of the union of the second set and the third set.

Set.subset_diff_union.code: Set.subset_diff_union.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s ⊆ s \ t ∪ t
Set.subset_diff_union.description: A set is a subset of the union of its difference with another set and that other set itself.

Set.diff_union_of_subset.code: Set.diff_union_of_subset.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : t ⊆ s) : s \ t ∪ t = s
Set.diff_union_of_subset.description: The union of the difference of two sets and the subset results in the original set.

Set.diff_singleton_subset_iff.code: Set.diff_singleton_subset_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {s t : Set α} : s \ {x} ⊆ t ↔ s ⊆ insert x t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.diff_singleton_subset_iff.description: The difference between a set and a singleton is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the set obtained by inserting the element of the singleton into the other set.

Set.subset_diff_singleton.code: Set.subset_diff_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {x : α} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) (hx : x ∉ s) : s ⊆ t \ {x}
Set.subset_diff_singleton.description: If one set is a subset of another set and does not contain a specific element, then it is also a subset of the second set with that element removed.

Set.subset_insert_diff_singleton.code: Set.subset_insert_diff_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} (x : α) (s : Set α) : s ⊆ insert x (s \ {x})

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.subset_insert_diff_singleton.description: Any set is a subset of the set formed by inserting an element into the difference between that set and a singleton containing that same element.

Set.diff_subset_comm.code: Set.diff_subset_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s \ t ⊆ u ↔ s \ u ⊆ t
Set.diff_subset_comm.description: The difference between two sets is a subset of a third set if and only if the difference between the first set and the third set is a subset of the second set.

Set.diff_inter.code: Set.diff_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s \ (t ∩ u) = s \ t ∪ s \ u
Set.diff_inter.description: The difference between a set and the intersection of two other sets is equal to the union of the differences of the first set with each of the other two sets.

Set.diff_inter_diff.code: Set.diff_inter_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s \ t ∩ (s \ u) = s \ (t ∪ u)
Set.diff_inter_diff.description: The intersection of the difference between one set and another set with the difference between that set and a third set is equivalent to the difference between the first set and the union of the second and third sets.

Set.diff_compl.code: Set.diff_compl.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s \ tᶜ = s ∩ t
Set.diff_compl.description: The difference between a set and the complement of another set is equal to the intersection of the first set with the second set.

Set.diff_diff_right.code: Set.diff_diff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} : s \ (t \ u) = s \ t ∪ s ∩ u
Set.diff_diff_right.description: The difference between a set and the difference of two other sets is equal to the difference of the first set and the second set, combined with the intersection of the first set and the third set.

Set.insert_diff_of_mem.code: Set.insert_diff_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {t : Set α} (s : Set α) (h : a ∈ t) : insert a s \ t = s \ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_diff_of_mem.description: Inserting an element into a set while removing a different set from it yields the same result as removing that other set without the inserted element, provided the inserted element belongs to the other set.

Set.insert_diff_of_not_mem.code:
Set.insert_diff_of_not_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {t : Set α} (s : Set α) (h : a ∉ t) :
  insert a s \ t = insert a (s \ t)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_diff_of_not_mem.description: Inserting an element into a set and then taking the difference with another set is equivalent to taking the difference first and then inserting the element if the element is not in the second set.

Set.insert_diff_self_of_not_mem.code: Set.insert_diff_self_of_not_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} (h : a ∉ s) : insert a s \ {a} = s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_diff_self_of_not_mem.description: Inserting an element into a set and then removing that same element results in the original set if the element was not initially a member of the set.

Set.insert_diff_eq_singleton.code: Set.insert_diff_eq_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} (h : a ∉ s) : insert a s \ s = {a}

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_diff_eq_singleton.description: The difference between the union of a set with a single element and that set itself is equal to the singleton set containing that element, provided the element is not already in the set.

Set.inter_insert_of_mem.code: Set.inter_insert_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (h : a ∈ s) : s ∩ insert a t = insert a (s ∩ t)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.inter_insert_of_mem.description: The intersection of a set with the insertion of an element into another set is equal to the insertion of that element into the intersection of the first set and the second set, provided the element is a member of the first set.

Set.insert_inter_of_mem.code: Set.insert_inter_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (h : a ∈ t) : insert a s ∩ t = insert a (s ∩ t)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_inter_of_mem.description: Inserting an element into a set and then intersecting with another set yields the same result as intersecting the first set with the second set and then inserting the element into that intersection.

Set.inter_insert_of_not_mem.code: Set.inter_insert_of_not_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (h : a ∉ s) : s ∩ insert a t = s ∩ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.inter_insert_of_not_mem.description: The intersection of a set with the result of inserting an element into another set equals the intersection of the first set with the second set if the element is not a member of the first set.

Set.insert_inter_of_not_mem.code: Set.insert_inter_of_not_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} (h : a ∉ t) : insert a s ∩ t = s ∩ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_inter_of_not_mem.description: The intersection of a set with another set remains unchanged if an element from the first set is not a member of the second set being intersected.

Set.union_diff_self.code: Set.union_diff_self.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ∪ t \ s = s ∪ t
Set.union_diff_self.description: The union of a set with the difference of another set from it is equal to the union of the two sets.

Set.diff_union_self.code: Set.diff_union_self.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s \ t ∪ t = s ∪ t
Set.diff_union_self.description: The union of the difference of one set from another with the second set is equal to the union of both sets.

Set.diff_inter_self.code: Set.diff_inter_self.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : Set α} : b \ a ∩ a = ∅
Set.diff_inter_self.description: The intersection of the difference of one set from another and the first set itself is empty.

Set.diff_inter_self_eq_diff.code: Set.diff_inter_self_eq_diff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s \ (t ∩ s) = s \ t
Set.diff_inter_self_eq_diff.description: The difference between a set and the intersection of that set with another set is equal to the difference between the original set and the second set.

Set.diff_self_inter.code: Set.diff_self_inter.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s \ (s ∩ t) = s \ t
Set.diff_self_inter.description: The difference of a set and the intersection of that set with another set is equal to the difference of the original set and the second set.

Set.diff_singleton_eq_self.code: Set.diff_singleton_eq_self.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} (h : a ∉ s) : s \ {a} = s
Set.diff_singleton_eq_self.description: Removing a single element from a set that does not contain that element results in the original set remaining unchanged.

Set.diff_singleton_sSubset.code: Set.diff_singleton_sSubset.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {a : α} : s \ {a} ⊂ s ↔ a ∈ s
Set.diff_singleton_sSubset.description: Removing a single element from a set creates a subset of the original set if and only if that element was part of the original set.

Set.insert_diff_singleton.code: Set.insert_diff_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} : insert a (s \ {a}) = insert a s

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_diff_singleton.description: Inserting an element into the difference of a set and a singleton containing that element is equivalent to simply inserting the element into the original set.

Set.insert_diff_singleton_comm.code:
Set.insert_diff_singleton_comm.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) (s : Set α) :
  insert a (s \ {b}) = insert a s \ {b}

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.insert_diff_singleton_comm.description: Inserting an element into a set after removing a singleton of a different element is equivalent to inserting the element into the original set and then removing the singleton.

Set.diff_self.code: Set.diff_self.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s \ s = ∅
Set.diff_self.description: The difference between a set and itself is empty.

Set.diff_diff_right_self.code: Set.diff_diff_right_self.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s \ (s \ t) = s ∩ t
Set.diff_diff_right_self.description: The difference of a set and the difference of that set with another results in the intersection of the original set with the second set.

Set.diff_diff_cancel_left.code: Set.diff_diff_cancel_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : t \ (t \ s) = s
Set.diff_diff_cancel_left.description: The difference between a set and the difference of that set from another set is equal to the original set if the original set is a subset of the second set.

Set.mem_diff_singleton.code: Set.mem_diff_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {x y : α} {s : Set α} : x ∈ s \ {y} ↔ x ∈ s ∧ x ≠ y
Set.mem_diff_singleton.description: An element is in the difference between a set and a singleton set if and only if it is in the original set and is not equal to the element in the singleton.

Set.mem_diff_singleton_empty.code: Set.mem_diff_singleton_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {t : Set (Set α)} : s ∈ t \ {∅} ↔ s ∈ t ∧ s.Nonempty
Set.mem_diff_singleton_empty.description: An element is in the difference of a set and the empty set if and only if it is in the set and is non-empty.

Set.union_eq_diff_union_diff_union_inter.code: Set.union_eq_diff_union_diff_union_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s ∪ t = s \ t ∪ t \ s ∪ s ∩ t
Set.union_eq_diff_union_diff_union_inter.description: The union of two sets can be expressed as the union of their symmetric difference and their intersection.

Set.pair_eq_singleton.description: A set containing two identical elements is equal to the singleton set containing just that element.

Set.pair_comm.code: Set.pair_comm.{u} {α : Type u} (a b : α) : {a, b} = {b, a}
Set.pair_comm.description: The pair of elements in a set is equal regardless of their order.

Set.pair_eq_pair_iff.code: Set.pair_eq_pair_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {x y z w : α} : {x, y} = {z, w} ↔ x = z ∧ y = w ∨ x = w ∧ y = z
Set.pair_eq_pair_iff.description: Two sets containing exactly two elements are equal if and only if their elements can be paired in such a way that each element from one set matches an element from the other.

Set.pair_diff_left.code: Set.pair_diff_left.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} (hne : a ≠ b) : {a, b} \ {a} = {b}
Set.pair_diff_left.description: Removing one element from a pair of distinct elements results in the set containing only the other element.

Set.pair_subset_iff.code: Set.pair_subset_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {a b : α} {s : Set α} : {a, b} ⊆ s ↔ a ∈ s ∧ b ∈ s
Set.pair_subset_iff.description: A set containing two elements is a subset of another set if and only if both of those elements are contained in the second set.

Set.subset_insert_iff.code: Set.subset_insert_iff.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} {x : α} : s ⊆ insert x t ↔ s ⊆ t ∨ x ∈ s ∧ s \ {x} ⊆ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.subset_insert_iff.description: A set is a subset of the union of a singleton and another set if and only if it is either a subset of the other set or includes an element from the singleton while excluding that element is still a subset of the other set.

Set.subset_pair_iff_eq.code: Set.subset_pair_iff_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x y : α} : s ⊆ {x, y} ↔ s = ∅ ∨ s = {x} ∨ s = {y} ∨ s = {x, y}
Set.subset_pair_iff_eq.description: A set is a subset of a pair of elements if and only if it is empty or consists of one or both of those elements.

Set.mem_symmDiff.code: Set.mem_symmDiff.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s t : Set α} : a ∈ s ∆ t ↔ a ∈ s ∧ a ∉ t ∨ a ∈ t ∧ a ∉ s
Set.mem_symmDiff.description: An element belongs to the symmetric difference of two sets if and only if it is in one of the sets but not the other.

Set.symmDiff_def.code: Set.symmDiff_def.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s ∆ t = s \ t ∪ t \ s
Set.symmDiff_def.description: The symmetric difference of two sets is defined as the union of their differences.

Set.symmDiff_subset_union.code: Set.symmDiff_subset_union.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ∆ t ⊆ s ∪ t
Set.symmDiff_subset_union.description: The symmetric difference of two sets is a subset of their union.

Set.symmDiff_eq_empty.code: Set.symmDiff_eq_empty.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : s ∆ t = ∅ ↔ s = t
Set.symmDiff_eq_empty.description: The symmetric difference of two sets is empty if and only if the two sets are equal.

Set.symmDiff_nonempty.code: Set.symmDiff_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : (s ∆ t).Nonempty ↔ s ≠ t
Set.symmDiff_nonempty.description: The symmetric difference of two sets is non-empty if and only if the two sets are not equal.

Set.inter_symmDiff_distrib_left.code: Set.inter_symmDiff_distrib_left.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∩ t ∆ u = (s ∩ t) ∆ (s ∩ u)
Set.inter_symmDiff_distrib_left.description: The intersection of the symmetric difference of two sets with a third set is equal to the symmetric difference of the intersection of the first two sets with the intersection of the first and third sets.

Set.inter_symmDiff_distrib_right.code: Set.inter_symmDiff_distrib_right.{u} {α : Type u} (s t u : Set α) : s ∆ t ∩ u = (s ∩ u) ∆ (t ∩ u)
Set.inter_symmDiff_distrib_right.description: The intersection of a symmetric difference of two sets and a third set is equal to the symmetric difference of the intersections of each of the first two sets with the third set.

Set.subset_symmDiff_union_symmDiff_left.code: Set.subset_symmDiff_union_symmDiff_left.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (h : Disjoint s t) : u ⊆ s ∆ u ∪ t ∆ u
Set.subset_symmDiff_union_symmDiff_left.description: A set is contained within the union of its symmetric differences with two other disjoint sets.

Set.subset_symmDiff_union_symmDiff_right.code: Set.subset_symmDiff_union_symmDiff_right.{u} {α : Type u} {s t u : Set α} (h : Disjoint t u) : s ⊆ s ∆ t ∪ s ∆ u
Set.subset_symmDiff_union_symmDiff_right.description: The inclusion of a set in the symmetric difference of two disjoint sets is guaranteed by the union of the symmetric differences formed with a third set.

Set.mem_powerset.code: Set.mem_powerset.{u} {α : Type u} {x s : Set α} (h : x ⊆ s) : x ∈ 𝒫 s
Set.mem_powerset.description: If one set is a subset of another set, then it belongs to the powerset of the larger set.

Set.subset_of_mem_powerset.code: Set.subset_of_mem_powerset.{u} {α : Type u} {x s : Set α} (h : x ∈ 𝒫 s) : x ⊆ s
Set.subset_of_mem_powerset.description: If a set is a member of the powerset of another set, then it is a subset of that set.

Set.mem_powerset_iff.code: Set.mem_powerset_iff.{u} {α : Type u} (x s : Set α) : x ∈ 𝒫 s ↔ x ⊆ s
Set.mem_powerset_iff.description: An element belongs to the power set of a set if and only if it is a subset of that set.

Set.powerset_inter.code: Set.powerset_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : 𝒫(s ∩ t) = 𝒫 s ∩ 𝒫 t
Set.powerset_inter.description: The power set of the intersection of two sets is equal to the intersection of their respective power sets.

Set.powerset_mono.code: Set.powerset_mono.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} : 𝒫 s ⊆ 𝒫 t ↔ s ⊆ t
Set.powerset_mono.description: The collection of all subsets of one set is a subset of the collection of all subsets of another set if and only if the first set is a subset of the second set.

Set.monotone_powerset.description: The powerset operation is monotonic, meaning that if one set is a subset of another, the corresponding powersets maintain this ordering.

Set.powerset_nonempty.code: Set.powerset_nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : (𝒫 s).Nonempty
Set.powerset_nonempty.description: The powerset of any set is always non-empty.

Set.powerset_empty.description: The powerset of the empty set consists solely of the empty set itself.

Set.powerset_univ.code: Set.powerset_univ.{u} {α : Type u} : 𝒫 univ = univ
Set.powerset_univ.description: The powerset of the universal set is equal to the universal set itself.

Set.powerset_singleton.comment: The powerset of a singleton contains only `∅` and the singleton itself.
Set.powerset_singleton.description: The powerset of a singleton set consists of only the empty set and the set containing the single element.

Set.mem_dite_univ_right.code:
Set.mem_dite_univ_right.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : p → Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if h : p then t h else univ) ↔ ∀ (h : p), x ∈ t h
Set.mem_dite_univ_right.description: An element belongs to a set defined by a proposition if and only if it belongs to that set for every case where the proposition holds.

Set.mem_ite_univ_right.code:
Set.mem_ite_univ_right.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if p then t else univ) ↔ p → x ∈ t
Set.mem_ite_univ_right.description: For an element to belong to a set defined by an if-else expression involving a property, it is equivalent to the condition that the property holds leading to membership in that specific set.

Set.mem_dite_univ_left.code:
Set.mem_dite_univ_left.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : ¬p → Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if h : p then univ else t h) ↔ ∀ (h : ¬p), x ∈ t h
Set.mem_dite_univ_left.description: An element belongs to a set defined by a conditional expression if and only if it belongs to the set specified in the alternative case whenever the condition is false.

Set.mem_ite_univ_left.code:
Set.mem_ite_univ_left.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if p then univ else t) ↔ ¬p → x ∈ t
Set.mem_ite_univ_left.description: An element belongs to either the universal set or a specified set based on the truth value of a proposition, and if the proposition is false, it is equivalent to the element being in the specified set.

Set.mem_dite.code:
Set.mem_dite.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (s : p → Set α) (t : ¬p → Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if h : p then s h else t h) ↔ (∀ (h : p), x ∈ s h) ∧ ∀ (h : ¬p), x ∈ t h
Set.mem_dite.description: An element belongs to a set defined by a conditional expression if and only if it belongs to both sets associated with the true and false cases of the condition.

Set.mem_dite_empty_right.code:
Set.mem_dite_empty_right.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : p → Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if h : p then t h else ∅) ↔ ∃ (h : p), x ∈ t h
Set.mem_dite_empty_right.description: An element belongs to the result of a conditional set based on a proposition if and only if it can be found in the corresponding set defined by that proposition.

Set.mem_ite_empty_right.code:
Set.mem_ite_empty_right.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if p then t else ∅) ↔ p ∧ x ∈ t
Set.mem_ite_empty_right.description: An element belongs to a set defined by a conditional statement if and only if the condition holds and the element is in the specified set.

Set.mem_dite_empty_left.code:
Set.mem_dite_empty_left.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : ¬p → Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if h : p then ∅ else t h) ↔ ∃ (h : ¬p), x ∈ t h
Set.mem_dite_empty_left.description: An element belongs to a set defined by a conditional on a proposition if and only if there exists a proof of the negation of that proposition such that the element is in the alternative set.

Set.mem_ite_empty_left.code:
Set.mem_ite_empty_left.{u} {α : Type u} (p : Prop) [Decidable p] (t : Set α) (x : α) :
  (x ∈ if p then ∅ else t) ↔ ¬p ∧ x ∈ t
Set.mem_ite_empty_left.description: An element belongs to a set that is either empty or another set based on a condition if and only if the condition is false and the element is in the other set.

Set.ite.code: Set.ite.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : Set α
Set.ite.comment:
`ite` for sets: `Set.ite t s s' ∩ t = s ∩ t`, `Set.ite t s s' ∩ tᶜ = s' ∩ tᶜ`.
Defined as `s ∩ t ∪ s' \ t`.
Set.ite.fullDefinition: protected def ite (t s s' : Set α) : Set α :=   s ∩ t ∪ s' \ t
Set.ite.description: The definition describes a construction that produces a set based on a condition, resulting in elements from one set if the condition is true and from another set otherwise, while ensuring specified relationships with the intersection and complement of those sets.

Set.ite.eq_1.code: Set.ite.eq_1.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : t.ite s s' = s ∩ t ∪ s' \ t
Set.ite.eq_1.description: The result of a ternary operation on a set equals the union of the intersection of the set with one outcome and the difference between the other outcome and the set.

Set.ite_inter_self.code: Set.ite_inter_self.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : t.ite s s' ∩ t = s ∩ t
Set.ite_inter_self.description: The intersection of a set with the result of a conditional expression based on that set equals the intersection of the set itself with the original set used in the conditional expression.

Set.ite_compl.code: Set.ite_compl.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : tᶜ.ite s s' = t.ite s' s
Set.ite_compl.description: The complement of a set combined with a conditional selection of two sets is equivalent to the conditional selection of the other two sets with respect to the original set.

Set.ite_inter_compl_self.code: Set.ite_inter_compl_self.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : t.ite s s' ∩ tᶜ = s' ∩ tᶜ
Set.ite_inter_compl_self.description: The intersection of a set chosen based on a condition with the complement of that set equals the intersection of an alternative set with the complement of the same set.

Set.ite_diff_self.code: Set.ite_diff_self.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : t.ite s s' \ t = s' \ t
Set.ite_diff_self.description: The difference between a set defined by an if-then-else condition and another set is equal to the latter set when the first set is excluded from the former.

Set.ite_same.code: Set.ite_same.{u} {α : Type u} (t s : Set α) : t.ite s s = s
Set.ite_same.description: The result of applying an indexed ternary operation to two identical sets produces the same set as the output.

Set.ite_left.code: Set.ite_left.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s.ite s t = s ∪ t
Set.ite_left.description: The result of applying a certain operation on a set and itself along with another set is equal to the union of those two sets.

Set.ite_right.code: Set.ite_right.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) : s.ite t s = t ∩ s
Set.ite_right.description: The selection of elements from a set based on a condition equals the intersection of that set with another set.

Set.ite_empty.code: Set.ite_empty.{u} {α : Type u} (s s' : Set α) : ∅.ite s s' = s'
Set.ite_empty.description: If the empty set is used as the condition in a conditional statement on sets, the result is equal to the second set used in the statement.

Set.ite_univ.code: Set.ite_univ.{u} {α : Type u} (s s' : Set α) : univ.ite s s' = s
Set.ite_univ.description: For any two sets, applying a conditional operation on the universe with respect to those sets results in the first set.

Set.ite_empty_left.code: Set.ite_empty_left.{u} {α : Type u} (t s : Set α) : t.ite ∅ s = s \ t
Set.ite_empty_left.description: The conditional set intersection with an empty set on the left side results in the difference of the second set and the first set.

Set.ite_empty_right.code: Set.ite_empty_right.{u} {α : Type u} (t s : Set α) : t.ite s ∅ = s ∩ t
Set.ite_empty_right.description: The intersection of a set with the empty set, when conditioned by the inclusion of another set, is equal to that other set under specific conditions.

Set.ite_mono.code:
Set.ite_mono.{u} {α : Type u} (t : Set α) {s₁ s₁' s₂ s₂' : Set α} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) (h' : s₁' ⊆ s₂') :
  t.ite s₁ s₁' ⊆ t.ite s₂ s₂'
Set.ite_mono.description: If one set is a subset of another and a second pair of sets is similarly related, then an indexed choice from the first set will also be a subset of the corresponding choice from the second set.

Set.ite_subset_union.code: Set.ite_subset_union.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : t.ite s s' ⊆ s ∪ s'
Set.ite_subset_union.description: The set obtained by applying an indexed selection to two sets is a subset of their union.

Set.inter_subset_ite.code: Set.inter_subset_ite.{u} {α : Type u} (t s s' : Set α) : s ∩ s' ⊆ t.ite s s'

explanatories.Set.ite: The definition describes a construction that produces a set based on a condition, resulting in elements from one set if the condition is true and from another set otherwise, while ensuring specified relationships with the intersection and complement of those sets.

Set.inter_subset_ite.description: The intersection of two sets is contained within a conditional set that selects one of the two sets based on a specified condition.

Set.ite_inter_inter.code:
Set.ite_inter_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (t s₁ s₂ s₁' s₂' : Set α) :
  t.ite (s₁ ∩ s₂) (s₁' ∩ s₂') = t.ite s₁ s₁' ∩ t.ite s₂ s₂'
Set.ite_inter_inter.description: The intersection of two sets, determined conditionally by a third set, is equal to the intersection of their individual conditional results.

Set.ite_inter.code: Set.ite_inter.{u} {α : Type u} (t s₁ s₂ s : Set α) : t.ite (s₁ ∩ s) (s₂ ∩ s) = t.ite s₁ s₂ ∩ s
Set.ite_inter.description: The intersection of a set with the result of a conditional selection is equal to the intersection of that set with each of the options in the selection.

Set.ite_inter_of_inter_eq.code:
Set.ite_inter_of_inter_eq.{u} {α : Type u} (t : Set α) {s₁ s₂ s : Set α} (h : s₁ ∩ s = s₂ ∩ s) :
  t.ite s₁ s₂ ∩ s = s₁ ∩ s
Set.ite_inter_of_inter_eq.description: The intersection of a set with a choice between two sets is equal to the choice itself when the intersections of those sets with another set are equal.

Set.subset_ite.code: Set.subset_ite.{u} {α : Type u} {t s s' u : Set α} : u ⊆ t.ite s s' ↔ u ∩ t ⊆ s ∧ u \ t ⊆ s'

explanatories.Set.ite: The definition describes a construction that produces a set based on a condition, resulting in elements from one set if the condition is true and from another set otherwise, while ensuring specified relationships with the intersection and complement of those sets.

Set.subset_ite.description: A set is a subset of a conditionally defined set if and only if the intersection of the set with the first condition is contained in the first alternative and the difference of the set and the first condition is contained in the second alternative.

Set.monotoneOn_iff_monotone.code:
Set.monotoneOn_iff_monotone.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} :
  MonotoneOn f s ↔ Monotone fun a => f ↑a
Set.monotoneOn_iff_monotone.description: A function defined on a set is monotonically increasing if and only if its restriction to that set maintains the same property when considering the function's outputs in the codomain's order.

Set.antitoneOn_iff_antitone.code:
Set.antitoneOn_iff_antitone.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} :
  AntitoneOn f s ↔ Antitone fun a => f ↑a
Set.antitoneOn_iff_antitone.description: A function restricted to a set is antitone if and only if the corresponding function on the entire preorder is antitone.

Set.strictMonoOn_iff_strictMono.code:
Set.strictMonoOn_iff_strictMono.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} :
  StrictMonoOn f s ↔ StrictMono fun a => f ↑a
Set.strictMonoOn_iff_strictMono.description: A function is strictly monotone on a set if and only if it remains strictly monotone when restricted to the images of that set.

Set.strictAntiOn_iff_strictAnti.code:
Set.strictAntiOn_iff_strictAnti.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} [Preorder α] [Preorder β] {f : α → β} :
  StrictAntiOn f s ↔ StrictAnti fun a => f ↑a
Set.strictAntiOn_iff_strictAnti.description: A function is strictly order-preserving on a subset if and only if it preserves strict order when applied to elements of that subset.

Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_ex.code:
Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_exists_le_le.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} [LinearOrder α]
  [LinearOrder β] {f : α → β} :
  ¬MonotoneOn f s ∧ ¬AntitoneOn f s ↔
    ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ s, ∃ c ∈ s, a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c ∧ (f a < f b ∧ f c < f b ∨ f b < f a ∧ f b < f c)
Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_ex.comment:
A function between linear orders which is neither monotone nor antitone makes a dent upright or
downright.
Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_ex.description: A function defined on a set is neither monotone nor antitone if and only if there exist three elements in the set such that the function's values create a specific "dent" pattern relative to those elements.

Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_ex.code:
Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_exists_lt_lt.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {s : Set α} [LinearOrder α]
  [LinearOrder β] {f : α → β} :
  ¬MonotoneOn f s ∧ ¬AntitoneOn f s ↔
    ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ s, ∃ c ∈ s, a < b ∧ b < c ∧ (f a < f b ∧ f c < f b ∨ f b < f a ∧ f b < f c)
Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_ex.comment:
A function between linear orders which is neither monotone nor antitone makes a dent upright or
downright.
Set.not_monotoneOn_not_antitoneOn_iff_ex.description: A function defined on a set that is neither monotone nor antitone must demonstrate a specific pattern of increasing or decreasing values between three elements of the set.

Function.Injective.nonempty_apply_iff.code:
Function.Injective.nonempty_apply_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {f : Set α → Set β} (hf : Injective f)
  (h2 : f ∅ = ∅) {s : Set α} : (f s).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty
Function.Injective.nonempty_apply_iff.description: A function that is injective maps a non-empty set to a non-empty set if and only if the original set is non-empty.

Set.inclusion.code: Set.inclusion.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : ↑s → ↑t
Set.inclusion.comment: `inclusion` is the "identity" function between two subsets `s` and `t`, where `s ⊆ t`
Set.inclusion.fullDefinition: def inclusion (h : s ⊆ t) : s → t := fun x : s => (⟨x, h x.2⟩ : t)
Set.inclusion.description: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.

Set.inclusion_self.code: Set.inclusion_self.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} (x : ↑s) : inclusion ⋯ x = x
Set.inclusion_self.description: The inclusion of an element from a set back into that set is equal to the original element itself.

Set.inclusion_eq_id.code: Set.inclusion_eq_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} (h : s ⊆ s) : inclusion h = id
Set.inclusion_eq_id.description: The inclusion map of a set to itself is equal to the identity map when the set is a subset of itself.

Set.inclusion_mk.code: Set.inclusion_mk.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} {h : s ⊆ t} (a : α) (ha : a ∈ s) : inclusion h ⟨a, ha⟩ = ⟨a, ⋯⟩
Set.inclusion_mk.description: The inclusion of an element into a subset is equal to the element being included with respect to the defining property of the subset.

Set.inclusion_right.code: Set.inclusion_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) (x : ↑t) (m : ↑x ∈ s) : inclusion h ⟨↑x, m⟩ = x
Set.inclusion_right.description: If a subset is included in another set, then the inclusion of an element from the larger set into the subset corresponds to that element itself.

Set.inclusion_inclusion.code:
Set.inclusion_inclusion.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t u : Set α} (hst : s ⊆ t) (htu : t ⊆ u) (x : ↑s) :
  inclusion htu (inclusion hst x) = inclusion ⋯ x
Set.inclusion_inclusion.description: If one set is included in a second set and the second in a third, then the inclusion of an element from the first set into the second set is equivalent to the inclusion of that element directly into the third set.

Set.inclusion_comp_inclusion.code:
Set.inclusion_comp_inclusion.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} {s t u : Set α} (hst : s ⊆ t) (htu : t ⊆ u) :
  inclusion htu ∘ inclusion hst = inclusion ⋯
Set.inclusion_comp_inclusion.description: The composition of inclusion functions preserves the subset relationships among three sets.

Set.coe_inclusion.code: Set.coe_inclusion.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) (x : ↑s) : ↑(inclusion h x) = ↑x

explanatories.Set.inclusion: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.

Set.coe_inclusion.description: If an element is included in a set through a specific subset inclusion, then its representation in both the original and the included set remains the same.

Set.inclusion_injective.code: Set.inclusion_injective.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : Injective (inclusion h)
Set.inclusion_injective.description: The inclusion function from one set to another is injective if the first set is a subset of the second set.

Set.eq_of_inclusion_surjective.code:
Set.eq_of_inclusion_surjective.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} {h : s ⊆ t} (h_surj : Surjective (inclusion h)) :
  s = t

explanatories.Set.inclusion: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.

Set.eq_of_inclusion_surjective.description: If a set is included in another set and the inclusion function is surjective, then the two sets are equal.

Subsingleton.eq_univ_of_nonempty.code: Subsingleton.eq_univ_of_nonempty.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Subsingleton α] {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty → s = univ

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Subsingleton.eq_univ_of_nonempty.description: If a set contains at least one element and its type is a subsingleton, then the set must be the universal set.

Subsingleton.set_cases.code:
Subsingleton.set_cases.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Subsingleton α] {p : Set α → Prop} (h0 : p ∅) (h1 : p univ) (s : Set α) :
  p s

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Subsingleton.set_cases.description: In a context where every element in a type is identical, if a property holds for the empty set and for the universe, it must also hold for any subset of that type.

Subsingleton.mem_iff_nonempty.code: Subsingleton.mem_iff_nonempty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Subsingleton α] {s : Set α} {x : α} : x ∈ s ↔ s.Nonempty

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Subsingleton.mem_iff_nonempty.description: An element belongs to a set if and only if that set contains at least one element when the element's type is a subsingleton.

Set.decidableSdiff.code:
Set.decidableSdiff.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) (a : α) [Decidable (a ∈ s)] [Decidable (a ∈ t)] :
  Decidable (a ∈ s \ t)

explanatories.inferInstanceAs: This mechanism generates an instance of a specified type by explicitly providing the type, aiding in typeclass inference when the desired instance is only registered for that type.

Set.decidableSdiff.fullDefinition: instance decidableSdiff [Decidable (a ∈ s)] [Decidable (a ∈ t)] : Decidable (a ∈ s \ t) :=   inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a ∈ s ∧ a ∉ t))
Set.decidableSdiff.description: The decidability of membership in the set difference between two sets is determined based on the decidability of membership of the element in each of the original sets.

Set.decidableInter.code:
Set.decidableInter.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) (a : α) [Decidable (a ∈ s)] [Decidable (a ∈ t)] :
  Decidable (a ∈ s ∩ t)

explanatories.inferInstanceAs: This mechanism generates an instance of a specified type by explicitly providing the type, aiding in typeclass inference when the desired instance is only registered for that type.

Set.decidableInter.fullDefinition: instance decidableInter [Decidable (a ∈ s)] [Decidable (a ∈ t)] : Decidable (a ∈ s ∩ t) :=   inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a ∈ s ∧ a ∈ t))
Set.decidableInter.description: The existence of a decision procedure for determining membership in the intersection of two sets is established when membership in each of the individual sets can be decidably verified.

Set.decidableUnion.code:
Set.decidableUnion.{u} {α : Type u} (s t : Set α) (a : α) [Decidable (a ∈ s)] [Decidable (a ∈ t)] :
  Decidable (a ∈ s ∪ t)

explanatories.inferInstanceAs: This mechanism generates an instance of a specified type by explicitly providing the type, aiding in typeclass inference when the desired instance is only registered for that type.

Set.decidableUnion.fullDefinition: instance decidableUnion [Decidable (a ∈ s)] [Decidable (a ∈ t)] : Decidable (a ∈ s ∪ t) :=   inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a ∈ s ∨ a ∈ t))
Set.decidableUnion.description: The membership of an element in the union of two sets is decidable if the membership in each individual set is also decidable.

Set.decidableCompl.code: Set.decidableCompl.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) (a : α) [Decidable (a ∈ s)] : Decidable (a ∈ sᶜ)

explanatories.inferInstanceAs: This mechanism generates an instance of a specified type by explicitly providing the type, aiding in typeclass inference when the desired instance is only registered for that type.

Set.decidableCompl.fullDefinition: instance decidableCompl [Decidable (a ∈ s)] : Decidable (a ∈ sᶜ) :=   inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a ∉ s))
Set.decidableCompl.description: The complement of a set is decidable regarding an element if the membership of that element in the original set is decidable.

explanatories.Decidable.isFalse: This theorem establishes that if a proposition is shown to be false, then it can be concluded that the proposition is decidable.

Set.decidableEmptyset.fullDefinition: instance decidableEmptyset : Decidable (a ∈ (∅ : Set α)) := Decidable.isFalse (by simp)
Set.decidableEmptyset.description: It is decidable that no element belongs to the empty set.

Set.decidableUniv.code: Set.decidableUniv.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) : Decidable (a ∈ univ)

explanatories.Decidable.isTrue: This shows that if a proposition is proven to be true, then it can be classified as decidable.

Set.decidableUniv.fullDefinition: instance decidableUniv : Decidable (a ∈ univ) := Decidable.isTrue (by simp)
Set.decidableUniv.description: An element is decidably in the universal set for a given type.

Set.decidableSetOf.code: Set.decidableSetOf.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) (p : α → Prop) [Decidable (p a)] : Decidable (a ∈ {a | p a})
Set.decidableSetOf.fullDefinition: instance decidableSetOf (p : α → Prop) [Decidable (p a)] : Decidable (a ∈ { a | p a }) := by   assumption
Set.decidableSetOf.description: The membership of an element in a set defined by a predicate is decidable if the predicate itself is decidable for that element.

Monotone.inter.code:
Monotone.inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} (hf : Monotone f)
  (hg : Monotone g) : Monotone fun x => f x ∩ g x
Monotone.inter.description: The intersection of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.

MonotoneOn.inter.code:
MonotoneOn.inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} {s : Set β}
  (hf : MonotoneOn f s) (hg : MonotoneOn g s) : MonotoneOn (fun x => f x ∩ g x) s

explanatories.Monotone.inter: The intersection of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.

MonotoneOn.inter.description: The intersection of two monotone functions defined on a set remains monotone on that same set.

Antitone.inter.code:
Antitone.inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} (hf : Antitone f)
  (hg : Antitone g) : Antitone fun x => f x ∩ g x

explanatories.Monotone.inter: The intersection of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.
explanatories.MonotoneOn.inter: The intersection of two monotone functions defined on a set remains monotone on that same set.

Antitone.inter.description: The intersection of two antitone functions produces another antitone function.

AntitoneOn.inter.code:
AntitoneOn.inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} {s : Set β}
  (hf : AntitoneOn f s) (hg : AntitoneOn g s) : AntitoneOn (fun x => f x ∩ g x) s

explanatories.Monotone.inter: The intersection of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.
explanatories.MonotoneOn.inter: The intersection of two monotone functions defined on a set remains monotone on that same set.
explanatories.Antitone.inter: The intersection of two antitone functions produces another antitone function.

AntitoneOn.inter.description: The intersection of two antitone functions over a specified set is also an antitone function on that set.

Monotone.union.code:
Monotone.union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} (hf : Monotone f)
  (hg : Monotone g) : Monotone fun x => f x ∪ g x
Monotone.union.description: The union of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.

MonotoneOn.union.code:
MonotoneOn.union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} {s : Set β}
  (hf : MonotoneOn f s) (hg : MonotoneOn g s) : MonotoneOn (fun x => f x ∪ g x) s

explanatories.Monotone.union: The union of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.

MonotoneOn.union.description: The union of two monotone functions defined on the same set is also a monotone function on that set.

Antitone.union.code:
Antitone.union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} (hf : Antitone f)
  (hg : Antitone g) : Antitone fun x => f x ∪ g x

explanatories.Monotone.union: The union of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.
explanatories.MonotoneOn.union: The union of two monotone functions defined on the same set is also a monotone function on that set.

Antitone.union.description: The union of two antitone functions is also an antitone function.

AntitoneOn.union.code:
AntitoneOn.union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder β] {f g : β → Set α} {s : Set β}
  (hf : AntitoneOn f s) (hg : AntitoneOn g s) : AntitoneOn (fun x => f x ∪ g x) s

explanatories.Monotone.union: The union of two monotone functions is also a monotone function.
explanatories.MonotoneOn.union: The union of two monotone functions defined on the same set is also a monotone function on that set.
explanatories.Antitone.union: The union of two antitone functions is also an antitone function.

AntitoneOn.union.description: The union of two antitone functions over a common set is also an antitone function over that set.

Set.monotone_setOf.code:
Set.monotone_setOf.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder α] {p : α → β → Prop}
  (hp : ∀ (b : β), Monotone fun a => p a b) : Monotone fun a => {b | p a b}
Set.monotone_setOf.description: A property that is monotone with respect to one variable implies that the set of elements related to that property also forms a monotone set associated with the other variable.

Set.antitone_setOf.code:
Set.antitone_setOf.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [Preorder α] {p : α → β → Prop}
  (hp : ∀ (b : β), Antitone fun a => p a b) : Antitone fun a => {b | p a b}
Set.antitone_setOf.description: A property defined over a set is antitone if, whenever it holds for an element, it also holds for any lesser element in a preordered context.

Set.antitone_bforall.code: Set.antitone_bforall.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {P : α → Prop} : Antitone fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, P x
Set.antitone_bforall.comment: Quantifying over a set is antitone in the set
Set.antitone_bforall.description: The property of a predicate being true for all elements in a set is antitone with respect to the inclusion of sets.

Disjoint.union_left.code: Disjoint.union_left.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t u : Set α} (hs : Disjoint s u) (ht : Disjoint t u) : Disjoint (s ∪ t) u
Disjoint.union_left.description: If two sets are disjoint from a third set, then the union of the first two sets is also disjoint from that third set.

Disjoint.union_right.code: Disjoint.union_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t u : Set α} (ht : Disjoint s t) (hu : Disjoint s u) : Disjoint s (t ∪ u)
Disjoint.union_right.description: If two sets are disjoint from a third set, then the first set is also disjoint from the union of the two other sets.

Disjoint.inter_left.code: Disjoint.inter_left.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (u : Set α) (h : Disjoint s t) : Disjoint (s ∩ u) t
Disjoint.inter_left.description: The intersection of a set with another set that is disjoint from a third set is also disjoint from the third set.

Disjoint.inter_left'.code: Disjoint.inter_left'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (u : Set α) (h : Disjoint s t) : Disjoint (u ∩ s) t
Disjoint.inter_left'.description: The intersection of a set with a disjoint set remains disjoint from that set.

Disjoint.inter_right.code: Disjoint.inter_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (u : Set α) (h : Disjoint s t) : Disjoint s (t ∩ u)
Disjoint.inter_right.description: If two sets are disjoint, then their intersection with any other set remains disjoint from the first set.

Disjoint.inter_right'.code: Disjoint.inter_right'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Set α} (u : Set α) (h : Disjoint s t) : Disjoint s (u ∩ t)
Disjoint.inter_right'.description: The disjointness of two sets remains true when one set is intersected with another set, provided the original two sets are disjoint.

Disjoint.subset_left_of_subset_union.code: Disjoint.subset_left_of_subset_union.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t u : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t ∪ u) (hac : Disjoint s u) : s ⊆ t
Disjoint.subset_left_of_subset_union.description: If a set is a subset of the union of two sets and it is disjoint from one of them, then it must also be a subset of the other set.

Disjoint.subset_right_of_subset_union.code: Disjoint.subset_right_of_subset_union.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t u : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t ∪ u) (hab : Disjoint s t) : s ⊆ u
Disjoint.subset_right_of_subset_union.description: If a set is a subset of the union of two other sets and is disjoint from one of them, then it must be a subset of the other set.

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Prop.compl_singleton.description: The complement of a singleton set containing a proposition is equal to the singleton set containing the negation of that proposition.

Set.Subsingleton.code: Set.Subsingleton.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : Prop
Set.Subsingleton.comment: A set `s` is a `Subsingleton` if it has at most one element.

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.Subsingleton.fullDefinition: protected def Subsingleton (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃x⦄ (_ : x ∈ s) ⦃y⦄ (_ : y ∈ s), x = y
Set.Subsingleton.description: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.

Set.Subsingleton.anti.code: Set.Subsingleton.anti.{u} {α : Type u} {s t : Set α} (ht : t.Subsingleton) (hst : s ⊆ t) : s.Subsingleton
Set.Subsingleton.anti.description: If one set is a Subsingleton and is a superset of another set, then the latter set is also a Subsingleton.

Set.Subsingleton.eq_singleton_of_mem.code: Set.Subsingleton.eq_singleton_of_mem.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (hs : s.Subsingleton) {x : α} (hx : x ∈ s) : s = {x}
Set.Subsingleton.eq_singleton_of_mem.description: If a set contains at most one element and an element belongs to that set, then the set is equal to the singleton containing that element.

Set.subsingleton_empty.description: The empty set is classified as a Subsingleton since it contains no elements.

Set.subsingleton_singleton.description: A singleton set is classified as a Subsingleton since it contains exactly one element.

Set.subsingleton_of_subset_singleton.code: Set.subsingleton_of_subset_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {a : α} {s : Set α} (h : s ⊆ {a}) : s.Subsingleton
Set.subsingleton_of_subset_singleton.description: A set that is a subset of a singleton set is also classified as a Subsingleton.

Set.subsingleton_of_forall_eq.code: Set.subsingleton_of_forall_eq.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (a : α) (h : ∀ b ∈ s, b = a) : s.Subsingleton
Set.subsingleton_of_forall_eq.description: If every element of a set is equal to a specific element, then that set is classified as a Subsingleton.

Set.subsingleton_iff_singleton.code: Set.subsingleton_iff_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x : α} (hx : x ∈ s) : s.Subsingleton ↔ s = {x}

explanatories.Set.Subsingleton: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.subsingleton_iff_singleton.description: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if and only if it is equal to the singleton set containing any of its elements.

Set.Subsingleton.eq_empty_or_singleton.code: Set.Subsingleton.eq_empty_or_singleton.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (hs : s.Subsingleton) : s = ∅ ∨ ∃ x, s = {x}
Set.Subsingleton.eq_empty_or_singleton.description: A set that is classified as a Subsingleton is either empty or contains exactly one element.

Set.Subsingleton.induction_on.code:
Set.Subsingleton.induction_on.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {p : Set α → Prop} (hs : s.Subsingleton) (he : p ∅)
  (h₁ : ∀ (x : α), p {x}) : p s
Set.Subsingleton.induction_on.description: For a set that contains at most one element, if a property holds for the empty set and also for any singleton set, then it holds for that set.

explanatories.Set.Subsingleton: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.subsingleton_univ.description: The universal set is classified as a Subsingleton if its elements belong to a type that contains at most one element.

Set.subsingleton_of_univ_subsingleton.code: Set.subsingleton_of_univ_subsingleton.{u} {α : Type u} (h : univ.Subsingleton) : Subsingleton α

explanatories.Set.Subsingleton: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.subsingleton_of_univ_subsingleton.description: If the universe set is a Subsingleton, then any type is also classified as a Subsingleton.

Set.subsingleton_univ_iff.code: Set.subsingleton_univ_iff.{u} {α : Type u} : univ.Subsingleton ↔ Subsingleton α

explanatories.Set.Subsingleton: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.subsingleton_univ_iff.description: The universal set is a Subsingleton if and only if its elements all belong to a single element type.

Set.subsingleton_of_subsingleton.code: Set.subsingleton_of_subsingleton.{u} {α : Type u} [Subsingleton α] {s : Set α} : s.Subsingleton

explanatories.Set.Subsingleton: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.subsingleton_of_subsingleton.description: Any set composed of elements from a type that is a Subsingleton must also be a Subsingleton itself.

Set.subsingleton_isTop.code: Set.subsingleton_isTop.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [PartialOrder α] : {x | IsTop x}.Subsingleton

explanatories.IsTop: An element in a partially ordered set is considered a top element if it is greater than or equal to every other element in that set.

Set.subsingleton_isTop.description: The set of all maximum elements in a partially ordered type is classified as a Subsingleton.

Set.subsingleton_isBot.code: Set.subsingleton_isBot.{u_1} (α : Type u_1) [PartialOrder α] : {x | IsBot x}.Subsingleton

explanatories.IsBot: An element in a partially ordered set is considered a bottom element if it is less than or equal to every other element in that set.

Set.subsingleton_isBot.description: The set of all minimum elements in a partially ordered type is classified as a Subsingleton.

Set.exists_eq_singleton_iff_nonempty_sub.code:
Set.exists_eq_singleton_iff_nonempty_subsingleton.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} :
  (∃ a, s = {a}) ↔ s.Nonempty ∧ s.Subsingleton

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.exists_eq_singleton_iff_nonempty_sub.description: A set is a singleton if and only if it is nonempty and contains no more than one element.

Set.subsingleton_coe.code: Set.subsingleton_coe.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : Subsingleton ↑s ↔ s.Subsingleton
Set.subsingleton_coe.comment: `s`, coerced to a type, is a subsingleton type if and only if `s` is a subsingleton set.

explanatories.Set.Subsingleton: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.subsingleton_coe.description: A set, when considered as a type, is a Subsingleton type if and only if the set itself contains at most one element.

Set.Subsingleton.coe_sort.code: Set.Subsingleton.coe_sort.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} : s.Subsingleton → Subsingleton ↑s

explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.

Set.Subsingleton.coe_sort.description: If a set is a Subsingleton, then its elements can be viewed as a Subsingleton type when considered with their natural inclusion.

Set.subsingleton_coe_of_subsingleton.code: Set.subsingleton_coe_of_subsingleton.{u} {α : Type u} [Subsingleton α] {s : Set α} : Subsingleton ↑s
Set.subsingleton_coe_of_subsingleton.comment:
The `coe_sort` of a set `s` in a subsingleton type is a subsingleton.
For the corresponding result for `Subtype`, see `subtype.subsingleton`.

explanatories.Set.Subsingleton: A set is classified as a Subsingleton if it contains no more than one element.
explanatories.Singleton.singleton: This defines a function that associates an element with a singleton collection containing only that element.
explanatories.Set.subsingleton_of_subsingleton: Any set composed of elements from a type that is a Subsingleton must also be a Subsingleton itself.

Set.subsingleton_coe_of_subsingleton.fullDefinition: instance subsingleton_coe_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton α] {s : Set α} : Subsingleton s := by   rw [s.subsingleton_coe]   exact subsingleton_of_subsingleton
Set.subsingleton_coe_of_subsingleton.description: The canonical representation of a set derived from a type classified as a Subsingleton is also regarded as a Subsingleton.

Set.Nontrivial.code: Set.Nontrivial.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : Prop
Set.Nontrivial.comment: A set `s` is `Set.Nontrivial` if it has at least two distinct elements.
Set.Nontrivial.fullDefinition: protected def Nontrivial (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ s, x ≠ y
Set.Nontrivial.description: A set is classified as nontrivial if it contains at least two distinct elements.

Set.nontrivial_of_mem_mem_ne.code:
