Set.nontrivial_of_mem_mem_ne.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} {x y : α} (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) (hxy : x ≠ y) :
  s.Nontrivial
Set.nontrivial_of_mem_mem_ne.description: A set containing at least two distinct elements is classified as Nontrivial.

Set.Nontrivial.choose.code: Set.Nontrivial.choose.{u} {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (hs : s.Nontrivial) : α × α
Set.Nontrivial.choose.comment:
Extract witnesses from s.nontrivial. This function might be used instead of case analysis on the
argument. Note that it makes a proof depend on the classical.choice axiom.

explanatories.And.right: The theorem allows one to derive the second component of a conjunction from a given statement that asserts both components are true.
explanatories.Exists.choose: The operation extracts an element satisfying a specified property from an existential statement asserting that such an element exists.
explanatories.Exists.choose_spec: An element extracted from an existential statement satisfies the specified property.

Set.Nontrivial.choose.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def Nontrivial.choose (hs : s.Nontrivial) : α × α :=   (Exists.choose hs, hs.choose_spec.right.choose)
Set.Nontrivial.choose.description: This function selects two distinct elements from a nontrivial set.

Set.enumerate.code: Set.enumerate.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (sel : Set α → Option α) : Set α → ℕ → Option α
Set.enumerate.comment:
Given a choice function `sel`, enumerates the elements of a set in the order
`a 0 = sel s`, `a 1 = sel (s \ {a 0})`, `a 2 = sel (s \ {a 0, a 1})`, ... and stops when
`sel (s \ {a 0, ..., a n}) = none`. Note that we don't require `sel` to be a choice function.
Set.enumerate.fullDefinition: def enumerate : Set α → ℕ → Option α   | s, 0 => sel s   | s, n + 1 => do     let a ← sel s     enumerate (s \ {a}) n
Set.enumerate.description: This definition describes a function that enumerates the elements of a set using a selection function, progressively removing previously selected elements until no more can be selected.

explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."

Set.enumerate_eq_none_of_sel.description: If the selection function returns none for a set, then enumerating that set will result in none for any number of elements.

Set.preimage_congr.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f g : α → β} {s : Set β} (h : ∀ (x : α), f x = g x) :
  f ⁻¹' s = g ⁻¹' s
Set.preimage_congr.description: If two functions produce the same output for all inputs, then the preimages of any set under both functions are identical.

Set.preimage_mono.code: Set.preimage_mono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s t : Set β} (h : s ⊆ t) : f ⁻¹' s ⊆ f ⁻¹' t
Set.preimage_mono.description: If one set is a subset of another, then the preimage of the first set under any function is a subset of the preimage of the second set.

Set.preimage_univ.code: Set.preimage_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} : f ⁻¹' univ = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.preimage_univ.description: The preimage of the universal set under any function is the universal set itself.

Set.subset_preimage_univ.code: Set.subset_preimage_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} : s ⊆ f ⁻¹' univ
Set.subset_preimage_univ.description: Any set is a subset of the preimage of the universal set under any function.

Set.preimage_inter.code:
Set.preimage_inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s t : Set β} :
  f ⁻¹' (s ∩ t) = f ⁻¹' s ∩ f ⁻¹' t
Set.preimage_inter.description: The preimage of the intersection of two sets under a function is equal to the intersection of the preimages of those sets under the same function.

Set.preimage_union.code:
Set.preimage_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s t : Set β} :
  f ⁻¹' (s ∪ t) = f ⁻¹' s ∪ f ⁻¹' t
Set.preimage_union.description: The preimage of the union of two sets under a function is equal to the union of the preimages of those sets under the same function.

Set.preimage_compl.code: Set.preimage_compl.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set β} : f ⁻¹' sᶜ = (f ⁻¹' s)ᶜ
Set.preimage_compl.description: The preimage of the complement of a set under any function is equal to the complement of the preimage of that set.

Set.preimage_diff.code: Set.preimage_diff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s t : Set β) : f ⁻¹' (s \ t) = f ⁻¹' s \ f ⁻¹' t
Set.preimage_diff.description: The preimage of the difference between two sets under a function is equal to the difference between the preimage of the first set and the preimage of the second set.

Set.preimage_symmDiff.code:
Set.preimage_symmDiff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} (s t : Set β) :
  f ⁻¹' symmDiff s t = symmDiff (f ⁻¹' s) (f ⁻¹' t)
Set.preimage_symmDiff.description: The preimage of the symmetric difference of two sets under a function is equal to the symmetric difference of the preimages of those sets under the same function.

Set.preimage_ite.code:
Set.preimage_ite.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s t₁ t₂ : Set β) :
  f ⁻¹' s.ite t₁ t₂ = (f ⁻¹' s).ite (f ⁻¹' t₁) (f ⁻¹' t₂)

explanatories.Set.ite: The definition describes a construction that produces a set based on a condition, resulting in elements from one set if the condition is true and from another set otherwise, while ensuring specified relationships with the intersection and complement of those sets.

Set.preimage_ite.description: The preimage of a conditional set under a function is equal to the conditional on the preimages of the sets involved.

Set.preimage_setOf_eq.code:
Set.preimage_setOf_eq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {p : α → Prop} {f : β → α} :
  f ⁻¹' {a | p a} = {a | p (f a)}
Set.preimage_setOf_eq.description: The preimage of the set of elements satisfying a property under a function is equal to the set of elements in the domain that map to elements satisfying that property.

Set.preimage_id_eq.code: Set.preimage_id_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} : preimage id = id

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Set.preimage_id_eq.description: The preimage of the identity function is the identity function itself.

Set.preimage_id.code: Set.preimage_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} : id ⁻¹' s = s
Set.preimage_id.description: The preimage of any set under the identity function is the set itself.

Set.preimage_id'.code: Set.preimage_id'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} : (fun x => x) ⁻¹' s = s
Set.preimage_id'.description: The preimage of a set under the identity function is the set itself.

Set.preimage_const_of_mem.code:
Set.preimage_const_of_mem.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {s : Set β} (h : b ∈ s) :
  (fun x => b) ⁻¹' s = univ
Set.preimage_const_of_mem.description: The preimage of a set under a constant function that maps every element to a specific value is the universal set if that value is an element of the original set.

Set.preimage_const_of_not_mem.code:
Set.preimage_const_of_not_mem.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {s : Set β} (h : b ∉ s) :
  (fun x => b) ⁻¹' s = ∅
Set.preimage_const_of_not_mem.description: The preimage of a set under a constant function is empty if the constant value is not an element of that set.

Set.preimage_const.code:
Set.preimage_const.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (b : β) (s : Set β) [Decidable (b ∈ s)] :
  (fun x => b) ⁻¹' s = if b ∈ s then univ else ∅

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.preimage_const.description: The preimage of a set under a constant function returns the universal set if the constant is in the set, and the empty set otherwise.

Set.preimage_comp.code:
Set.preimage_comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} {s : Set γ} :
  g ∘ f ⁻¹' s = f ⁻¹' (g ⁻¹' s)
Set.preimage_comp.description: The preimage of a set under the composition of two functions equals the preimage of that set under the second function, followed by the preimage under the first function.

Set.preimage_comp_eq.code:
Set.preimage_comp_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} :
  preimage (g ∘ f) = preimage f ∘ preimage g

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Set.preimage_comp_eq.description: The preimage of the composition of two functions is equal to the composition of their individual preimages.

Set.preimage_iterate_eq.code: Set.preimage_iterate_eq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {f : α → α} {n : ℕ} : preimage f^[n] = (preimage f)^[n]

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Set.preimage_iterate_eq.description: The preimage of a function applied multiple times is equal to the iterated application of the preimage operation.

Set.preimage_preimage.code:
Set.preimage_preimage.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {g : β → γ} {f : α → β} {s : Set γ} :
  f ⁻¹' (g ⁻¹' s) = (fun x => g (f x)) ⁻¹' s
Set.preimage_preimage.description: The preimage of the preimage of a set under a composition of functions is equal to the preimage of that set under the composite function formed by those functions.

Set.eq_preimage_subtype_val_iff.code:
Set.eq_preimage_subtype_val_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {p : α → Prop} {s : Set (Subtype p)} {t : Set α} :
  s = Subtype.val ⁻¹' t ↔ ∀ (x : α) (h : p x), ⟨x, h⟩ ∈ s ↔ x ∈ t

explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.

Set.eq_preimage_subtype_val_iff.description: A set of subtypes is equal to the preimage of another set if and only if an element with a certain property belongs to the first set if and only if its corresponding element belongs to the second set.

Set.nonempty_of_nonempty_preimage.code:
Set.nonempty_of_nonempty_preimage.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set β} {f : α → β}
  (hf : (f ⁻¹' s).Nonempty) : s.Nonempty
Set.nonempty_of_nonempty_preimage.description: If the preimage of a set under a function is nonempty, then the original set is also nonempty.

Set.preimage_singleton_true.code: Set.preimage_singleton_true.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (p : α → Prop) : p ⁻¹' {True} = {a | p a}
Set.preimage_singleton_true.description: The preimage of the singleton set containing true under a predicate is the set of all elements that satisfy that predicate.

Set.preimage_singleton_false.code: Set.preimage_singleton_false.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (p : α → Prop) : p ⁻¹' {False} = {a | ¬p a}
Set.preimage_singleton_false.description: The preimage of a singleton set containing false is the set of all elements for which the corresponding predicate does not hold true.

Set.preimage_subtype_coe_eq_compl.code:
Set.preimage_subtype_coe_eq_compl.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s u v : Set α} (hsuv : s ⊆ u ∪ v) (H : s ∩ (u ∩ v) = ∅) :
  Subtype.val ⁻¹' u = (Subtype.val ⁻¹' v)ᶜ

explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.

Set.preimage_subtype_coe_eq_compl.description: The preimage of a set under a function that projects to elements of the set is equal to the complement of the preimage of another set if the first set is disjoint from the intersection of the two sets involved.

Set.mem_image_iff_bex.code:
Set.mem_image_iff_bex.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {y : β} :
  y ∈ f '' s ↔ ∃ x, ∃ (_ : x ∈ s), f x = y
Set.mem_image_iff_bex.description: An element belongs to the image of a set under a function if and only if there exists a corresponding element in the original set that maps to it.

Set.image_eta.code: Set.image_eta.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} (f : α → β) : f '' s = (fun x => f x) '' s
Set.image_eta.description: The image of a set under a function is equal to the image of that set under the function expressed as a lambda function.

Function.Injective.mem_set_image.code:
Function.Injective.mem_set_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} (hf : Injective f) {s : Set α}
  {a : α} : f a ∈ f '' s ↔ a ∈ s

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Function.Injective.mem_set_image.description: If a function is injective, an element is in the image of a set under that function if and only if the original element was in the set.

Set.forall_mem_image.code:
Set.forall_mem_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {p : β → Prop} :
  (∀ y ∈ f '' s, p y) ↔ ∀ ⦃x : α⦄, x ∈ s → p (f x)
Set.forall_mem_image.description: The condition that a property holds for all images of elements from a set under a function is equivalent to saying that the property holds for the function's output applied to every element of that set.

Set.exists_mem_image.code:
Set.exists_mem_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {p : β → Prop} :
  (∃ y ∈ f '' s, p y) ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, p (f x)
Set.exists_mem_image.description: There exists an element in the image of a set under a function satisfying a property if and only if there exists an element in the original set such that applying the function to it also satisfies that property.

Set.ball_image_of_ball.code:
Set.ball_image_of_ball.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {p : β → Prop} :
  (∀ ⦃x : α⦄, x ∈ s → p (f x)) → ∀ y ∈ f '' s, p y
Set.ball_image_of_ball.description: If a property holds for the images of all elements in a set under a function, then it also holds for all elements in the image of that set.

Set.mem_image_elim.code:
Set.mem_image_elim.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {C : β → Prop}
  (h : ∀ x ∈ s, C (f x)) {y : β} : y ∈ f '' s → C y
Set.mem_image_elim.description: If every element in a set maps to a property through a function, then any element in the image of that set also satisfies the same property.

Set.mem_image_elim_on.code:
Set.mem_image_elim_on.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {C : β → Prop} {y : β}
  (h_y : y ∈ f '' s) (h : ∀ x ∈ s, C (f x)) : C y
Set.mem_image_elim_on.description: If an element belongs to the image of a set under a function and all elements in that set satisfy a certain property, then the element in the image also satisfies that property.

Set.image_congr.code:
Set.image_congr.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f g : α → β} {s : Set α} (h : ∀ a ∈ s, f a = g a) :
  f '' s = g '' s
Set.image_congr.description: If two functions agree on all elements of a set, their images on that set will be identical.

Set.image_congr'.code:
Set.image_congr'.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f g : α → β} {s : Set α} (h : ∀ (x : α), f x = g x) :
  f '' s = g '' s
Set.image_congr'.description: If two functions agree on all elements of a set, then their images over that set are equal.

Set.image_comp.code:
Set.image_comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (f : β → γ) (g : α → β) (a : Set α) :
  f ∘ g '' a = f '' (g '' a)
Set.image_comp.description: The image of a set under the composition of two functions is equal to the image of the set under the second function followed by the first function applied to the resulting set.

Set.image_image.code:
Set.image_image.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (g : β → γ) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) :
  g '' (f '' s) = (fun x => g (f x)) '' s
Set.image_image.comment: A variant of `image_comp`, useful for rewriting
Set.image_image.description: The image of a set obtained by applying one function followed by another is equal to the image obtained by directly applying the composite function to the original set.

Set.image_comm.code:
Set.image_comm.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set α} {β' : Type u_6} {f : β → γ}
  {g : α → β} {f' : α → β'} {g' : β' → γ} (h_comm : ∀ (a : α), f (g a) = g' (f' a)) : f '' (g '' s) = g' '' (f' '' s)
Set.image_comm.description: The image of the composition of two functions over a set is equal to the image under a different composition of those functions if the two compositions commute.

Function.Semiconj.set_image.code:
Function.Semiconj.set_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {ga : α → α} {gb : β → β}
  (h : Semiconj f ga gb) : Semiconj (image f) (image ga) (image gb)

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Function.Semiconj.set_image.description: If a function is semi-conjugate to another pair of functions, then the image of the first function is also semi-conjugate to the images of the corresponding functions.

Function.Commute.set_image.code:
Function.Commute.set_image.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {f g : α → α} (h : Function.Commute f g) :
  Function.Commute (image f) (image g)

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Function.Semiconj.set_image: If a function is semi-conjugate to another pair of functions, then the image of the first function is also semi-conjugate to the images of the corresponding functions.

Function.Commute.set_image.description: The images of two commuting functions are themselves commuting when applied to the same set.

Set.image_subset.code: Set.image_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {a b : Set α} (f : α → β) (h : a ⊆ b) : f '' a ⊆ f '' b
Set.image_subset.comment:
Image is monotone with respect to `⊆`. See `Set.monotone_image` for the statement in
terms of `≤`.
Set.image_subset.description: The image of a subset under a function is contained within the image of the superset.

Set.monotone_image.code: Set.monotone_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} : Monotone (image f)
Set.monotone_image.comment: `Set.image` is monotone. See `Set.image_subset` for the statement in terms of `⊆`.

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

Set.monotone_image.description: The image of a monotone function preserves the monotonicity property.

Set.image_union.code: Set.image_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s t : Set α) : f '' (s ∪ t) = f '' s ∪ f '' t
Set.image_union.description: The image of the union of two sets under a function is equal to the union of the images of each set under that function.

Set.image_empty.code: Set.image_empty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) : f '' ∅ = ∅
Set.image_empty.description: The image of an empty set under any function is also an empty set.

Set.image_inter_subset.code:
Set.image_inter_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s t : Set α) :
  f '' (s ∩ t) ⊆ f '' s ∩ f '' t
Set.image_inter_subset.description: The image of the intersection of two sets under a function is a subset of the intersection of their respective images.

Set.image_inter_on.code:
Set.image_inter_on.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s t : Set α}
  (h : ∀ x ∈ t, ∀ y ∈ s, f x = f y → x = y) : f '' (s ∩ t) = f '' s ∩ f '' t
Set.image_inter_on.description: The image of the intersection of two sets under a function is equal to the intersection of their respective images if the function is injective on the intersection.

Set.image_inter.code:
Set.image_inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s t : Set α} (H : Injective f) :
  f '' (s ∩ t) = f '' s ∩ f '' t

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Set.image_inter.description: The image of the intersection of two sets under an injective function is equal to the intersection of the images of each set under that function.

Set.image_univ_of_surjective.code: Set.image_univ_of_surjective.{u_2, u_6} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_6} {f : ι → β} (H : Surjective f) : f '' univ = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.image_univ_of_surjective.description: If a function is surjective, the image of the universal set under that function is the universal set itself.

Set.image_singleton.code: Set.image_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {a : α} : f '' {a} = {f a}
Set.image_singleton.description: The image of a singleton set under a function is the singleton set containing the image of the sole element in the original set.

Set.Nonempty.image_const.code:
Set.Nonempty.image_const.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} (hs : s.Nonempty) (a : β) :
  (fun x => a) '' s = {a}
Set.Nonempty.image_const.description: The image of a non-empty set under a constant function consists solely of the single value that the function outputs.

Set.image_eq_empty.code: Set.image_eq_empty.{u_6, u_7} {α : Type u_6} {β : Type u_7} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} : f '' s = ∅ ↔ s = ∅
Set.image_eq_empty.description: The image of a set under a function is empty if and only if the original set itself is empty.

Set.preimage_compl_eq_image_compl.code: Set.preimage_compl_eq_image_compl.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [BooleanAlgebra α] (S : Set α) : compl ⁻¹' S = compl '' S

explanatories.HasCompl.compl: A function that returns the complement of an element in a set or lattice structure.

Set.preimage_compl_eq_image_compl.description: The preimage of a set under the complement function is equal to the image of that set under the complement operation.

Set.mem_compl_image.code: Set.mem_compl_image.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [BooleanAlgebra α] (t : α) (S : Set α) : t ∈ compl '' S ↔ tᶜ ∈ S

explanatories.HasCompl.compl: A function that returns the complement of an element in a set or lattice structure.

Set.mem_compl_image.description: An element belongs to the image of the complement of a set if and only if its complement belongs to the original set.

Set.image_id'.code: Set.image_id'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : (fun x => x) '' s = s
Set.image_id'.description: The image of a set under the identity function is equal to the set itself.

Set.image_id.code: Set.image_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : id '' s = s
Set.image_id.description: The image of a set under the identity function is equal to the set itself.

Set.image_comp_eq.code:
Set.image_comp_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} :
  image (g ∘ f) = image g ∘ image f
Set.image_comp_eq.description: The image of the composition of two functions is equal to the composition of their images.

Set.compl_compl_image.code: Set.compl_compl_image.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [BooleanAlgebra α] (S : Set α) : compl '' (compl '' S) = S

explanatories.HasCompl.compl: A function that returns the complement of an element in a set or lattice structure.

Set.compl_compl_image.description: The image of the complement of a set under a Boolean algebra operation is equal to the original set.

Set.image_insert_eq.code:
Set.image_insert_eq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {a : α} {s : Set α} :
  f '' insert a s = insert (f a) (f '' s)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.image_insert_eq.description: The image of a set formed by inserting an element and applying a function is equal to inserting the image of that element along with the image of the original set.

Set.image_pair.code: Set.image_pair.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (a b : α) : f '' {a, b} = {f a, f b}
Set.image_pair.description: The image of a set containing two elements under a function is the set of the images of those two elements.

Set.image_subset_preimage_of_inverse.code:
Set.image_subset_preimage_of_inverse.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α}
  (I : LeftInverse g f) (s : Set α) : f '' s ⊆ g ⁻¹' s

explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.

Set.image_subset_preimage_of_inverse.description: The image of a set under a function with a left inverse is contained within the preimage of that set under the inverse function.

Set.preimage_subset_image_of_inverse.code:
Set.preimage_subset_image_of_inverse.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α}
  (I : LeftInverse g f) (s : Set β) : f ⁻¹' s ⊆ g '' s

explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.

Set.preimage_subset_image_of_inverse.description: The preimage of any set under a function is contained within the image of that set under its left inverse.

Set.image_eq_preimage_of_inverse.code:
Set.image_eq_preimage_of_inverse.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α} (h₁ : LeftInverse g f)
  (h₂ : Function.RightInverse g f) : image f = preimage g

explanatories.Set.preimage: The preimage of a set under a function consists of all elements that map into the set when the function is applied.
explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.
explanatories.Function.RightInverse: This definition describes a relationship where one function serves as a right inverse to another by ensuring the composition of the two produces the identity function.

Set.image_eq_preimage_of_inverse.description: The image of a function equals the preimage of its left inverse when the two functions are indeed inverses of each other.

Set.mem_image_iff_of_inverse.code:
Set.mem_image_iff_of_inverse.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α} {b : β} {s : Set α}
  (h₁ : LeftInverse g f) (h₂ : Function.RightInverse g f) : b ∈ f '' s ↔ g b ∈ s

explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.
explanatories.Function.RightInverse: This definition describes a relationship where one function serves as a right inverse to another by ensuring the composition of the two produces the identity function.

Set.mem_image_iff_of_inverse.description: An element is in the image of a set under a function if and only if its preimage under the inverse function is in the original set, given that the functions are mutually inverse.

Set.image_compl_subset.code:
Set.image_compl_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (H : Injective f) :
  f '' sᶜ ⊆ (f '' s)ᶜ

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Set.image_compl_subset.description: The image of the complement of a set under an injective function is a subset of the complement of the image of that set.

Set.subset_image_compl.code:
Set.subset_image_compl.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (H : Surjective f) :
  (f '' s)ᶜ ⊆ f '' sᶜ

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.subset_image_compl.description: The complement of the image of a set under a surjective function is a subset of the image of the complement of that set.

Set.image_compl_eq.code:
Set.image_compl_eq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} (H : Bijective f) :
  f '' sᶜ = (f '' s)ᶜ

explanatories.Function.Bijective: This definition states that a function is classified as bijective when it possesses the properties of being both injective and surjective.

Set.image_compl_eq.description: The image of the complement of a set under a bijective function is equal to the complement of the image of that set.

Set.subset_image_diff.code:
Set.subset_image_diff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s t : Set α) :
  f '' s \ f '' t ⊆ f '' (s \ t)
Set.subset_image_diff.description: The image of the set difference between two sets under a function is a subset of the image of the first set after removing the elements that are also in the second set.

Set.subset_image_symmDiff.code:
Set.subset_image_symmDiff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s t : Set α} :
  symmDiff (f '' s) (f '' t) ⊆ f '' symmDiff s t
Set.subset_image_symmDiff.description: The symmetric difference of the images of two sets under a function is a subset of the image of the symmetric difference of those sets.

Set.image_diff.code:
Set.image_diff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} (hf : Injective f) (s t : Set α) :
  f '' (s \ t) = f '' s \ f '' t

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Set.image_diff.description: The image of the difference between two sets under an injective function is equal to the difference between the images of those sets.

Set.image_symmDiff.code:
Set.image_symmDiff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} (hf : Injective f) (s t : Set α) :
  f '' symmDiff s t = symmDiff (f '' s) (f '' t)

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Set.image_symmDiff.description: The image of the symmetric difference of two sets under an injective function is equal to the symmetric difference of the images of those sets under the same function.

Set.Nonempty.image.code: Set.Nonempty.image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) {s : Set α} : s.Nonempty → (f '' s).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.image.description: The image of a nonempty set under any function is also nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.of_image.code: Set.Nonempty.of_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} : (f '' s).Nonempty → s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_image.description: If the image of a set under a function is nonempty, then the original set must also be nonempty.

Set.image_nonempty.code: Set.image_nonempty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} : (f '' s).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.image_nonempty.description: The image of a set under a function is non-empty if and only if the original set is non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.preimage.code:
Set.Nonempty.preimage.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set β} (hs : s.Nonempty) {f : α → β}
  (hf : Surjective f) : (f ⁻¹' s).Nonempty

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.Nonempty.preimage.description: The preimage of a non-empty set under a surjective function is non-empty.

Set.image_subset_iff.code:
Set.image_subset_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {f : α → β} :
  f '' s ⊆ t ↔ s ⊆ f ⁻¹' t
Set.image_subset_iff.comment: image and preimage are a Galois connection
Set.image_subset_iff.description: The image of a set under a function is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the preimage of that other set, illustrating a Galois connection between image and preimage.

Set.image_preimage_subset.code: Set.image_preimage_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s : Set β) : f '' (f ⁻¹' s) ⊆ s
Set.image_preimage_subset.description: The image of the preimage of a set under a function is a subset of the original set.

Set.subset_preimage_image.code: Set.subset_preimage_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : s ⊆ f ⁻¹' (f '' s)
Set.subset_preimage_image.description: Any set is a subset of its preimage under the image of a function.

Set.preimage_image_eq.code:
Set.preimage_image_eq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} (s : Set α) (h : Injective f) :
  f ⁻¹' (f '' s) = s

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Set.preimage_image_eq.description: The preimage of the image of a set under an injective function is equal to the original set.

Set.image_preimage_eq.code:
Set.image_preimage_eq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} (s : Set β) (h : Surjective f) :
  f '' (f ⁻¹' s) = s

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.image_preimage_eq.description: The image of the preimage of a set under a surjective function equals the original set.

Set.preimage_eq_preimage.code:
Set.preimage_eq_preimage.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s t : Set α} {f : β → α} (hf : Surjective f) :
  f ⁻¹' s = f ⁻¹' t ↔ s = t

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.preimage_eq_preimage.description: For a surjective function, the preimages of two sets are equal if and only if the two sets themselves are equal.

Set.image_inter_preimage.code:
Set.image_inter_preimage.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
  f '' (s ∩ f ⁻¹' t) = f '' s ∩ t
Set.image_inter_preimage.description: The image of the intersection of a set and the preimage of another set under a function equals the intersection of the image of the first set and the second set.

Set.image_preimage_inter.code:
Set.image_preimage_inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
  f '' (f ⁻¹' t ∩ s) = t ∩ f '' s
Set.image_preimage_inter.description: The image of the intersection of a set and the preimage of another set under a function is equal to the intersection of that second set and the image of the first set under the same function.

Set.image_inter_nonempty_iff.code:
Set.image_inter_nonempty_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} :
  (f '' s ∩ t).Nonempty ↔ (s ∩ f ⁻¹' t).Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.image_inter_nonempty_iff.description: The intersection of the image of a set under a function and another set is nonempty if and only if the intersection of the first set and the preimage of the second set is also nonempty.

Set.image_diff_preimage.code:
Set.image_diff_preimage.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} :
  f '' (s \ f ⁻¹' t) = f '' s \ t
Set.image_diff_preimage.description: The image of the difference between a set and the preimage of another set under a function is equivalent to the image of the original set minus the second set.

Set.compl_image.code: Set.compl_image.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} : image compl = preimage compl

explanatories.Set.preimage: The preimage of a set under a function consists of all elements that map into the set when the function is applied.
explanatories.HasCompl.compl: A function that returns the complement of an element in a set or lattice structure.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image: The image of a nonempty set under any function is also nonempty.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.preimage: The preimage of a non-empty set under a surjective function is non-empty.

Set.compl_image.description: The image of the complement of a set is equal to the preimage of the complement of a set.

Set.compl_image_set_of.code: Set.compl_image_set_of.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {p : Set α → Prop} : compl '' {s | p s} = {s | p sᶜ}

explanatories.HasCompl.compl: A function that returns the complement of an element in a set or lattice structure.

Set.compl_image_set_of.description: The complement of the image of sets satisfying a property is equal to the set of complements of those sets that satisfy the same property.

Set.inter_preimage_subset.code:
Set.inter_preimage_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : Set β) (f : α → β) :
  s ∩ f ⁻¹' t ⊆ f ⁻¹' (f '' s ∩ t)
Set.inter_preimage_subset.description: The intersection of a set and the preimage of another set under a function is a subset of the preimage of the intersection of the image of the first set under the function and the second set.

Set.union_preimage_subset.code:
Set.union_preimage_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : Set β) (f : α → β) :
  s ∪ f ⁻¹' t ⊆ f ⁻¹' (f '' s ∪ t)
Set.union_preimage_subset.description: The union of a set and the preimage of another set under a function is a subset of the preimage of the union of the image of the first set and the second set.

Set.subset_image_union.code:
Set.subset_image_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
  f '' (s ∪ f ⁻¹' t) ⊆ f '' s ∪ t
Set.subset_image_union.description: The image of the union of a set and the preimage of another set under a function is a subset of the union of the function's image of the first set and the second set.

Set.preimage_subset_iff.code:
Set.preimage_subset_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {A : Set α} {B : Set β} {f : α → β} :
  f ⁻¹' B ⊆ A ↔ ∀ (a : α), f a ∈ B → a ∈ A
Set.preimage_subset_iff.description: The preimage of a set is a subset of another set if and only if whenever an element is mapped into the first set, it belongs to the second set.

Set.image_eq_image.code:
Set.image_eq_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s t : Set α} {f : α → β} (hf : Injective f) :
  f '' s = f '' t ↔ s = t

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Set.image_eq_image.description: The images of two sets under an injective function are equal if and only if the sets themselves are equal.

Set.image_mono.code: Set.image_mono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : f '' s ⊆ f '' t
Set.image_mono.description: The image of a subset under a function is contained within the image of a superset if the subset is included in the superset.

Set.subset_image_iff.code:
Set.subset_image_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} :
  t ⊆ f '' s ↔ ∃ u ⊆ s, f '' u = t
Set.subset_image_iff.description: A set is a subset of the image under a function if and only if there exists a smaller set mapped by the function that produces this subset.

Set.image_subset_image_iff.code:
Set.image_subset_image_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s t : Set α} {f : α → β} (hf : Injective f) :
  f '' s ⊆ f '' t ↔ s ⊆ t

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Set.image_subset_image_iff.description: The image of one set under an injective function is a subset of the image of another set if and only if the first set is a subset of the second.

Set.prod_quotient_preimage_eq_image.code:
Set.prod_quotient_preimage_eq_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [s : Setoid α] (g : Quotient s → β)
  {h : α → β} (Hh : h = g ∘ Quotient.mk'') (r : Set (β × β)) :
  {x | (g x.1, g x.2) ∈ r} = (fun a => (⟦a.1⟧, ⟦a.2⟧)) '' ((fun a => (h a.1, h a.2)) ⁻¹' r)

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.
explanatories.Quotient: This definition introduces a type that represents the set of equivalence classes for elements of a type, given a specific equivalence relation known as a setoid.

Set.prod_quotient_preimage_eq_image.description: The preimage of a relation on the image of equivalence classes corresponds to the image of pairs of elements in the quotient set under the composed function.

Set.exists_image_iff.code:
Set.exists_image_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (x : Set α) (P : β → Prop) :
  (∃ a, P ↑a) ↔ ∃ a, P (f ↑a)
Set.exists_image_iff.description: Existence of an element satisfying a property in a set is equivalent to the existence of an element in the image of that set under a function that also satisfies the property.

Set.imageFactorization_eq.code:
Set.imageFactorization_eq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} :
  Subtype.val ∘ imageFactorization f s = f ∘ Subtype.val

explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.

Set.imageFactorization_eq.description: The image factorization of a function through a set is equivalent to the composition of the function with the projection from the subtype of that set.

Set.surjective_onto_image.code:
Set.surjective_onto_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} :
  Surjective (imageFactorization f s)

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.
explanatories.Set.imageFactorization: The function's restriction to a set creates a mapping from that set to the image of the set under the function.

Set.surjective_onto_image.description: The image factorization of a function over a set is surjective if the function itself is surjective.

Set.image_perm.code: Set.image_perm.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} {σ : Equiv.Perm α} (hs : {a | σ a ≠ a} ⊆ s) : ⇑σ '' s = s
Set.image_perm.comment: If the only elements outside `s` are those left fixed by `σ`, then mapping by `σ` has no effect.

explanatories.Equiv.Perm: This definition introduces the type that represents all bijections from a set to itself.

Set.image_perm.description: If the only elements not in a set are those unchanged by a permutation, then the image of the set under that permutation remains the same.

Set.powerset_insert.code: Set.powerset_insert.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) (a : α) : 𝒫 insert a s = 𝒫 s ∪ insert a '' 𝒫 s
Set.powerset_insert.comment: The powerset of `{a} ∪ s` is `𝒫 s` together with `{a} ∪ t` for each `t ∈ 𝒫 s`.

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.powerset_insert.description: The powerset of a set that includes an element is equal to the union of the powerset of the original set and the set of all combinations that include that element with each subset of the original set.

Set.forall_mem_range.code:
Set.forall_mem_range.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → α} {p : α → Prop} :
  (∀ a ∈ range f, p a) ↔ ∀ (i : ι), p (f i)

Set.forall_mem_range.description: A property holds for all elements in the range of a function if and only if it holds for all inputs of that function.

Set.forall_subtype_range_iff.code:
Set.forall_subtype_range_iff.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → α} {p : ↑(range f) → Prop} :

Set.forall_subtype_range_iff.description: The property that a predicate holds for all elements in the range of a function is equivalent to that predicate holding for all inputs of the function.

Set.exists_range_iff.code:
Set.exists_range_iff.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → α} {p : α → Prop} :
  (∃ a ∈ range f, p a) ↔ ∃ i, p (f i)

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.exists_range_iff.description: There exists an element in the range of a function that satisfies a property if and only if there exists an index for which the function produces an element that satisfies that property.

Set.exists_range_iff'.code:
Set.exists_range_iff'.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → α} {p : α → Prop} :
  (∃ a ∈ range f, p a) ↔ ∃ i, p (f i)

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.exists_range_iff'.description: The existence of an element in the range of a function satisfying a property is equivalent to the existence of an index such that the function evaluated at that index also satisfies the property.

Set.exists_subtype_range_iff.code:
Set.exists_subtype_range_iff.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → α} {p : ↑(range f) → Prop} :
  (∃ a, p a) ↔ ∃ i, p ⟨f i, ⋯⟩

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.exists_subtype_range_iff.description: The existence of an element satisfying a property in the range of a function is equivalent to the existence of an index such that the property holds for the corresponding value in that range.

Set.range_iff_surjective.code: Set.range_iff_surjective.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → α} : range f = univ ↔ Surjective f

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.range_iff_surjective.description: The range of a function is equal to the universal set if and only if the function is surjective.

Function.Surjective.range_eq.code: Function.Surjective.range_eq.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → α} : Surjective f → range f = univ

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Function.Surjective.range_eq.description: If a function is surjective, then its range is equal to the universal set.

Set.image_univ.code: Set.image_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} : f '' univ = range f

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.image_univ.description: The image of the universal set under a function is equal to the range of that function.

Set.image_subset_range.code: Set.image_subset_range.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : f '' s ⊆ range f

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.image_subset_range.description: The image of any set under a function is a subset of the function's range.

Set.mem_range_of_mem_image.code:
Set.mem_range_of_mem_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) {x : β} (h : x ∈ f '' s) :

Set.exists_prod_set.description: The theorem states that there exists an element in the Cartesian product of two sets satisfying a property if and only if there exist elements in each of the sets that together satisfy that property.

Set.prod_empty.code: Set.prod_empty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} : s ×ˢ ∅ = ∅
Set.prod_empty.description: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of any set with an empty set results in an empty set.

Set.empty_prod.code: Set.empty_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {t : Set β} : ∅ ×ˢ t = ∅
Set.empty_prod.description: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of the empty set with any set is equal to the empty set.

Set.univ_prod_univ.code: Set.univ_prod_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} : univ ×ˢ univ = univ
Set.univ_prod_univ.description: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of two universal sets is equal to the universal set itself.

Set.univ_prod.code: Set.univ_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {t : Set β} : univ ×ˢ t = Prod.snd ⁻¹' t

explanatories.Prod.snd: The second element of a pair.

Set.univ_prod.description: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of a universal set with any set is equal to the preimage of that set under the projection onto the second component.

Set.prod_univ.code: Set.prod_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} : s ×ˢ univ = Prod.fst ⁻¹' s

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Prod.fst: The first element of a pair.

Set.prod_univ.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of any set with a universal set is equal to the preimage of that set under the projection onto the first component.

Set.singleton_prod.code: Set.singleton_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {t : Set β} {a : α} : {a} ×ˢ t = Prod.mk a '' t

explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This constructs a subtype from a value and a property that the value satisfies.

Set.singleton_prod.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of a singleton set containing one element and another set is equivalent to the image of that element under the projection function from the Cartesian product.

Set.prod_singleton.code: Set.prod_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {b : β} : s ×ˢ {b} = (fun a => (a, b)) '' s
Set.prod_singleton.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of a set with a singleton set is equivalent to the image of the original set under the function that pairs each element with the element from the singleton.

Set.singleton_prod_singleton.code: Set.singleton_prod_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {a : α} {b : β} : {a} ×ˢ {b} = {(a, b)}
Set.singleton_prod_singleton.description: The theorem indicates that the Cartesian product of single-element sets results in a set containing the ordered pair of their respective elements.

Set.union_prod.code: Set.union_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} {t : Set β} : (s₁ ∪ s₂) ×ˢ t = s₁ ×ˢ t ∪ s₂ ×ˢ t
Set.union_prod.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of the union of two sets with another set is equal to the union of the Cartesian products of each set with the same set.

Set.prod_union.code: Set.prod_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t₁ t₂ : Set β} : s ×ˢ (t₁ ∪ t₂) = s ×ˢ t₁ ∪ s ×ˢ t₂
Set.prod_union.description: The theorem establishes that the Cartesian product of a set with the union of two other sets is equal to the union of the Cartesian products of the first set with each of the other two sets.

Set.inter_prod.code: Set.inter_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} {t : Set β} : (s₁ ∩ s₂) ×ˢ t = s₁ ×ˢ t ∩ s₂ ×ˢ t
Set.inter_prod.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of the intersection of two sets with another set is equal to the intersection of the Cartesian products of each of the first two sets with the third set.

Set.prod_inter.code: Set.prod_inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t₁ t₂ : Set β} : s ×ˢ (t₁ ∩ t₂) = s ×ˢ t₁ ∩ s ×ˢ t₂
Set.prod_inter.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of a set with the intersection of two other sets is equal to the intersection of the Cartesian products of the first set with each of the two sets.

Set.prod_inter_prod.code:
Set.prod_inter_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} {t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  s₁ ×ˢ t₁ ∩ s₂ ×ˢ t₂ = (s₁ ∩ s₂) ×ˢ (t₁ ∩ t₂)
Set.prod_inter_prod.description: The theorem states that the intersection of the Cartesian products of two pairs of sets is equal to the Cartesian product of the intersections of the corresponding sets.

Set.disjoint_prod.code:
Set.disjoint_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} {t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  Disjoint (s₁ ×ˢ t₁) (s₂ ×ˢ t₂) ↔ Disjoint s₁ s₂ ∨ Disjoint t₁ t₂

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_prod.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian products of two sets are disjoint if and only if either the sets from the first component or the sets from the second component are disjoint.

Set.Disjoint.set_prod_left.code:
Set.Disjoint.set_prod_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s₁ s₂ : Set α} (hs : Disjoint s₁ s₂)
  (t₁ t₂ : Set β) : Disjoint (s₁ ×ˢ t₁) (s₂ ×ˢ t₂)
Set.Disjoint.set_prod_left.description: The theorem asserts that if two sets are disjoint, then their Cartesian products with any other sets will also be disjoint.

Set.Disjoint.set_prod_right.code:
Set.Disjoint.set_prod_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {t₁ t₂ : Set β} (ht : Disjoint t₁ t₂)
  (s₁ s₂ : Set α) : Disjoint (s₁ ×ˢ t₁) (s₂ ×ˢ t₂)
Set.Disjoint.set_prod_right.description: The theorem asserts that if two sets are disjoint, then the Cartesian products of each set with two other sets remain disjoint.

Set.insert_prod.code:
Set.insert_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {a : α} :
  insert a s ×ˢ t = Prod.mk a '' t ∪ s ×ˢ t

explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This constructs a subtype from a value and a property that the value satisfies.

Set.insert_prod.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of the insertion of an element into a set with another set is equal to the union of the image of that element paired with the other set and the Cartesian product of the original set with the other set.

Set.prod_insert.code:
Set.prod_insert.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {b : β} :
  s ×ˢ insert b t = (fun a => (a, b)) '' s ∪ s ×ˢ t

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.prod_insert.description: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of a set with the insertion of an element into another set is equal to the union of the set's image paired with the inserted element and the Cartesian product of the original set with the other set.

Set.prod_preimage_eq.code:
Set.prod_preimage_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4} {s : Set α}
  {t : Set β} {f : γ → α} {g : δ → β} : (f ⁻¹' s) ×ˢ (g ⁻¹' t) = (fun p => (f p.1, g p.2)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t
Set.prod_preimage_eq.description: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of the preimages of two sets under two functions is equal to the preimage of the Cartesian product of those two sets under the pair of functions applied to their respective elements.

Set.prod_preimage_left.code:
Set.prod_preimage_left.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set α} {t : Set β}
  {f : γ → α} : (f ⁻¹' s) ×ˢ t = (fun p => (f p.1, p.2)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t
Set.prod_preimage_left.description: The theorem states that the preimage of a set under a function, when taken with the Cartesian product of another set, can be expressed as the preimage of the Cartesian product of both sets with respect to a related function.

Set.prod_preimage_right.code:
Set.prod_preimage_right.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {δ : Type u_4} {s : Set α} {t : Set β}
  {g : δ → β} : s ×ˢ (g ⁻¹' t) = (fun p => (p.1, g p.2)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t
Set.prod_preimage_right.description: The theorem asserts that the preimage of a set under a function, when taken with the Cartesian product of another set, can be expressed as the preimage of the Cartesian product of both sets, considering the function applied to one component.

Set.preimage_prod_map_prod.code:
Set.preimage_prod_map_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4} (f : α → β)
  (g : γ → δ) (s : Set β) (t : Set δ) : Prod.map f g ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = (f ⁻¹' s) ×ˢ (g ⁻¹' t)

explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

Set.preimage_prod_map_prod.description: The theorem establishes that the preimage of the Cartesian product of two sets under a product of functions is equivalent to the Cartesian product of the preimages of each set under their respective functions.

Set.mk_preimage_prod.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} (f : γ → α)
  (g : γ → β) : (fun x => (f x, g x)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = f ⁻¹' s ∩ g ⁻¹' t
Set.mk_preimage_prod.description: The theorem establishes that the preimage of the Cartesian product formed by two functions is equivalent to the intersection of their respective preimages.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_left.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {b : β} (hb : b ∈ t) :
  (fun a => (a, b)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = s
Set.mk_preimage_prod_left.description: The theorem states that the preimage of the Cartesian product of a set with a constant element is equal to that set when the constant element belongs to the second set.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {a : α} (ha : a ∈ s) :
  Prod.mk a ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = t

explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This constructs a subtype from a value and a property that the value satisfies.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right.description: The theorem states that the preimage of a Cartesian product involving a fixed element from one set is simply equal to the other set when that element belongs to the specified subset.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_eq_empty.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_eq_empty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {b : β}
  (hb : b ∉ t) : (fun a => (a, b)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = ∅
Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_eq_empty.description: The theorem states that if an element is not in a set, the preimage of the Cartesian product formed by pairing elements with that element is empty.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_eq_empty.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_eq_empty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {a : α}
  (ha : a ∉ s) : Prod.mk a ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = ∅

explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This constructs a subtype from a value and a property that the value satisfies.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_eq_empty.description: The theorem establishes that if an element is not in a set, then the Cartesian product of the singleton containing that element with another set's preimage results in an empty set.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_eq_if.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_eq_if.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {b : β}
  [DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ t] : (fun a => (a, b)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = if b ∈ t then s else ∅

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_eq_if.description: The theorem establishes that the preimage of a function that pairs each element of one set with a fixed element from another set equals the original set if that element is in the second set, and is empty otherwise.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_eq_if.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_eq_if.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {a : α}
  [DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ s] : Prod.mk a ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = if a ∈ s then t else ∅

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.
explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This constructs a subtype from a value and a property that the value satisfies.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_eq_if.description: The theorem asserts that the preimage of the Cartesian product involving a specified element is equal to a set corresponding to whether that element is in another specified set.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_fn_eq_if.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_fn_eq_if.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set α} {t : Set β}
  {b : β} [DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ t] (f : γ → α) : (fun a => (f a, b)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = if b ∈ t then f ⁻¹' s else ∅

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_left_fn_eq_if.description: The theorem shows that the preimage of the Cartesian product of a function and a fixed element equals the preimage of the set if the element is in the target set, otherwise it is empty.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_fn_eq_if.code:
Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_fn_eq_if.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {δ : Type u_4} {s : Set α} {t : Set β}
  {a : α} [DecidablePred fun x => x ∈ s] (g : δ → β) : (fun b => (a, g b)) ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = if a ∈ s then g ⁻¹' t else ∅

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

Set.mk_preimage_prod_right_fn_eq_if.description: The theorem states that the preimage of a Cartesian product formed by a fixed element and a function is equal to a set that depends on whether the fixed element belongs to a specified set.

Set.preimage_swap_prod.code: Set.preimage_swap_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prod.swap ⁻¹' s ×ˢ t = t ×ˢ s

explanatories.Prod.swap: A function exists that exchanges the positions of the elements in a pair.

Set.preimage_swap_prod.description: The theorem establishes that the preimage of the Cartesian product of two sets under a function that swaps their order is equal to the Cartesian product of those sets with their positions reversed.

Set.image_swap_prod.code: Set.image_swap_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prod.swap '' s ×ˢ t = t ×ˢ s

explanatories.Prod.swap: A function exists that exchanges the positions of the elements in a pair.

Set.image_swap_prod.description: The theorem asserts that the image of the Cartesian product of two sets under a function that swaps their order is equivalent to the Cartesian product of those sets with their positions reversed.

Set.prod_image_image_eq.code:
Set.prod_image_image_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4} {s : Set α}
  {t : Set β} {m₁ : α → γ} {m₂ : β → δ} : (m₁ '' s) ×ˢ (m₂ '' t) = (fun p => (m₁ p.1, m₂ p.2)) '' s ×ˢ t
Set.prod_image_image_eq.description: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of the images of two sets under separate functions is equivalent to the image of the Cartesian product formed by those two sets under a combined mapping.

Set.prod_range_range_eq.code:
Set.prod_range_range_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4} {m₁ : α → γ}
  {m₂ : β → δ} : range m₁ ×ˢ range m₂ = range fun p => (m₁ p.1, m₂ p.2)

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.prod_range_range_eq.description: The theorem establishes that the Cartesian product of the ranges of two functions is equal to the range of a function that maps pairs from the first range to pairs formed by applying each function to their respective components.

Set.range_prod_map.code:
Set.range_prod_map.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4} {m₁ : α → γ}
  {m₂ : β → δ} : range (Prod.map m₁ m₂) = range m₁ ×ˢ range m₂

explanatories.Prod.map: A function is defined that transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

Set.range_prod_map.description: The theorem establishes that the range of the product of two functions is equal to the Cartesian product of their individual ranges.

Set.prod_range_univ_eq.code:
Set.prod_range_univ_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {m₁ : α → γ} :
  range m₁ ×ˢ univ = range fun p => (m₁ p.1, p.2)

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.prod_range_univ_eq.description: The theorem demonstrates that the Cartesian product of the range of a function and the universal set is equivalent to the range of a function that pairs each element of the range with every element of the second set.

Set.prod_univ_range_eq.code:
Set.prod_univ_range_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {δ : Type u_4} {m₂ : β → δ} :
  univ ×ˢ range m₂ = range fun p => (p.1, m₂ p.2)

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.prod_univ_range_eq.description: The theorem shows that the Cartesian product of the universal set and the range of a function is equivalent to the range of a function that pairs each element of the universal set with the corresponding value from the range.

Set.range_pair_subset.code:
Set.range_pair_subset.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (f : α → β) (g : α → γ) :
  (range fun x => (f x, g x)) ⊆ range f ×ˢ range g
Set.range_pair_subset.description: The theorem states that the range of a function that pairs outputs from two different functions is a subset of the Cartesian product of their respective ranges.

Set.Nonempty.prod.code:
Set.Nonempty.prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} :
  s.Nonempty → t.Nonempty → (s ×ˢ t).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.prod.description: The theorem asserts that if both sets are nonempty, then their Cartesian product is also nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.fst.code: Set.Nonempty.fst.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} : (s ×ˢ t).Nonempty → s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.fst.description: The theorem states that if the Cartesian product of two sets is nonempty, then the first set must also be nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.snd.code: Set.Nonempty.snd.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} : (s ×ˢ t).Nonempty → t.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.snd.description: The theorem asserts that if the Cartesian product of two sets is non-empty, then the second set must also be non-empty.

Set.prod_nonempty_iff.code:
Set.prod_nonempty_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} :
  (s ×ˢ t).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty ∧ t.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.prod_nonempty_iff.description: The theorem establishes that the Cartesian product of two sets is nonempty if and only if both individual sets are nonempty.

Set.prod_eq_empty_iff.code: Set.prod_eq_empty_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} : s ×ˢ t = ∅ ↔ s = ∅ ∨ t = ∅
Set.prod_eq_empty_iff.description: The theorem asserts that the Cartesian product of two sets is empty if and only if at least one of the sets is empty.

Set.prod_sub_preimage_iff.code:
Set.prod_sub_preimage_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set α} {t : Set β}
  {W : Set γ} {f : α × β → γ} : s ×ˢ t ⊆ f ⁻¹' W ↔ ∀ (a : α) (b : β), a ∈ s → b ∈ t → f (a, b) ∈ W
Set.prod_sub_preimage_iff.description: The theorem demonstrates that the Cartesian product of two sets is a subset of the preimage of another set under a function if and only if every pair of elements from the first two sets is mapped into the second set by that function.

Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod.code:
Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {f : α → β} {g : α → γ}
  {s : Set α} : (fun x => (f x, g x)) '' s ⊆ (f '' s) ×ˢ (g '' s)
Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod.description: The theorem asserts that the image of a set under a function that produces ordered pairs is a subset of the Cartesian product of the images of that set under each function.

Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod_left.code:
Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {b : β}
  (hb : b ∈ t) : (fun a => (a, b)) '' s ⊆ s ×ˢ t
Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod_left.description: The theorem asserts that the image of a set under a function that pairs each element with a fixed element from another set is a subset of the Cartesian product of the original set and the second set.

Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod_right.code:
Set.image_prod_mk_subset_prod_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {a : α}

Set.prod_subset_prod_iff.code:
Set.prod_subset_prod_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s s₁ : Set α} {t t₁ : Set β} :

A product set is included in a product set if and only factors are included, or a factor of the
first set is empty.
Set.prod_subset_prod_iff.description: The theorem indicates that the inclusion of one Cartesian product set in another is equivalent to the inclusion of their respective factors or the emptiness of at least one of the sets involved.

Set.prod_eq_prod_iff_of_nonempty.code:
Set.prod_eq_prod_iff_of_nonempty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s s₁ : Set α} {t t₁ : Set β}
  (h : (s ×ˢ t).Nonempty) : s ×ˢ t = s₁ ×ˢ t₁ ↔ s = s₁ ∧ t = t₁
Set.prod_eq_prod_iff_of_nonempty.description: The theorem states that if the Cartesian product of two sets is nonempty, then this product is equal to another product if and only if the individual sets involved in the products are equal.

Set.prod_eq_prod_iff.code:

Set.prod_eq_prod_iff.description: The theorem asserts that two Cartesian products are equal if and only if the respective sets are equal or at least one of the products is empty, along with the corresponding condition for the other product.

Set.prod_eq_iff_eq.code:

explanatories.Set.LeftInvOn.comp: The theorem establishes that if a function has a left inverse and another function also has a left inverse, then the composition of these inverses corresponds to the composition of the original functions on their respective sets.
explanatories.Set.RightInvOn.comp: The theorem states that if one function has a right inverse on a specific set and another function also has a right inverse on a separate set, then the composition of their right inverses will serve as a right inverse for the composition of the original functions over the appropriate set.

Set.InvOn.comp.description: The theorem states that if two pairs of functions are inverses on respective sets and the first function maps a set into a second set, then the composition of the inverses is also an inverse of the composition of the original functions between those sets.
