Set.iUnion₂_subset_iff.code:
Set.iUnion₂_subset_iff.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α}
  {t : Set α} : ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j ⊆ t ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), s i j ⊆ t
Set.iUnion₂_subset_iff.description: The union of sets defined by two indices is a subset of another set if and only if every individual set defined by the indices is a subset of that set.

Set.subset_iInter_iff.code:
Set.subset_iInter_iff.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s : Set α} {t : ι → Set α} :
  s ⊆ ⋂ i, t i ↔ ∀ (i : ι), s ⊆ t i
Set.subset_iInter_iff.description: A set is a subset of the intersection of other sets if and only if it is a subset of each individual set in that intersection.

Set.subset_iInter₂_iff.code:
Set.subset_iInter₂_iff.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : Set α}
  {t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} : s ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), s ⊆ t i j
Set.subset_iInter₂_iff.description: A set is contained in the intersection of a family of sets if and only if it is contained in each individual set of that family.

Set.subset_iUnion.code: Set.subset_iUnion.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : ι → Set β) (i : ι) : s i ⊆ ⋃ i, s i
Set.subset_iUnion.description: The set associated with a specific index is a subset of the union of sets corresponding to all indices.

Set.iInter_subset.code: Set.iInter_subset.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : ι → Set β) (i : ι) : ⋂ i, s i ⊆ s i
Set.iInter_subset.description: The intersection of a family of sets is a subset of any individual set in that family.

Set.subset_iUnion₂.code:
Set.subset_iUnion₂.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} (i : ι)
  (j : κ i) : s i j ⊆ ⋃ i', ⋃ j', s i' j'
Set.subset_iUnion₂.description: Any individual set defined by two indices is contained within the union of all sets defined by those indices.

Set.iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.iInter₂_subset.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} (i : ι)
  (j : κ i) : ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j ⊆ s i j
Set.iInter₂_subset.description: The intersection of sets formed by taking intersections over all indices is a subset of the set corresponding to a specific index and value.

Set.subset_iUnion_of_subset.code:
Set.subset_iUnion_of_subset.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s : Set α} {t : ι → Set α} (i : ι) (h : s ⊆ t i) :
  s ⊆ ⋃ i, t i
Set.subset_iUnion_of_subset.comment:
This rather trivial consequence of `subset_iUnion`is convenient with `apply`, and has `i`
explicit for this purpose.
Set.subset_iUnion_of_subset.description: If a set is a subset of another set indexed by an element, then it is also a subset of the union of all sets indexed by that element.

Set.iInter_subset_of_subset.code:
Set.iInter_subset_of_subset.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s : ι → Set α} {t : Set α} (i : ι) (h : s i ⊆ t) :
  ⋂ i, s i ⊆ t
Set.iInter_subset_of_subset.comment:
This rather trivial consequence of `iInter_subset`is convenient with `apply`, and has `i`
explicit for this purpose.
Set.iInter_subset_of_subset.description: The intersection of a family of sets is a subset of another set whenever each individual set in the family is contained within that other set.

Set.subset_iUnion₂_of_subset.code:
Set.subset_iUnion₂_of_subset.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : Set α}
  {t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} (i : ι) (j : κ i) (h : s ⊆ t i j) : s ⊆ ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j
Set.subset_iUnion₂_of_subset.comment:
This rather trivial consequence of `subset_iUnion₂` is convenient with `apply`, and has `i` and
`j` explicit for this purpose.
Set.subset_iUnion₂_of_subset.description: If a set is a subset of a set indexed by two elements, then it is also a subset of the union of all sets indexed by those elements.

Set.iInter₂_subset_of_subset.code:
Set.iInter₂_subset_of_subset.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7}
  {s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} {t : Set α} (i : ι) (j : κ i) (h : s i j ⊆ t) : ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j ⊆ t
Set.iInter₂_subset_of_subset.comment:
This rather trivial consequence of `iInter₂_subset` is convenient with `apply`, and has `i` and
`j` explicit for this purpose.
Set.iInter₂_subset_of_subset.description: The intersection of intersections of sets is a subset of any set if each individual set in the intersections is a subset of that set.

Set.iUnion_mono.code:
Set.iUnion_mono.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s t : ι → Set α} (h : ∀ (i : ι), s i ⊆ t i) :
  ⋃ i, s i ⊆ ⋃ i, t i
Set.iUnion_mono.description: The union of sets indexed by one collection is contained within the union of another collection of sets if each individual set in the first collection is a subset of the corresponding set in the second collection.

Set.iUnion₂_mono.code:
Set.iUnion₂_mono.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α}
  (h : ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), s i j ⊆ t i j) : ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j ⊆ ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j
Set.iUnion₂_mono.description: The union of unions of sets is a subset of another union of unions if every individual set in the first family is contained within the corresponding set in the second family.

Set.iInter_mono.code:
Set.iInter_mono.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s t : ι → Set α} (h : ∀ (i : ι), s i ⊆ t i) :
  ⋂ i, s i ⊆ ⋂ i, t i
Set.iInter_mono.description: The intersection of a family of sets is contained within another intersection if each individual set in the family is a subset of the corresponding set in the other family.

Set.iInter₂_mono.code:
Set.iInter₂_mono.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α}
  (h : ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), s i j ⊆ t i j) : ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j
Set.iInter₂_mono.description: If one family of sets is contained within another for every indexed element, then the intersection of all the sets in the first family is also contained within the intersection of all the sets in the second family.

Set.iUnion_mono'.code:
Set.iUnion_mono'.{u_1, u_4, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι₂ : Sort u_6} {s : ι → Set α} {t : ι₂ → Set α}
  (h : ∀ (i : ι), ∃ j, s i ⊆ t j) : ⋃ i, s i ⊆ ⋃ i, t i
Set.iUnion_mono'.description: If for every set in one collection there exists a set in another collection such that the first set is a subset of the corresponding second set, then the union of the first collection is a subset of the union of the second collection.

Set.iUnion₂_mono'.description: If a family of sets is shown to be contained within another family of sets for every indexed element, then the union of all sets in the first family is also contained within the union of all sets in the second family.

Set.iInter_mono'.code:
Set.iInter_mono'.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} {s : ι → Set α} {t : ι' → Set α}
  (h : ∀ (j : ι'), ∃ i, s i ⊆ t j) : ⋂ i, s i ⊆ ⋂ j, t j
Set.iInter_mono'.description: If every set in one family is contained within some set of another family, then the intersection of all sets from the first family is also contained within the intersection of all sets from the second family.

Set.iInter₂_mono'.description: The intersection of intersections of one family of sets is a subset of the intersection of intersections of another family if every set in the first family is contained within some set of the second family based on a mapping of indices.

Set.iUnion₂_subset_iUnion.code:
Set.iUnion₂_subset_iUnion.{u_1, u_4, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (κ : ι → Sort u_11) (s : ι → Set α) :
  ⋃ i, ⋃ x, s i ⊆ ⋃ i, s i
Set.iUnion₂_subset_iUnion.description: The union of sets indexed by a family of sets is contained within the union of those sets.

Set.iInter_subset_iInter₂.code:
Set.iInter_subset_iInter₂.{u_1, u_4, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (κ : ι → Sort u_11) (s : ι → Set α) :
  ⋂ i, s i ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ x, s i
Set.iInter_subset_iInter₂.description: The intersection of sets indexed by a family is contained within the intersection of all sets formed by the same family, where each set is further intersected with elements indexed by another set.

Set.iUnion_setOf.code: Set.iUnion_setOf.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (P : ι → α → Prop) : ⋃ i, {x | P i x} = {x | ∃ i, P i x}
Set.iUnion_setOf.description: The union of sets defined by a property for each index is equivalent to the set of elements that satisfy the property for some index.

Set.iInter_setOf.code: Set.iInter_setOf.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (P : ι → α → Prop) : ⋂ i, {x | P i x} = {x | ∀ (i : ι), P i x}
Set.iInter_setOf.description: The intersection of sets defined by a property for each index equals the set of elements that satisfy the property for all indices.

Set.iUnion_congr_of_surjective.code:
Set.iUnion_congr_of_surjective.{u_1, u_4, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι₂ : Sort u_6} {f : ι → Set α}
  {g : ι₂ → Set α} (h : ι → ι₂) (h1 : Surjective h) (h2 : ∀ (x : ι), g (h x) = f x) : ⋃ x, f x = ⋃ y, g y

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.iUnion_congr_of_surjective.description: The union of sets defined by a surjective mapping between two indices is preserved under the equivalence of those sets' images.

Set.iInter_congr_of_surjective.code:
Set.iInter_congr_of_surjective.{u_1, u_4, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι₂ : Sort u_6} {f : ι → Set α}
  {g : ι₂ → Set α} (h : ι → ι₂) (h1 : Surjective h) (h2 : ∀ (x : ι), g (h x) = f x) : ⋂ x, f x = ⋂ y, g y

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.

Set.iInter_congr_of_surjective.description: The intersection of two families of sets is equal when one family is related to the other through a surjective function and the sets correspond under that function.

Set.iUnion_congr.code:
Set.iUnion_congr.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s t : ι → Set α} (h : ∀ (i : ι), s i = t i) :
  ⋃ i, s i = ⋃ i, t i
Set.iUnion_congr.description: If two families of sets are equal at each corresponding index, then their unions are also equal.

Set.iInter_congr.code:
Set.iInter_congr.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s t : ι → Set α} (h : ∀ (i : ι), s i = t i) :
  ⋂ i, s i = ⋂ i, t i
Set.iInter_congr.description: If two families of sets are equal for each indexed element, then the intersection of all the sets in the first family is equal to the intersection of all the sets in the second family.

Set.iUnion₂_congr.code:
Set.iUnion₂_congr.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α}
  (h : ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), s i j = t i j) : ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j
Set.iUnion₂_congr.description: The union of unions of two families of sets is equal if every corresponding set in the two families is equal.

Set.iInter₂_congr.code:
Set.iInter₂_congr.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α}
  (h : ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), s i j = t i j) : ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j = ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j
Set.iInter₂_congr.description: The intersection of sets defined by two equivalent families is equal to the intersection of sets defined by the second family if each corresponding pair of sets is equal.

Set.iUnion_const.code: Set.iUnion_const.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] (s : Set β) : ⋃ x, s = s

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.iUnion_const.description: If the indexing set is non-empty, then the union of a constant set over that indexing set is equal to the constant set itself.

Set.iInter_const.code: Set.iInter_const.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] (s : Set β) : ⋂ x, s = s

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.iInter_const.description: The intersection of a constant set across a nonempty indexing set is equal to that constant set itself.

Set.iUnion_eq_const.code:
Set.iUnion_eq_const.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] {f : ι → Set α} {s : Set α}
  (hf : ∀ (i : ι), f i = s) : ⋃ i, f i = s

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.iUnion_eq_const.description: The union of sets indexed by a nonempty index set is equal to a specified set if all indexed sets are equal to that set.

Set.iInter_eq_const.code:
Set.iInter_eq_const.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] {f : ι → Set α} {s : Set α}
  (hf : ∀ (i : ι), f i = s) : ⋂ i, f i = s

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.iInter_eq_const.description: The intersection of a family of sets is equal to a specific set when every set in the family is identical to that specific set.

Set.compl_iUnion.code: Set.compl_iUnion.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : ι → Set β) : (⋃ i, s i)ᶜ = ⋂ i, (s i)ᶜ
Set.compl_iUnion.description: The complement of the union of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the complements of each set in that family.

Set.compl_iUnion₂.code:
Set.compl_iUnion₂.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) :
  (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j)ᶜ = ⋂ i, ⋂ j, (s i j)ᶜ
Set.compl_iUnion₂.description: The complement of the union of unions of sets is equal to the intersection of the complements of those sets.

Set.compl_iInter.code: Set.compl_iInter.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : ι → Set β) : (⋂ i, s i)ᶜ = ⋃ i, (s i)ᶜ
Set.compl_iInter.description: The complement of the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the union of the complements of each set in that family.

Set.compl_iInter₂.code:
Set.compl_iInter₂.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) :
  (⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j)ᶜ = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, (s i j)ᶜ
Set.compl_iInter₂.description: The complement of the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the union of the complements of each set in that family.

Set.iUnion_eq_compl_iInter_compl.code: Set.iUnion_eq_compl_iInter_compl.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : ι → Set β) : ⋃ i, s i = (⋂ i, (s i)ᶜ)ᶜ
Set.iUnion_eq_compl_iInter_compl.description: The union of a family of sets is equal to the complement of the intersection of their complements.

Set.iInter_eq_compl_iUnion_compl.code: Set.iInter_eq_compl_iUnion_compl.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : ι → Set β) : ⋂ i, s i = (⋃ i, (s i)ᶜ)ᶜ
Set.iInter_eq_compl_iUnion_compl.description: The intersection of sets is equal to the complement of the union of their complements.

Set.inter_iUnion.code: Set.inter_iUnion.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) : s ∩ ⋃ i, t i = ⋃ i, s ∩ t i
Set.inter_iUnion.description: The intersection of a set with the union of a family of sets equals the union of the intersections of that set with each individual set from the family.

Set.iUnion_inter.code: Set.iUnion_inter.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) : (⋃ i, t i) ∩ s = ⋃ i, t i ∩ s
Set.iUnion_inter.description: The intersection of a set with a union of indexed sets equals the union of the intersections of those indexed sets with the original set.

Set.iUnion_union_distrib.code:
Set.iUnion_union_distrib.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s t : ι → Set β) :
  ⋃ i, s i ∪ t i = (⋃ i, s i) ∪ ⋃ i, t i
Set.iUnion_union_distrib.description: The union of the indexed union of two sets is equal to the union of their individual indexed unions.

Set.iInter_inter_distrib.code:
Set.iInter_inter_distrib.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s t : ι → Set β) :
  ⋂ i, s i ∩ t i = (⋂ i, s i) ∩ ⋂ i, t i
Set.iInter_inter_distrib.description: The intersection of indexed sets is equal to the intersection of their individual intersections.

Set.union_iUnion.code:
Set.union_iUnion.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) :
  s ∪ ⋃ i, t i = ⋃ i, s ∪ t i

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.union_iUnion.description: The union of a set with the union of a family of sets equals the union of the set with each individual set in the family.

Set.iUnion_union.code:
Set.iUnion_union.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) :
  (⋃ i, t i) ∪ s = ⋃ i, t i ∪ s

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.iUnion_union.description: The union of the supremum of a family of sets with another set is equivalent to the supremum of the union of that family of sets with the other set.

Set.inter_iInter.code:
Set.inter_iInter.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) :
  s ∩ ⋂ i, t i = ⋂ i, s ∩ t i

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.inter_iInter.description: The intersection of a set with the intersection of a family of sets is equivalent to the intersection of that set with each individual set in the family, uniformly taken.

Set.iInter_inter.code:
Set.iInter_inter.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) :
  (⋂ i, t i) ∩ s = ⋂ i, t i ∩ s

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.iInter_inter.description: The intersection of a family of sets alongside an additional set is equal to the intersection of the family with that set taken separately.

Set.union_iInter.code: Set.union_iInter.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) : s ∪ ⋂ i, t i = ⋂ i, s ∪ t i
Set.union_iInter.description: The union of a set with the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the union of the set with each individual set in that family.

Set.iInter_union.code: Set.iInter_union.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : ι → Set β) (t : Set β) : (⋂ i, s i) ∪ t = ⋂ i, s i ∪ t
Set.iInter_union.description: The union of a set with the intersection of a collection of sets is equal to the intersection of the same collection of sets with the added set.

Set.iUnion_diff.code: Set.iUnion_diff.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) : (⋃ i, t i) \ s = ⋃ i, t i \ s
Set.iUnion_diff.description: The difference between the union of a family of sets and another set is equal to the union of the differences of each set in the family with that other set.

Set.diff_iUnion.code:
Set.diff_iUnion.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} [Nonempty ι] (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) :
  s \ ⋃ i, t i = ⋂ i, s \ t i

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.diff_iUnion.description: The difference between a set and the union of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the differences of the set with each individual set in that family.

Set.diff_iInter.code: Set.diff_iInter.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) : s \ ⋂ i, t i = ⋃ i, s \ t i
Set.diff_iInter.description: The difference between a set and the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the union of the differences between the set and each individual set in the family.

Set.iUnion_inter_subset.code:
Set.iUnion_inter_subset.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Sort u_11} {α : Type u_12} {s t : ι → Set α} :
  ⋃ i, s i ∩ t i ⊆ (⋃ i, s i) ∩ ⋃ i, t i
Set.iUnion_inter_subset.description: The union of the intersections of two collections of sets is a subset of the intersection of their respective unions.

Set.iUnion_inter_of_monotone.code:
Set.iUnion_inter_of_monotone.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Type u_11} {α : Type u_12} [Preorder ι]
  [IsDirected ι fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1] {s t : ι → Set α} (hs : Monotone s) (ht : Monotone t) :
  ⋃ i, s i ∩ t i = (⋃ i, s i) ∩ ⋃ i, t i

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.
explanatories.Directed: A family of elements is considered directed with respect to a given relation if there exists an element that is greater than or equal to every pair in the family.

Set.iUnion_inter_of_monotone.description: The union of the intersections of two monotone families of sets is equal to the intersection of their individual unions.

Set.iUnion_inter_of_antitone.code:
Set.iUnion_inter_of_antitone.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Type u_11} {α : Type u_12} [Preorder ι]
  [IsDirected ι (swap fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1)] {s t : ι → Set α} (hs : Antitone s) (ht : Antitone t) :
  ⋃ i, s i ∩ t i = (⋃ i, s i) ∩ ⋃ i, t i

explanatories.Function.swap: This definition indicates the absence of any specified content or structure within the provided context.
explanatories.Antitone: A function is considered antitone if it reverses the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.
explanatories.Directed: A family of elements is considered directed with respect to a given relation if there exists an element that is greater than or equal to every pair in the family.

Set.iUnion_inter_of_antitone.description: The union of the intersections of two antitone families of sets equals the intersection of the unions of those two families.

Set.iInter_union_of_monotone.code:
Set.iInter_union_of_monotone.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Type u_11} {α : Type u_12} [Preorder ι]
  [IsDirected ι (swap fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1)] {s t : ι → Set α} (hs : Monotone s) (ht : Monotone t) :
  ⋂ i, s i ∪ t i = (⋂ i, s i) ∪ ⋂ i, t i

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.
explanatories.Function.swap: This definition indicates the absence of any specified content or structure within the provided context.
explanatories.Directed: A family of elements is considered directed with respect to a given relation if there exists an element that is greater than or equal to every pair in the family.

Set.iInter_union_of_monotone.description: The intersection of the unions of two monotone families of sets is equal to the union of the intersections of each family of sets.

Set.iInter_union_of_antitone.code:
Set.iInter_union_of_antitone.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Type u_11} {α : Type u_12} [Preorder ι]
  [IsDirected ι fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1] {s t : ι → Set α} (hs : Antitone s) (ht : Antitone t) :
  ⋂ i, s i ∪ t i = (⋂ i, s i) ∪ ⋂ i, t i

explanatories.Antitone: A function is considered antitone if it reverses the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.
explanatories.Directed: A family of elements is considered directed with respect to a given relation if there exists an element that is greater than or equal to every pair in the family.

Set.iInter_union_of_antitone.description: The intersection of the unions of two antitone families of sets is equal to the union of their individual intersections.

Set.iUnion_iInter_subset.code:
Set.iUnion_iInter_subset.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} {s : ι → ι' → Set α} :
  ⋃ j, ⋂ i, s i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋃ j, s i j
Set.iUnion_iInter_subset.comment: An equality version of this lemma is `iUnion_iInter_of_monotone` in `Data.Set.Finite`.
Set.iUnion_iInter_subset.description: The union of intersections of sets indexed by one variable is a subset of the intersection of unions of the same sets indexed by another variable.

Set.iUnion_option.code:
Set.iUnion_option.{u_1, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_11} (s : Option ι → Set α) :
  ⋃ o, s o = s none ∪ ⋃ i, s (some i)

explanatories.Nonempty.some: A nonempty type guarantees the existence of an element that can be extracted from it.
explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.

Set.iUnion_option.description: The union of sets indexed by an option type is equal to the union of the set corresponding to the absence of a value combined with the union of sets for all present values.

Set.iInter_option.code:
Set.iInter_option.{u_1, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_11} (s : Option ι → Set α) :
  ⋂ o, s o = s none ∩ ⋂ i, s (some i)

explanatories.Nonempty.some: A nonempty type guarantees the existence of an element that can be extracted from it.
explanatories.Option.none: The representation of an absence of value in an option type is denoted by "none."
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.

Set.iInter_option.description: The intersection of a set defined by an option is equal to the intersection of the set for the "none" case combined with the intersection of the set for all "some" cases.

Set.iUnion_dite.code:
Set.iUnion_dite.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (f : (i : ι) → p i → Set α)
  (g : (i : ι) → ¬p i → Set α) :
  (⋃ i, if h : p i then f i h else g i h) = (⋃ i, ⋃ (h : p i), f i h) ∪ ⋃ i, ⋃ (h : ¬p i), g i h

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

Set.iUnion_dite.description: The union of sets constructed by a branching condition based on a predicate is equal to the union of sets where the predicate holds combined with the union of sets where the predicate does not hold.

Set.iUnion_ite.code:
Set.iUnion_ite.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (f g : ι → Set α) :
  (⋃ i, if p i then f i else g i) = (⋃ i, ⋃ (_ : p i), f i) ∪ ⋃ i, ⋃ (_ : ¬p i), g i

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

Set.iUnion_ite.description: The union of two sets determined by a condition can be expressed as the union of the result for the true cases combined with the union of the result for the false cases.

Set.iInter_dite.code:
Set.iInter_dite.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (f : (i : ι) → p i → Set α)
  (g : (i : ι) → ¬p i → Set α) :
  (⋂ i, if h : p i then f i h else g i h) = (⋂ i, ⋂ (h : p i), f i h) ∩ ⋂ i, ⋂ (h : ¬p i), g i h

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

Set.iInter_dite.description: The intersection of a family of sets defined by a dependent condition can be expressed as the intersection of the sets corresponding to true conditions combined with the intersection of sets corresponding to false conditions.

Set.iInter_ite.code:
Set.iInter_ite.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} (p : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (f g : ι → Set α) :
  (⋂ i, if p i then f i else g i) = (⋂ i, ⋂ (_ : p i), f i) ∩ ⋂ i, ⋂ (_ : ¬p i), g i

explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a type of logical statement for which it can be determined whether the statement is true or false.

Set.iInter_ite.description: The intersection of a family of sets formed by a conditional function is equal to the intersection of the sets where the condition holds and the intersection of the sets where the condition does not hold.

Set.image_projection_prod.code:
Set.image_projection_prod.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Type u_11} {α : ι → Type u_12} {v : (i : ι) → Set (α i)}
  (hv : (univ.pi v).Nonempty) (i : ι) : (fun x => x i) '' ⋂ k, (fun x => x k) ⁻¹' v k = v i

explanatories.Set.pi: The set of dependent functions can be defined for a given index set and a family of sets, where each function's values belong to the corresponding set whenever the index is part of the specified set.

Set.image_projection_prod.description: The image of the projection from a non-empty product of sets to a specific index set equals the original set at that index.

Set.iInter_false.code: Set.iInter_false.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : False → Set α} : iInter s = univ
Set.iInter_false.description: The intersection of sets defined by a proposition that is always false is equivalent to the universal set.

Set.iUnion_false.code: Set.iUnion_false.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : False → Set α} : iUnion s = ∅
Set.iUnion_false.description: The indexed union of a family of sets that depend on a false condition is empty.

Set.iInter_true.code: Set.iInter_true.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : True → Set α} : iInter s = s trivial

explanatories.trivial: This theorem provides a proof that a trivial proposition affirming the truth of the statement "True" is indeed true.

Set.iInter_true.description: The intersection of sets defined by a constant truth value is equivalent to the set corresponding to that truth value.

Set.iUnion_true.code: Set.iUnion_true.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : True → Set α} : iUnion s = s trivial

explanatories.trivial: This theorem provides a proof that a trivial proposition affirming the truth of the statement "True" is indeed true.

Set.iUnion_true.description: The union of a family of sets indexed by a truth value is equal to the set corresponding to the true value of that index.

Set.iInter_exists.code:
Set.iInter_exists.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {p : ι → Prop} {f : Exists p → Set α} :
  ⋂ (x : Exists p), f x = ⋂ i, ⋂ (h : p i), f ⋯
Set.iInter_exists.description: The intersection over a family of sets defined by a property is equal to the intersection over the elements satisfying that property.

Set.iUnion_exists.code:
Set.iUnion_exists.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {p : ι → Prop} {f : Exists p → Set α} :
  ⋃ (x : Exists p), f x = ⋃ i, ⋃ (h : p i), f ⋯
Set.iUnion_exists.description: The union of the images of a set under an existential quantifier is equivalent to the union of the images over indices satisfying a given property.

Set.iUnion_empty.code: Set.iUnion_empty.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} : ⋃ x, ∅ = ∅
Set.iUnion_empty.description: The union of an empty family of sets is the empty set.

Set.iInter_univ.code: Set.iInter_univ.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} : ⋂ x, univ = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.iInter_univ.description: The intersection of a family of sets that are all equal to the universal set is equal to the universal set itself.

Set.iUnion_eq_empty.code: Set.iUnion_eq_empty.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s : ι → Set α} : ⋃ i, s i = ∅ ↔ ∀ (i : ι), s i = ∅
Set.iUnion_eq_empty.description: The union of a collection of sets is empty if and only if each individual set in that collection is empty.

Set.iInter_eq_univ.code: Set.iInter_eq_univ.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s : ι → Set α} : ⋂ i, s i = univ ↔ ∀ (i : ι), s i = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.iInter_eq_univ.description: The intersection of a collection of sets is equal to the universal set if and only if every individual set in the collection is the universal set.

Set.nonempty_iUnion.code: Set.nonempty_iUnion.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {s : ι → Set α} : (⋃ i, s i).Nonempty ↔ ∃ i, (s i).Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.nonempty_iUnion.description: The union of a family of sets is non-empty if and only if at least one of those sets is non-empty.

Set.nonempty_biUnion.code:
Set.nonempty_biUnion.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {t : Set α} {s : α → Set β} :
  (⋃ i ∈ t, s i).Nonempty ↔ ∃ i ∈ t, (s i).Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.nonempty_biUnion.description: The union of sets indexed by a collection is non-empty if and only if there exists at least one index from the collection for which the corresponding set is non-empty.

Set.iUnion_nonempty_index.code:
Set.iUnion_nonempty_index.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : s.Nonempty → Set β) :
  ⋃ (h : s.Nonempty), t h = ⋃ x, ⋃ (h : x ∈ s), t ⋯

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.iUnion_nonempty_index.description: The union over a non-empty indexed set is equal to the union of the images of that set, given the appropriate conditions on the maps involved.

Set.iInter_iInter_eq_left.code:
Set.iInter_iInter_eq_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {s : (x : β) → x = b → Set α} :
  ⋂ x, ⋂ (h : x = b), s x h = s b ⋯
Set.iInter_iInter_eq_left.description: The intersection of sets defined by a variable and a condition that is true for that variable is equal to the set defined by that variable with the condition applied to it.

Set.iInter_iInter_eq_right.code:
Set.iInter_iInter_eq_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {s : (x : β) → b = x → Set α} :
  ⋂ x, ⋂ (h : b = x), s x h = s b ⋯
Set.iInter_iInter_eq_right.description: The intersection of indexed sets over a variable and the corresponding equality conditions reduces to the set defined at that particular variable.

Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_left.code:
Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {s : (x : β) → x = b → Set α} :
  ⋃ x, ⋃ (h : x = b), s x h = s b ⋯
Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_left.description: The union of sets defined by a condition on an element being equal to a specific value is equal to the corresponding set defined at that value.

Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_right.code:
Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {s : (x : β) → b = x → Set α} :
  ⋃ x, ⋃ (h : b = x), s x h = s b ⋯
Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_right.description: The union over a variable of unions indexed by equalities results in the original set evaluated at the specific value corresponding to that equality.

Set.iInter_or.code:
Set.iInter_or.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {p q : Prop} (s : p ∨ q → Set α) :
  ⋂ (h : p ∨ q), s h = (⋂ (h : p), s ⋯) ∩ ⋂ (h : q), s ⋯
Set.iInter_or.description: The intersection of sets defined by a disjunction can be expressed as the intersection of the sets corresponding to each individual case of the disjunction.

Set.iUnion_or.code:
Set.iUnion_or.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {p q : Prop} (s : p ∨ q → Set α) :
  ⋃ (h : p ∨ q), s h = (⋃ (i : p), s ⋯) ∪ ⋃ (j : q), s ⋯
Set.iUnion_or.description: The union of sets indexed by a disjunction of propositions corresponds to the union of the sets indexed separately by each proposition.

Set.iUnion_and.code: Set.iUnion_and.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {p q : Prop} (s : p ∧ q → Set α) : ⋃ (h : p ∧ q), s h = ⋃ (hp : p), ⋃ (hq : q), s ⋯
Set.iUnion_and.description: The union of sets defined by a conjunction of two propositions can be expressed as the union of sets defined separately by each proposition.

Set.iInter_and.code: Set.iInter_and.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {p q : Prop} (s : p ∧ q → Set α) : ⋂ (h : p ∧ q), s h = ⋂ (hp : p), ⋂ (hq : q), s ⋯
Set.iInter_and.description: The intersection over a conjunction of two propositions applied to a set function equals the intersection of the individual intersections over each proposition.

Set.iUnion_comm.code:
Set.iUnion_comm.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} (s : ι → ι' → Set α) :
  ⋃ i, ⋃ i', s i i' = ⋃ i', ⋃ i, s i i'
Set.iUnion_comm.description: The order of taking unions over two indexed families of sets can be interchanged without affecting the result.

Set.iInter_comm.code:
Set.iInter_comm.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} (s : ι → ι' → Set α) :
  ⋂ i, ⋂ i', s i i' = ⋂ i', ⋂ i, s i i'
Set.iInter_comm.description: The order of intersection can be swapped without changing the resulting set when intersecting a family of sets indexed by two variables.

Set.iUnion₂_comm.description: The union of sets generated by two pairs of indices can be reordered without changing the overall set.

Set.iInter₂_comm.description: The order of intersections across multiple indexed sets does not affect the result, meaning they can be rearranged freely.

Set.biUnion_and.code:
Set.biUnion_and.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} (p : ι → Prop) (q : ι → ι' → Prop)
  (s : (x : ι) → (y : ι') → p x ∧ q x y → Set α) :
  ⋃ x, ⋃ y, ⋃ (h : p x ∧ q x y), s x y h = ⋃ x, ⋃ (hx : p x), ⋃ y, ⋃ (hy : q x y), s x y ⋯
Set.biUnion_and.description: The double union over pairs of indices satisfying two properties is interchangeable with performing the unions independently over each property before combining the results.

Set.biUnion_and'.code:
Set.biUnion_and'.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} (p : ι' → Prop) (q : ι → ι' → Prop)
  (s : (x : ι) → (y : ι') → p y ∧ q x y → Set α) :
  ⋃ x, ⋃ y, ⋃ (h : p y ∧ q x y), s x y h = ⋃ y, ⋃ (hy : p y), ⋃ x, ⋃ (hx : q x y), s x y ⋯
Set.biUnion_and'.description: The iterated union of sets defined by two properties and their dependencies is equivalent to restructuring the order of the unions while maintaining the same conditions.

Set.biInter_and.code:
Set.biInter_and.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} (p : ι → Prop) (q : ι → ι' → Prop)
  (s : (x : ι) → (y : ι') → p x ∧ q x y → Set α) :
  ⋂ x, ⋂ y, ⋂ (h : p x ∧ q x y), s x y h = ⋂ x, ⋂ (hx : p x), ⋂ y, ⋂ (hy : q x y), s x y ⋯
Set.biInter_and.description: The intersection of sets defined by a conjunction of properties corresponds to an intersection defined by separating the properties into individual conditions applied to the sets.

Set.biInter_and'.code:
Set.biInter_and'.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι' : Sort u_5} (p : ι' → Prop) (q : ι → ι' → Prop)
  (s : (x : ι) → (y : ι') → p y ∧ q x y → Set α) :
  ⋂ x, ⋂ y, ⋂ (h : p y ∧ q x y), s x y h = ⋂ y, ⋂ (hy : p y), ⋂ x, ⋂ (hx : q x y), s x y ⋯
Set.biInter_and'.description: The intersection of sets defined by a pair of properties can be expressed in two different ways that respect the order of quantifying over the parameters defining those properties.

Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_or_left.code:
Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_or_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {p : β → Prop}
  {s : (x : β) → x = b ∨ p x → Set α} : ⋃ x, ⋃ (h : x = b ∨ p x), s x h = s b ⋯ ∪ ⋃ x, ⋃ (h : p x), s x ⋯
Set.iUnion_iUnion_eq_or_left.description: The union of a family of sets indexed by an element or a property of elements can be broken down into the union of contributions from a specific element and the union of contributions from elements satisfying a property.

Set.iInter_iInter_eq_or_left.code:
Set.iInter_iInter_eq_or_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {b : β} {p : β → Prop}
  {s : (x : β) → x = b ∨ p x → Set α} : ⋂ x, ⋂ (h : x = b ∨ p x), s x h = s b ⋯ ∩ ⋂ x, ⋂ (h : p x), s x ⋯
Set.iInter_iInter_eq_or_left.description: The intersection of the family of intersections indexed by a condition is equal to the intersection of the set evaluated at a specific element combined with the intersections that satisfy another condition.

Set.mem_biUnion.code:
Set.mem_biUnion.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : α → Set β} {x : α} {y : β} (xs : x ∈ s)
  (ytx : y ∈ t x) : y ∈ ⋃ x ∈ s, t x
Set.mem_biUnion.description: An element belongs to the union of sets generated by a function if it belongs to the original set and is an element of the set assigned to that element by the function.

Set.mem_biInter.code:
Set.mem_biInter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : α → Set β} {y : β} (h : ∀ x ∈ s, y ∈ t x) :
  y ∈ ⋂ x ∈ s, t x
Set.mem_biInter.description: If an element belongs to every set in a collection indexed by members of another set, it is included in the intersection of those sets.

Set.subset_biUnion_of_mem.code:
Set.subset_biUnion_of_mem.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {u : α → Set β} {x : α} (xs : x ∈ s) :
  u x ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ s, u x
Set.subset_biUnion_of_mem.description: If an element belongs to a set, then the set generated by that element is contained within the union of sets generated by all elements in the original set.

Set.biInter_subset_of_mem.code:
Set.biInter_subset_of_mem.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : α → Set β} {x : α} (xs : x ∈ s) :
  ⋂ x ∈ s, t x ⊆ t x
Set.biInter_subset_of_mem.description: The intersection of sets generated by a function over a specific set is contained within the set generated by the function at any given point within that specific set.

Set.biUnion_subset_biUnion_left.code:
Set.biUnion_subset_biUnion_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s s' : Set α} {t : α → Set β} (h : s ⊆ s') :
  ⋃ x ∈ s, t x ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ s', t x
Set.biUnion_subset_biUnion_left.description: The union of sets indexed by a subset is contained within the union of sets indexed by the larger set.

Set.biInter_subset_biInter_left.code:
Set.biInter_subset_biInter_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s s' : Set α} {t : α → Set β} (h : s' ⊆ s) :
  ⋂ x ∈ s, t x ⊆ ⋂ x ∈ s', t x
Set.biInter_subset_biInter_left.description: The intersection of the sets defined by a function over a subset is contained within the intersection of the sets defined by the same function over a larger set if the subset is included in the larger set.

Set.biUnion_mono.code:
Set.biUnion_mono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s s' : Set α} {t t' : α → Set β} (hs : s' ⊆ s)
  (h : ∀ x ∈ s, t x ⊆ t' x) : ⋃ x ∈ s', t x ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ s, t' x
Set.biUnion_mono.description: If one set is a subset of another set and a family of sets is contained within another family for every element of the first set, then the union of the first family over the first set is a subset of the union of the second family over the second set.

Set.biInter_mono.code:
Set.biInter_mono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s s' : Set α} {t t' : α → Set β} (hs : s ⊆ s')
  (h : ∀ x ∈ s, t x ⊆ t' x) : ⋂ x ∈ s', t x ⊆ ⋂ x ∈ s, t' x
Set.biInter_mono.description: If one set is a subset of another and for each element in the first set the corresponding sets satisfy a certain inclusion property, then the intersection of the images defined by the second sets is contained within the intersection of the images defined by the first sets.

Set.biUnion_eq_iUnion.code:
Set.biUnion_eq_iUnion.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : (x : α) → x ∈ s → Set β) :
  ⋃ x, ⋃ (h : x ∈ s), t x h = ⋃ x, t ↑x ⋯
Set.biUnion_eq_iUnion.description: The iterated union over a set and its dependencies is equivalent to the union over the set treated as individual elements while preserving the same structure.

Set.biInter_eq_iInter.code:
Set.biInter_eq_iInter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : (x : α) → x ∈ s → Set β) :
  ⋂ x, ⋂ (h : x ∈ s), t x h = ⋂ x, t ↑x ⋯
Set.biInter_eq_iInter.description: The intersection over a set and a function defined on its elements is equivalent to the intersection of the function evaluated at each element of the set.

Set.iUnion_subtype.code:
Set.iUnion_subtype.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (p : α → Prop) (s : { x // p x } → Set β) :
  ⋃ x, s x = ⋃ x, ⋃ (hx : p x), s ⟨x, hx⟩
Set.iUnion_subtype.description: The union of a function defined on a subtype can be expressed as the union of that function over the entire underlying set, taking into account the property that defines the subtype.

Set.iInter_subtype.code:
Set.iInter_subtype.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (p : α → Prop) (s : { x // p x } → Set β) :
  ⋂ x, s x = ⋂ x, ⋂ (hx : p x), s ⟨x, hx⟩
Set.iInter_subtype.description: The intersection of sets defined by a property is equal to the intersection of the sets formed by elements that satisfy that property.

Set.biInter_empty.code: Set.biInter_empty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (u : α → Set β) : ⋂ x ∈ ∅, u x = univ
Set.biInter_empty.description: The intersection of sets defined by an empty index results in the universal set.

Set.biInter_univ.code: Set.biInter_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (u : α → Set β) : ⋂ x ∈ univ, u x = ⋂ x, u x

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.biInter_univ.description: The intersection of a family of sets indexed by the universal set is equal to the intersection of those sets without reference to the index.

Set.biUnion_self.code: Set.biUnion_self.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : ⋃ x ∈ s, s = s
Set.biUnion_self.description: The union of a set with itself, indexed by its elements, is equal to the original set.

Set.iUnion_nonempty_self.code: Set.iUnion_nonempty_self.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : ⋃ (_ : s.Nonempty), s = s
Set.iUnion_nonempty_self.description: The union of a non-empty set, based on its non-emptiness condition, is equal to the set itself.

Set.biInter_singleton.code: Set.biInter_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (a : α) (s : α → Set β) : ⋂ x ∈ {a}, s x = s a
Set.biInter_singleton.description: The intersection of a family of sets indexed by a singleton containing an element is equal to the set corresponding to that element.

Set.biInter_union.code:
Set.biInter_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s t : Set α) (u : α → Set β) :
  ⋂ x ∈ s ∪ t, u x = (⋂ x ∈ s, u x) ∩ ⋂ x ∈ t, u x
Set.biInter_union.description: The intersection of a function applied to elements from the union of two sets is equal to the intersection of the function applied to elements from each set individually.

Set.biInter_insert.code:
Set.biInter_insert.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (a : α) (s : Set α) (t : α → Set β) :
  ⋂ x ∈ insert a s, t x = t a ∩ ⋂ x ∈ s, t x

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.biInter_insert.description: The intersection of sets indexed by an element inserted into another set is equal to the intersection of the set containing that element and the intersection of the original set.

Set.biInter_pair.code: Set.biInter_pair.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (a b : α) (s : α → Set β) : ⋂ x ∈ {a, b}, s x = s a ∩ s b
Set.biInter_pair.description: The intersection of a family of sets evaluated at two specific elements is equal to the intersection of the sets obtained from each element individually.

Set.biInter_inter.code:
Set.biInter_inter.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Type u_11} {α : Type u_12} {s : Set ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : ⋂ i ∈ s, f i ∩ t = (⋂ i ∈ s, f i) ∩ t
Set.biInter_inter.description: The intersection of sets defined by a collection of functions can be expressed as the intersection of the individual sets produced by those functions along with another set.

Set.inter_biInter.code:
Set.inter_biInter.{u_11, u_12} {ι : Type u_11} {α : Type u_12} {s : Set ι} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : ⋂ i ∈ s, t ∩ f i = t ∩ ⋂ i ∈ s, f i
Set.inter_biInter.description: The intersection of a non-empty set with the intersection of multiple other sets can be expressed as the intersection of that set with each individual set defined by the elements of the original set.

Set.biUnion_empty.code: Set.biUnion_empty.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : α → Set β) : ⋃ x ∈ ∅, s x = ∅
Set.biUnion_empty.description: The union of sets from an empty indexing set is the empty set.

Set.biUnion_univ.code: Set.biUnion_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : α → Set β) : ⋃ x ∈ univ, s x = ⋃ x, s x

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.biUnion_univ.description: The union of sets formed by taking elements from the universal set is equivalent to the union of the sets defined by those elements directly.

Set.biUnion_singleton.code: Set.biUnion_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (a : α) (s : α → Set β) : ⋃ x ∈ {a}, s x = s a
Set.biUnion_singleton.description: The union of sets generated by a singleton element is equal to the set defined at that element.

Set.biUnion_of_singleton.code: Set.biUnion_of_singleton.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : ⋃ x ∈ s, {x} = s
Set.biUnion_of_singleton.description: The union over single-element sets formed from the elements of a set is equal to the set itself.

Set.biUnion_union.code:
Set.biUnion_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s t : Set α) (u : α → Set β) :
  ⋃ x ∈ s ∪ t, u x = (⋃ x ∈ s, u x) ∪ ⋃ x ∈ t, u x
Set.biUnion_union.description: The union of the images of a set under a function, when applied to the union of two sets, is equal to the union of the images of each set under that function.

Set.iUnion_coe_set.code:
Set.iUnion_coe_set.{u_11, u_12} {α : Type u_11} {β : Type u_12} (s : Set α) (f : ↑s → Set β) :
  ⋃ i, f i = ⋃ i, ⋃ (h : i ∈ s), f ⟨i, h⟩
Set.iUnion_coe_set.description: The union of sets indexed by elements of a set is equal to the union of sets indexed by those elements with the corresponding membership conditions explicitly included.

Set.iInter_coe_set.code:
Set.iInter_coe_set.{u_11, u_12} {α : Type u_11} {β : Type u_12} (s : Set α) (f : ↑s → Set β) :
  ⋂ i, f i = ⋂ i, ⋂ (h : i ∈ s), f ⟨i, h⟩
Set.iInter_coe_set.description: The intersection of a family of sets defined by a function over a set is equivalent to the intersection of the same family taken over the index elements that belong to that set.

Set.biUnion_insert.code:
Set.biUnion_insert.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (a : α) (s : Set α) (t : α → Set β) :
  ⋃ x ∈ insert a s, t x = t a ∪ ⋃ x ∈ s, t x

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.biUnion_insert.description: The union over a set formed by inserting an element into another set is equal to the union of the set's image at that element and the union of the images of the remaining elements in the original set.

Set.biUnion_pair.code: Set.biUnion_pair.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (a b : α) (s : α → Set β) : ⋃ x ∈ {a, b}, s x = s a ∪ s b
Set.biUnion_pair.description: The union of sets defined by two specific elements can be expressed as the union of the sets corresponding to each of those elements.

Set.inter_iUnion₂.code:
Set.inter_iUnion₂.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s ∩ ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s ∩ t i j
Set.inter_iUnion₂.description: The intersection of a set with the union of a family of unions can be expressed as the union of the intersections of the set with each individual union.

Set.iUnion₂_inter.code:
Set.iUnion₂_inter.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j) ∩ t = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j ∩ t
Set.iUnion₂_inter.description: The intersection of the union of a family of sets with another set equals the union of the intersections of each individual set in the family with that other set.

Set.union_iInter₂.code:
Set.union_iInter₂.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s ∪ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j = ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s ∪ t i j
Set.union_iInter₂.description: The union of a set with the intersection of a family of sets equals the intersection of the set with each individual set of that family.

Set.iInter₂_union.code:
Set.iInter₂_union.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : (⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j) ∪ t = ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j ∪ t
Set.iInter₂_union.description: The intersection of sets defined by two parameters can be combined with another set through a union operation without changing the order of the intersection.

Set.mem_sUnion_of_mem.code: Set.mem_sUnion_of_mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {x : α} {t : Set α} {S : Set (Set α)} (hx : x ∈ t) (ht : t ∈ S) : x ∈ ⋃₀ S
Set.mem_sUnion_of_mem.description: If an element belongs to a set that is a member of a collection of sets, then that element is also a member of the union of all sets in the collection.

Set.not_mem_of_not_mem_sUnion.code:
Set.not_mem_of_not_mem_sUnion.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {x : α} {t : Set α} {S : Set (Set α)} (hx : x ∉ ⋃₀ S) (ht : t ∈ S) :
  x ∉ t
Set.not_mem_of_not_mem_sUnion.description: If an element is not in the union of a collection of sets, then it is not in any of the individual sets within that collection.

Set.sInter_subset_of_mem.code: Set.sInter_subset_of_mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} {t : Set α} (tS : t ∈ S) : ⋂₀ S ⊆ t
Set.sInter_subset_of_mem.description: The intersection of sets contained in a given collection includes any set that is a member of that collection.

Set.subset_sUnion_of_mem.code: Set.subset_sUnion_of_mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} {t : Set α} (tS : t ∈ S) : t ⊆ ⋃₀ S
Set.subset_sUnion_of_mem.description: If a set belongs to a collection of sets, then it is a subset of their union.

Set.subset_sUnion_of_subset.code:
Set.subset_sUnion_of_subset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} (t : Set (Set α)) (u : Set α) (h₁ : s ⊆ u) (h₂ : u ∈ t) :
  s ⊆ ⋃₀ t
Set.subset_sUnion_of_subset.description: If a set is a subset of another set that belongs to a collection of sets, then it is also a subset of the union of all sets in that collection.

Set.sUnion_subset.code: Set.sUnion_subset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} {t : Set α} (h : ∀ t' ∈ S, t' ⊆ t) : ⋃₀ S ⊆ t
Set.sUnion_subset.description: The union of all sets contained in a collection of sets is also contained within another set if each individual set in the collection is contained within that set.

Set.sUnion_subset_iff.code: Set.sUnion_subset_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set (Set α)} {t : Set α} : ⋃₀ s ⊆ t ↔ ∀ t' ∈ s, t' ⊆ t
Set.sUnion_subset_iff.description: The union of a collection of sets is a subset of another set if and only if each set in the collection is a subset of that other set.

Set.subset_sInter.code: Set.subset_sInter.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} {t : Set α} (h : ∀ t' ∈ S, t ⊆ t') : t ⊆ ⋂₀ S
Set.subset_sInter.description: A set is a subset of the intersection of a collection of sets if it is a subset of each set within that collection.

Set.subset_sInter_iff.code: Set.subset_sInter_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} {t : Set α} : t ⊆ ⋂₀ S ↔ ∀ t' ∈ S, t ⊆ t'
Set.subset_sInter_iff.description: A set is a subset of the intersection of a collection of sets if and only if it is a subset of each set in that collection.

Set.sUnion_subset_sUnion.code: Set.sUnion_subset_sUnion.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S T : Set (Set α)} (h : S ⊆ T) : ⋃₀ S ⊆ ⋃₀ T
Set.sUnion_subset_sUnion.description: If one collection of sets is contained within another collection of sets, then the union of the sets from the first collection is also contained within the union of the sets from the second collection.

Set.sInter_subset_sInter.code: Set.sInter_subset_sInter.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S T : Set (Set α)} (h : S ⊆ T) : ⋂₀ T ⊆ ⋂₀ S
Set.sInter_subset_sInter.description: The intersection of the sets in one collection is a subset of the intersection of the sets in another collection if every set in the first collection is a subset of the corresponding sets in the second collection.

Set.sUnion_empty.description: The union of sets over an empty collection is itself empty.

Set.sInter_empty.description: The intersection of an empty collection of sets is equal to the universal set.

Set.sUnion_singleton.code: Set.sUnion_singleton.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : ⋃₀ {s} = s
Set.sUnion_singleton.description: The union of a singleton set is equal to the set itself.

Set.sInter_singleton.code: Set.sInter_singleton.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : ⋂₀ {s} = s
Set.sInter_singleton.description: The intersection of a singleton set containing a set is equal to that set itself.

Set.sUnion_eq_empty.code: Set.sUnion_eq_empty.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} : ⋃₀ S = ∅ ↔ ∀ s ∈ S, s = ∅
Set.sUnion_eq_empty.description: The union of a collection of sets is empty if and only if each set in that collection is empty.

Set.sInter_eq_univ.code: Set.sInter_eq_univ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} : ⋂₀ S = univ ↔ ∀ s ∈ S, s = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.sInter_eq_univ.description: The intersection of a collection of sets is equal to the universal set if and only if every set in the collection is the universal set.

Set.nonempty_sUnion.code: Set.nonempty_sUnion.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} : (⋃₀ S).Nonempty ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, s.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.nonempty_sUnion.description: The union of a collection of non-empty sets is non-empty if and only if there exists at least one set in the collection that is non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.of_sUnion.code: Set.Nonempty.of_sUnion.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set (Set α)} (h : (⋃₀ s).Nonempty) : s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_sUnion.description: If the union of all sets in a collection is non-empty, then the collection itself must contain at least one non-empty set.

Set.Nonempty.of_sUnion_eq_univ.code: Set.Nonempty.of_sUnion_eq_univ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Nonempty α] {s : Set (Set α)} (h : ⋃₀ s = univ) : s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_sUnion_eq_univ.description: If the union of a collection of sets equals the universal set, then the collection must be non-empty.

Set.sUnion_union.code: Set.sUnion_union.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (S T : Set (Set α)) : ⋃₀ (S ∪ T) = ⋃₀ S ∪ ⋃₀ T
Set.sUnion_union.description: The union of the union of sets is equal to the union of the unions of the individual sets contained in those sets.

Set.sInter_union.code: Set.sInter_union.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (S T : Set (Set α)) : ⋂₀ (S ∪ T) = ⋂₀ S ∩ ⋂₀ T
Set.sInter_union.description: The intersection of the union of two collections of sets is equal to the intersection of each collection taken separately.

Set.sUnion_insert.code: Set.sUnion_insert.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) (T : Set (Set α)) : ⋃₀ insert s T = s ∪ ⋃₀ T

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.sUnion_insert.description: The union of a set with another set formed by the union of a collection of sets is equal to the union of the first set with the union of the collection.

Set.sInter_insert.code: Set.sInter_insert.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) (T : Set (Set α)) : ⋂₀ insert s T = s ∩ ⋂₀ T

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.sInter_insert.description: The intersection of a set with the union of another set of sets can be expressed as the intersection of the given set with the intersection of those sets.

Set.sUnion_diff_singleton_empty.code: Set.sUnion_diff_singleton_empty.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set (Set α)) : ⋃₀ (s \ {∅}) = ⋃₀ s
Set.sUnion_diff_singleton_empty.description: The union of a collection of sets minus the empty set is equal to the union of the original collection of sets.

Set.sInter_diff_singleton_univ.code: Set.sInter_diff_singleton_univ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set (Set α)) : ⋂₀ (s \ {univ}) = ⋂₀ s
Set.sInter_diff_singleton_univ.description: The intersection of a collection of sets excluding the universe set is equal to the intersection of the original collection of sets.

Set.sUnion_pair.code: Set.sUnion_pair.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s t : Set α) : ⋃₀ {s, t} = s ∪ t
Set.sUnion_pair.description: The union of two sets is equal to the union of the collection containing both sets.

Set.sInter_pair.code: Set.sInter_pair.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s t : Set α) : ⋂₀ {s, t} = s ∩ t
Set.sInter_pair.description: The intersection of a pair of sets is equal to the intersection of the set containing those two sets.

Set.sUnion_image.code: Set.sUnion_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → Set β) (s : Set α) : ⋃₀ (f '' s) = ⋃ x ∈ s, f x
Set.sUnion_image.description: The union of the images of a set under a function corresponds to the union of the sets produced by applying the function to each element of that set.

Set.sInter_image.code: Set.sInter_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α → Set β) (s : Set α) : ⋂₀ (f '' s) = ⋂ x ∈ s, f x
Set.sInter_image.description: The intersection of the images of a set under a function is equal to the intersection over the individual sets obtained from each element of that set.

Set.sUnion_range.code: Set.sUnion_range.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (f : ι → Set β) : ⋃₀ range f = ⋃ x, f x

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.sUnion_range.description: The union of the range of a function that produces sets equals the union of the sets obtained by applying that function to each element in the range.

Set.sInter_range.code: Set.sInter_range.{u_2, u_4} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} (f : ι → Set β) : ⋂₀ range f = ⋂ x, f x

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.sInter_range.description: The intersection of the sets in the image of a function is equal to the intersection over all elements in the domain of that function.

Set.iUnion_eq_univ_iff.code:
Set.iUnion_eq_univ_iff.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → Set α} :
  ⋃ i, f i = univ ↔ ∀ (x : α), ∃ i, x ∈ f i

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.iUnion_eq_univ_iff.description: The union of a family of sets equals the universal set if and only if every element in the universal set belongs to at least one of the sets in the family.

Set.iUnion₂_eq_univ_iff.code:
Set.iUnion₂_eq_univ_iff.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} :
  ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j = univ ↔ ∀ (a : α), ∃ i j, a ∈ s i j

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.iUnion₂_eq_univ_iff.description: The union of unions of sets equals the entire space if and only if every element in the space belongs to at least one of those sets.

Set.sUnion_eq_univ_iff.code: Set.sUnion_eq_univ_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {c : Set (Set α)} : ⋃₀ c = univ ↔ ∀ (a : α), ∃ b ∈ c, a ∈ b

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.sUnion_eq_univ_iff.description: The union of a collection of sets equals the universal set if and only if every element from the universal set belongs to at least one of the sets in the collection.

Set.iInter_eq_empty_iff.code:
Set.iInter_eq_empty_iff.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {f : ι → Set α} :
  ⋂ i, f i = ∅ ↔ ∀ (x : α), ∃ i, x ∉ f i
Set.iInter_eq_empty_iff.description: The intersection of a family of sets is empty if and only if every element is not contained in at least one of those sets.

Set.iInter₂_eq_empty_iff.code:
Set.iInter₂_eq_empty_iff.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} :
  ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j = ∅ ↔ ∀ (a : α), ∃ i j, a ∉ s i j
Set.iInter₂_eq_empty_iff.description: The intersection of a family of sets is empty if and only if every element in the overall set can be found outside at least one of the sets in the family.

Set.sUnion_prod_const.description: The union of the Cartesian products of a set with a constant set is equal to the union of the Cartesian products of each individual set in the original set with the constant set.
