Set.iUnion_prod.{u_11, u_12, u_13, u_14} {ι : Type u_11} {ι' : Type u_12} {α : Type u_13} {β : Type u_14}
  (s : ι → Set α) (t : ι' → Set β) : ⋃ x, s x.1 ×ˢ t x.2 = (⋃ i, s i) ×ˢ ⋃ i, t i
Set.iUnion_prod.description: The union of the Cartesian products of two sets indexed by corresponding pairs is equal to the Cartesian product of their individual unions.

Set.iUnion_prod_of_monotone.code:
Set.iUnion_prod_of_monotone.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} [SemilatticeSup α]
  {s : α → Set β} {t : α → Set γ} (hs : Monotone s) (ht : Monotone t) : ⋃ x, s x ×ˢ t x = (⋃ x, s x) ×ˢ ⋃ x, t x

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

Set.iUnion_prod_of_monotone.description: The union of products of monotone sets is equal to the product of the union of those sets in each dimension.

Set.sInter_prod_sInter_subset.code:
Set.sInter_prod_sInter_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (S : Set (Set α)) (T : Set (Set β)) :
  ⋂₀ S ×ˢ ⋂₀ T ⊆ ⋂ r ∈ S ×ˢ T, r.1 ×ˢ r.2
Set.sInter_prod_sInter_subset.description: The intersection of the Cartesian product of two families of sets is contained within the intersection of their individual products taken across all combinations of sets from each family.

Set.sInter_prod_sInter.code:
Set.sInter_prod_sInter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {S : Set (Set α)} {T : Set (Set β)} (hS : S.Nonempty)
  (hT : T.Nonempty) : ⋂₀ S ×ˢ ⋂₀ T = ⋂ r ∈ S ×ˢ T, r.1 ×ˢ r.2
Set.sInter_prod_sInter.description: The intersection of the Cartesian product of the intersections of two nonempty families of sets is equal to the intersection taken over the products formed by each pair of sets from those families.

Set.sInter_prod.code:
Set.sInter_prod.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {S : Set (Set α)} (hS : S.Nonempty) (t : Set β) :
  ⋂₀ S ×ˢ t = ⋂ s ∈ S, s ×ˢ t
Set.sInter_prod.description: The intersection of a non-empty collection of sets crossed with another set equals the intersection of each set in the collection crossed with that other set.

Set.prod_sInter.code:
Set.prod_sInter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {T : Set (Set β)} (hT : T.Nonempty) (s : Set α) :
  s ×ˢ ⋂₀ T = ⋂ t ∈ T, s ×ˢ t
Set.prod_sInter.description: The Cartesian product of a set and the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the Cartesian products of that set with each individual set in the family.

Set.prod_iInter.code:
Set.prod_iInter.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_4} {s : Set α} {t : ι → Set β}
  [hι : Nonempty ι] : s ×ˢ ⋂ i, t i = ⋂ i, s ×ˢ t i

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.prod_iInter.description: The Cartesian product of a set with the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the Cartesian products of that set with each individual set in the family.

Set.image2_eq_iUnion.code:
Set.image2_eq_iUnion.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (f : α → β → γ) (s : Set α)
  (t : Set β) : image2 f s t = ⋃ i ∈ s, ⋃ j ∈ t, {f i j}
Set.image2_eq_iUnion.description: The image of a two-parameter function applied to two sets is equal to the union of the images of each individual pair formed by elements from those sets.

Set.iUnion_image_left.code:
Set.iUnion_image_left.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (f : α → β → γ) {s : Set α}
  {t : Set β} : ⋃ a ∈ s, f a '' t = image2 f s t

explanatories.Set.image2: The image of a binary function, when applied to two sets, is defined as the resulting set of values obtained by applying the function to all pairs of elements from the sets.

Set.iUnion_image_left.description: The union of the images of a set under a function from another set is equal to the image of the two sets combined under that function.

Set.iUnion_image_right.code:
Set.iUnion_image_right.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (f : α → β → γ) {s : Set α}
  {t : Set β} : ⋃ b ∈ t, (fun x => f x b) '' s = image2 f s t

explanatories.Set.image2: The image of a binary function, when applied to two sets, is defined as the resulting set of values obtained by applying the function to all pairs of elements from the sets.

Set.iUnion_image_right.description: The union of the images of a set under a function with a fixed second argument is equal to the image of the Cartesian product of the two sets under that function.

Set.image2_iUnion_left.code:
Set.image2_iUnion_left.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_4} (f : α → β → γ)
  (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set β) : image2 f (⋃ i, s i) t = ⋃ i, image2 f (s i) t
Set.image2_iUnion_left.description: The image of the Cartesian product of a function applied to the union of sets is equal to the union of the images of that function applied to each individual set.

Set.image2_iUnion_right.code:
Set.image2_iUnion_right.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_4} (f : α → β → γ)
  (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set β) : image2 f s (⋃ i, t i) = ⋃ i, image2 f s (t i)
Set.image2_iUnion_right.description: The image of a function applied to a set and the union of a collection of sets is equal to the union of the images of the function applied to the set and each individual set in the collection.

Set.image2_iUnion₂_left.description: The image of the union of the sets formed by applying a function to pairs of elements is equal to the union of the images obtained by applying the function to each individual set.

Set.image2_iUnion₂_right.description: The image of a binary function applied to a set and the union of sets is equal to the union of the images taken over each component set.

Set.image2_iInter_subset_left.code:
Set.image2_iInter_subset_left.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_4}
  (f : α → β → γ) (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set β) : image2 f (⋂ i, s i) t ⊆ ⋂ i, image2 f (s i) t
Set.image2_iInter_subset_left.description: The image under a binary function of the intersection of a family of sets is a subset of the intersection of the images under that function of each set in the family.

Set.image2_iInter_subset_right.code:
Set.image2_iInter_subset_right.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_4}
  (f : α → β → γ) (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set β) : image2 f s (⋂ i, t i) ⊆ ⋂ i, image2 f s (t i)
Set.image2_iInter_subset_right.description: The image of the Cartesian product of a set and the intersection of a family of sets is a subset of the intersection of the images of that set with each individual set in the family.

Set.image2_iInter₂_subset_left.description: The image of the intersection of sets under a two-argument function is a subset of the intersection of the images of those sets under the same function combined with another set.

Set.image2_iInter₂_subset_right.description: The image of a function applied to a set and the intersection of sets generated by another function is contained within the intersection of images obtained by applying the first function to each of those sets individually.

Set.prod_eq_biUnion_left.code:
Set.prod_eq_biUnion_left.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} :
  s ×ˢ t = ⋃ a ∈ s, (fun b => (a, b)) '' t
Set.prod_eq_biUnion_left.description: The Cartesian product of two sets is equal to the union of the images of each element from one set paired with all elements from the other set.

Set.prod_eq_biUnion_right.code:
Set.prod_eq_biUnion_right.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} :
  s ×ˢ t = ⋃ b ∈ t, (fun a => (a, b)) '' s
Set.prod_eq_biUnion_right.description: The Cartesian product of a set with another set is equal to the union of the images of that set under the functions that pair each element of the first set with each element of the second set.

Set.seq_def.code: Set.seq_def.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set (α → β)} {t : Set α} : s.seq t = ⋃ f ∈ s, f '' t
Set.seq_def.description: The sequence of a set of functions applied to a set of inputs is equivalent to the union of the images of the inputs under each function in that set.

Set.seq_subset.code:
Set.seq_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set (α → β)} {t : Set α} {u : Set β} :
  s.seq t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ f ∈ s, ∀ a ∈ t, f a ∈ u
Set.seq_subset.description: The sequence of applying functions from a set to another set is a subset of a third set if and only if every function applied to each element from the second set results in elements that lie within the third set.

Set.seq_mono.code:
Set.seq_mono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s₀ s₁ : Set (α → β)} {t₀ t₁ : Set α} (hs : s₀ ⊆ s₁)
  (ht : t₀ ⊆ t₁) : s₀.seq t₀ ⊆ s₁.seq t₁
Set.seq_mono.description: The sequence formed by applying a set of functions to a set of inputs is contained within the sequence formed by applying a larger set of functions to a larger set of inputs if both the function sets and the input sets are related by inclusion.

Set.singleton_seq.code: Set.singleton_seq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {t : Set α} : {f}.seq t = f '' t

explanatories.Set.seq: The sequence of a set of functions applied to another set consists of all values that result from applying each function to each element of the second set.

Set.singleton_seq.description: The sequence generated by a singleton set of a function is equal to the image of that function applied to a set of its arguments.

Set.seq_singleton.code: Set.seq_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set (α → β)} {a : α} : s.seq {a} = (fun f => f a) '' s
Set.seq_singleton.description: The sequence formed by a set of functions applied to a singleton set is equal to the image of that set of functions evaluated at the element of the singleton.

Set.seq_seq.code:
Set.seq_seq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {s : Set (β → γ)} {t : Set (α → β)}
  {u : Set α} : s.seq (t.seq u) = (((fun x x_1 => x ∘ x_1) '' s).seq t).seq u
Set.seq_seq.description: The sequential application of sets of functions is preserved when nesting sequence operations, resulting in equivalence between nested sequences and compositions of the function sets.

Set.image_seq.code:
Set.image_seq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {f : β → γ} {s : Set (α → β)} {t : Set α} :
  f '' s.seq t = ((fun x => f ∘ x) '' s).seq t

explanatories.Set.seq: The sequence of a set of functions applied to another set consists of all values that result from applying each function to each element of the second set.

Set.image_seq.description: The image of the sequential application of a function to sets is equal to the sequential application of the function to the image of those sets.

Set.prod_eq_seq.code: Set.prod_eq_seq.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} : s ×ˢ t = (Prod.mk '' s).seq t

explanatories.Sigma.mk: This theorem constructs a dependent pair consisting of an element from one type and an element from a type that depends on the first element.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This constructs a subtype from a value and a property that the value satisfies.
explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.Set.seq: The sequence of a set of functions applied to another set consists of all values that result from applying each function to each element of the second set.

Set.prod_eq_seq.description: The Cartesian product of two sets is equal to the collection of sequences formed by pairing elements from the first set with elements from the second set.

Set.prod_image_seq_comm.code:
Set.prod_image_seq_comm.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
  (Prod.mk '' s).seq t = ((fun b a => (a, b)) '' t).seq s

explanatories.Sigma.mk: This theorem constructs a dependent pair consisting of an element from one type and an element from a type that depends on the first element.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This constructs a subtype from a value and a property that the value satisfies.
explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.Set.seq: The sequence of a set of functions applied to another set consists of all values that result from applying each function to each element of the second set.

Set.prod_image_seq_comm.description: The sequence of pairs formed by the image of a set under the product operation is commutative with respect to the order of the sets involved.

Set.image2_eq_seq.code:
Set.image2_eq_seq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (f : α → β → γ) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
  image2 f s t = (f '' s).seq t

explanatories.Set.seq: The sequence of a set of functions applied to another set consists of all values that result from applying each function to each element of the second set.

Set.image2_eq_seq.description: The image of a two-parameter function applied to two sets is equal to the sequence obtained by applying the function to each element from the first set and taking images in the second set.

Set.pi_def.code:
Set.pi_def.{u_1, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {π : α → Type u_11} (i : Set α) (s : (a : α) → Set (π a)) :
  i.pi s = ⋂ a ∈ i, eval a ⁻¹' s a

explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.Function.eval: This defines a way to evaluate a function at a specific argument, yielding a result that corresponds to that argument.

Set.pi_def.description: The product of a family of sets indexed by a set is defined as the intersection of the inverse images of the individual sets under the evaluation function for each element of the index set.

Set.univ_pi_eq_iInter.code:
Set.univ_pi_eq_iInter.{u_1, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {π : α → Type u_11} (t : (i : α) → Set (π i)) :
  univ.pi t = ⋂ i, eval i ⁻¹' t i

explanatories.Set.pi: The set of dependent functions can be defined for a given index set and a family of sets, where each function's values belong to the corresponding set whenever the index is part of the specified set.
explanatories.Set.Sigma.univ: The universe set is equivalent to the union of all ranges of pairs formed by each element of a given type and its corresponding type.
explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.Function.eval: This defines a way to evaluate a function at a specific argument, yielding a result that corresponds to that argument.

Set.univ_pi_eq_iInter.description: The product of a family of sets indexed by a type is equal to the intersection of the preimages of those sets under the product evaluation function.

Set.pi_diff_pi_subset.code:
Set.pi_diff_pi_subset.{u_1, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {π : α → Type u_11} (i : Set α) (s t : (a : α) → Set (π a)) :
  i.pi s \ i.pi t ⊆ ⋃ a ∈ i, eval a ⁻¹' (s a \ t a)

explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element of the type that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.Function.eval: This defines a way to evaluate a function at a specific argument, yielding a result that corresponds to that argument.

Set.pi_diff_pi_subset.description: The difference between the product of sets indexed by a given set and another is a subset of the union of preimages of the differences of those sets for each element in the indexing set.

Set.iUnion_univ_pi.code:
Set.iUnion_univ_pi.{u_1, u_11, u_12} {α : Type u_1} {π : α → Type u_11} {ι : α → Type u_12}
  (t : (a : α) → ι a → Set (π a)) : (⋃ x, univ.pi fun a => t a (x a)) = univ.pi fun a => ⋃ j, t a j

explanatories.Set.pi: The set of dependent functions can be defined for a given index set and a family of sets, where each function's values belong to the corresponding set whenever the index is part of the specified set.
explanatories.Set.Sigma.univ: The universe set is equivalent to the union of all ranges of pairs formed by each element of a given type and its corresponding type.

Set.iUnion_univ_pi.description: The union of a family of sets formed by a product of a universal set and a function is equal to the product of the universal set with the unions of those sets at each index.

Set.directedOn_iUnion.code:
Set.directedOn_iUnion.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {r : α → α → Prop} {f : ι → Set α}
  (hd : Directed (fun x x_1 => x ⊆ x_1) f) (h : ∀ (x : ι), DirectedOn r (f x)) : DirectedOn r (⋃ x, f x)

explanatories.Directed: A family of elements is considered directed with respect to a given relation if there exists an element that is greater than or equal to every pair in the family.
explanatories.DirectedOn: A subset of elements is directed if there exists an element within the set that is greater than or equal to every pair of elements in that set.

Set.directedOn_iUnion.description: If a family of sets is directed under inclusion and each set in the family is directed under a given relation, then the union of all these sets is also directed under that relation.

Function.Surjective.iUnion_comp.code:
Function.Surjective.iUnion_comp.{u_1, u_4, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι₂ : Sort u_6} {f : ι → ι₂}
  (hf : Surjective f) (g : ι₂ → Set α) : ⋃ x, g (f x) = ⋃ y, g y

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Function.Surjective.iUnion_comp.description: The union of sets formed by applying a function to a surjective mapping is equal to the union of the sets directly formed from the image of that function.

Function.Surjective.iInter_comp.code:
Function.Surjective.iInter_comp.{u_1, u_4, u_6} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {ι₂ : Sort u_6} {f : ι → ι₂}
  (hf : Surjective f) (g : ι₂ → Set α) : ⋂ x, g (f x) = ⋂ y, g y

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Function.Surjective.iInter_comp.description: The intersection of sets obtained by applying a function to elements from one set is equal to the intersection of those sets evaluated directly at the images of the function, when the function is surjective.

Set.disjoint_iUnion_left.code:
Set.disjoint_iUnion_left.{u_1, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {t : Set α} {ι : Sort u_11} {s : ι → Set α} :
  Disjoint (⋃ i, s i) t ↔ ∀ (i : ι), Disjoint (s i) t

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_iUnion_left.description: The union of a collection of sets is disjoint from another set if and only if each individual set in the collection is disjoint from that other set.

Set.disjoint_iUnion_right.code:
Set.disjoint_iUnion_right.{u_1, u_11} {α : Type u_1} {t : Set α} {ι : Sort u_11} {s : ι → Set α} :
  Disjoint t (⋃ i, s i) ↔ ∀ (i : ι), Disjoint t (s i)

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_iUnion_right.description: A set is disjoint from the union of a family of sets if and only if it is disjoint from each individual set in that family.

Set.disjoint_iUnion₂_left.code:
Set.disjoint_iUnion₂_left.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α}
  {t : Set α} : Disjoint (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j) t ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), Disjoint (s i j) t

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_iUnion₂_left.description: The condition that the union of two nested sets is disjoint from another set is equivalent to the disjointness of each individual nested set from that same set.

Set.disjoint_iUnion₂_right.code:
Set.disjoint_iUnion₂_right.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} {s : Set α}
  {t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α} : Disjoint s (⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j) ↔ ∀ (i : ι) (j : κ i), Disjoint s (t i j)

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_iUnion₂_right.description: A set is disjoint from the union of sets indexed by two families if and only if it is disjoint from each individual set defined by the indices.

Set.disjoint_sUnion_left.code: Set.disjoint_sUnion_left.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {S : Set (Set α)} {t : Set α} : Disjoint (⋃₀ S) t ↔ ∀ s ∈ S, Disjoint s t

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_sUnion_left.description: The union of a collection of disjoint sets does not intersect with another set if and only if each set in the collection is disjoint from that other set.

Set.disjoint_sUnion_right.code: Set.disjoint_sUnion_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Set α} {S : Set (Set α)} : Disjoint s (⋃₀ S) ↔ ∀ t ∈ S, Disjoint s t

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

Set.disjoint_sUnion_right.description: A set is disjoint from the union of a collection of sets if and only if it is disjoint from each individual set in that collection.

Set.nonempty_iInter_Iic_iff.code:
Set.nonempty_iInter_Iic_iff.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} [Preorder α] {f : ι → α} :
  (⋂ i, Iic (f i)).Nonempty ↔ BddBelow (range f)

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.Set.Iic: This definition identifies the set of elements that are less than or equal to a given element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-infinite and right-closed interval.
explanatories.BddBelow: This definition states that a set is considered bounded below if there exists at least one element that serves as a lower bound for all elements in the set within a preorder structure.

Set.nonempty_iInter_Iic_iff.description: The intersection of lower intervals defined by a function is non-empty if and only if the range of that function is bounded below.

Set.Ici_iSup.code: Set.Ici_iSup.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ι → α) : Ici (⨆ i, f i) = ⋂ i, Ici (f i)
Set.Ici_iSup.description: The interval defined by the supremum of a family of elements is equal to the intersection of the intervals defined by each individual element in the family.

Set.Iic_iInf.code: Set.Iic_iInf.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} [CompleteLattice α] (f : ι → α) : Iic (⨅ i, f i) = ⋂ i, Iic (f i)
Set.Iic_iInf.description: The set of all elements less than or equal to the infimum of a family of values is equal to the intersection of the sets of all elements less than or equal to each individual value in that family.

Set.Ici_iSup₂.code:
Set.Ici_iSup₂.{u_1, u_4, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_4} {κ : ι → Sort u_7} [CompleteLattice α]
  (f : (i : ι) → κ i → α) : Ici (⨆ i, ⨆ j, f i j) = ⋂ i, ⋂ j, Ici (f i j)
Set.Ici_iSup₂.description: The interval of non-negative values generated by the supremum of a family of functions is equal to the intersection of the intervals of the values produced by each function in the family.

Set.Iic_iInf₂.code:

explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.

Set.Iic_sInf.description: The lower closure of the infimum of a set is equal to the intersection of all lower closures of its elements.

Set.biUnion_diff_biUnion_subset.code:
Set.biUnion_diff_biUnion_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (t : α → Set β) (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :

explanatories.Pairwise: A relation is considered "pairwise" if it holds between every pair of distinct elements in its domain.

Set.sigmaToiUnion_bijective.description: The function that maps a family of disjoint sets to their union is a bijection.

explanatories.Equiv.ofBijective: This definition states that if a function is bijective, then there exists an equivalence relationship between its domain and codomain.

Set.unionEqSigmaOfDisjoint.description: The disjoint union of sets corresponds to a dependent sum, providing a way to relate the elements of the sets with their indices.

Set.iUnion_ge_eq_iUnion_nat_add.code: Set.iUnion_ge_eq_iUnion_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (u : ℕ → Set α) (n : ℕ) : ⋃ i, ⋃ (_ : i ≥ n), u i = ⋃ i, u (i + n)
Set.iUnion_ge_eq_iUnion_nat_add.description: The union of sets indexed by integers greater than or equal to a certain number is equal to the union of those sets shifted by that number.

Set.iInter_ge_eq_iInter_nat_add.code: Set.iInter_ge_eq_iInter_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (u : ℕ → Set α) (n : ℕ) : ⋂ i, ⋂ (_ : i ≥ n), u i = ⋂ i, u (i + n)
Set.iInter_ge_eq_iInter_nat_add.description: The intersection of sets defined by elements greater than or equal to a certain natural number is equal to the intersection of sets defined by those elements shifted by that number.

Monotone.iUnion_nat_add.code: Monotone.iUnion_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {f : ℕ → Set α} (hf : Monotone f) (k : ℕ) : ⋃ n, f (n + k) = ⋃ n, f n

Antitone.iInter_nat_add.code: Antitone.iInter_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {f : ℕ → Set α} (hf : Antitone f) (k : ℕ) : ⋂ n, f (n + k) = ⋂ n, f n

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Antitone.iInter_nat_add.description: The intersection of decreasing sets indexed by natural numbers remains unchanged when the indices are shifted by a fixed natural number.

Set.iUnion_iInter_ge_nat_add.code:
Set.iUnion_iInter_ge_nat_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (f : ℕ → Set α) (k : ℕ) :

Set.iUnion_iInter_ge_nat_add.description: The union of the intersections of a shifted sequence of sets is equal to the union of the intersections of the original sequence of sets.

Set.union_iUnion_nat_succ.code: Set.union_iUnion_nat_succ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (u : ℕ → Set α) : u 0 ∪ ⋃ i, u (i + 1) = ⋃ i, u i
Set.union_iUnion_nat_succ.description: The union of a set at zero and the union of its successors is equal to the union of all sets indexed by the natural numbers starting from zero.

Set.inter_iInter_nat_succ.code: Set.inter_iInter_nat_succ.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (u : ℕ → Set α) : u 0 ∩ ⋂ i, u (i + 1) = ⋂ i, u i
Set.inter_iInter_nat_succ.description: The intersection of a set at zero and the intersection of sets at all subsequent natural numbers is equal to the intersection of the sets at each natural number.

iInf_iUnion.code:

sSup_sUnion.code: sSup_sUnion.{u_2} {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLattice β] (s : Set (Set β)) : sSup (⋃₀ s) = ⨆ t ∈ s, sSup t

Set.union_neg.description: The theorem demonstrates that the negation of the union of two sets is equivalent to the union of their negations.

Set.iInter_inv.code: Set.iInter_inv.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Inv α] (s : ι → Set α) : (⋂ i, s i)⁻¹ = ⋂ i, (s i)⁻¹
Set.iInter_inv.description: The theorem demonstrates that the inverse of the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the inverses of those individual sets.

Set.iInter_neg.code: Set.iInter_neg.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Neg α] (s : ι → Set α) : -⋂ i, s i = ⋂ i, -s i
Set.iInter_neg.description: The theorem states that the negation of the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the negations of those sets.

Set.iUnion_inv.code: Set.iUnion_inv.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Inv α] (s : ι → Set α) : (⋃ i, s i)⁻¹ = ⋃ i, (s i)⁻¹
Set.iUnion_inv.description: The theorem states that the inverse of the union of sets is equal to the union of the inverses of each individual set.

Set.iUnion_neg.code: Set.iUnion_neg.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Neg α] (s : ι → Set α) : -⋃ i, s i = ⋃ i, -s i
Set.iUnion_neg.description: The theorem states that the negation of the union of sets indexed by a certain collection is equal to the union of the negated sets indexed by the same collection.

Set.compl_inv.code: Set.compl_inv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Inv α] {s : Set α} : sᶜ⁻¹ = s⁻¹ᶜ
Set.compl_inv.description: The theorem asserts that the inverse of the complement of a set is equal to the complement of the inverse of that set.

Set.compl_neg.code: Set.compl_neg.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Neg α] {s : Set α} : -sᶜ = (-s)ᶜ
Set.compl_neg.description: The theorem asserts that the complement of the negation of a set is equal to the negation of the complement of that set.

Set.inv_mem_inv.code: Set.inv_mem_inv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {s : Set α} {a : α} : a⁻¹ ∈ s⁻¹ ↔ a ∈ s
Set.inv_mem_inv.description: The theorem states that an element's inverse is in the inverse set if and only if the element itself is in the original set.

Set.neg_mem_neg.code: Set.neg_mem_neg.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {s : Set α} {a : α} : -a ∈ -s ↔ a ∈ s
Set.neg_mem_neg.description: The theorem establishes a relationship between the negation of an element being in the negation of a set and the element being in the set itself, under the condition that negation is involutive.

Set.nonempty_inv.code: Set.nonempty_inv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {s : Set α} : s⁻¹.Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.nonempty_inv.description: The theorem states that a set is nonempty if and only if its inverse is nonempty, assuming the inverse operation is involutive.

Set.nonempty_neg.code: Set.nonempty_neg.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {s : Set α} : (-s).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.nonempty_neg.description: The theorem states that a set is nonempty if and only if its negation is nonempty, assuming the negation operation is involutive.

Set.Nonempty.inv.code: Set.Nonempty.inv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {s : Set α} (h : s.Nonempty) : s⁻¹.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.inv.description: The theorem states that if a set is nonempty and there exists an involutive inverse operation, then the set formed by applying this inverse to each element of the original set is also nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.neg.code: Set.Nonempty.neg.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {s : Set α} (h : s.Nonempty) : (-s).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.neg.description: The theorem establishes that if a set is non-empty, then the negation of that set is also non-empty.

Set.image_inv.code: Set.image_inv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {s : Set α} : Inv.inv '' s = s⁻¹

explanatories.Inv.inv: This expression defines a function that computes the inverse of an element within a specified type.
explanatories.Set.inv: The definition describes the inversion operation on sets, which produces a new set containing elements that are the inverses of those in the original set.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.inv: The theorem states that if a set is nonempty and there exists an involutive inverse operation, then the set formed by applying this inverse to each element of the original set is also nonempty.
explanatories.Equiv.inv: Inversion in a group or group with zero acts as a permutation of the elements in the underlying type.

Set.image_inv.description: The theorem establishes that the image of a set under the inversion function equals the set of inverses of its elements when the inversion is involutive.

Set.image_neg.code: Set.image_neg.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {s : Set α} : Neg.neg '' s = -s

explanatories.Set.neg: The definition describes the pointwise negation of a set, which consists of all elements whose negations belong to the original set.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.neg: The theorem establishes that if a set is non-empty, then the negation of that set is also non-empty.

Set.image_neg.description: The theorem states that the image of a set under negation coincides with the negation of the original set when negation is involutive.

Set.inv_subset_inv.code: Set.inv_subset_inv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {s t : Set α} : s⁻¹ ⊆ t⁻¹ ↔ s ⊆ t
Set.inv_subset_inv.description: The theorem states that a set is included in another set if and only if the inverse of the first set is included in the inverse of the second set.

Set.neg_subset_neg.code: Set.neg_subset_neg.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {s t : Set α} : -s ⊆ -t ↔ s ⊆ t
Set.neg_subset_neg.description: The theorem states that the negation of one set is a subset of the negation of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the second set.

Set.inv_subset.code: Set.inv_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {s t : Set α} : s⁻¹ ⊆ t ↔ s ⊆ t⁻¹
Set.inv_subset.description: The theorem states that the inverse of a set is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the inverse of that other set, assuming the inversion operation is involutive.

Set.neg_subset.code: Set.neg_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {s t : Set α} : -s ⊆ t ↔ s ⊆ -t
Set.neg_subset.description: The theorem states that the negation of one set being a subset of another is equivalent to the original set being a subset of the negation of the second set, under the condition that negation is involutive.

Set.inv_singleton.description: The theorem states that the inverse of a singleton set containing an element is equal to the singleton set containing the inverse of that element, given that the inversion operation is involutive.

Set.neg_singleton.description: The theorem asserts that the negation of a singleton set containing an element is equal to the singleton set containing the negation of that element, assuming the negation operation is involutive.

Set.inv_insert.code: Set.inv_insert.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] (a : α) (s : Set α) : (insert a s)⁻¹ = insert a⁻¹ s⁻¹

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.inv_insert.description: The theorem states that the inverse of a set with an inserted element is equal to the set formed by inserting the inverse of that element into the inverse of the original set.

Set.neg_insert.code: Set.neg_insert.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] (a : α) (s : Set α) : -insert a s = insert (-a) (-s)

explanatories.Insert.insert: This defines a function that inserts an element into a collection.

Set.neg_insert.description: The theorem shows that the negation of the insertion of an element into a set is the same as the insertion of the negation of that element into the negation of the set.

Set.inv_range.code:
Set.inv_range.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {ι : Sort u_5} {f : ι → α} :
  (range f)⁻¹ = range fun i => (f i)⁻¹

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.inv_range.description: The theorem asserts that the inverse of the range of a function equals the range of the inverse of the function's values, under the assumption that the inversion operation is involutive.

Set.neg_range.code: Set.neg_range.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {ι : Sort u_5} {f : ι → α} : -range f = range fun i => -f i

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.neg_range.description: The theorem states that the negation of the range of a function is equal to the range of the negated function values.

Set.image_op_inv.code: Set.image_op_inv.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveInv α] {s : Set α} : op '' s⁻¹ = (op '' s)⁻¹

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.image_op_inv.description: The theorem shows that applying an operation to the inverse of a set yields the same result as taking the inverse of the image of that set under the operation.

Set.image_op_neg.code: Set.image_op_neg.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [InvolutiveNeg α] {s : Set α} : AddOpposite.op '' (-s) = -AddOpposite.op '' s

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.image_op_neg.description: The theorem states that the image under the additive opposite operation of the negated set is equal to the negation of the image under the additive opposite operation of the original set.

Set.mul.code: Set.mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] : Mul (Set α)
Set.mul.comment:
The pointwise multiplication of sets `s * t` and `t` is defined as `{x * y | x ∈ s, y ∈ t}` in
locale `Pointwise`.

explanatories.Set.image2: The image of a binary function, when applied to two sets, is defined as the resulting set of values obtained by applying the function to all pairs of elements from the sets.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.

Set.mul.description: This definition establishes pointwise multiplication of sets as the set of all products formed by multiplying elements from two sets.

Set.add.code: Set.add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] : Add (Set α)
Set.add.comment:
The pointwise addition of sets `s + t` is defined as `{x + y | x ∈ s, y ∈ t}` in locale
`Pointwise`.

explanatories.Set.image2: The image of a binary function, when applied to two sets, is defined as the resulting set of values obtained by applying the function to all pairs of elements from the sets.
explanatories.Set.mul: This definition establishes pointwise multiplication of sets as the set of all products formed by multiplying elements from two sets.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.

Set.add.fullDefinition: @[to_additive       "The pointwise addition of sets `s + t` is defined as `{x + y | x ∈ s, y ∈ t}` in locale       `Pointwise`."] protected def mul : Mul (Set α) :=   ⟨image2 (· * ·)⟩
Set.add.description: The definition describes the pointwise addition of sets, which consists of all elements that result from adding elements of one set to elements of another set.

Set.image2_mul.code: Set.image2_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : image2 (fun x x_1 => x * x_1) s t = s * t

explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.

Set.image2_mul.description: The theorem asserts that the image of the Cartesian product of two sets, under multiplication, is equal to the set obtained by multiplying the elements of the individual sets.

Set.image2_add.code: Set.image2_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : image2 (fun x x_1 => x + x_1) s t = s + t

explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.

Set.image2_add.description: The theorem states that the image of the pairwise addition of elements from two sets is equal to the set formed by the sum of those two sets.

Set.mem_mul.code: Set.mem_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} {a : α} : a ∈ s * t ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t, x * y = a
Set.mem_mul.description: The theorem states that an element belongs to the product of two sets if and only if it can be expressed as the product of an element from each set.

Set.mem_add.code: Set.mem_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} {a : α} : a ∈ s + t ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t, x + y = a
Set.mem_add.description: The theorem states that an element belongs to the sum of two sets if and only if it can be expressed as the sum of an element from each of those sets.

Set.mul_mem_mul.code: Set.mul_mem_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} {a b : α} : a ∈ s → b ∈ t → a * b ∈ s * t
Set.mul_mem_mul.description: The theorem states that if an element belongs to one set and another element belongs to a second set, then the product of these elements belongs to the set formed by the products of the two original sets.

Set.add_mem_add.code: Set.add_mem_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} {a b : α} : a ∈ s → b ∈ t → a + b ∈ s + t
Set.add_mem_add.description: The theorem states that if an element belongs to one set and another element belongs to a second set, then the sum of those elements belongs to the sum set formed by adding the two original sets.

Set.image_mul_prod.code: Set.image_mul_prod.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : (fun x => x.1 * x.2) '' s ×ˢ t = s * t
Set.image_mul_prod.description: The theorem asserts that the image of the Cartesian product of two sets under the multiplication of their elements is equal to the set formed by multiplying the individual sets.

Set.add_image_prod.code: Set.add_image_prod.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : (fun x => x.1 + x.2) '' s ×ˢ t = s + t
Set.add_image_prod.description: The theorem states that the image of the Cartesian product of two sets under the addition of their elements is equal to the sum of the two sets.

Set.empty_mul.code: Set.empty_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s : Set α} : ∅ * s = ∅
Set.empty_mul.description: This theorem states that multiplying the empty set by any set results in the empty set.

Set.empty_add.code: Set.empty_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s : Set α} : ∅ + s = ∅
Set.empty_add.description: The theorem states that adding an empty set to any set results in the empty set.

Set.mul_empty.code: Set.mul_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s : Set α} : s * ∅ = ∅
Set.mul_empty.description: The theorem asserts that the product of any set with the empty set is the empty set.

Set.add_empty.code: Set.add_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s : Set α} : s + ∅ = ∅
Set.add_empty.description: The theorem states that the union of any set with the empty set results in the empty set.

Set.mul_eq_empty.code: Set.mul_eq_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : s * t = ∅ ↔ s = ∅ ∨ t = ∅
Set.mul_eq_empty.description: The theorem concludes that the product of two sets is empty if and only if at least one of the sets is empty.

Set.add_eq_empty.code: Set.add_eq_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : s + t = ∅ ↔ s = ∅ ∨ t = ∅
Set.add_eq_empty.description: The theorem states that the sum of two sets is empty if and only if at least one of the sets is empty.

Set.mul_nonempty.code: Set.mul_nonempty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : (s * t).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty ∧ t.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.mul_nonempty.description: The theorem states that the product of two sets is nonempty if and only if each of the individual sets is nonempty.

Set.add_nonempty.code: Set.add_nonempty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : (s + t).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty ∧ t.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.add_nonempty.description: The theorem states that the sum of two sets is nonempty if and only if both of the individual sets are nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.mul.code: Set.Nonempty.mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : s.Nonempty → t.Nonempty → (s * t).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.mul.description: The theorem states that the product of two non-empty sets is also non-empty if both component sets are non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.add.code: Set.Nonempty.add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : s.Nonempty → t.Nonempty → (s + t).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.add.description: The theorem asserts that if both sets are nonempty, then their sum is also nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.of_mul_left.code: Set.Nonempty.of_mul_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : (s * t).Nonempty → s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_mul_left.description: The theorem states that if the product of two sets is nonempty, then at least one of the sets must also be nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.of_add_left.code: Set.Nonempty.of_add_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : (s + t).Nonempty → s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_add_left.description: The theorem states that if the sum of two sets is non-empty, then at least one of the sets must also be non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.of_mul_right.code: Set.Nonempty.of_mul_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : (s * t).Nonempty → t.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_mul_right.description: The theorem concludes that if the product of two sets is non-empty, then at least one of the sets must also be non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.of_add_right.code: Set.Nonempty.of_add_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : (s + t).Nonempty → t.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_add_right.description: The theorem states that if the sum of two sets is nonempty, then one of those sets must also be nonempty.

Set.mul_singleton.code: Set.mul_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s : Set α} {b : α} : s * {b} = (fun x => x * b) '' s
Set.mul_singleton.description: The theorem states that the product of a set with a singleton set is equal to the image of the original set under the multiplication with the element from the singleton.

Set.add_singleton.code: Set.add_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s : Set α} {b : α} : s + {b} = (fun x => x + b) '' s
Set.add_singleton.description: The theorem asserts that the sum of a set and a singleton set can be represented as the image of the original set under the function that adds a fixed element from the singleton set.

Set.singleton_mul.code: Set.singleton_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {t : Set α} {a : α} : {a} * t = (fun x => a * x) '' t
Set.singleton_mul.description: The theorem states that the product of a singleton set containing an element with another set is equivalent to the image of that second set under the function that multiplies by the singleton element.

Set.singleton_add.code: Set.singleton_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {t : Set α} {a : α} : {a} + t = (fun x => a + x) '' t
Set.singleton_add.description: The theorem states that the sum of a singleton set containing an element and another set is equivalent to the image of that other set under the function that adds the singleton element to each of its elements.

Set.singleton_mul_singleton.code: Set.singleton_mul_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {a b : α} : {a} * {b} = {a * b}
Set.singleton_mul_singleton.description: The theorem asserts that the product of two singleton sets containing elements results in a singleton set containing the product of those two elements.

Set.singleton_add_singleton.code: Set.singleton_add_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {a b : α} : {a} + {b} = {a + b}
Set.singleton_add_singleton.description: The theorem asserts that the sum of two singleton sets containing elements is equal to a singleton set containing the sum of those two elements.

Set.mul_subset_mul.code: Set.mul_subset_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ t₁ → s₂ ⊆ t₂ → s₁ * s₂ ⊆ t₁ * t₂
Set.mul_subset_mul.description: The theorem asserts that if one set is a subset of another and a second set is also a subset of a third set, then the product of the first two sets is a subset of the product of the last two sets.

Set.add_subset_add.code: Set.add_subset_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ t₁ → s₂ ⊆ t₂ → s₁ + s₂ ⊆ t₁ + t₂
Set.add_subset_add.description: The theorem establishes that if one set is a subset of another and a second set is also a subset of a third, then the sum of the first two sets is a subset of the sum of the last two sets.

Set.mul_subset_mul_left.code: Set.mul_subset_mul_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : t₁ ⊆ t₂ → s * t₁ ⊆ s * t₂
Set.mul_subset_mul_left.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then scaling both sets by a fixed set leads to a new set that is a subset of the scaled version of the second set.

Set.add_subset_add_left.code: Set.add_subset_add_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : t₁ ⊆ t₂ → s + t₁ ⊆ s + t₂
Set.add_subset_add_left.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then adding the same set to both results preserves the subset relationship.

Set.mul_subset_mul_right.code: Set.mul_subset_mul_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₁ * t ⊆ s₂ * t
Set.mul_subset_mul_right.description: The theorem asserts that if one set is a subset of another, then the product of that set with a third set is also a subset of the product of the second set with the same third set.

Set.add_subset_add_right.code: Set.add_subset_add_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₁ + t ⊆ s₂ + t
Set.add_subset_add_right.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then the sum of that set with a third set is also a subset of the sum of the second set with the same third set.

Set.mul_subset_iff.code: Set.mul_subset_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t u : Set α} : s * t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, x * y ∈ u
Set.mul_subset_iff.description: The theorem establishes that the product of two sets is a subset of a third set if and only if every element formed by multiplying elements from the first two sets belongs to the third set.

Set.add_subset_iff.code: Set.add_subset_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t u : Set α} : s + t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, x + y ∈ u
Set.add_subset_iff.description: The theorem states that the sum of two sets is a subset of a third set if and only if every element formed by adding an element from the first set to an element from the second set belongs to the third set.

Set.union_mul.code: Set.union_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : (s₁ ∪ s₂) * t = s₁ * t ∪ s₂ * t
Set.union_mul.description: The theorem demonstrates that the product of the union of two sets with another set is equal to the union of the products of each set with the third set.

Set.union_add.code: Set.union_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ∪ s₂ + t = s₁ + t ∪ (s₂ + t)
Set.union_add.description: The theorem states that the union of two sets added to a third set is equal to the union of the first set added to the third set and the second set added to the third set.

Set.mul_union.code: Set.mul_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s * (t₁ ∪ t₂) = s * t₁ ∪ s * t₂
Set.mul_union.description: The theorem states that the product of a set with the union of two other sets is equal to the union of the products of the first set with each of the other two sets.

Set.add_union.code: Set.add_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s + (t₁ ∪ t₂) = s + t₁ ∪ (s + t₂)
Set.add_union.description: The theorem states that adding a set to the union of two other sets is equivalent to taking the union of the sums of the first set with each of the two sets individually.

Set.inter_mul_subset.code: Set.inter_mul_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ∩ s₂ * t ⊆ s₁ * t ∩ (s₂ * t)
Set.inter_mul_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the intersection of two sets multiplied by a third set is contained within the intersection of the products of each of the first two sets with the third set.

Set.inter_add_subset.code: Set.inter_add_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ∩ s₂ + t ⊆ (s₁ + t) ∩ (s₂ + t)
Set.inter_add_subset.description: The theorem states that the sum of the intersection of two sets with a third set is a subset of the intersection of the sums of the first two sets with that same third set.

Set.mul_inter_subset.code: Set.mul_inter_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s * (t₁ ∩ t₂) ⊆ s * t₁ ∩ (s * t₂)
Set.mul_inter_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the product of a set with the intersection of two other sets is contained within the intersection of the products of the first set with each of the other two sets.

Set.add_inter_subset.code: Set.add_inter_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s + t₁ ∩ t₂ ⊆ (s + t₁) ∩ (s + t₂)
Set.add_inter_subset.description: The theorem states that the sum of a set with the intersection of two other sets is a subset of the intersection of the sums formed by adding the original set to each of the two sets.

Set.inter_mul_union_subset_union.code:
Set.inter_mul_union_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∩ s₂ * (t₁ ∪ t₂) ⊆ s₁ * t₁ ∪ s₂ * t₂
Set.inter_mul_union_subset_union.description: The theorem states that the product of the intersection of two sets with the union of two other sets is a subset of the union of the products of each original set with the respective other sets.

Set.inter_add_union_subset_union.code:
Set.inter_add_union_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∩ s₂ + (t₁ ∪ t₂) ⊆ s₁ + t₁ ∪ (s₂ + t₂)
Set.inter_add_union_subset_union.description: The theorem states that the intersection of two sets combined with the union of two other sets is a subset of the union of the first set with one of the other sets and the second set with the other set.

Set.union_mul_inter_subset_union.code:
Set.union_mul_inter_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  (s₁ ∪ s₂) * (t₁ ∩ t₂) ⊆ s₁ * t₁ ∪ s₂ * t₂
Set.union_mul_inter_subset_union.description: The theorem asserts that the product of the union of two sets with the intersection of two other sets is a subset of the union of the products formed by each set and the respective other set.

Set.union_add_inter_subset_union.code:
Set.union_add_inter_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∪ s₂ + t₁ ∩ t₂ ⊆ s₁ + t₁ ∪ (s₂ + t₂)
Set.union_add_inter_subset_union.description: The theorem demonstrates that the union of two sets added to the intersection of two other sets is contained within the union of one set with another added to the respective second set.

Set.iUnion_mul_left_image.code: Set.iUnion_mul_left_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ s, (fun x => a * x) '' t = s * t
Set.iUnion_mul_left_image.description: The theorem states that the union of the images of a set under multiplication by each element of another set equals the product of those two sets.

Set.iUnion_add_left_image.code: Set.iUnion_add_left_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ s, (fun x => a + x) '' t = s + t
Set.iUnion_add_left_image.description: The theorem establishes that the union of the left translations of a set by elements of another set is equal to the addition of the two sets, assuming the elements can be added.

Set.iUnion_mul_right_image.code: Set.iUnion_mul_right_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ t, (fun x => x * a) '' s = s * t
Set.iUnion_mul_right_image.description: The theorem states that the union of the images of a set under multiplication by elements of another set is equal to the product of the original set and the second set.

Set.iUnion_add_right_image.code: Set.iUnion_add_right_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ t, (fun x => x + a) '' s = s + t
Set.iUnion_add_right_image.description: The theorem states that the union of the images of a set under the addition of each element in another set is equal to the sum of the original set and the second set.

Set.iUnion_mul.code:
Set.iUnion_mul.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Mul α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋃ i, s i) * t = ⋃ i, s i * t
Set.iUnion_mul.description: The theorem states that the product of the union of a family of sets with a third set is equal to the union of the products of each individual set in the family with that same third set.

Set.iUnion_add.code:
Set.iUnion_add.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Add α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋃ i, s i) + t = ⋃ i, s i + t
Set.iUnion_add.description: The theorem states that the union of a collection of sets, each added to a fixed set, is equal to the union of the same collection of sets added to that fixed set.

Set.mul_iUnion.code:
Set.mul_iUnion.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Mul α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s * ⋃ i, t i = ⋃ i, s * t i
Set.mul_iUnion.description: The theorem asserts that the product of a set with the union of another family of sets is equal to the union of the products of the first set with each individual set in the family.

Set.add_iUnion.code:
Set.add_iUnion.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Add α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s + ⋃ i, t i = ⋃ i, s + t i
Set.add_iUnion.description: The theorem states that the sum of a set and the union of a family of sets is equal to the union of the sums of the set with each individual set in the family.

Set.iUnion₂_mul.code:
Set.iUnion₂_mul.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Mul α] (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j) * t = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j * t
Set.iUnion₂_mul.description: The theorem establishes that the product of the union of indexed sets with another set is equivalent to the union of the products of each indexed set with that other set.

Set.iUnion₂_add.code:
Set.iUnion₂_add.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Add α] (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j) + t = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j + t
Set.iUnion₂_add.description: The theorem establishes that the union of the sums of a family of sets and an additional set is equal to the sum of the union of the family of sets and the additional set.

Set.mul_iUnion₂.code:
Set.mul_iUnion₂.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Mul α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s * ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s * t i j
Set.mul_iUnion₂.description: The theorem states that the product of a set with the union of unions from a family of sets is equal to the union of unions formed by multiplying the set with each of the members of the inner sets.

Set.add_iUnion₂.code:
Set.add_iUnion₂.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Add α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s + ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s + t i j
Set.add_iUnion₂.description: The theorem states that the pointwise addition of a set and the union of sets indexed by multiple indices is equal to the union of the pointwise addition of the original set with each of the indexed sets.

Set.iInter_mul_subset.code:
Set.iInter_mul_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Mul α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋂ i, s i) * t ⊆ ⋂ i, s i * t
Set.iInter_mul_subset.description: The theorem demonstrates that the product of the intersection of a family of sets with another set is a subset of the intersection of the products of those sets with the same set.

Set.iInter_add_subset.code:
Set.iInter_add_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Add α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋂ i, s i) + t ⊆ ⋂ i, s i + t
Set.iInter_add_subset.description: The theorem states that the sum of an intersection of indexed sets with another set is a subset of the intersection of the indexed sets summed with that other set.

Set.mul_iInter_subset.code:
Set.mul_iInter_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Mul α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s * ⋂ i, t i ⊆ ⋂ i, s * t i
Set.mul_iInter_subset.description: The theorem states that the product of a set with the intersection of a collection of sets is a subset of the intersection of the products of that set with each individual set in the collection.

Set.add_iInter_subset.code:
Set.add_iInter_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Add α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s + ⋂ i, t i ⊆ ⋂ i, s + t i
Set.add_iInter_subset.description: The theorem states that the sum of a set with the intersection of a family of sets is a subset of the intersection of sums formed by adding the set to each of the individual sets in the family.

Set.iInter₂_mul_subset.code:
Set.iInter₂_mul_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Mul α]
  (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) (t : Set α) : (⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j) * t ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j * t
Set.iInter₂_mul_subset.description: The theorem states that the intersection of products formed by two indexed families of sets and a single set is a subset of the intersection of those same products with the single set.

Set.iInter₂_add_subset.code:
Set.iInter₂_add_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Add α]
  (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) (t : Set α) : (⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j) + t ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j + t
Set.iInter₂_add_subset.description: The theorem states that the sum of the intersection of a collection of sets with another set is a subset of the intersection of the sums of those sets with the other set.

Set.mul_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.mul_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Mul α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s * ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s * t i j
Set.mul_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the product of a set with the intersection of multiple sets is a subset of the intersection of the products of the first set with each of those sets.

Set.add_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.add_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Add α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s + ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s + t i j
Set.add_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the sum of a set with the intersection of family of intersections of sets is a subset of the intersection of the sum of the set with each of those sets.

Set.singletonMulHom_apply.code: Set.singletonMulHom_apply.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] (a : α) : singletonMulHom a = {a}
Set.singletonMulHom_apply.description: The theorem asserts that the multiplicative homomorphism from a singleton set results in a set containing only the single element of that singleton.

Set.singletonAddHom_apply.code: Set.singletonAddHom_apply.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] (a : α) : singletonAddHom a = {a}

`Pointwise`.

explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.
explanatories.Div.div: This defines an operation for performing division between two values of a type that supports division.

Set.sub.comment:

`Pointwise`.

explanatories.Set.image2: The image of a binary function, when applied to two sets, is defined as the resulting set of values obtained by applying the function to all pairs of elements from the sets.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.
explanatories.Set.div: This definition establishes the concept of pointwise division for sets, where each element in one set is divided by each element in another set.
explanatories.Div.div: This defines an operation for performing division between two values of a type that supports division.

Set.sub.description: This definition introduces the concept of pointwise subtraction for sets, where each element in one set has every element of another set subtracted from it.

Set.image2_div.code: Set.image2_div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : image2 Div.div s t = s / t

explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.
explanatories.Set.div: This definition establishes the concept of pointwise division for sets, where each element in one set is divided by each element in another set.
explanatories.Div.div: This defines an operation for performing division between two values of a type that supports division.

Set.image2_div.description: The theorem asserts that the image of the Cartesian product of two sets under division corresponds to the quotient of those two sets.

Set.image2_sub.code: Set.image2_sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : image2 Sub.sub s t = s - t

explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.
explanatories.Set.sub: This definition introduces the concept of pointwise subtraction for sets, where each element in one set has every element of another set subtracted from it.

Set.image2_sub.description: The theorem asserts that the image of the subtraction operation applied to two sets is equal to the difference of the first set and the second set.

Set.mem_div.code: Set.mem_div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} {a : α} : a ∈ s / t ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t, x / y = a
Set.mem_div.description: The theorem states that an element belongs to the set formed by dividing one set by another if and only if it can be expressed as the quotient of two elements, one from each of those sets.

Set.mem_sub.code: Set.mem_sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} {a : α} : a ∈ s - t ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t, x - y = a
Set.mem_sub.description: The theorem asserts that an element belongs to the set difference between two sets if and only if it can be expressed as the difference of two elements, one from each set.

Set.div_mem_div.code: Set.div_mem_div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} {a b : α} : a ∈ s → b ∈ t → a / b ∈ s / t
Set.div_mem_div.description: The theorem asserts that if an element belongs to one set and another element belongs to a second set, then the quotient of these two elements is in the quotient of the corresponding sets.

Set.sub_mem_sub.code: Set.sub_mem_sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} {a b : α} : a ∈ s → b ∈ t → a - b ∈ s - t
Set.sub_mem_sub.description: The theorem indicates that if an element belongs to one set and another element belongs to a second set, then the difference of the first element and the second element belongs to the difference of the two sets.

Set.image_div_prod.code: Set.image_div_prod.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : (fun x => x.1 / x.2) '' s ×ˢ t = s / t
Set.image_div_prod.description: The theorem establishes that the image of the product set formed by the division of pairs from one set by elements of another set is equal to the division of the first set by the second set.

Set.sub_image_prod.code: Set.sub_image_prod.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : (fun x => x.1 - x.2) '' s ×ˢ t = s - t
Set.sub_image_prod.description: The theorem states that the image of the product of two sets under the operation of subtracting the elements of one from the other equals the difference of those two sets.

Set.empty_div.code: Set.empty_div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s : Set α} : ∅ / s = ∅
Set.empty_div.description: The theorem asserts that dividing the empty set by any set results in the empty set.

Set.empty_sub.code: Set.empty_sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s : Set α} : ∅ - s = ∅
Set.empty_sub.description: The theorem establishes that the difference between the empty set and any set is still the empty set.

Set.div_empty.code: Set.div_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s : Set α} : s / ∅ = ∅
Set.div_empty.description: The theorem establishes that dividing any set by the empty set results in the empty set.

Set.sub_empty.code: Set.sub_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s : Set α} : s - ∅ = ∅
Set.sub_empty.description: The theorem confirms that subtracting the empty set from any set results in the empty set.

Set.div_eq_empty.code: Set.div_eq_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : s / t = ∅ ↔ s = ∅ ∨ t = ∅
Set.div_eq_empty.description: The theorem states that the division of one set by another results in an empty set if and only if at least one of the two sets is empty.

Set.sub_eq_empty.code: Set.sub_eq_empty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : s - t = ∅ ↔ s = ∅ ∨ t = ∅
Set.sub_eq_empty.description: The theorem states that the difference between two sets is empty if and only if at least one of the sets is also empty.
