Set.div_nonempty.description: The theorem states that the non-emptiness of the quotient of two sets is equivalent to both sets being non-empty.

Set.sub_nonempty.code: Set.sub_nonempty.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : (s - t).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty ∧ t.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.sub_nonempty.description: The theorem states that the non-emptiness of the difference between two sets is equivalent to both sets being non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.div.code: Set.Nonempty.div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : s.Nonempty → t.Nonempty → (s / t).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.div.description: The theorem asserts that if two sets are nonempty, then the set formed by dividing one of those sets by the other is also nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.sub.code: Set.Nonempty.sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : s.Nonempty → t.Nonempty → (s - t).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.sub.description: The theorem states that if two sets are nonempty, then their difference is also nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.of_div_left.code: Set.Nonempty.of_div_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : (s / t).Nonempty → s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_div_left.description: The theorem concludes that if the division of two sets is non-empty, then at least one of the original sets must also be non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.of_sub_left.code: Set.Nonempty.of_sub_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : (s - t).Nonempty → s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_sub_left.description: The theorem states that if the difference between two sets is nonempty, then the original set must also be nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.of_div_right.code: Set.Nonempty.of_div_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : (s / t).Nonempty → t.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_div_right.description: The theorem asserts that if the quotient of two sets is nonempty under a division operation, then the second set must also be nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.of_sub_right.code: Set.Nonempty.of_sub_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : (s - t).Nonempty → t.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_sub_right.description: The theorem states that if the difference between a set and another is nonempty, then the second set must also be nonempty.

Set.div_singleton.code: Set.div_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s : Set α} {b : α} : s / {b} = (fun x => x / b) '' s
Set.div_singleton.description: The theorem shows that dividing a set by a singleton set containing an element is equivalent to applying division by that element to each member of the original set.

Set.sub_singleton.code: Set.sub_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s : Set α} {b : α} : s - {b} = (fun x => x - b) '' s
Set.sub_singleton.description: The theorem states that removing a single element from a set is equivalent to applying a specific function to each element of the set, resulting in the image of the set under this transformation.

Set.singleton_div.code: Set.singleton_div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {t : Set α} {a : α} : {a} / t = (fun x x_1 => x / x_1) a '' t
Set.singleton_div.description: The theorem asserts that the set formed by dividing a singleton containing a specific element by another set is equivalent to the image of that element under the division operation applied to each element of the second set.

Set.singleton_sub.code: Set.singleton_sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {t : Set α} {a : α} : {a} - t = (fun x x_1 => x - x_1) a '' t
Set.singleton_sub.description: The theorem states that the difference between a singleton set containing an element and another set is equal to the image of that other set under the operation of subtraction from the singleton element.

Set.singleton_div_singleton.code: Set.singleton_div_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {a b : α} : {a} / {b} = {a / b}
Set.singleton_div_singleton.description: The theorem states that the division of two singleton sets results in a singleton set containing the quotient of their elements.

Set.singleton_sub_singleton.code: Set.singleton_sub_singleton.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {a b : α} : {a} - {b} = {a - b}
Set.singleton_sub_singleton.description: The theorem asserts that the difference between two singleton sets is equal to a singleton set containing the result of subtracting one element from the other.

Set.div_subset_div.code: Set.div_subset_div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ t₁ → s₂ ⊆ t₂ → s₁ / s₂ ⊆ t₁ / t₂
Set.div_subset_div.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another and a second set is also a subset of a third set, then the set formed by dividing the first set by the second set is a subset of the set formed by dividing the third set by the second set.

Set.sub_subset_sub.code: Set.sub_subset_sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ t₁ → s₂ ⊆ t₂ → s₁ - s₂ ⊆ t₁ - t₂
Set.sub_subset_sub.description: The theorem establishes that if one set is a subset of another, and a second set is also a subset of a third, then the difference of the first two sets is a subset of the difference of the second two sets.

Set.div_subset_div_left.code: Set.div_subset_div_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : t₁ ⊆ t₂ → s / t₁ ⊆ s / t₂
Set.div_subset_div_left.description: The theorem establishes that if one set is a subset of another, then the set formed by dividing a fixed set by the first set is also a subset of the set formed by dividing the same fixed set by the second set.

Set.sub_subset_sub_left.code: Set.sub_subset_sub_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : t₁ ⊆ t₂ → s - t₁ ⊆ s - t₂
Set.sub_subset_sub_left.description: The theorem asserts that if one set is a subset of another, then the difference of a third set with the first set is also a subset of its difference with the second set.

Set.div_subset_div_right.code: Set.div_subset_div_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₁ / t ⊆ s₂ / t
Set.div_subset_div_right.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then the quotient of the first set by a third set is also a subset of the quotient of the second set by the same third set.

Set.sub_subset_sub_right.code: Set.sub_subset_sub_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₁ - t ⊆ s₂ - t
Set.sub_subset_sub_right.description: The theorem asserts that if one set is a subset of another, then the set obtained by subtracting a third set from the first is also a subset of the set obtained by subtracting the same third set from the second.

Set.div_subset_iff.code: Set.div_subset_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t u : Set α} : s / t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, x / y ∈ u
Set.div_subset_iff.description: The theorem equates the condition that the quotient of one set by another is a subset of a third set with the statement that every element from the first set divided by every element from the second set belongs to the third set.

Set.sub_subset_iff.code: Set.sub_subset_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t u : Set α} : s - t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, x - y ∈ u
Set.sub_subset_iff.description: The theorem asserts that a set minus another set is a subset of a third set if and only if every element formed by subtracting elements from the first and second sets belongs to the third set.

Set.union_div.code: Set.union_div.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : (s₁ ∪ s₂) / t = s₁ / t ∪ s₂ / t
Set.union_div.description: The theorem establishes that the quotient of the union of two sets by another set is equal to the union of the quotients of each set by that same set.

Set.union_sub.code: Set.union_sub.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ∪ s₂ - t = s₁ - t ∪ (s₂ - t)
Set.union_sub.description: The theorem states that the difference of the union of two sets and a third set is equal to the union of the differences of each of the first two sets with the third set.

Set.div_union.code: Set.div_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s / (t₁ ∪ t₂) = s / t₁ ∪ s / t₂
Set.div_union.description: The theorem states that dividing a set by the union of two other sets is equivalent to the union of the divisions of the first set by each of the two sets.

Set.sub_union.code: Set.sub_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s - (t₁ ∪ t₂) = s - t₁ ∪ (s - t₂)
Set.sub_union.description: The theorem shows that the difference of a set from the union of two other sets is equal to the union of the differences of the first set from each of the two other sets.

Set.inter_div_subset.code: Set.inter_div_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ∩ s₂ / t ⊆ s₁ / t ∩ (s₂ / t)
Set.inter_div_subset.description: The theorem states that the intersection of two sets divided by another set is a subset of the intersection of each of the two sets divided by that same set.

Set.inter_sub_subset.code: Set.inter_sub_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ∩ s₂ - t ⊆ (s₁ - t) ∩ (s₂ - t)
Set.inter_sub_subset.description: The theorem states that the difference of the intersection of two sets and a third set is a subset of the intersection of the differences of the first two sets and that same third set.

Set.div_inter_subset.code: Set.div_inter_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s / (t₁ ∩ t₂) ⊆ s / t₁ ∩ (s / t₂)
Set.div_inter_subset.description: The theorem states that the set division of a set by the intersection of two other sets is included in the intersection of the divisions of the first set by each of the two sets.

Set.sub_inter_subset.code: Set.sub_inter_subset.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s - t₁ ∩ t₂ ⊆ (s - t₁) ∩ (s - t₂)
Set.sub_inter_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the difference of a set from the intersection of two other sets is a subset of the intersection of the differences of the set from each of the two sets.

Set.inter_div_union_subset_union.code:
Set.inter_div_union_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∩ s₂ / (t₁ ∪ t₂) ⊆ s₁ / t₁ ∪ s₂ / t₂
Set.inter_div_union_subset_union.description: The theorem states that the intersection of two sets divided by the union of two other sets is a subset of the union of the divisions of the two sets by each of the individual sets.

Set.inter_sub_union_subset_union.code:
Set.inter_sub_union_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∩ s₂ - (t₁ ∪ t₂) ⊆ s₁ - t₁ ∪ (s₂ - t₂)
Set.inter_sub_union_subset_union.description: The theorem establishes that the difference of the intersection of two sets and the union of two other sets is contained within the union of the differences of each intersecting set with the corresponding union set.

Set.union_div_inter_subset_union.code:
Set.union_div_inter_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  (s₁ ∪ s₂) / (t₁ ∩ t₂) ⊆ s₁ / t₁ ∪ s₂ / t₂
Set.union_div_inter_subset_union.description: The theorem asserts that the set formed by dividing the union of two sets by the intersection of two other sets is a subset of the union of the sets formed by dividing each of the first two sets by the corresponding second sets.

Set.union_sub_inter_subset_union.code:
Set.union_sub_inter_subset_union.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set α} :
  s₁ ∪ s₂ - t₁ ∩ t₂ ⊆ s₁ - t₁ ∪ (s₂ - t₂)
Set.union_sub_inter_subset_union.description: The theorem establishes that the difference between the union of two sets and the intersection of two other sets is a subset of the union of the difference of each set with their corresponding set.

Set.iUnion_div_left_image.code: Set.iUnion_div_left_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ s, (fun x => a / x) '' t = s / t
Set.iUnion_div_left_image.description: The theorem asserts that the image of the union of sets under division yields a result equivalent to the division of the first set by the second set.

Set.iUnion_sub_left_image.code: Set.iUnion_sub_left_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ s, (fun x => a - x) '' t = s - t
Set.iUnion_sub_left_image.description: The theorem asserts that the union of the images of a set under subtraction from each element of another set results in the difference between the two sets.

Set.iUnion_div_right_image.code: Set.iUnion_div_right_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Div α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ t, (fun x => x / a) '' s = s / t
Set.iUnion_div_right_image.description: The theorem proposes that the image of a set under division by each element of another set corresponds to the quotient of the first set by the second set.

Set.iUnion_sub_right_image.code: Set.iUnion_sub_right_image.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Sub α] {s t : Set α} : ⋃ a ∈ t, (fun x => x - a) '' s = s - t
Set.iUnion_sub_right_image.description: The theorem expresses that the union over the images of a set translated by the subtraction of elements from another set is equal to the original set with those elements removed.

Set.iUnion_div.code:
Set.iUnion_div.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Div α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋃ i, s i) / t = ⋃ i, s i / t
Set.iUnion_div.description: The theorem establishes that the division of the union of a collection of sets by another set is equal to the union of each set divided by that same set.

Set.iUnion_sub.code:
Set.iUnion_sub.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Sub α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋃ i, s i) - t = ⋃ i, s i - t
Set.iUnion_sub.description: The theorem states that the difference between the union of a family of sets and another set is equal to the union of the differences of each individual set in the family from that same set.

Set.div_iUnion.code:
Set.div_iUnion.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Div α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s / ⋃ i, t i = ⋃ i, s / t i
Set.div_iUnion.description: The theorem states that the division of a set by the union of a family of sets is equal to the union of the divisions of the set by each individual set in the family.

Set.sub_iUnion.code:
Set.sub_iUnion.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Sub α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s - ⋃ i, t i = ⋃ i, s - t i
Set.sub_iUnion.description: The theorem indicates that the difference between a set and the union of a collection of sets is equal to the union of the differences between the set and each individual set in the collection.

Set.iUnion₂_div.code:
Set.iUnion₂_div.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Div α] (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j) / t = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j / t
Set.iUnion₂_div.description: The theorem states that the division of the union of sets formed by iterating over two indices with respect to a division operation equals the union of the divided sets formed by the same indices.

Set.iUnion₂_sub.code:
Set.iUnion₂_sub.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Sub α] (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α)
  (t : Set α) : (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j) - t = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j - t
Set.iUnion₂_sub.description: The theorem asserts that the difference between the union of a family of sets and a given set is equal to the union of the differences between the individual sets in the family and the given set.

Set.div_iUnion₂.code:
Set.div_iUnion₂.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Div α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s / ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s / t i j
Set.div_iUnion₂.description: The theorem asserts that dividing a set by the union of sets indexed by two indices is equivalent to taking the union of the divisions of the original set by each of those indexed sets.

Set.sub_iUnion₂.code:
Set.sub_iUnion₂.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Sub α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s - ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s - t i j
Set.sub_iUnion₂.description: The theorem states that the difference between a set and the union of the unions of sets indexed by two collections is equal to the union of the differences of that set with each of the individual sets from the second union.

Set.iInter_div_subset.code:
Set.iInter_div_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Div α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋂ i, s i) / t ⊆ ⋂ i, s i / t
Set.iInter_div_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the intersection of the divisions of a collection of sets by another set is a subset of the division of the intersection of those sets by the same set.

Set.iInter_sub_subset.code:
Set.iInter_sub_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Sub α] (s : ι → Set α) (t : Set α) :
  (⋂ i, s i) - t ⊆ ⋂ i, s i - t
Set.iInter_sub_subset.description: The theorem states that the difference between the intersection of a collection of sets and another set is a subset of the intersection of the differences of each set in the collection and the other set.

Set.div_iInter_subset.code:
Set.div_iInter_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Div α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s / ⋂ i, t i ⊆ ⋂ i, s / t i
Set.div_iInter_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the division of a set by the intersection of a family of sets is a subset of the intersection of the divisions of that set by each individual set in the family.

Set.sub_iInter_subset.code:
Set.sub_iInter_subset.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} [Sub α] (s : Set α) (t : ι → Set α) :
  s - ⋂ i, t i ⊆ ⋂ i, s - t i
Set.sub_iInter_subset.description: The theorem demonstrates that the difference between a set and the intersection of a collection of sets is a subset of the intersection of the differences between that set and each of the individual sets in the collection.

Set.iInter₂_div_subset.code:
Set.iInter₂_div_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Div α]
  (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) (t : Set α) : (⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j) / t ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j / t
Set.iInter₂_div_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the division of the intersection of sets formed by applying a function over pairs of indices is a subset of the intersection of those sets divided by another set.

Set.iInter₂_sub_subset.code:
Set.iInter₂_sub_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Sub α]
  (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) (t : Set α) : (⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j) - t ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j - t
Set.iInter₂_sub_subset.description: The theorem states that the difference between the intersection of sets indexed by two parameters and another set is a subset of the intersection of the same indexed sets minus that other set.

Set.div_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.div_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Div α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s / ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s / t i j
Set.div_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the set formed by dividing a set by the intersection of sets indexed by two variables is a subset of the intersection of the sets formed by dividing the original set by each of the indexed sets.

Set.sub_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.sub_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [Sub α] (s : Set α)
  (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set α) : s - ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s - t i j
Set.sub_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the difference of a set and the intersection of a family of intersections of other sets is a subset of the intersection of the difference of the original set with each of those sets.

Set.NSMul.code: Set.NSMul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] [Add α] : SMul ℕ (Set α)
Set.NSMul.comment:
Repeated pointwise addition (not the same as pointwise repeated addition!) of a `Set`. See
note [pointwise nat action].
Set.NSMul.fullDefinition: protected def NSMul [Zero α] [Add α] : SMul ℕ (Set α) :=   ⟨nsmulRec⟩
Set.NSMul.description: This definition describes a natural number action on sets through repeated pointwise addition.

Set.NPow.code: Set.NPow.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [One α] [Mul α] : Pow (Set α) ℕ
Set.NPow.comment:
Repeated pointwise multiplication (not the same as pointwise repeated multiplication!) of a
`Set`. See note [pointwise nat action].

explanatories.npowRec: This definition describes a power function in a monoid that computes the product of an element multiplied by itself a specified number of times.

Set.NPow.fullDefinition: protected def NPow [One α] [Mul α] : Pow (Set α) ℕ :=   ⟨fun s n => npowRec n s⟩
Set.NPow.description: The definition describes a type of operation that performs repeated multiplication on sets of elements using natural numbers, effectively extending the concept of exponentiation to the context of sets.

Set.ZSMul.code: Set.ZSMul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] [Add α] [Neg α] : SMul ℤ (Set α)
Set.ZSMul.comment:
Repeated pointwise addition/subtraction (not the same as pointwise repeated
addition/subtraction!) of a `Set`. See note [pointwise nat action].
Set.ZSMul.fullDefinition: protected def ZSMul [Zero α] [Add α] [Neg α] : SMul ℤ (Set α) :=   ⟨zsmulRec⟩
Set.ZSMul.description: This definition describes a scalar multiplication operation for sets using integers, where the operation involves repeated pointwise addition and subtraction of the set elements.

Set.ZPow.code: Set.ZPow.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [One α] [Mul α] [Inv α] : Pow (Set α) ℤ
Set.ZPow.comment:
Repeated pointwise multiplication/division (not the same as pointwise repeated
multiplication/division!) of a `Set`. See note [pointwise nat action].

explanatories.npowRec: This definition describes a power function in a monoid that computes the product of an element multiplied by itself a specified number of times.
explanatories.zpowRec: This definition describes a function that computes the power of an element in a group for integer exponents, where positive exponents correspond to repeated multiplication and negative exponents represent taking the inverse of the element.

Set.ZPow.fullDefinition: protected def ZPow [One α] [Mul α] [Inv α] : Pow (Set α) ℤ :=   ⟨fun s n => zpowRec npowRec n s⟩
Set.ZPow.description: This definition introduces a concept for repeated pointwise multiplication or division of a set, utilizing integer exponents to describe its operations.

Set.semigroup.code: Set.semigroup.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Semigroup α] : Semigroup (Set α)
Set.semigroup.comment: `Set α` is a `Semigroup` under pointwise operations if `α` is.

explanatories.Set.mul: This definition establishes pointwise multiplication of sets as the set of all products formed by multiplying elements from two sets.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.mul: The theorem states that the product of two non-empty sets is also non-empty if both component sets are non-empty.
explanatories.Set.image2_assoc: The image of a function applied to the image of a binary function over two sets is equal to the image obtained by first applying another function to the first set and then applying the binary function to the second set and a third set, given a specific associative condition.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.

Set.semigroup.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def semigroup [Semigroup α] : Semigroup (Set α) :=   { Set.mul with mul_assoc := fun _ _ _ => image2_assoc mul_assoc }
Set.semigroup.description: The definition states that the collection of all subsets of a type equipped with an associative binary operation also forms a semigroup under the operation applied pointwise to the subsets.

Set.preimage_mul_right_one'.code: Set.preimage_mul_right_one'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Group α] {b : α} : (fun x => x * b⁻¹) ⁻¹' 1 = {b}

Set.preimage_add_right_zero'.code: Set.preimage_add_right_zero'.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [AddGroup α] {b : α} : (fun x => x + -b) ⁻¹' 0 = {b}

Set.iInter₂_vadd_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [VAdd α β]

Set.iInter₂_vadd_subset.description: The theorem states that the vector addition of the intersection of sets indexed by two indices with another set is a subset of the intersection of the same sets, each added to that set.

Set.smul_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.smul_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [SMul α β]
  (s : Set α) (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : s • ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s • t i j
Set.smul_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of a set with the intersection of sets indexed by two indices is a subset of the intersection of the scalar multiplications of the set with each of those indexed sets.

Set.vadd_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.vadd_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [VAdd α β]
  (s : Set α) (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : s +ᵥ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s +ᵥ t i j
Set.vadd_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem demonstrates that the vector addition of a set with the intersection of sets formed by varying indices is contained within the intersection of the vector addition of the original set with those varying sets.

Set.smul_set_subset_smul.code:
Set.smul_set_subset_smul.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {t : Set β} {a : α} {s : Set α} :
  a ∈ s → a • t ⊆ s • t
Set.smul_set_subset_smul.description: The theorem states that if an element belongs to a set, then the scalar multiplication of another set by that element is a subset of the scalar multiplication of the first set by the same other set.

Set.vadd_set_subset_vadd.code:
Set.vadd_set_subset_vadd.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {t : Set β} {a : α} {s : Set α} :
  a ∈ s → a +ᵥ t ⊆ s +ᵥ t
Set.vadd_set_subset_vadd.description: The theorem states that if an element belongs to a set, then the vector addition of that element with any set is a subset of the vector addition of the original set with that same set.

Set.iUnion_smul_set.code: Set.iUnion_smul_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : ⋃ a ∈ s, a • t = s • t
Set.iUnion_smul_set.description: The theorem states that the union of the scalar multiplication of each element in one set with another set is equal to the scalar multiplication of the first set with the second set.

Set.iUnion_vadd_set.code:
Set.iUnion_vadd_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
  ⋃ a ∈ s, a +ᵥ t = s +ᵥ t
Set.iUnion_vadd_set.description: The theorem establishes that the union of vector additions of each element in a set with another set is equal to the vector addition of that original set with the other set.

Set.image_smul.code: Set.image_smul.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {t : Set β} {a : α} : (fun x => a • x) '' t = a • t
Set.image_smul.description: The theorem asserts that the image of a set under scalar multiplication by a fixed element is equivalent to the scalar multiplication of that element with the entire set.

Set.image_vadd.code: Set.image_vadd.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {t : Set β} {a : α} : (fun x => a +ᵥ x) '' t = a +ᵥ t
Set.image_vadd.description: The theorem states that the image of a set under a vector addition operation, where a fixed vector is added to each element, is equal to the result of adding that fixed vector to the entire set.

Set.mem_smul_set.code:
Set.mem_smul_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {t : Set β} {a : α} {x : β} :
  x ∈ a • t ↔ ∃ y ∈ t, a • y = x
Set.mem_smul_set.description: The theorem states that an element belongs to the scalar multiplication of a set by an element if and only if there exists an element in the set such that the scalar multiplication of that element with the given scalar equals the element in question.

Set.mem_vadd_set.code:
Set.mem_vadd_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {t : Set β} {a : α} {x : β} :
  x ∈ a +ᵥ t ↔ ∃ y ∈ t, a +ᵥ y = x
Set.mem_vadd_set.description: The theorem establishes a condition for membership in the vector addition of a single element with a set, stating that an element belongs to this sum if and only if it can be expressed as the sum of that element and some other element from the set.

Set.smul_mem_smul_set.code:
Set.smul_mem_smul_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} {b : β} :
  b ∈ s → a • b ∈ a • s
Set.smul_mem_smul_set.description: The theorem states that if an element belongs to a set, then the scalar product of that element with another scalar also belongs to the scalar product of the set with the same scalar.

Set.vadd_mem_vadd_set.code:
Set.vadd_mem_vadd_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} {b : β} :
  b ∈ s → a +ᵥ b ∈ a +ᵥ s
Set.vadd_mem_vadd_set.description: The theorem asserts that if an element belongs to a set, then the vector addition of that element with another element from a vector space also belongs to the set formed by the vector addition of all elements in the original set with the same vector.

Set.smul_set_empty.code: Set.smul_set_empty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {a : α} : a • ∅ = ∅
Set.smul_set_empty.description: The theorem establishes that scaling the empty set by any scalar results in the empty set.

Set.vadd_set_empty.code: Set.vadd_set_empty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {a : α} : a +ᵥ ∅ = ∅
Set.vadd_set_empty.description: The theorem asserts that adding a specific element to an empty set results in an empty set.

Set.smul_set_eq_empty.code: Set.smul_set_eq_empty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} : a • s = ∅ ↔ s = ∅
Set.smul_set_eq_empty.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of a set by an element results in an empty set if and only if the original set is empty.

Set.vadd_set_eq_empty.code: Set.vadd_set_eq_empty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} : a +ᵥ s = ∅ ↔ s = ∅
Set.vadd_set_eq_empty.description: The theorem asserts that the pointwise vector addition of a set with a single element results in an empty set if and only if the original set is empty.

Set.smul_set_nonempty.code:
Set.smul_set_nonempty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} :
  (a • s).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.smul_set_nonempty.description: The theorem asserts that the scalar multiplication of a set by an element is nonempty if and only if the original set is nonempty.

Set.vadd_set_nonempty.code:
Set.vadd_set_nonempty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} :
  (a +ᵥ s).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.vadd_set_nonempty.description: The theorem asserts that a set formed by vector addition with a non-empty set is non-empty if and only if the original set is non-empty.

Set.smul_set_singleton.code: Set.smul_set_singleton.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {a : α} {b : β} : a • {b} = {a • b}
Set.smul_set_singleton.description: The theorem indicates that scaling a singleton set containing one element by a scalar results in a singleton set containing the scaled value of that element.

Set.vadd_set_singleton.code: Set.vadd_set_singleton.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {a : α} {b : β} : a +ᵥ {b} = {a +ᵥ b}
Set.vadd_set_singleton.description: The theorem asserts that adding a vector to a singleton set of another vector results in a set containing the sum of the original vector and the vector from the singleton set.

Set.smul_set_mono.code: Set.smul_set_mono.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} : s ⊆ t → a • s ⊆ a • t
Set.smul_set_mono.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then scaling both sets by a constant results in the scaled version of the first set being a subset of the scaled version of the second set.

Set.vadd_set_mono.code: Set.vadd_set_mono.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} : s ⊆ t → a +ᵥ s ⊆ a +ᵥ t
Set.vadd_set_mono.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then adding a fixed element to each set results in the first set being a subset of the second after the addition.

Set.smul_set_subset_iff.code:
Set.smul_set_subset_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a • s ⊆ t ↔ ∀ ⦃b : β⦄, b ∈ s → a • b ∈ t
Set.smul_set_subset_iff.description: The theorem states that a set obtained by scalar multiplication of another set is a subset of a third set if and only if every element in the original set, when multiplied by the scalar, is contained in the third set.

Set.vadd_set_subset_iff.code:
Set.vadd_set_subset_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a +ᵥ s ⊆ t ↔ ∀ ⦃b : β⦄, b ∈ s → a +ᵥ b ∈ t
Set.vadd_set_subset_iff.description: The theorem expresses that the sum of a vector and a set is contained within another set if and only if every element obtained by adding the vector to elements of the first set is included in the second set.

Set.smul_set_union.code:
Set.smul_set_union.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {t₁ t₂ : Set β} {a : α} :
  a • (t₁ ∪ t₂) = a • t₁ ∪ a • t₂
Set.smul_set_union.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of a set formed by the union of two other sets is equal to the union of the scalar multiplications of each individual set.

Set.vadd_set_union.code:
Set.vadd_set_union.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {t₁ t₂ : Set β} {a : α} :
  a +ᵥ (t₁ ∪ t₂) = a +ᵥ t₁ ∪ (a +ᵥ t₂)
Set.vadd_set_union.description: The theorem shows that the vector addition of a single element with the union of two sets is equal to the union of the vector additions of that element with each set separately.

Set.smul_set_inter_subset.code:
Set.smul_set_inter_subset.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {t₁ t₂ : Set β} {a : α} :
  a • (t₁ ∩ t₂) ⊆ a • t₁ ∩ a • t₂
Set.smul_set_inter_subset.description: The theorem shows that scaling the intersection of two sets by a scalar results in a set that is contained within the intersection of the scaled individual sets.

Set.vadd_set_inter_subset.code:
Set.vadd_set_inter_subset.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {t₁ t₂ : Set β} {a : α} :
  a +ᵥ t₁ ∩ t₂ ⊆ (a +ᵥ t₁) ∩ (a +ᵥ t₂)
Set.vadd_set_inter_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the intersection of a set translated by a vector is a subset of the intersection of the individually translated sets.

Set.smul_set_iUnion.code:
Set.smul_set_iUnion.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [SMul α β] (a : α) (s : ι → Set β) :
  a • ⋃ i, s i = ⋃ i, a • s i
Set.smul_set_iUnion.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of an element with the union of a collection of sets is equal to the union of the scalar multiplication of that element with each individual set in the collection.

Set.vadd_set_iUnion.code:
Set.vadd_set_iUnion.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [VAdd α β] (a : α) (s : ι → Set β) :
  a +ᵥ ⋃ i, s i = ⋃ i, a +ᵥ s i
Set.vadd_set_iUnion.description: The theorem asserts that the vector addition of a single element with the union of a family of sets is equal to the union of the vector additions of that element with each individual set in the family.

Set.smul_set_iUnion₂.code:
Set.smul_set_iUnion₂.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [SMul α β]
  (a : α) (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : a • ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, a • s i j
Set.smul_set_iUnion₂.description: The theorem states that scaling the union of sets by an element is equivalent to the union of the scaled individual sets.

Set.vadd_set_iUnion₂.code:
Set.vadd_set_iUnion₂.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [VAdd α β]
  (a : α) (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : a +ᵥ ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, a +ᵥ s i j
Set.vadd_set_iUnion₂.description: The theorem demonstrates that adding a fixed vector to the union of a family of sets is equivalent to taking the union of the sets after adding the same vector to each individual set within the family.

Set.smul_set_iInter_subset.code:
Set.smul_set_iInter_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [SMul α β] (a : α)
  (t : ι → Set β) : a • ⋂ i, t i ⊆ ⋂ i, a • t i
Set.smul_set_iInter_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of the intersection of a family of sets is a subset of the intersection of the scalar multiplication of each individual set in the family.

Set.vadd_set_iInter_subset.code:
Set.vadd_set_iInter_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [VAdd α β] (a : α)
  (t : ι → Set β) : a +ᵥ ⋂ i, t i ⊆ ⋂ i, a +ᵥ t i
Set.vadd_set_iInter_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the vector addition of an element with the intersection of a family of sets is contained within the intersection of the vector additions of that element with each set in the family.

Set.smul_set_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.smul_set_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6}
  [SMul α β] (a : α) (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : a • ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, a • t i j
Set.smul_set_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem states that scalar multiplication of the intersection of sets defined by a function is a subset of the intersection of the scalar multiplications of each set defined by that function.

Set.vadd_set_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.vadd_set_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6}
  [VAdd α β] (a : α) (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : a +ᵥ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, a +ᵥ t i j
Set.vadd_set_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem establishes that adding a vector to the intersection of sets defined by a function yields a set that is contained within the intersection of sets formed by adding the vector to each of those sets.

Set.Nonempty.smul_set.code:
Set.Nonempty.smul_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} :
  s.Nonempty → (a • s).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.smul_set.description: The theorem states that if a set is non-empty, then the scalar multiplication of that set by an element is also non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.vadd_set.code:
Set.Nonempty.vadd_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {s : Set β} {a : α} :
  s.Nonempty → (a +ᵥ s).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.vadd_set.description: The theorem states that if a set is non-empty, then the set formed by adding a fixed vector to each element of that set is also non-empty.

Set.op_smul_set_subset_mul.code: Set.op_smul_set_subset_mul.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t : Set α} {a : α} : a ∈ t → op a • s ⊆ s * t

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.op_smul_set_subset_mul.description: The theorem asserts that if an element belongs to one set, then the scalar multiplication of that element with another set is a subset of the product of the two sets.

Set.op_vadd_set_subset_add.code: Set.op_vadd_set_subset_add.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t : Set α} {a : α} : a ∈ t → AddOpposite.op a +ᵥ s ⊆ s + t

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.op_vadd_set_subset_add.description: The theorem asserts that if an element belongs to a set, then the vector addition of the additive inverse of that element with another set is a subset of the result obtained by adding the original set to the first set.

Set.iUnion_op_smul_set.code: Set.iUnion_op_smul_set.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] (s t : Set α) : ⋃ a ∈ t, op a • s = s * t

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.iUnion_op_smul_set.description: The theorem states that the union of a set scaled by elements from another set is equal to the product of the first set with the second set.

Set.iUnion_op_vadd_set.code: Set.iUnion_op_vadd_set.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] (s t : Set α) : ⋃ a ∈ t, AddOpposite.op a +ᵥ s = s + t

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.iUnion_op_vadd_set.description: The theorem states that the union of pointwise vector additions of a set with the elements of another set is equal to the pointwise vector addition of that set with the entire second set.

Set.mul_subset_iff_left.code: Set.mul_subset_iff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t u : Set α} : s * t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ a ∈ s, a • t ⊆ u
Set.mul_subset_iff_left.description: The theorem states that the product of one set with another is a subset of a third set if and only if the scaling of every element in the first set with the second set is also a subset of the third set.

Set.add_subset_iff_left.code: Set.add_subset_iff_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t u : Set α} : s + t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ a ∈ s, a +ᵥ t ⊆ u
Set.add_subset_iff_left.description: The theorem states that the sum of one set with another is a subset of a third set if and only if the addition of every element in the first set with the second set is also a subset of the third set.

Set.mul_subset_iff_right.code: Set.mul_subset_iff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] {s t u : Set α} : s * t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ b ∈ t, op b • s ⊆ u

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.mul_subset_iff_right.description: The theorem describes a condition under which the product of two sets is a subset of a third set in terms of the action of elements from the second set on the first set.

Set.add_subset_iff_right.code: Set.add_subset_iff_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] {s t u : Set α} : s + t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ b ∈ t, AddOpposite.op b +ᵥ s ⊆ u

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.add_subset_iff_right.description: The theorem establishes a condition for the sum of two sets to be a subset of a third set, which is equivalent to stating that for every element in the second set, the set formed by adding it to elements of the first set is contained in the third set.

Set.range_smul_range.code:
Set.range_smul_range.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_5} {κ : Type u_6} [SMul α β]
  (b : ι → α) (c : κ → β) : range b • range c = range fun p => b p.1 • c p.2
Set.range_smul_range.description: The theorem asserts that the image of the product of the ranges of two functions under scalar multiplication is equal to the range of the function that maps each pair of elements from these ranges to their scaled product.

Set.range_vadd_range.code:
Set.range_vadd_range.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_5} {κ : Type u_6} [VAdd α β]
  (b : ι → α) (c : κ → β) : range b +ᵥ range c = range fun p => b p.1 +ᵥ c p.2
Set.range_vadd_range.description: The theorem states that the sum of the ranges of two vector-valued functions is equal to the range of a new function formed by adding the outputs of the original functions for each input pair.

Set.smul_set_range.code:
Set.smul_set_range.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {ι : Sort u_5} (a : α) (f : ι → β) :
  a • range f = range fun i => a • f i

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.smul_set_range.description: The theorem asserts that the scalar multiplication of the range of a function is equivalent to the range of the function where each output is multiplied by the scalar.

Set.vadd_set_range.code:
Set.vadd_set_range.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VAdd α β] {ι : Sort u_5} (a : α) (f : ι → β) :
  a +ᵥ range f = range fun i => a +ᵥ f i

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Set.vadd_set_range.description: The theorem states that adding a fixed vector to the range of a function is equivalent to the range of the function applied to each element after adding the same vector.

Set.range_smul.code:
Set.range_smul.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SMul α β] {ι : Sort u_5} (a : α) (f : ι → β) :
  (range fun i => a • f i) = a • range f
Set.range_smul.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of a function's range is equal to the range of that function after applying the scalar multiplication to each element.
