explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Set.smul: The definition establishes pointwise scalar multiplication of two sets, resulting in a new set of products formed by multiplying each element from the first set with each element from the second set.
explanatories.SMul.smul: This expression defines a function that computes the product of two elements, where the types involved in the operation determine its specific meaning, particularly for left actions.
explanatories.Set.image_smul: The theorem asserts that the image of a set under scalar multiplication by a fixed element is equivalent to the scalar multiplication of that element with the entire set.
explanatories.Set.image_image: The image of a set obtained by applying one function followed by another is equal to the image obtained by directly applying the composite function to the original set.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.Set.image_id': The image of a set under the identity function is equal to the set itself.
explanatories.MulAction.mul_smul: This theorem states that the action of multiplying two elements behaves associatively with respect to both multiplication and the action on another element.
explanatories.Set.mulActionSet: This definition describes how a multiplicative action of a monoid on a type can induce a multiplicative action on the set of elements of that type.

Set.addActionSet.fullDefinition: @[to_additive       "An additive action of an additive monoid on a type `β` gives an additive action on `Set β`."] protected def mulActionSet [Monoid α] [MulAction α β] : MulAction α (Set β) where   mul_smul _ _ _ := by simp only [← image_smul, image_image, ← mul_smul]   one_smul _ := by simp only [← image_smul, one_smul, image_id']
Set.addActionSet.description: This definition establishes that an additive action of an additive monoid on a type creates an additive action on the set of that type.

Set.smulZeroClassSet.code: Set.smulZeroClassSet.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero β] [SMulZeroClass α β] : SMulZeroClass α (Set β)
Set.smulZeroClassSet.comment:
If scalar multiplication by elements of `α` sends `(0 : β)` to zero,
then the same is true for `(0 : Set β)`.

explanatories.Set.image_singleton: The image of a singleton set under a function is the singleton set containing the image of the sole element in the original set.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Set.singleton_zero: The theorem asserts that the set containing the single element zero is equal to the zero element defined by the type.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.

Set.smulZeroClassSet.fullDefinition: protected def smulZeroClassSet [Zero β] [SMulZeroClass α β] :     SMulZeroClass α (Set β) where   smul_zero _ := image_singleton.trans <| by rw [smul_zero, singleton_zero]
Set.smulZeroClassSet.description: This definition establishes that if scalar multiplication of elements in one type sends zero to zero in another type, then the same property holds for the zero set in that second type.

Set.distribSMulSet.code: Set.distribSMulSet.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddZeroClass β] [DistribSMul α β] : DistribSMul α (Set β)
Set.distribSMulSet.comment:
If the scalar multiplication `(· • ·) : α → β → β` is distributive,
then so is `(· • ·) : α → Set β → Set β`.

explanatories.Set.image_image2_distrib: The image of a function transformed by another function, when applied to the image of a binary function over two sets, is equal to the image of a corresponding transformed binary function applied to the images of the sets.

Set.distribSMulSet.fullDefinition: protected def distribSMulSet [AddZeroClass β] [DistribSMul α β] :     DistribSMul α (Set β) where   smul_add _ _ _ := image_image2_distrib <| smul_add _
Set.distribSMulSet.description: The definition establishes that if scalar multiplication is distributive for individual elements, then it is also distributive when applied to sets.

Set.distribMulActionSet.code:
Set.distribMulActionSet.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Monoid α] [AddMonoid β] [DistribMulAction α β] :
  DistribMulAction α (Set β)
Set.distribMulActionSet.comment:
A distributive multiplicative action of a monoid on an additive monoid `β` gives a distributive
multiplicative action on `Set β`.
Set.distribMulActionSet.fullDefinition: protected def distribMulActionSet [Monoid α] [AddMonoid β] [DistribMulAction α β] :     DistribMulAction α (Set β) where   smul_add := smul_add   smul_zero := smul_zero
Set.distribMulActionSet.description: This definition asserts that when there is a distributive multiplicative action of a monoid on an additive monoid, this structure can be extended to act on the set of elements from the additive monoid.

Set.mulDistribMulActionSet.code:
Set.mulDistribMulActionSet.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Monoid α] [Monoid β] [MulDistribMulAction α β] :
  MulDistribMulAction α (Set β)
Set.mulDistribMulActionSet.comment: A multiplicative action of a monoid on a monoid `β` gives a multiplicative action on `Set β`.

explanatories.Set.image_singleton: The image of a singleton set under a function is the singleton set containing the image of the sole element in the original set.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Set.image_image2_distrib: The image of a function transformed by another function, when applied to the image of a binary function over two sets, is equal to the image of a corresponding transformed binary function applied to the images of the sets.
explanatories.Set.singleton_one: The theorem states that the set containing the single element one is equal to the one element defined by the type.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.

Set.mulDistribMulActionSet.fullDefinition: protected def mulDistribMulActionSet [Monoid α] [Monoid β] [MulDistribMulAction α β] :     MulDistribMulAction α (Set β) where   smul_mul _ _ _ := image_image2_distrib <| smul_mul' _   smul_one _ := image_singleton.trans <| by rw [smul_one, singleton_one]
Set.mulDistribMulActionSet.description: The definition establishes that a multiplicative action of a monoid on another monoid induces a corresponding multiplicative action on the set of elements of that monoid.

Set.noZeroSMulDivisors_set.code:
Set.noZeroSMulDivisors_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMul α β]
  [NoZeroSMulDivisors α β] : NoZeroSMulDivisors α (Set β)

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.Set.smul_mem_smul_set: The theorem states that if an element belongs to a set, then the scalar product of that element with another scalar also belongs to the scalar product of the set with the same scalar.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.SMulCommClass.symm: This theorem demonstrates that if one scalar multiplication action commutes with another, then the second action also commutes with the first, highlighting the symmetry of this relationship.
explanatories.Eq.subst: This theorem states that if two values are equal and a certain property holds for one of them, then it also holds for the other.
explanatories.Set.zero_nonempty: The theorem asserts that the empty set is nonempty, which is a contradiction in conventional set theory.
explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.subset_zero_iff: The theorem establishes that a nonempty set is a subset of the empty set if and only if it is equal to the empty set.
explanatories.Set.not_subset: The assertion that a set is not a subset of another is equivalent to the existence of at least one element in the first set that is not contained in the second set.
explanatories.NoZeroSMulDivisors.eq_zero_or_eq_zero_of: This theorem states that if the product of a scalar and an element of a module is zero, then at least one of them must be zero.
explanatories.Eq.subset: Equality of two sets implies that one set is a subset of the other.
explanatories.Or.elim: This theorem establishes that if at least one of two propositions is true and both imply a third proposition, then the third proposition must also be true.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.of_image: If the image of a set under a function is nonempty, then the original set must also be nonempty.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

Set.noZeroSMulDivisors_set.fullDefinition: instance noZeroSMulDivisors_set [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMul α β] [NoZeroSMulDivisors α β] :     NoZeroSMulDivisors α (Set β) :=   ⟨fun {a s} h ↦ by     by_contra! H     have hst : (a • s).Nonempty := h.symm.subst zero_nonempty     rw [Ne, Ne, ← hst.of_image.subset_zero_iff, not_subset] at H     obtain ⟨ha, b, ht, hb⟩ := H     exact (eq_zero_or_eq_zero_of_smul_eq_zero <| h.subset <| smul_mem_smul_set ht).elim ha hb⟩
Set.noZeroSMulDivisors_set.description: The definition indicates that when a scalar type has no zero divisors and is used to scale sets, the resulting sets also do not have zero divisors.

Set.vsub.code: Set.vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] : VSub (Set α) (Set β)

explanatories.Set.image2: The image of a binary function, when applied to two sets, is defined as the resulting set of values obtained by applying the function to all pairs of elements from the sets.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.
explanatories.VSub.vsub: This expression defines a function that calculates the difference between two elements, with the operation being influenced by the types involved in the context of additive torsors.

Set.vsub.description: This definition establishes a vector subtraction operation for sets, allowing for the resulting set of differences between elements from two given sets.

Set.image2_vsub.code: Set.image2_vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} : image2 VSub.vsub s t = s -ᵥ t

explanatories.Set.Nonempty.image2: If both sets are non-empty, then the image of a binary function applied to those two sets is also non-empty.
explanatories.VSub.vsub: This expression defines a function that calculates the difference between two elements, with the operation being influenced by the types involved in the context of additive torsors.
explanatories.Set.vsub: This definition establishes a vector subtraction operation for sets, allowing for the resulting set of differences between elements from two given sets.

Set.image2_vsub.description: The theorem states that the set obtained by applying the vector subtraction operation to pairs of elements from two sets is equal to the difference of the two sets.

Set.image_vsub_prod.code:
Set.image_vsub_prod.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} :
  (fun x => x.1 -ᵥ x.2) '' s ×ˢ t = s -ᵥ t
Set.image_vsub_prod.description: The theorem states that the image of the pairwise vector subtraction of elements from two sets in a product space is equivalent to the vector subtraction of those two sets.

Set.mem_vsub.code:
Set.mem_vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a ∈ s -ᵥ t ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t, x -ᵥ y = a
Set.mem_vsub.description: The theorem establishes that an element belongs to the vector subtraction of two sets if and only if there exist elements in each set such that their vector subtraction equals that element.

Set.vsub_mem_vsub.code:
Set.vsub_mem_vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} {b c : β} (hb : b ∈ s)
  (hc : c ∈ t) : b -ᵥ c ∈ s -ᵥ t
Set.vsub_mem_vsub.description: The theorem proves that the difference of two vectors from respective sets belongs to the difference of those sets given that each vector is an element of its respective set.

Set.empty_vsub.code: Set.empty_vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] (t : Set β) : ∅ -ᵥ t = ∅
Set.empty_vsub.description: The theorem asserts that the vector subtraction of an empty set from any set results in an empty set.

Set.vsub_empty.code: Set.vsub_empty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] (s : Set β) : s -ᵥ ∅ = ∅
Set.vsub_empty.description: This theorem asserts that subtracting the empty set from any set results in the empty set.

Set.vsub_eq_empty.code: Set.vsub_eq_empty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} : s -ᵥ t = ∅ ↔ s = ∅ ∨ t = ∅
Set.vsub_eq_empty.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of two sets is empty if and only if at least one of the sets is empty.

Set.vsub_nonempty.code:
Set.vsub_nonempty.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} :
  (s -ᵥ t).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty ∧ t.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.vsub_nonempty.description: The theorem states that the difference of two sets is nonempty if and only if both sets are nonempty.

Set.Nonempty.vsub.code:
Set.Nonempty.vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} :
  s.Nonempty → t.Nonempty → (s -ᵥ t).Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.vsub.description: The theorem states that the difference of two non-empty sets, when the operation is defined appropriately, is also non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.of_vsub_left.code:
Set.Nonempty.of_vsub_left.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} :
  (s -ᵥ t).Nonempty → s.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_vsub_left.description: If the difference of two sets is non-empty, then at least one of those sets must also be non-empty.

Set.Nonempty.of_vsub_right.code:
Set.Nonempty.of_vsub_right.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} :
  (s -ᵥ t).Nonempty → t.Nonempty
Set.Nonempty.of_vsub_right.description: The theorem states that if the difference between two sets, when translated by a vector, is non-empty, then the second set must also be non-empty.

Set.vsub_singleton.code:
Set.vsub_singleton.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] (s : Set β) (b : β) :
  s -ᵥ {b} = (fun x => x -ᵥ b) '' s
Set.vsub_singleton.description: The theorem asserts that the vector subtraction of a set with a singleton set results in the image of that set under the operation of subtracting the element of the singleton.

Set.singleton_vsub.code:
Set.singleton_vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] (t : Set β) (b : β) :
  {b} -ᵥ t = (fun x => b -ᵥ x) '' t
Set.singleton_vsub.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of a singleton set from another set is equal to the image of the second set under the function that subtracts each element from the single element in the singleton.

Set.singleton_vsub_singleton.code: Set.singleton_vsub_singleton.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {b c : β} : {b} -ᵥ {c} = {b -ᵥ c}
Set.singleton_vsub_singleton.description: The theorem shows that the vector subtraction of two single-element sets results in a set containing the vector subtraction of their elements.

Set.vsub_subset_vsub.code:
Set.vsub_subset_vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  s₁ ⊆ s₂ → t₁ ⊆ t₂ → s₁ -ᵥ t₁ ⊆ s₂ -ᵥ t₂
Set.vsub_subset_vsub.description: The theorem asserts that if one set is a subset of another and a second set is also a subset of a third, then the vector subtraction of the first set from the second set will be a subset of the vector subtraction of the third from the fourth.

Set.vsub_subset_vsub_left.code:
Set.vsub_subset_vsub_left.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  t₁ ⊆ t₂ → s -ᵥ t₁ ⊆ s -ᵥ t₂
Set.vsub_subset_vsub_left.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then the vector subtraction of a fixed set from the first set is also a subset of the vector subtraction from the second set.

Set.vsub_subset_vsub_right.code:
Set.vsub_subset_vsub_right.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s₁ s₂ t : Set β} :
  s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₁ -ᵥ t ⊆ s₂ -ᵥ t
Set.vsub_subset_vsub_right.description: The theorem asserts that if one set is a subset of another, then subtracting the same vector from both sets results in a set that maintains this subset relation.

Set.vsub_subset_iff.code:
Set.vsub_subset_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} {u : Set α} :
  s -ᵥ t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ t, x -ᵥ y ∈ u
Set.vsub_subset_iff.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of one set from another is a subset of a third set if and only if the vector subtraction of every element from the first set with every element from the second set is contained in the third set.

Set.vsub_self_mono.code: Set.vsub_self_mono.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} (h : s ⊆ t) : s -ᵥ s ⊆ t -ᵥ t
Set.vsub_self_mono.description: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then the set of differences of the first set with itself is a subset of the set of differences of the second set with itself.

Set.union_vsub.code:
Set.union_vsub.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s₁ s₂ t : Set β} :
  s₁ ∪ s₂ -ᵥ t = s₁ -ᵥ t ∪ (s₂ -ᵥ t)
Set.union_vsub.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of the union of two sets with another set is equal to the union of the vector subtractions of each of the two sets with that same set.

Set.vsub_union.code:
Set.vsub_union.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  s -ᵥ (t₁ ∪ t₂) = s -ᵥ t₁ ∪ (s -ᵥ t₂)
Set.vsub_union.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of a set from the union of two other sets is equal to the union of the vector subtraction of the first set from each of the two sets individually.

Set.inter_vsub_subset.code:
Set.inter_vsub_subset.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s₁ s₂ t : Set β} :
  s₁ ∩ s₂ -ᵥ t ⊆ (s₁ -ᵥ t) ∩ (s₂ -ᵥ t)
Set.inter_vsub_subset.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of the intersection of two sets with a third set is a subset of the intersection of the vector subtractions of each set with that third set.

Set.vsub_inter_subset.code:
Set.vsub_inter_subset.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  s -ᵥ t₁ ∩ t₂ ⊆ (s -ᵥ t₁) ∩ (s -ᵥ t₂)
Set.vsub_inter_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the intersection of the vector subtraction of a set with two others is a subset of the intersection of the vector subtractions of the first set with each of the two sets.

Set.inter_vsub_union_subset_union.code:
Set.inter_vsub_union_subset_union.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  s₁ ∩ s₂ -ᵥ (t₁ ∪ t₂) ⊆ s₁ -ᵥ t₁ ∪ (s₂ -ᵥ t₂)
Set.inter_vsub_union_subset_union.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of the intersection of two sets from the union of two other sets is a subset of the union of the vector subtraction of each set from their respective sets.

Set.union_vsub_inter_subset_union.code:
Set.union_vsub_inter_subset_union.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : Set β} :
  s₁ ∪ s₂ -ᵥ t₁ ∩ t₂ ⊆ s₁ -ᵥ t₁ ∪ (s₂ -ᵥ t₂)
Set.union_vsub_inter_subset_union.description: The theorem states that the difference of the union of two sets with the intersection of two other sets is a subset of the union of the differences of each set with the corresponding set in the intersection.

Set.iUnion_vsub_left_image.code:
Set.iUnion_vsub_left_image.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} :
  ⋃ a ∈ s, (fun x => a -ᵥ x) '' t = s -ᵥ t
Set.iUnion_vsub_left_image.description: The theorem asserts that the union of translated images of a set under all elements of another set is equivalent to the subtraction of the latter set from the former set.

Set.iUnion_vsub_right_image.code:
Set.iUnion_vsub_right_image.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [VSub α β] {s t : Set β} :
  ⋃ a ∈ t, (fun x => x -ᵥ a) '' s = s -ᵥ t
Set.iUnion_vsub_right_image.description: The theorem states that the image of a set under subtraction from all elements of another set is equal to the set resulting from subtracting the second set from the first set.

Set.iUnion_vsub.code:
Set.iUnion_vsub.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [VSub α β] (s : ι → Set β) (t : Set β) :
  (⋃ i, s i) -ᵥ t = ⋃ i, s i -ᵥ t
Set.iUnion_vsub.description: The theorem demonstrates that the difference of the union of sets, when subjected to a vector subtraction operation, is equivalent to the union of the differences of each individual set with another set.

Set.vsub_iUnion.code:
Set.vsub_iUnion.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [VSub α β] (s : Set β) (t : ι → Set β) :
  s -ᵥ ⋃ i, t i = ⋃ i, s -ᵥ t i
Set.vsub_iUnion.description: The theorem asserts that the vector subtraction of a set from the union of a family of sets is equal to the union of the vector subtractions of that set from each individual set in the family.

Set.iUnion₂_vsub.code:
Set.iUnion₂_vsub.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [VSub α β]
  (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) (t : Set β) : (⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j) -ᵥ t = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s i j -ᵥ t
Set.iUnion₂_vsub.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of the union of sets indexed by two parameters with another set is equal to the union of the vector subtractions of each of those sets with the same set.

Set.vsub_iUnion₂.code:
Set.vsub_iUnion₂.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [VSub α β]
  (s : Set β) (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : s -ᵥ ⋃ i, ⋃ j, t i j = ⋃ i, ⋃ j, s -ᵥ t i j
Set.vsub_iUnion₂.description: The theorem shows that the difference between a set and the union of multiple sets can be expressed as the union of the differences between that set and each of the individual sets.

Set.iInter_vsub_subset.code:
Set.iInter_vsub_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [VSub α β] (s : ι → Set β)
  (t : Set β) : (⋂ i, s i) -ᵥ t ⊆ ⋂ i, s i -ᵥ t
Set.iInter_vsub_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the vector subtraction of a set from the intersection of a family of sets is a subset of the intersection of the individual vector subtractions of each set from the given set.

Set.vsub_iInter_subset.code:
Set.vsub_iInter_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} [VSub α β] (s : Set β)
  (t : ι → Set β) : s -ᵥ ⋂ i, t i ⊆ ⋂ i, s -ᵥ t i
Set.vsub_iInter_subset.description: The theorem states that the subtraction of a set from the intersection of a family of sets is contained within the intersection of the results of subtracting the set from each individual set in the family.

Set.iInter₂_vsub_subset.code:
Set.iInter₂_vsub_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [VSub α β]
  (s : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) (t : Set β) : (⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j) -ᵥ t ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s i j -ᵥ t
Set.iInter₂_vsub_subset.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of a set from the intersection of a family of sets is contained within the intersection of the vector subtracted sets, ensuring that the operation respects the defined structure of vector spaces.

Set.vsub_iInter₂_subset.code:
Set.vsub_iInter₂_subset.{u_2, u_3, u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {ι : Sort u_5} {κ : ι → Sort u_6} [VSub α β]
  (s : Set β) (t : (i : ι) → κ i → Set β) : s -ᵥ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, t i j ⊆ ⋂ i, ⋂ j, s -ᵥ t i j
Set.vsub_iInter₂_subset.description: The theorem states that the vector subtraction of a set from the intersection of a family of sets is a subset of the intersection of the vector subtractions of that set from each of the family of sets.

Set.image_smul_comm.code:
Set.image_smul_comm.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [SMul α β] [SMul α γ] (f : β → γ)
  (a : α) (s : Set β) : (∀ (b : β), f (a • b) = a • f b) → f '' (a • s) = a • f '' s
Set.image_smul_comm.description: The theorem indicates that if a function preserves the scalar multiplication structure between two sets, then applying that function to the scalar multiplication of one set equates to the scalar multiplication of the image of that set under the function.

Set.image_vadd_comm.code:
Set.image_vadd_comm.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [VAdd α β] [VAdd α γ] (f : β → γ)
  (a : α) (s : Set β) : (∀ (b : β), f (a +ᵥ b) = a +ᵥ f b) → f '' (a +ᵥ s) = a +ᵥ f '' s
Set.image_vadd_comm.description: The theorem states that if a function preserves the structure of vector addition, then the image of a set under this function, when shifted by a vector, equals the shift of the image of that set.

Set.image_smul_distrib.code:
Set.image_smul_distrib.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {F : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [MulOneClass α] [MulOneClass β]
  [FunLike F α β] [MonoidHomClass F α β] (f : F) (a : α) (s : Set α) : ⇑f '' (a • s) = f a • ⇑f '' s

explanatories.FunLike: This definition introduces a class that indicates certain terms can be coerced injectively into functions from one type to another.

Set.image_smul_distrib.description: The theorem demonstrates that the image of the scalar multiplication of a set transformed by a homomorphism equals the scalar multiplication of the image of that set transformed by the same homomorphism.

Set.image_vadd_distrib.code:
Set.image_vadd_distrib.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {F : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddZeroClass α] [AddZeroClass β]
  [FunLike F α β] [AddMonoidHomClass F α β] (f : F) (a : α) (s : Set α) : ⇑f '' (a +ᵥ s) = f a +ᵥ ⇑f '' s

explanatories.FunLike: This definition introduces a class that indicates certain terms can be coerced injectively into functions from one type to another.

Set.image_vadd_distrib.description: The theorem illustrates that applying a function to the translation of a set results in the same as translating the image of the set by the function and adding it to the image of a single element under the function.

Set.op_smul_set_smul_eq_smul_smul_set.code:
Set.op_smul_set_smul_eq_smul_smul_set.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [SMul αᵐᵒᵖ β]
  [SMul β γ] [SMul α γ] (a : α) (s : Set β) (t : Set γ) (h : ∀ (a : α) (b : β) (c : γ), (op a • b) • c = b • a • c) :
  (op a • s) • t = s • a • t

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.op_smul_set_smul_eq_smul_smul_set.description: The theorem demonstrates that under a specific operation involving scalar multiplication and the provided property, the scalar multiplication of one set followed by another is equivalent to the operation applying the first set's elements to the second set scaled by the same scalar.

Set.op_vadd_set_vadd_eq_vadd_vadd_set.code:
Set.op_vadd_set_vadd_eq_vadd_vadd_set.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [VAdd αᵃᵒᵖ β]
  [VAdd β γ] [VAdd α γ] (a : α) (s : Set β) (t : Set γ)
  (h : ∀ (a : α) (b : β) (c : γ), AddOpposite.op a +ᵥ b +ᵥ c = b +ᵥ (a +ᵥ c)) :
  AddOpposite.op a +ᵥ s +ᵥ t = s +ᵥ (a +ᵥ t)

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.op_vadd_set_vadd_eq_vadd_vadd_set.description: The theorem asserts that the sum of a set with an element shifted by an opposite addition operation results in the same as the individual addition of that element to the sum of the set with another set, under a specific condition on the addition operation.

Set.smul_zero_subset.code: Set.smul_zero_subset.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero β] [SMulZeroClass α β] (s : Set α) : s • 0 ⊆ 0
Set.smul_zero_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the set formed by scaling each element of a given set by zero is a subset of the set containing only zero.

Set.Nonempty.smul_zero.code:
Set.Nonempty.smul_zero.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero β] [SMulZeroClass α β] {s : Set α}
  (hs : s.Nonempty) : s • 0 = 0
Set.Nonempty.smul_zero.description: The theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of a non-empty set with the zero element results in the zero element.

Set.zero_mem_smul_set.code:
Set.zero_mem_smul_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero β] [SMulZeroClass α β] {t : Set β} {a : α}
  (h : 0 ∈ t) : 0 ∈ a • t
Set.zero_mem_smul_set.description: The theorem states that if zero is an element of a set, then the zero vector is also an element of the set scaled by any scalar.

Set.zero_mem_smul_set_iff.code:
Set.zero_mem_smul_set_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero β] [SMulZeroClass α β] {t : Set β} {a : α}
  [Zero α] [NoZeroSMulDivisors α β] (ha : a ≠ 0) : 0 ∈ a • t ↔ 0 ∈ t
Set.zero_mem_smul_set_iff.description: The theorem states that for a non-zero scalar and a set, the zero element is in the scalar multiplication of the set if and only if it is present in the original set.

Set.zero_smul_subset.code:
Set.zero_smul_subset.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMulWithZero α β] (t : Set β) :
  0 • t ⊆ 0
Set.zero_smul_subset.description: The theorem asserts that the scalar multiplication of zero with any set results in a subset that contains only the zero element.

Set.Nonempty.zero_smul.code:
Set.Nonempty.zero_smul.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMulWithZero α β] {t : Set β}
  (ht : t.Nonempty) : 0 • t = 0
Set.Nonempty.zero_smul.description: The theorem states that if a set is non-empty, then the scalar multiplication of that set by zero results in the set containing only the zero element.

Set.zero_smul_set.code:
Set.zero_smul_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMulWithZero α β] {s : Set β}
  (h : s.Nonempty) : 0 • s = 0
Set.zero_smul_set.comment: A nonempty set is scaled by zero to the singleton set containing 0.
Set.zero_smul_set.description: The theorem asserts that scaling a nonempty set by zero results in the singleton set containing only the zero element.

Set.zero_smul_set_subset.code:
Set.zero_smul_set_subset.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMulWithZero α β] (s : Set β) :
  0 • s ⊆ 0
Set.zero_smul_set_subset.description: The theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of a set by zero results in a subset that only includes the zero element.

Set.subsingleton_zero_smul_set.code:
Set.subsingleton_zero_smul_set.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMulWithZero α β]
  (s : Set β) : (0 • s).Subsingleton
Set.subsingleton_zero_smul_set.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of the zero element with any set results in a subset that contains at most one element.

Set.zero_mem_smul_iff.code:
Set.zero_mem_smul_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Zero α] [Zero β] [SMulWithZero α β] {s : Set α}
  {t : Set β} [NoZeroSMulDivisors α β] : 0 ∈ s • t ↔ 0 ∈ s ∧ t.Nonempty ∨ 0 ∈ t ∧ s.Nonempty

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

Set.zero_mem_smul_iff.description: The theorem states that the zero vector is in the scalar multiplication of two sets if and only if at least one of the sets contains the zero vector and the other set is nonempty.

Set.op_smul_set_mul_eq_mul_smul_set.code: Set.op_smul_set_mul_eq_mul_smul_set.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Semigroup α] (a : α) (s t : Set α) : op a • s * t = s * a • t

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.op_smul_set_mul_eq_mul_smul_set.description: The theorem states that scaling a set by an element and then multiplying it by another set is the same as multiplying the first set by the element and then scaling it by the second set.

Set.op_vadd_set_add_eq_add_vadd_set.code:
Set.op_vadd_set_add_eq_add_vadd_set.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [AddSemigroup α] (a : α) (s t : Set α) :
  AddOpposite.op a +ᵥ s + t = s + (a +ᵥ t)

explanatories.MulOpposite.op: This definition specifies a function that maps an element from a type to its corresponding element in the multiplicative opposite type.

Set.op_vadd_set_add_eq_add_vadd_set.description: The theorem asserts that the pointwise vector addition of a set with the opposite of a scalar followed by the addition of another set is equal to the addition of the first set with the scalar added to the second set.

Set.pairwiseDisjoint_smul_iff.code:
Set.pairwiseDisjoint_smul_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Mul α] [IsLeftCancelMul α] {s t : Set α} :
  (s.PairwiseDisjoint fun x => x • t) ↔ InjOn (fun p => p.1 * p.2) (s ×ˢ t)

explanatories.Set.PairwiseDisjoint: A set is considered pairwise disjoint under a function if the images of any two distinct elements from the set do not overlap.
explanatories.Set.InjOn: A function is considered injective on a set if it maps distinct elements of that set to distinct elements in the codomain.

Set.pairwiseDisjoint_smul_iff.description: The theorem states that a set is pairwise disjoint under pointwise scalar multiplication with another set if and only if the function defined by the product of pairs from the Cartesian product of the two sets is injective.

Set.pairwiseDisjoint_vadd_iff.code:
Set.pairwiseDisjoint_vadd_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [Add α] [IsLeftCancelAdd α] {s t : Set α} :
  (s.PairwiseDisjoint fun x => x +ᵥ t) ↔ InjOn (fun p => p.1 + p.2) (s ×ˢ t)

explanatories.Set.PairwiseDisjoint: A set is considered pairwise disjoint under a function if the images of any two distinct elements from the set do not overlap.
explanatories.Set.InjOn: A function is considered injective on a set if it maps distinct elements of that set to distinct elements in the codomain.

Set.pairwiseDisjoint_vadd_iff.description: The theorem states that a family of sets is pairwise disjoint under vector addition with a fixed set if and only if the function mapping pairs of elements from both sets to their sum is injective.

Set.smul_mem_smul_set_iff.code:
Set.smul_mem_smul_set_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {s : Set β} {a : α}
  {x : β} : a • x ∈ a • s ↔ x ∈ s
Set.smul_mem_smul_set_iff.description: The theorem states that an element obtained by scaling another element by a group action belongs to the scaled set if and only if the original element is a member of the set.

Set.vadd_mem_vadd_set_iff.code:
Set.vadd_mem_vadd_set_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {s : Set β} {a : α}
  {x : β} : a +ᵥ x ∈ a +ᵥ s ↔ x ∈ s
Set.vadd_mem_vadd_set_iff.description: The theorem indicates that an element obtained by adding a vector to a fixed vector is in the resulting set formed by adding that fixed vector to a set if and only if the original element is in the set.

Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem.code:
Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {A : Set β} {a : α}
  {x : β} : x ∈ a • A ↔ a⁻¹ • x ∈ A
Set.mem_smul_set_iff_inv_smul_mem.description: The theorem states that an element belongs to the scalar multiplication of a set by an element if and only if the inversely multiplied element belongs to the original set.

Set.mem_vadd_set_iff_neg_vadd_mem.code:
Set.mem_vadd_set_iff_neg_vadd_mem.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {A : Set β}
  {a : α} {x : β} : x ∈ a +ᵥ A ↔ -a +ᵥ x ∈ A
Set.mem_vadd_set_iff_neg_vadd_mem.description: The theorem states that an element belongs to the sum of a group element and a set if and only if the negation of that group element added to the element is contained within the set.

Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff.code:
Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {A : Set β} {a : α}
  {x : β} : x ∈ a⁻¹ • A ↔ a • x ∈ A
Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff.description: This theorem states that an element is in the set formed by scaling another set by the inverse of an element if and only if scaling that element by the original element results in a member of the set.

Set.mem_neg_vadd_set_iff.code:
Set.mem_neg_vadd_set_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {A : Set β} {a : α}
  {x : β} : x ∈ -a +ᵥ A ↔ a +ᵥ x ∈ A
Set.mem_neg_vadd_set_iff.description: The theorem provides a condition indicating that an element belongs to the vector addition of the negation of an element with a set if and only if the addition of the original element with that element belongs to the set.

Set.preimage_smul.code:
Set.preimage_smul.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] (a : α) (t : Set β) :
  (fun x => a • x) ⁻¹' t = a⁻¹ • t
Set.preimage_smul.description: The theorem establishes that the preimage under scalar multiplication by an element from a group of a set is equivalent to the scalar multiplication of that set by the inverse of the element.

Set.preimage_vadd.code:
Set.preimage_vadd.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] (a : α) (t : Set β) :
  (fun x => a +ᵥ x) ⁻¹' t = -a +ᵥ t
Set.preimage_vadd.description: The theorem states that the preimage of a set under the operation of vector addition with a fixed vector is equivalent to translating that set back by the negative of the fixed vector.

Set.preimage_smul_inv.code:
Set.preimage_smul_inv.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] (a : α) (t : Set β) :
  (fun x => a⁻¹ • x) ⁻¹' t = a • t
Set.preimage_smul_inv.description: The theorem states that the preimage of a set under scalar multiplication by the inverse of an element is equal to the result of scalar multiplication of that set by the element itself.

Set.preimage_vadd_neg.code:
Set.preimage_vadd_neg.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] (a : α) (t : Set β) :
  (fun x => -a +ᵥ x) ⁻¹' t = a +ᵥ t
Set.preimage_vadd_neg.description: The theorem shows that the preimage of a set under the transformation of adding the negation of an element is equal to the result of adding that element to the original set.

Set.set_smul_subset_set_smul_iff.code:
Set.set_smul_subset_set_smul_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {A B : Set β}
  {a : α} : a • A ⊆ a • B ↔ A ⊆ B
Set.set_smul_subset_set_smul_iff.description: The theorem states that multiplying a set by an element preserves the subset relationship if and only if the original sets maintain the same subset relationship without the scalar multiplication.

Set.set_vadd_subset_set_vadd_iff.code:
Set.set_vadd_subset_set_vadd_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {A B : Set β}
  {a : α} : a +ᵥ A ⊆ a +ᵥ B ↔ A ⊆ B
Set.set_vadd_subset_set_vadd_iff.description: The theorem describes a condition where the translated version of one set by a vector addition is a subset of the translated version of another set if and only if the first set itself is a subset of the second set.

Set.set_smul_subset_iff.code:
Set.set_smul_subset_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {A B : Set β} {a : α} :
  a • A ⊆ B ↔ A ⊆ a⁻¹ • B
Set.set_smul_subset_iff.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of a set by an element is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the scalar multiplication of the inverse of that element with the second set.

Set.set_vadd_subset_iff.code:
Set.set_vadd_subset_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {A B : Set β} {a : α} :
  a +ᵥ A ⊆ B ↔ A ⊆ -a +ᵥ B
Set.set_vadd_subset_iff.description: The theorem states that the vector addition of a set to a single element is a subset of another set if and only if the original set is a subset of the set obtained by subtracting that element from the vector addition of the second set.

Set.subset_set_smul_iff.code:
Set.subset_set_smul_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {A B : Set β} {a : α} :
  A ⊆ a • B ↔ a⁻¹ • A ⊆ B
Set.subset_set_smul_iff.description: The theorem establishes a condition for set inclusion under scalar multiplication, stating that a set is a subset of the scalar multiplication of another set if and only if applying the inverse scalar multiplication to the first set yields a subset of the second set.

Set.subset_set_vadd_iff.code:
Set.subset_set_vadd_iff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {A B : Set β} {a : α} :
  A ⊆ a +ᵥ B ↔ -a +ᵥ A ⊆ B
Set.subset_set_vadd_iff.description: The theorem states that a set is a subset of the translation of another set by a vector if and only if the translated inverse of the first set is a subset of the second set.

Set.smul_set_inter.code:
Set.smul_set_inter.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a • (s ∩ t) = a • s ∩ a • t
Set.smul_set_inter.description: The theorem demonstrates that the scalar multiplication of the intersection of two sets is equal to the intersection of the scalar multiplications of each set.

Set.vadd_set_inter.code:
Set.vadd_set_inter.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a +ᵥ s ∩ t = (a +ᵥ s) ∩ (a +ᵥ t)
Set.vadd_set_inter.description: The theorem states that the vector addition of a set with a vector is the same as the intersection of the vector addition of that set with another set.

Set.smul_set_sdiff.code:
Set.smul_set_sdiff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a • (s \ t) = a • s \ a • t
Set.smul_set_sdiff.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of a set difference results in the difference of the scalar multiplications of the individual sets.

Set.vadd_set_sdiff.code:
Set.vadd_set_sdiff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a +ᵥ s \ t = (a +ᵥ s) \ (a +ᵥ t)
Set.vadd_set_sdiff.description: The theorem asserts that the difference between a set obtained by vector addition with a single element and another set is equal to the difference of the two resulting sets obtained by vector addition with that same element.

Set.smul_set_symmDiff.code:
Set.smul_set_symmDiff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a • symmDiff s t = symmDiff (a • s) (a • t)
Set.smul_set_symmDiff.description: The theorem establishes that scaling the symmetric difference of two sets by a scalar results in the symmetric difference of the scaled versions of those sets.

Set.vadd_set_symmDiff.code:
Set.vadd_set_symmDiff.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {s t : Set β} {a : α} :
  a +ᵥ symmDiff s t = symmDiff (a +ᵥ s) (a +ᵥ t)
Set.vadd_set_symmDiff.description: This theorem states that adding a vector to the symmetric difference of two sets results in the symmetric difference of the sets each translated by that vector.

Set.smul_set_univ.code: Set.smul_set_univ.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {a : α} : a • univ = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.smul_set_univ.description: The theorem states that the scalar multiplication of any element with the universal set results in the universal set itself.

Set.vadd_set_univ.code: Set.vadd_set_univ.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [AddGroup α] [AddAction α β] {a : α} : a +ᵥ univ = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.vadd_set_univ.description: The theorem states that adding a specific element to the universal set results in the universal set remaining unchanged.

Set.smul_univ.code:
Set.smul_univ.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [Group α] [MulAction α β] {s : Set α} (hs : s.Nonempty) :
  s • univ = univ

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.

Set.smul_univ.description: The theorem asserts that if a non-empty set is scaled by a group action on the universal set, the result is the universal set itself.

Set.vadd_univ.code:

Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff₀.code:

Set.set_smul_subset_set_smul_iff₀.code:

  (hs : (fun x => x ^ n) ⁻¹' s = s) {g : G} {j : ℕ} (hg : g ^ n ^ j = 1) : g • s = s
smul_eq_self_of_preimage_zpow_eq_self.comment:
Let `n : ℤ` and `s` a subset of a commutative group `G` that is invariant under preimage for
the map `x ↦ x^n`. Then `s` is invariant under the pointwise action of the subgroup of elements
`g : G` such that `g^(n^j) = 1` for some `j : ℕ`. (This subgroup is called the Prüfer subgroup when
 `G` is the `Circle` and `n` is prime.)

smul_eq_self_of_preimage_zpow_eq_self.description: The theorem states that if a subset of a commutative group is invariant under a specific power map and if an element raised to a certain power equals the identity, then the action of that element on the subset does not change it.

vadd_eq_self_of_preimage_zsmul_eq_self.comment:
Let `n : ℤ` and `s` a subset of an additive commutative group `G` that is invariant
under preimage for the map `x ↦ n • x`. Then `s` is invariant under the pointwise action of
the additive subgroup of elements `g : G` such that `(n^j) • g = 0` for some `j : ℕ`.
(This additive subgroup is called the Prüfer subgroup when `G` is the `AddCircle` and `n` is
prime.)

vadd_eq_self_of_preimage_zsmul_eq_self.description: The theorem asserts that if a subset of an additive commutative group is invariant under a specific scalar multiplication and if an element multiplied by that scalar raised to a certain power equals zero, then the addition of that element to the subset does not alter it.

Set.sigma_diff_sigma.description: The difference between two indexed sums of sets is equal to the union of the indexed sum of the first set with the difference of the second set and the indexed sum of the complement of the first set with the original second set.

Set.iUnionLift.code:
Set.iUnionLift.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_2} {β : Sort u_3} (S : ι → Set α) (f : (i : ι) → ↑(S i) → β) :
  (∀ (i j : ι) (x : α) (hxi : x ∈ S i) (hxj : x ∈ S j), f i ⟨x, hxi⟩ = f j ⟨x, hxj⟩) →
    (T : Set α) → T ⊆ iUnion S → ↑T → β
Set.iUnionLift.comment:
Given a union of sets `iUnion S`, define a function on the Union by defining
it on each component, and proving that it agrees on the intersections.

explanatories.Classical.indefiniteDescription: An indefinite description associates a property with an existing element that satisfies that property, resulting in a dependent type containing that element.
explanatories.Set.mem_iUnion: An element belongs to the union of a collection of sets if and only if it is an element of at least one set within that collection.
explanatories.Subtype.prop: This theorem asserts that for a specific subtype, the property defining the subtype holds when applied to its element.

Set.iUnionLift.fullDefinition: noncomputable def iUnionLift (S : ι → Set α) (f : ∀ i, S i → β)     (_ : ∀ (i j) (x : α) (hxi : x ∈ S i) (hxj : x ∈ S j), f i ⟨x, hxi⟩ = f j ⟨x, hxj⟩) (T : Set α)     (hT : T ⊆ iUnion S) (x : T) : β :=   let i := Classical.indefiniteDescription _ (mem_iUnion.1 (hT x.prop))   f i ⟨x, i.prop⟩
Set.iUnionLift.description: This definition allows the construction of a function on the union of a collection of sets by specifying its values on each set and ensuring that these values are consistent on shared elements of intersecting sets.

Set.iUnionLift_mk.description: This theorem establishes that if an element belongs to a set within a union of collections, then the value assigned to that element using a specified function agrees with the value defined on the union.

explanatories.Set.inclusion: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.

Set.iUnionLift_inclusion.description: This theorem asserts that when an element from a set within a union is included in a larger set, the value assigned to that element using a specified function matches the value defined for the original set.

Set.iUnionLift_of_mem.description: This theorem states that if an element belongs to a set within a union and is also included in a larger set, then the value assigned to that element using a specified function corresponds to the value defined for the set containing that element.

Set.iUnionLift_const.comment:
`iUnionLift_const` is useful for proving that `iUnionLift` is a homomorphism
of algebraic structures when defined on the Union of algebraic subobjects.
For example, it could be used to prove that the lift of a collection
of group homomorphisms on a union of subgroups preserves `1`.
Set.iUnionLift_const.description: This theorem demonstrates that when a constant value is assigned to all elements from a union of sets using a specified function, the result remains consistent across the entire union, providing a basis for proving homomorphism properties in algebraic structures.

Set.iUnionLift_unary.comment:
`iUnionLift_unary` is useful for proving that `iUnionLift` is a homomorphism
of algebraic structures when defined on the Union of algebraic subobjects.
For example, it could be used to prove that the lift of a collection
of linear_maps on a union of submodules preserves scalar multiplication.

explanatories.Set.inclusion: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.

Set.iUnionLift_unary.description: This theorem demonstrates that under certain conditions, applying a specified transformation to the output of a function defined on a union of sets will result in the same transformation applied to the output of that function for any element within those sets.

Set.iUnionLift_binary.code:
Set.iUnionLift_binary.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_2} {β : Sort u_3} {S : ι → Set α}
  {f : (i : ι) → ↑(S i) → β} {hf : ∀ (i j : ι) (x : α) (hxi : x ∈ S i) (hxj : x ∈ S j), f i ⟨x, hxi⟩ = f j ⟨x, hxj⟩}
  {T : Set α} {hT : T ⊆ iUnion S} (hT' : T = iUnion S) (dir : Directed (fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1) S) (op : ↑T → ↑T → ↑T)
  (opi : (i : ι) → ↑(S i) → ↑(S i) → ↑(S i))
  (hopi : ∀ (i : ι) (x y : ↑(S i)), inclusion ⋯ (opi i x y) = op (inclusion ⋯ x) (inclusion ⋯ y)) (opβ : β → β → β)
  (h : ∀ (i : ι) (x y : ↑(S i)), f i (opi i x y) = opβ (f i x) (f i y)) (x y : ↑T) :
  iUnionLift S f hf T ⋯ (op x y) = opβ (iUnionLift S f hf T ⋯ x) (iUnionLift S f hf T ⋯ y)
Set.iUnionLift_binary.comment:
`iUnionLift_binary` is useful for proving that `iUnionLift` is a homomorphism
of algebraic structures when defined on the Union of algebraic subobjects.
For example, it could be used to prove that the lift of a collection
of group homomorphisms on a union of subgroups preserves `*`.

explanatories.Set.inclusion: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.
explanatories.Directed: A family of elements is considered directed with respect to a given relation if there exists an element that is greater than or equal to every pair in the family.

Set.iUnionLift_binary.description: This theorem establishes that under certain conditions, combining two elements from a union of sets using a specified binary operation will yield the same result as applying that operation to the outputs of a function defined on those elements, thus supporting the homomorphism properties of algebraic structures.

Set.liftCover.code:
Set.liftCover.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Sort u_2} {β : Sort u_3} (S : ι → Set α) (f : (i : ι) → ↑(S i) → β)
  (hf : ∀ (i j : ι) (x : α) (hxi : x ∈ S i) (hxj : x ∈ S j), f i ⟨x, hxi⟩ = f j ⟨x, hxj⟩) (hS : iUnion S = univ)
  (a : α) : β
Set.liftCover.comment:
Glue together functions defined on each of a collection `S` of sets that cover a type. See
also `Set.iUnionLift`.

explanatories.Set.iUnion: A function that constructs the union of a collection of sets indexed by a family of indices.
explanatories.Set.iUnionLift: This definition allows the construction of a function on the union of a collection of sets by specifying its values on each set and ensuring that these values are consistent on shared elements of intersecting sets.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Eq.subset: Equality of two sets implies that one set is a subset of the other.
explanatories.trivial: This theorem provides a proof that a trivial proposition affirming the truth of the statement "True" is indeed true.

Set.liftCover.fullDefinition: noncomputable def liftCover (S : ι → Set α) (f : ∀ i, S i → β)     (hf : ∀ (i j) (x : α) (hxi : x ∈ S i) (hxj : x ∈ S j), f i ⟨x, hxi⟩ = f j ⟨x, hxj⟩)     (hS : iUnion S = univ) (a : α) : β :=   iUnionLift S f hf univ hS.symm.subset ⟨a, trivial⟩
Set.liftCover.description: This definition provides a way to combine functions defined on a collection of sets that cover an entire type, ensuring that these functions agree on overlapping elements.

explanatories.Set.iUnion: A function that constructs the union of a collection of sets indexed by a family of indices.

Set.liftCover_coe.description: This theorem asserts that when the union of a collection of sets equals the universal set, the function defined on the sets can be retrieved from an element in one of the sets using the corresponding value from that function.

explanatories.Set.iUnion: A function that constructs the union of a collection of sets indexed by a family of indices.

Set.liftCover_of_mem.description: This theorem states that when an element is from a specified set that entirely covers a universal set, the value assigned to that element using a defined function matches the value for that set.

explanatories.Set.iUnion: A function that constructs the union of a collection of sets indexed by a family of indices.

explanatories.Set.inclusion: The inclusion function maps each element of a subset to its corresponding element in a larger set, assuming the subset is contained within the larger set.

Set.preimage_iUnionLift.description: This theorem establishes that the preimage of a set under a function defined on the union of collections of sets can be expressed in terms of the preimages of the individual sets within that union and their corresponding functions.

Set.monad.comment:
The `Set` functor is a monad.

This is not a global instance because it does not have computational content,
so it does not make much sense using `do` notation in general.
Plus, this would cause monad-related coercions and monad lifting logic to become activated.
Either use `attribute [local instance] Set.monad` to make it be a local instance
or use `SetM.run do ...` when `do` notation is wanted.

explanatories.Set.seq: The sequence of a set of functions applied to another set consists of all values that result from applying each function to each element of the second set.
explanatories.Bind.bind: The bind operation allows for chaining operations in a context by taking a value from that context and applying a function to it that returns a new value within the same context.
explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.
explanatories.Seq.seq: A sequence application operation allows for taking a sequence of functions and applying them lazily to a sequence of arguments to produce a new sequence of results.
explanatories.Pure.pure: The operation produces a monadic action that encapsulates a given value without altering it.

Set.monad.fullDefinition: protected def monad : Monad.{u} Set where   pure a := {a}   bind s f := ⋃ i ∈ s, f i   seq s t := Set.seq s (t ())   map := Set.image
Set.monad.description: The set functor is classified as a monad, which encapsulates a structure that allows for certain operations and compositions within the context of set theory.

Set.bind_def.code: Set.bind_def.{u} {α β : Type u} {s : Set α} {f : α → Set β} : s >>= f = ⋃ i ∈ s, f i
Set.bind_def.description: The bind operation for the set functor yields the union of the images of elements in a set when a function is applied to them.

Set.fmap_eq_image.code: Set.fmap_eq_image.{u} {α β : Type u} {s : Set α} (f : α → β) : f <$> s = f '' s
Set.fmap_eq_image.description: The fmap operation for the set functor is defined to be equal to the image of the set when a function is applied to its elements.

Set.seq_eq_set_seq.description: The sequence of a set of functions applied to a set of values is equivalent to the result obtained by applying the set of functions directly to that set of values.

Set.pure_def.code: Set.pure_def.{u} {α : Type u} (a : α) : pure a = {a}

explanatories.Pure.pure: The operation produces a monadic action that encapsulates a given value without altering it.

Set.pure_def.description: The pure operation for the set functor encapsulates a value by creating a singleton set containing that value.

explanatories.Set.seq: The sequence of a set of functions applied to another set consists of all values that result from applying each function to each element of the second set.
explanatories.Seq.seq: A sequence application operation allows for taking a sequence of functions and applying them lazily to a sequence of arguments to produce a new sequence of results.

SetSemiring.comment:

multiplication `*` as "multiplication".
SetSemiring.fullDefinition: def SetSemiring (α : Type*) : Type _ :=   Set α

explanatories.SetSemiring: This defines a set that has a semiring structure with union as addition and pointwise multiplication.
explanatories.Equiv.refl: This definition states that every type is self-equivalent, meaning it has an equivalence relation to itself.

Set.up.fullDefinition: protected def Set.up : Set α ≃ SetSemiring α :=   Equiv.refl _
Set.up.description: This defines an isomorphism between the set of elements in a type and its corresponding semiring structure.

SetSemiring.down.comment: The identity function `SetSemiring α → Set α`.

explanatories.Equiv.refl: This definition states that every type is self-equivalent, meaning it has an equivalence relation to itself.

explanatories.Set.up: This defines an isomorphism between the set of elements in a type and its corresponding semiring structure.

Set.sups_subset_left.code: Set.sups_subset_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : t₁ ⊆ t₂ → s ⊻ t₁ ⊆ s ⊻ t₂
Set.sups_subset_left.description: This theorem establishes that if one set is a subset of another, then the supremum of that set with a third set is also a subset of the supremum with the corresponding second set.

Set.sups_subset_right.code: Set.sups_subset_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : s₁ ⊆ s₂ → s₁ ⊻ t ⊆ s₂ ⊻ t
Set.sups_subset_right.description: This theorem establishes that if one set is a subset of another, then the supremum of that set with a third set is also a subset of the supremum of the second set with the same third set.

Set.image_subset_sups_left.code:

Set.image_subset_sups_right.code:
Set.image_subset_sups_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] {s t : Set α} {a : α} :

Set.sups_subset_iff.code: Set.sups_subset_iff.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] {s t u : Set α} : s ⊻ t ⊆ u ↔ ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ t, a ⊔ b ∈ u

Set.Nonempty.of_sups_right.code: Set.Nonempty.of_sups_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] {s t : Set α} : (s ⊻ t).Nonempty → t.Nonempty

Set.sups_union_left.code: Set.sups_union_left.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] {s₁ s₂ t : Set α} : (s₁ ∪ s₂) ⊻ t = s₁ ⊻ t ∪ s₂ ⊻ t

Set.sups_inter_subset_right.code: Set.sups_inter_subset_right.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] {s t₁ t₂ : Set α} : s ⊻ (t₁ ∩ t₂) ⊆ s ⊻ t₁ ∩ s ⊻ t₂

Set.iUnion_image_sup_left.code:

Set.sups_right_comm.code: Set.sups_right_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] (s t u : Set α) : s ⊻ t ⊻ u = s ⊻ u ⊻ t

Set.sups_sups_sups_comm.code: Set.sups_sups_sups_comm.{u_2} {α : Type u_2} [SemilatticeSup α] (s t u v : Set α) : s ⊻ t ⊻ (u ⊻ v) = s ⊻ u ⊻ (t ⊻ v)
