Multiset.induction_on'.description: This theorem proves that if a property holds for the empty multiset and is preserved under the operation of inserting an element into any subset of a multiset, then it holds for any multiset.

Multiset.toList.code: Multiset.toList.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Multiset α) : List α
Multiset.toList.comment: Produces a list of the elements in the multiset using choice.
Multiset.toList.fullDefinition: noncomputable def toList (s : Multiset α) :=   s.out'
Multiset.toList.description: This definition describes a method to convert a multiset into a list containing all its elements.

Multiset.coe_toList.code: Multiset.coe_toList.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Multiset α) : ↑s.toList = s

explanatories.Multiset.toList: This definition describes a method to convert a multiset into a list containing all its elements.

Multiset.coe_toList.description: This theorem demonstrates that converting a multiset to a list and then back results in the original multiset itself.

Multiset.toList_eq_nil.code: Multiset.toList_eq_nil.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} : s.toList = [] ↔ s = 0
Multiset.toList_eq_nil.description: This theorem states that a multiset is empty if and only if its list representation is also empty.

Multiset.empty_toList.code: Multiset.empty_toList.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} : s.toList.isEmpty = true ↔ s = 0

explanatories.List.isEmpty: There exists a function that determines whether a list is empty, returning true if it is and false otherwise.
explanatories.Bool.true: The value `true` represents one of the two possible truth values in Boolean logic.

Multiset.empty_toList.description: This theorem establishes an equivalence between a multiset being empty and its representation as an empty list.

Multiset.toList_zero.description: This theorem states that the list representation of an empty multiset is an empty list.

Multiset.mem_toList.code: Multiset.mem_toList.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {a : α} {s : Multiset α} : a ∈ s.toList ↔ a ∈ s

explanatories.Multiset.toList: This definition describes a method to convert a multiset into a list containing all its elements.

Multiset.mem_toList.description: This theorem states that an element is a member of a multiset if and only if it appears in the list formed from that multiset.

Multiset.toList_eq_singleton_iff.code: Multiset.toList_eq_singleton_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {a : α} {m : Multiset α} : m.toList = [a] ↔ m = {a}
Multiset.toList_eq_singleton_iff.description: This theorem asserts that a multiset is equivalent to a singleton set containing a specific element if and only if the list representation of the multiset contains only that single element.

Multiset.toList_singleton.description: This theorem demonstrates that the list representation of a singleton multiset containing a single element matches a list containing just that element.

Multiset.Le.code: Multiset.Le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s t : Multiset α) : Prop
Multiset.Le.comment:
`s ≤ t` means that `s` is a sublist of `t` (up to permutation).
Equivalently, `s ≤ t` means that `count a s ≤ count a t` for all `a`.

explanatories.Iff.trans: The theorem demonstrates that if two propositions are equivalent to a third proposition, then the first and the third propositions are also equivalent.
explanatories.Multiset.Subset.trans: This theorem demonstrates that if one multiset is a subset of a second multiset, and the second is a subset of a third, then the first multiset is also a subset of the third multiset.
explanatories.Quotient.liftOn₂: This defines a way to extend a binary function so that it operates on elements within a quotient type for both of its arguments.
explanatories.trans: This theorem demonstrates that in a transitive relation, if the relation holds from the first element to the second and from the second to the third, it must also hold from the first element to the third.
explanatories.Eq.trans: This theorem asserts that equality is transitive, meaning if one value equals a second value and that second value equals a third value, then the first value must equal the third value.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

Multiset.Le.fullDefinition: protected def Le (s t : Multiset α) : Prop :=   (Quotient.liftOn₂ s t (· <+~ ·)) fun _ _ _ _ p₁ p₂ =>     propext (p₂.subperm_left.trans p₁.subperm_right)
Multiset.Le.description: This definition establishes a relation indicating that one multiset is a sublist of another, either in terms of permutation or by comparing the counts of individual elements.

Multiset.decidableLE.code: Multiset.decidableLE.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [DecidableEq α] : DecidableRel fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type with decidable equality allows for determining whether any two elements are equal or not.
explanatories.Quotient.recOnSubsingleton₂: This definition describes a method to extend a binary function so that it can operate on representatives from a quotient type for both of its arguments.
explanatories.DecidableRel: A decidable relation is a type of relationship between elements that can be algorithmically determined to be true or false.

Multiset.decidableLE.fullDefinition: instance decidableLE [DecidableEq α] : DecidableRel ((· ≤ ·) : Multiset α → Multiset α → Prop) :=   fun s t => Quotient.recOnSubsingleton₂ s t List.decidableSubperm
Multiset.decidableLE.description: This definition establishes a decidable relation for determining if one multiset is less than or equal to another based on a specified equality condition.

Multiset.subset_of_le.code: Multiset.subset_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} : s ≤ t → s ⊆ t
Multiset.subset_of_le.description: This theorem establishes that if one multiset is less than or equal to another, then it is a subset of the other multiset.

Multiset.Le.subset.code: Multiset.Le.subset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} : s ≤ t → s ⊆ t
Multiset.Le.subset.description: This theorem states that if one multiset is less than or equal to another, then the first multiset is a subset of the second.

Multiset.mem_of_le.code: Multiset.mem_of_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} {a : α} (h : s ≤ t) : a ∈ s → a ∈ t
Multiset.mem_of_le.description: This theorem states that if one multiset is less than or equal to another, then any element in the first multiset is also contained in the second multiset.

Multiset.not_mem_mono.code: Multiset.not_mem_mono.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} {a : α} (h : s ⊆ t) : a ∉ t → a ∉ s
Multiset.not_mem_mono.description: This theorem asserts that if one multiset is a subset of another and an element is not present in the larger multiset, then that element must also be absent from the smaller multiset.

Multiset.coe_le.code: Multiset.coe_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {l₁ l₂ : List α} : ↑l₁ ≤ ↑l₂ ↔ l₁ <+~ l₂
Multiset.coe_le.description: This theorem states that the inclusion of one list in another is equivalent to the inequality of their corresponding multisets.

Multiset.leInductionOn.code:
Multiset.leInductionOn.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {C : Multiset α → Multiset α → Prop} {s t : Multiset α} (h : s ≤ t)
  (H : ∀ {l₁ l₂ : List α}, l₁ <+ l₂ → C ↑l₁ ↑l₂) : C s t
Multiset.leInductionOn.description: This theorem establishes that if one multiset is less than or equal to another, then a certain property can be proven for those multisets based on their list representations when a specific condition is met.

Multiset.zero_le.code: Multiset.zero_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Multiset α) : 0 ≤ s
Multiset.zero_le.description: This theorem asserts that the value of an empty multiset is always greater than or equal to zero.

Multiset.bot_eq_zero.comment: This is a `rfl` and `simp` version of `bot_eq_zero`.
Multiset.bot_eq_zero.description: This theorem establishes that the bottom element of a type is equal to zero.

Multiset.le_zero.code: Multiset.le_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} : s ≤ 0 ↔ s = 0
Multiset.le_zero.description: This theorem states that a multiset is less than or equal to the empty multiset if and only if it is itself the empty multiset.

Multiset.lt_cons_self.code: Multiset.lt_cons_self.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Multiset α) (a : α) : s < a ::ₘ s
Multiset.lt_cons_self.description: This theorem states that any multiset is considered less than the multiset formed by adding an element to it.

Multiset.le_cons_self.code: Multiset.le_cons_self.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Multiset α) (a : α) : s ≤ a ::ₘ s
Multiset.le_cons_self.description: This theorem states that any multiset is less than or equal to the multiset formed by adding one of its elements to itself.

Multiset.cons_le_cons_iff.code: Multiset.cons_le_cons_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} (a : α) : a ::ₘ s ≤ a ::ₘ t ↔ s ≤ t
Multiset.cons_le_cons_iff.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between the less than or equal to comparison of multisets formed by adding the same element to both, indicating that this condition holds if and only if the underlying multisets themselves are comparable in the same way.

Multiset.cons_le_cons.code: Multiset.cons_le_cons.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} (a : α) : s ≤ t → a ::ₘ s ≤ a ::ₘ t
Multiset.cons_le_cons.description: This theorem demonstrates that if one multiset is less than or equal to another, then adding the same element to both multisets preserves this order.

Multiset.cons_lt_cons_iff.code: Multiset.cons_lt_cons_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} {a : α} : a ::ₘ s < a ::ₘ t ↔ s < t
Multiset.cons_lt_cons_iff.description: This theorem asserts that the comparison of two multisets formed by adding the same element is equivalent to the comparison of their underlying multisets.

Multiset.le_cons_of_not_mem.code: Multiset.le_cons_of_not_mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} {a : α} (m : a ∉ s) : s ≤ a ::ₘ t ↔ s ≤ t
Multiset.le_cons_of_not_mem.description: This theorem establishes that a multiset is less than or equal to a multiset formed by adding an element to another multiset if and only if it is less than or equal to the original multiset without that element, provided that the added element is not a member of the first multiset.

Multiset.singleton_ne_zero.description: This theorem states that a singleton multiset containing a single element is not empty.

Multiset.singleton_le.code: Multiset.singleton_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {a : α} {s : Multiset α} : {a} ≤ s ↔ a ∈ s
Multiset.singleton_le.description: This theorem states that a singleton multiset containing an element is less than or equal to another multiset if and only if that element is present in the other multiset.

Multiset.le_singleton.code: Multiset.le_singleton.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} {a : α} : s ≤ {a} ↔ s = 0 ∨ s = {a}
Multiset.le_singleton.description: This theorem indicates that a multiset is less than or equal to a singleton multiset if and only if it is either empty or exactly equal to that singleton.

Multiset.singleton_subset.code: Multiset.singleton_subset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} {a : α} : {a} ⊆ s ↔ a ∈ s
Multiset.singleton_subset.description: This theorem states that a singleton multiset is a subset of another multiset if and only if the element of the singleton is contained in that multiset.

Multiset.add.code: Multiset.add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s₁ s₂ : Multiset α) : Multiset α
Multiset.add.comment:
The sum of two multisets is the lift of the list append operation.
This adds the multiplicities of each element,
i.e. `count a (s + t) = count a s + count a t`.

explanatories.Quotient.sound: This theorem establishes that if two elements are related by an equivalence relation, then their corresponding equivalence classes are equal.
explanatories.Quotient.liftOn₂: This defines a way to extend a binary function so that it operates on elements within a quotient type for both of its arguments.

Multiset.add.fullDefinition: protected def add (s₁ s₂ : Multiset α) : Multiset α :=   (Quotient.liftOn₂ s₁ s₂ fun l₁ l₂ => ((l₁ ++ l₂ : List α) : Multiset α)) fun _ _ _ _ p₁ p₂ =>     Quot.sound <| p₁.append p₂
Multiset.add.description: This definition specifies the operation for adding two multisets by combining their elements and multiplicities, similar to appending lists.

Multiset.coe_add.code: Multiset.coe_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s t : List α) : ↑s + ↑t = ↑(s ++ t)
Multiset.coe_add.description: This theorem states that the sum of two multisets corresponding to lists is equal to the multiset corresponding to the concatenation of those lists.

Multiset.singleton_add.code: Multiset.singleton_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a : α) (s : Multiset α) : {a} + s = a ::ₘ s
Multiset.singleton_add.description: This theorem establishes that the union of a singleton multiset containing an element and another multiset is equivalent to a multiset created by prepending that element to the second multiset.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.code: Multiset.add_le_add_iff_left'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t u : Multiset α} : s + t ≤ s + u ↔ t ≤ u
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: This theorem asserts that the inequality of the sums of two multisets is equivalent to the inequality of the second summands.

Multiset.le_add_right.code: Multiset.le_add_right.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s t : Multiset α) : s ≤ s + t
Multiset.le_add_right.description: This theorem asserts that any multiset is less than or equal to the sum of itself and another multiset.

Multiset.le_add_left.code: Multiset.le_add_left.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s t : Multiset α) : s ≤ t + s
Multiset.le_add_left.description: This theorem states that any multiset is always less than or equal to the sum of itself and any other multiset.

Multiset.le_iff_exists_add.code: Multiset.le_iff_exists_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} : s ≤ t ↔ ∃ u, t = s + u
Multiset.le_iff_exists_add.description: This theorem states that one multiset is less than or equal to another if and only if there exists a multiset that, when added to the former, results in the latter.

Multiset.cons_add.code: Multiset.cons_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a : α) (s t : Multiset α) : a ::ₘ s + t = a ::ₘ (s + t)
Multiset.cons_add.description: This theorem asserts that adding an element to the front of a multiset and then summing it with another multiset is equivalent to first summing the two multisets and then adding the same element to the front of the result.

Multiset.add_cons.code: Multiset.add_cons.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a : α) (s t : Multiset α) : s + a ::ₘ t = a ::ₘ (s + t)
Multiset.add_cons.description: This theorem establishes that adding an element to a multiset and then combining it with another multiset is equivalent to combining the two multisets first and then adding the element to the result.

Multiset.mem_add.code: Multiset.mem_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {a : α} {s t : Multiset α} : a ∈ s + t ↔ a ∈ s ∨ a ∈ t
Multiset.mem_add.description: This theorem establishes that an element is a member of the sum of two multisets if and only if it is a member of at least one of the individual multisets.

Multiset.mem_of_mem_nsmul.code: Multiset.mem_of_mem_nsmul.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {a : α} {s : Multiset α} {n : ℕ} (h : a ∈ n • s) : a ∈ s
Multiset.mem_of_mem_nsmul.description: This theorem states that if an element belongs to the multisets formed by multiplying another multiset by a natural number, then it must also belong to the original multiset.

Multiset.mem_nsmul.code: Multiset.mem_nsmul.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {a : α} {s : Multiset α} {n : ℕ} (h0 : n ≠ 0) : a ∈ n • s ↔ a ∈ s
Multiset.mem_nsmul.description: This theorem indicates that an element belongs to the non-zero multiples of a multiset if and only if it belongs to the original multiset.

Multiset.nsmul_cons.code: Multiset.nsmul_cons.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} (n : ℕ) (a : α) : n • (a ::ₘ s) = n • {a} + n • s
Multiset.nsmul_cons.description: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying a multiset containing an element and another multiset by a natural number is equivalent to summing the result of multiplying a singleton multiset of that element by the same number with the result of multiplying the other multiset by the same number.

Multiset.card.code: Multiset.card.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} : Multiset α →+ ℕ
Multiset.card.comment:
The cardinality of a multiset is the sum of the multiplicities
of all its elements, or simply the length of the underlying list.

explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.Quot.liftOn: This defines an operation that rearranges the arguments of a lifting function to prioritize the quotient as the first input.
explanatories.Quot.inductionOn: This theorem states that if a property holds for all representatives of a quotient and if it holds for their quotients, then it also holds for the quotient itself.
explanatories.Quotient.inductionOn: This theorem indicates that every element of a quotient set can be represented as an equivalence class containing a specific element.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: It is established that any proposition is logically equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Quotient.inductionOn₂: There is no specific theorem provided, so no concept can be described.
explanatories.List.length_append: The theorem states that the length of the concatenated list formed by joining two lists is equal to the sum of their individual lengths.

Multiset.card.fullDefinition: def card : Multiset α →+ ℕ where   toFun s := (Quot.liftOn s length) fun _l₁ _l₂ => Perm.length_eq   map_zero' := rfl   map_add' s t := Quotient.inductionOn₂ s t length_append
Multiset.card.description: This definition specifies a function that calculates the cardinality of a multiset by summing the counts of each element, effectively representing the total number of elements in the multiset.

Multiset.coe_card.code: Multiset.coe_card.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (l : List α) : card ↑l = l.length

explanatories.Multiset.card: This definition specifies a function that calculates the cardinality of a multiset by summing the counts of each element, effectively representing the total number of elements in the multiset.

Multiset.coe_card.description: This theorem states that the cardinality of a multiset formed from a list is equal to the length of that list.

Multiset.length_toList.code: Multiset.length_toList.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Multiset α) : s.toList.length = card s

explanatories.List.length: The length of a list is defined as the number of elements it contains, with an empty list having a length of zero and the length of a non-empty list being one more than the length of its tail.
explanatories.Multiset.card: This definition specifies a function that calculates the cardinality of a multiset by summing the counts of each element, effectively representing the total number of elements in the multiset.

Multiset.length_toList.description: This theorem states that the length of the list representation of a multiset is equal to the number of elements contained in that multiset.

Multiset.card_zero.description: This theorem asserts that the cardinality of an empty multiset is zero.

Multiset.card_add.code: Multiset.card_add.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s t : Multiset α) : card (s + t) = card s + card t
Multiset.card_add.description: This theorem asserts that the cardinality of the sum of two multisets equals the sum of their individual cardinalities.

Multiset.card_nsmul.code: Multiset.card_nsmul.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Multiset α) (n : ℕ) : card (n • s) = n * card s
Multiset.card_nsmul.description: This theorem states that the cardinality of a multiset obtained by repeating it a specified number of times is equal to the product of that number and the cardinality of the original multiset.

Multiset.card_cons.code: Multiset.card_cons.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a : α) (s : Multiset α) : card (a ::ₘ s) = card s + 1
Multiset.card_cons.description: This theorem states that the cardinality of a multiset formed by adding an element to another multiset is equal to the cardinality of the second multiset plus one.

Multiset.card_singleton.description: This theorem states that the cardinality of a singleton multiset containing one element is equal to one.

Multiset.card_pair.code: Multiset.card_pair.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a b : α) : card {a, b} = 2
Multiset.card_pair.description: This theorem states that the cardinality of a multiset containing two elements is equal to two.

Multiset.card_eq_one.code: Multiset.card_eq_one.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} : card s = 1 ↔ ∃ a, s = {a}
Multiset.card_eq_one.description: This theorem states that a multiset has a cardinality of one if and only if it consists of exactly one element.

Multiset.card_le_card.code: Multiset.card_le_card.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} (h : s ≤ t) : card s ≤ card t
Multiset.card_le_card.description: This theorem establishes that if one multiset is a subset of another, then the number of elements in the first multiset is less than or equal to the number of elements in the second multiset.

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

Multiset.card_mono.description: This theorem states that the cardinality function for multisets is a monotone function, meaning that if one multiset is a subset of another, then its cardinality is less than or equal to that of the larger multiset.

Multiset.eq_of_le_of_card_le.code: Multiset.eq_of_le_of_card_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} (h : s ≤ t) : card t ≤ card s → s = t

explanatories.Multiset.card: This definition specifies a function that calculates the cardinality of a multiset by summing the counts of each element, effectively representing the total number of elements in the multiset.

Multiset.eq_of_le_of_card_le.description: This theorem demonstrates that if one multiset is less than or equal to another and the cardinality of the second is less than or equal to the first, then the two multisets must be equal.

Multiset.card_lt_card.code: Multiset.card_lt_card.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} (h : s < t) : card s < card t
Multiset.card_lt_card.description: This theorem asserts that if one multiset is strictly smaller than another, then the number of elements in the first multiset is also strictly less than the number of elements in the second.

Multiset.lt_iff_cons_le.code: Multiset.lt_iff_cons_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s t : Multiset α} : s < t ↔ ∃ a, a ::ₘ s ≤ t
Multiset.lt_iff_cons_le.description: This theorem states that one multiset is less than another if and only if there exists an element that can be added to the first multiset such that it becomes less than or equal to the second multiset.

Multiset.card_eq_zero.code: Multiset.card_eq_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {s : Multiset α} : card s = 0 ↔ s = 0
Multiset.card_eq_zero.description: This theorem states that a multiset has a cardinality of zero if and only if it is empty.

Multiset.strongInductionOn.description: This definition establishes a strong induction principle for multisets, enabling proofs about a property for a multiset based on its smaller subsets.

Multiset.strongInductionOn.eq_1.description: This theorem demonstrates that the result of applying strong induction on a multiset is equivalent to the original induction hypothesis when the hypothesis is defined in terms of the multiset and its elements.

Multiset.strongDownwardInduction.comment:
Suppose that, given that `p t` can be defined on all supersets of `s` of cardinality less than
`n`, one knows how to define `p s`. Then one can inductively define `p s` for all multisets `s` of
cardinality less than `n`, starting from multisets of card `n` and iterating. This
can be used either to define data, or to prove properties.

`map f s` is the lift of the list `map` operation. The multiplicity
of `b` in `map f s` is the number of `a ∈ s` (counting multiplicity)
such that `f a = b`.

Multiset.map_count_True_eq_filter_card.comment:
Mapping a multiset through a predicate and counting the `True`s yields the cardinality of the set
filtered by the predicate. Note that this uses the notion of a multiset of `Prop`s - due to the
decidability requirements of `count`, the decidability instance on the LHS is different from the
RHS. In particular, the decidability instance on the left leaks `Classical.decEq`.
See [here](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib/pull/11306#discussion_r782286812)
for more discussion.

Multiset.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (m : Multiset α) (t : ∀ a, Multiset (β a)) : Multiset (∀ a ∈ m, β a) :=   m.recOn {Pi.empty β}     (fun a m (p : Multiset (∀ a ∈ m, β a)) => (t a).bind fun b => p.map <| Pi.cons m a b)     (by       intro a a' m n       by_cases eq : a = a'       · subst eq; rfl       · simp only [map_bind, map_map, comp_apply, bind_bind (t a') (t a)]         apply bind_hcongr         · rw [cons_swap a a']         intro b _         apply bind_hcongr         · rw [cons_swap a a']         intro b' _         apply map_hcongr         · rw [cons_swap a a']         intro f _         exact Pi.cons_swap eq)
Multiset.pi.description: The construction of the Cartesian product over a specified type indexed by a multiset allows for the creation of dependent functions that map each indexed element to values determined by their presence in the multiset.

explanatories.Multiset.foldr: This definition defines a folding operation on multisets that applies a binary function from left to right, with the requirement that the function is left-commutative to ensure the operation is well-defined.
explanatories.Std.Commutative.comm: A commutative operation guarantees that the result of combining two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.Std.Associative.assoc: An operation is defined to be associative if it produces the same result when grouping operands in different ways.

Multiset.fold.fullDefinition: def fold : α → Multiset α → α :=   foldr op (left_comm _ hc.comm ha.assoc)
Multiset.fold.description: This defines a function that applies a commutative and associative operation to combine elements of a multiset starting from a given initial value.

Setoid.completeLattice.fullDefinition: instance completeLattice : CompleteLattice (Setoid α) :=   { (completeLatticeOfInf (Setoid α)) fun _ =>       ⟨fun _ hr _ _ h => h _ hr, fun _ hr _ _ h _ hr' => hr hr' h⟩ with     inf := Inf.inf     inf_le_left := fun _ _ _ _ h => h.1     inf_le_right := fun _ _ _ _ h => h.2     le_inf := fun _ _ _ h1 h2 _ _ h => ⟨h1 h, h2 h⟩     top := ⟨fun _ _ => True, ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun h => h, fun h1 _ => h1⟩⟩     le_top := fun _ _ _ _ => trivial     bot := ⟨(· = ·), ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun h => h.symm, fun h1 h2 => h1.trans h2⟩⟩     bot_le := fun r x _ h => h ▸ r.2.1 x }

Setoid.liftEquiv.fullDefinition: def liftEquiv (r : Setoid α) : { f : α → β // r ≤ ker f } ≃ (Quotient r → β) where   toFun f := Quotient.lift (f : α → β) f.2   invFun f := ⟨f ∘ Quotient.mk'', fun x y h => by simp [ker_def, Quotient.sound' h]⟩   left_inv := fun ⟨f, hf⟩ => Subtype.eq <| funext fun x => rfl   right_inv f := funext fun x => Quotient.inductionOn' x fun x => rfl

Setoid.quotientEquivClasses.fullDefinition: noncomputable def quotientEquivClasses (r : Setoid α) : Quotient r ≃ Setoid.classes r := by   let f (a : α) : Setoid.classes r := ⟨{ x | Setoid.r x a }, Setoid.mem_classes r a⟩   have f_respects_relation (a b : α) (a_rel_b : Setoid.r a b) : f a = f b := by     rw [Subtype.mk.injEq]     exact Setoid.eq_of_mem_classes (Setoid.mem_classes r a) (Setoid.symm a_rel_b)         (Setoid.mem_classes r b) (Setoid.refl b)   apply Equiv.ofBijective (Quot.lift f f_respects_relation)   constructor   · intro (q_a : Quotient r) (q_b : Quotient r) h_eq     induction' q_a using Quotient.ind with a     induction' q_b using Quotient.ind with b     simp only [Subtype.ext_iff, Quotient.lift_mk, Subtype.ext_iff] at h_eq     apply Quotient.sound     show a ∈ { x | Setoid.r x b }     rw [← h_eq]     exact Setoid.refl a   · rw [Quot.surjective_lift]     intro ⟨c, a, hc⟩     exact ⟨a, Subtype.ext hc.symm⟩

Mathlib.Vector.inductionOn.comment:
Define `C v` by induction on `v : Vector α n`.

This function has two arguments: `nil` handles the base case on `C nil`,
and `cons` defines the inductive step using `∀ x : α, C w → C (x ::ᵥ w)`.

It is used as the default induction principle for the `induction` tactic.

Mathlib.Vector.inductionOn.fullDefinition: def inductionOn {C : ∀ {n : ℕ}, Vector α n → Sort*} {n : ℕ} (v : Vector α n)     (nil : C nil) (cons : ∀ {n : ℕ} {x : α} {w : Vector α n}, C w → C (x ::ᵥ w)) : C v := by   -- Porting note: removed `generalizing`: already generalized   induction' n with n ih   · rcases v with ⟨_ | ⟨-, -⟩, - | -⟩     exact nil   · rcases v with ⟨_ | ⟨a, v⟩, v_property⟩     cases v_property     exact cons (ih ⟨v, (add_left_inj 1).mp v_property⟩)

Mathlib.Vector.inductionOn₂.fullDefinition: def inductionOn₂ {C : ∀ {n}, Vector α n → Vector β n → Sort*}     (v : Vector α n) (w : Vector β n)     (nil : C nil nil) (cons : ∀ {n a b} {x : Vector α n} {y}, C x y → C (a ::ᵥ x) (b ::ᵥ y)) :     C v w := by   -- Porting note: removed `generalizing`: already generalized   induction' n with n ih   · rcases v with ⟨_ | ⟨-, -⟩, - | -⟩     rcases w with ⟨_ | ⟨-, -⟩, - | -⟩     exact nil   · rcases v with ⟨_ | ⟨a, v⟩, v_property⟩     cases v_property     rcases w with ⟨_ | ⟨b, w⟩, w_property⟩     cases w_property     apply @cons n _ _ ⟨v, (add_left_inj 1).mp v_property⟩ ⟨w, (add_left_inj 1).mp w_property⟩     apply ih

  map₂ f (hd₁ ::ᵥ tl₁) (hd₂ ::ᵥ tl₂) = f hd₁ hd₂ ::ᵥ map₂ f tl₁ tl₂
Mathlib.Vector.map₂_cons.description: This theorem demonstrates that when applying a function to pairs of elements formed by the heads of two vectors, the result matches the application of that function to the heads followed by the results from applying the function to the tails of the vectors.

Mathlib.Vector.get_mem.code: Mathlib.Vector.get_mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) (v : Vector α n) : v.get i ∈ v.toList

explanatories.List.get_mem: If an element is retrieved from a list using an index that is within the bounds of the list's length, then that element is guaranteed to be a member of the original list.

Mathlib.Vector.get_mem.description: This theorem asserts that any element retrieved from a vector exists within the corresponding list representation of that vector.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_iff_get.code: Mathlib.Vector.mem_iff_get.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (a : α) (v : Vector α n) : a ∈ v.toList ↔ ∃ i, v.get i = a

explanatories.List.mem_iff_get: An element is a member of a list if and only if there exists an index such that the element at that index is equal to the member.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_iff_get.description: This theorem states that an element is a member of a vector's list representation if and only if there exists an index in the vector such that the element can be retrieved from that index.

Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_nil.code: Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_nil.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a : α) : a ∉ nil.toList

explanatories.List.not_mem_nil: An element is not a member of an empty list.

Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_nil.description: This theorem states that no element can be a member of an empty list.

Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_zero.code: Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (a : α) (v : Vector α 0) : a ∉ v.toList
Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_zero.description: This theorem states that no element can be a member of a vector with zero length's list representation.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_iff.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (a a' : α) (v : Vector α n) :
  a' ∈ (a ::ᵥ v).toList ↔ a' = a ∨ a' ∈ v.toList
Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_iff.description: This theorem states that an element belongs to the list representation of a vector constructed by adding a new element if and only if it is either that new element or an element of the original vector's list.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_succ_iff.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mem_succ_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (a : α) (v : Vector α (n + 1)) :
  a ∈ v.toList ↔ a = v.head ∨ a ∈ v.tail.toList
Mathlib.Vector.mem_succ_iff.description: This theorem states that an element belongs to the list representation of a vector with one additional element if and only if it is either the first element of the vector or an element of the remaining elements in the list representation.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_self.code: Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_self.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (a : α) (v : Vector α n) : a ∈ (a ::ᵥ v).toList
Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_self.description: This theorem asserts that an element is included in the list representation of a vector that starts with that element followed by another vector.

Mathlib.Vector.head_mem.code: Mathlib.Vector.head_mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (v : Vector α (n + 1)) : v.head ∈ v.toList
Mathlib.Vector.head_mem.description: This theorem asserts that the first element of a vector with one additional element is included in the list representation of the vector.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_of_mem.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_of_mem.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (a a' : α) (v : Vector α n) (ha' : a' ∈ v.toList) :
  a' ∈ (a ::ᵥ v).toList
Mathlib.Vector.mem_cons_of_mem.description: This theorem states that if an element is a member of the list representation of a vector, then it is also a member of the list representation of a new vector formed by prepending an element to the original vector.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_of_mem_tail.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mem_of_mem_tail.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (a : α) (v : Vector α n) (ha : a ∈ v.tail.toList) :
  a ∈ v.toList
Mathlib.Vector.mem_of_mem_tail.description: This theorem states that if an element belongs to the list representation of the tail of a vector, then it also belongs to the list representation of the entire vector.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_map_iff.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mem_map_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {n : ℕ} (b : β) (v : Vector α n) (f : α → β) :
  b ∈ (map f v).toList ↔ ∃ a ∈ v.toList, f a = b
Mathlib.Vector.mem_map_iff.description: This theorem establishes that an element belongs to the list representation of a vector after applying a function to its elements if and only if there exists an original element in the vector such that applying the function to that element yields the specified result.

Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_map_zero.code:
Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_map_zero.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (b : β) (v : Vector α 0) (f : α → β) :
  b ∉ (map f v).toList
Mathlib.Vector.not_mem_map_zero.description: This theorem states that no element can be a member of the list representation of the image of a zero-length vector under any function.

Mathlib.Vector.mem_map_succ_iff.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mem_map_succ_iff.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {n : ℕ} (b : β) (v : Vector α (n + 1))
  (f : α → β) : b ∈ (map f v).toList ↔ f v.head = b ∨ ∃ a ∈ v.tail.toList, f a = b
Mathlib.Vector.mem_map_succ_iff.description: This theorem establishes that an element is in the list representation of the map of a vector with one additional element if and only if it is the image of the first element under the mapping function or if there exists another element in the remaining vector that maps to that element.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith.code:
Mathlib.Vector.zipWith.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {n : ℕ} (f : α → β → γ) :
  Vector α n → Vector β n → Vector γ n
Mathlib.Vector.zipWith.comment: Apply the function `f : α → β → γ` to each corresponding pair of elements from two vectors.

explanatories.List.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines two lists by applying a given function to corresponding elements from each list, stopping at the end of the shorter list.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith.fullDefinition: def zipWith : Vector α n → Vector β n → Vector γ n := fun x y => ⟨List.zipWith f x.1 y.1, by simp⟩
Mathlib.Vector.zipWith.description: This definition specifies a function that combines elements from two vectors of the same length by applying a given function to corresponding pairs of elements.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_toList.code:
Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_toList.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {n : ℕ} (f : α → β → γ)
  (x : Vector α n) (y : Vector β n) : (zipWith f x y).toList = List.zipWith f x.toList y.toList

explanatories.List.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines two lists by applying a given function to corresponding elements from each list, stopping at the end of the shorter list.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_toList.description: This theorem states that applying a function to corresponding elements from two vectors yields the same result as applying the same function to the corresponding elements of their respective lists.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_get.code:
Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_get.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {n : ℕ} (f : α → β → γ)
  (x : Vector α n) (y : Vector β n) (i : Fin n) : (zipWith f x y).get i = f (x.get i) (y.get i)

explanatories.List.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines two lists by applying a given function to corresponding elements from each list, stopping at the end of the shorter list.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_get.description: This theorem states that the element at a specific index in the combined vector, formed by applying a function to pairs of elements from two vectors, is equal to the result of applying the same function to the elements at that index in the original vectors.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_tail.code:
Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_tail.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {n : ℕ} (f : α → β → γ)
  (x : Vector α n) (y : Vector β n) : (zipWith f x y).tail = zipWith f x.tail y.tail

explanatories.List.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines two lists by applying a given function to corresponding elements from each list, stopping at the end of the shorter list.

Mathlib.Vector.zipWith_tail.description: This theorem asserts that the tail of the combined vector, created by applying a function to corresponding elements from two vectors, is equal to the combined vector formed by applying the same function to the tails of the original vectors.

Mathlib.Vector.prod_mul_prod_eq_prod_zip.code:
Mathlib.Vector.prod_mul_prod_eq_prod_zipWith.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} [CommMonoid α] (x y : Vector α n) :
  x.toList.prod * y.toList.prod = (zipWith (fun x x_1 => x * x_1) x y).toList.prod

explanatories.List.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines two lists by applying a given function to corresponding elements from each list, stopping at the end of the shorter list.
explanatories.Mathlib.Vector.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines elements from two vectors of the same length by applying a given function to corresponding pairs of elements.
explanatories.List.prod: This definition describes the operation that computes the product of all elements in a list, starting with the identity element of multiplication.

Mathlib.Vector.prod_mul_prod_eq_prod_zip.description: This theorem states that the product of the elements from two vectors is equal to the product of the elements obtained by multiplying corresponding pairs of elements from those vectors.

Mathlib.Vector.sum_add_sum_eq_sum_zipWit.code:
Mathlib.Vector.sum_add_sum_eq_sum_zipWith.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} [AddCommMonoid α] (x y : Vector α n) :
  x.toList.sum + y.toList.sum = (zipWith (fun x x_1 => x + x_1) x y).toList.sum

explanatories.List.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines two lists by applying a given function to corresponding elements from each list, stopping at the end of the shorter list.
explanatories.Mathlib.Vector.zipWith: This definition specifies a function that combines elements from two vectors of the same length by applying a given function to corresponding pairs of elements.

Mathlib.Vector.sum_add_sum_eq_sum_zipWit.description: This theorem asserts that the sum of the elements in two vectors is equal to the sum of the elements obtained by adding corresponding pairs from each vector.

Mathlib.Vector.snoc.code: Mathlib.Vector.snoc.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} : Vector α n → α → Vector α (n + 1)
Mathlib.Vector.snoc.comment: Append a single element to the end of a vector

explanatories.Append.append: This defines a method for concatenating two elements of the same type into a single element, referred to as a concatenation operation.

Mathlib.Vector.snoc.fullDefinition: def snoc : Vector α n → α → Vector α (n+1) :=   fun xs x => append xs (x ::ᵥ Vector.nil)
Mathlib.Vector.snoc.description: This definition describes a method for adding a single element to the end of a vector, resulting in a new vector with one more element.

Mathlib.Vector.snoc_cons.code: Mathlib.Vector.snoc_cons.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {n : ℕ} (xs : Vector α n) {x y : α} : (x ::ᵥ xs).snoc y = x ::ᵥ xs.snoc y
Mathlib.Vector.snoc_cons.description: This theorem establishes that appending an element to a vector that has been extended by adding another element at the front results in the same vector structure as first appending the element to the original vector and then adding the new front element.

Mathlib.Vector.revInductionOn.code:
Mathlib.Vector.revInductionOn.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_2} {C : {n : ℕ} → Vector α n → Sort u_1} {n : ℕ} (v : Vector α n)
  (nil : C Mathlib.Vector.nil) (snoc : {n : ℕ} → (xs : Vector α n) → (x : α) → C xs → C (xs.snoc x)) : C v
Mathlib.Vector.revInductionOn.comment:
Define `C v` by *reverse* induction on `v : Vector α n`.
That is, break the vector down starting from the right-most element, using `snoc`

This function has two arguments: `nil` handles the base case on `C nil`,
and `snoc` defines the inductive step using `∀ x : α, C xs → C (xs.snoc x)`.

This can be used as `induction v using Vector.revInductionOn`.

explanatories.Mathlib.Vector.snoc: This definition describes a method for adding a single element to the end of a vector, resulting in a new vector with one more element.
explanatories.Mathlib.Vector.reverse: This definition describes a function that reverses the order of elements in a given vector.
explanatories.cast: This defines a function that enables the conversion of a value from one type to another when given an equality proof between those types.
explanatories.Mathlib.Vector.inductionOn: This definition describes a method for applying an inductive principle to a vector, specifying a base case for the empty vector and an inductive step for constructing vectors from their predecessors.

Mathlib.Vector.revInductionOn.fullDefinition: def revInductionOn {C : ∀ {n : ℕ}, Vector α n → Sort*} {n : ℕ} (v : Vector α n)     (nil : C nil)     (snoc : ∀ {n : ℕ} (xs : Vector α n) (x : α), C xs → C (xs.snoc x)) :     C v :=   cast (by simp) <| inductionOn     (C := fun v => C v.reverse)     v.reverse     nil     (@fun n x xs (r : C xs.reverse) => cast (by simp) <| snoc xs.reverse x r)
Mathlib.Vector.revInductionOn.description: This definition establishes a method for proving properties of vectors by applying reverse induction, where the process begins with the empty vector and continues by considering the last element of the vector and extending a property defined for shorter vectors.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_bisim.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_bisim.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_2} {n : ℕ} {xs : Vector α n} {σ₁ : Type} {β : Type u_1}
  {σ₂ : Type} {f₁ : α → σ₁ → σ₁ × β} {f₂ : α → σ₂ → σ₂ × β} {s₁ : σ₁} {s₂ : σ₂} (R : σ₁ → σ₂ → Prop) (h₀ : R s₁ s₂)
  (hR : ∀ {s : σ₁} {q : σ₂} (a : α), R s q → R (f₁ a s).1 (f₂ a q).1 ∧ (f₁ a s).2 = (f₂ a q).2) :
  R (mapAccumr f₁ xs s₁).1 (mapAccumr f₂ xs s₂).1 ∧ (mapAccumr f₁ xs s₁).2 = (mapAccumr f₂ xs s₂).2
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_bisim.description: This theorem demonstrates that under certain conditions of relationships between state transformations and corresponding outputs, the results of two mapping operations over a vector can be related in a way that preserves those relationships and outputs.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_bisim.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_bisim {α : Type} {n : ℕ} {xs : Vector α n} {β σ₁ γ σ₂ : Type} {ys : Vector β n}
  {f₁ : α → β → σ₁ → σ₁ × γ} {f₂ : α → β → σ₂ → σ₂ × γ} {s₁ : σ₁} {s₂ : σ₂} (R : σ₁ → σ₂ → Prop) (h₀ : R s₁ s₂)
  (hR : ∀ {s : σ₁} {q : σ₂} (a : α) (b : β), R s q → R (f₁ a b s).1 (f₂ a b q).1 ∧ (f₁ a b s).2 = (f₂ a b q).2) :
  R (mapAccumr₂ f₁ xs ys s₁).1 (mapAccumr₂ f₂ xs ys s₂).1 ∧ (mapAccumr₂ f₁ xs ys s₁).2 = (mapAccumr₂ f₂ xs ys s₂).2
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_bisim.description: This theorem establishes that when certain relationships between state transformations and outputs hold, the results of applying two related mapping operations over two vectors can be connected while preserving those relationships and outputs.

Mathlib.Vector.map_eq_mapAccumr.code:
Mathlib.Vector.map_eq_mapAccumr.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_2} {n : ℕ} {xs : Vector α n} :
  ∀ {α_1 : Type u_1} {f : α → α_1}, map f xs = (mapAccumr (fun x x_1 => ((), f x)) xs ()).2
Mathlib.Vector.map_eq_mapAccumr.description: This theorem asserts that mapping a function over a vector is equivalent to using a mapping process that accumulates results while discarding the intermediate states.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_bisim_tail.description: This theorem shows that if there exists a relationship between the initial states of two mapping functions that preserves certain properties, then the final outputs of those mappings over a vector will be equal.

Mathlib.Vector.map₂_eq_mapAccumr₂.code:
Mathlib.Vector.map₂_eq_mapAccumr₂ {α : Type} {n : ℕ} {β : Type} {xs : Vector α n} {ys : Vector β n} :
  ∀ {α_1 : Type} {f : α → β → α_1}, map₂ f xs ys = (mapAccumr₂ (fun x y x_1 => ((), f x y)) xs ys ()).2
Mathlib.Vector.map₂_eq_mapAccumr₂.description: This theorem establishes that applying a binary function to pairs of elements from two vectors is equivalent to using a mapping process that accumulates results while discarding the intermediate states.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_bisim_tail.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_bisim_tail {α : Type} {n : ℕ} {xs : Vector α n} {β σ₁ γ σ₂ : Type} {ys : Vector β n}
  {f₁ : α → β → σ₁ → σ₁ × γ} {f₂ : α → β → σ₂ → σ₂ × γ} {s₁ : σ₁} {s₂ : σ₂}
  (h :
    ∃ R,
      R s₁ s₂ ∧
        ∀ {s : σ₁} {q : σ₂} (a : α) (b : β), R s q → R (f₁ a b s).1 (f₂ a b q).1 ∧ (f₁ a b s).2 = (f₂ a b q).2) :
  (mapAccumr₂ f₁ xs ys s₁).2 = (mapAccumr₂ f₂ xs ys s₂).2
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_bisim_tail.description: This theorem shows that if there exists a relation between two state transformations that preserves both the resulting states and outputs for a mapping operation applied to two vectors, then their final outputs will be equal.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_eq_map.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_eq_map.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_2} {n : ℕ} {β : Type u_1} {xs : Vector α n} {σ : Type}
  {f : α → σ → σ × β} {s₀ : σ} (S : Set σ) (h₀ : s₀ ∈ S) (closure : ∀ (a : α), ∀ s ∈ S, (f a s).1 ∈ S)
  (out : ∀ (a : α) (s s' : σ), s ∈ S → s' ∈ S → (f a s).2 = (f a s').2) :
  (mapAccumr f xs s₀).2 = map (fun x => (f x s₀).2) xs
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_eq_map.comment:
If there is a set of states that is closed under `f`, and such that `f` produces that same output
for all states in this set, then the state is not actually needed.
Hence, then we can rewrite `mapAccumr` into just `map`

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr_eq_map.description: This theorem states that if a set of states remains closed under a specific transformation and produces the same output regardless of the state, then the operation of accumulating results can be simplified to merely mapping over the inputs.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_eq_map₂.code:
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_eq_map₂ {α : Type} {n : ℕ} {β : Type} {xs : Vector α n} {ys : Vector β n} {σ γ : Type}
  {f : α → β → σ → σ × γ} {s₀ : σ} (S : Set σ) (h₀ : s₀ ∈ S) (closure : ∀ (a : α) (b : β), ∀ s ∈ S, (f a b s).1 ∈ S)
  (out : ∀ (a : α) (b : β) (s s' : σ), s ∈ S → s' ∈ S → (f a b s).2 = (f a b s').2) :
  (mapAccumr₂ f xs ys s₀).2 = map₂ (fun x x_1 => (f x x_1 s₀).2) xs ys
Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_eq_map₂.comment:
If there is a set of states that is closed under `f`, and such that `f` produces that same output
for all states in this set, then the state is not actually needed.
Hence, then we can rewrite `mapAccumr₂` into just `map₂`

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Mathlib.Vector.mapAccumr₂_eq_map₂.description: This theorem states that if a function maintains certain outputs regardless of state within a closed set, the process of accumulating results can be simplified to a straightforward mapping of pairs from two vectors.

Rel.code: Rel.{u_4, u_5} (α : Type u_4) (β : Type u_5) : Type (max u_4 u_5)
Rel.comment: A relation on `α` and `β`, aka a set-valued function, aka a partial multifunction
Rel.fullDefinition: def Rel (α β : Type*) :=   α → β → Prop -- deriving CompleteLattice, Inhabited
Rel.description: This defines a relation between two types as a set-valued function or partial multifunction.

Rel.inv.code: Rel.inv.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : Rel β α
Rel.inv.comment: The inverse relation : `r.inv x y ↔ r y x`. Note that this is *not* a groupoid inverse.

explanatories.flip: This defines a function that reverses the order of arguments for another function that takes two inputs, effectively allowing it to be called with the second argument first.

Rel.inv.fullDefinition: def inv : Rel β α :=   flip r
Rel.inv.description: This defines the inverse of a relation, where the order of the related elements is reversed.

Rel.inv_def.code: Rel.inv_def.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) (x : α) (y : β) : r.inv y x ↔ r x y
Rel.inv_def.description: This theorem states that for a relation, the condition of the inverse relation being true for two elements is equivalent to the original relation being true for those elements in reverse order.

Rel.inv_inv.code: Rel.inv_inv.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : r.inv.inv = r
Rel.inv_inv.description: This theorem asserts that taking the inverse of an inverse relation returns the original relation.

Rel.dom.code: Rel.dom.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : Set α
Rel.dom.fullDefinition: def dom := { x | ∃ y, r x y }
Rel.dom.description: This defines the domain of a relation as the set of all elements from the first type that are related to some elements of the second type.

Rel.dom_mono.code: Rel.dom_mono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {r s : Rel α β} (h : r ≤ s) : r.dom ⊆ s.dom
Rel.dom_mono.description: This theorem states that if one relation is a subset of another, then the domain of the first relation is also a subset of the domain of the second relation.

Rel.codom.code: Rel.codom.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : Set β
Rel.codom.comment: Codomain aka range of a relation

explanatories.Rel.dom: This defines the domain of a relation as the set of all elements from the first type that are related to some elements of the second type.

Rel.codom.fullDefinition: def codom := { y | ∃ x, r x y }
Rel.codom.description: This defines the codomain of a relation as the set of all elements from the second type that are related to some elements of the first type.

Rel.codom_inv.code: Rel.codom_inv.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : r.inv.codom = r.dom

explanatories.Rel.dom: This defines the domain of a relation as the set of all elements from the first type that are related to some elements of the second type.

Rel.codom_inv.description: This theorem states that the codomain of the inverse of a relation is equal to the domain of the original relation.

Rel.dom_inv.code: Rel.dom_inv.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : r.inv.dom = r.codom
Rel.dom_inv.description: This theorem states that the domain of the inverse of a relation is equal to the codomain of the original relation.

Rel.comp.code: Rel.comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (r : Rel α β) (s : Rel β γ) : Rel α γ
Rel.comp.comment: Composition of relation; note that it follows the `CategoryTheory/` order of arguments.

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.

Rel.comp.fullDefinition: def comp (r : Rel α β) (s : Rel β γ) : Rel α γ := fun x z => ∃ y, r x y ∧ s y z
Rel.comp.description: This defines the composition of two relations, resulting in a new relation that connects the first and third types through the intermediate second type.

Rel.term_•_._@..lake.packages.mathlib.Ma.comment: Local syntax for composition of relations.

explanatories.GaloisConnection: A Galois connection consists of two functions that establish a relationship between elements of two ordered sets, such that the order of one set is preserved in relation to the mapping of the other.

Rel.term_•_._@..lake.packages.mathlib.Ma.description: This definition introduces a local syntax for composing relations.

Rel.comp_assoc.code:
Rel.comp_assoc.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4} (r : Rel α β)
  (s : Rel β γ) (t : Rel γ δ) : (r • s) • t = r • s • t
Rel.comp_assoc.description: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of three relations is associative, meaning that the grouping of the compositions does not affect the result.

Rel.comp_right_id.code: Rel.comp_right_id.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : r • Eq = r
Rel.comp_right_id.description: This theorem states that the composition of a relation with the equality relation on its codomain is equal to the original relation itself.

Rel.comp_left_id.code: Rel.comp_left_id.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : Eq • r = r
Rel.comp_left_id.description: This theorem states that composing a relation with the identity relation on the first type yields the original relation unchanged.

Rel.inv_id.code: Rel.inv_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} : inv Eq = Eq
Rel.inv_id.description: This theorem states that the inverse of the equality relation is the equality relation itself.

Rel.inv_comp.code:
Rel.inv_comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (r : Rel α β) (s : Rel β γ) :
  (r • s).inv = s.inv • r.inv
Rel.inv_comp.description: This theorem states that the inverse of the composition of two relations is equal to the composition of their inverses taken in reverse order.

Rel.image.code: Rel.image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) (s : Set α) : Set β
Rel.image.comment: Image of a set under a relation

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Rel.image.fullDefinition: def image (s : Set α) : Set β := { y | ∃ x ∈ s, r x y }
Rel.image.description: This defines the image of a set under a relation, producing a new set consisting of all elements related to elements of the original set.

Rel.mem_image.code:
Rel.mem_image.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) (y : β) (s : Set α) :
  y ∈ r.image s ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, r x y

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Rel.image: This defines the image of a set under a relation, producing a new set consisting of all elements related to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Rel.mem_image.description: This theorem states that an element belongs to the image of a relation applied to a set if and only if there exists an element in that set related to it by the relation.

Rel.image_subset.code:
Rel.image_subset.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) :
  ((fun x x_1 => x ⊆ x_1) ⇒ fun x x_1 => x ⊆ x_1) r.image r.image

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Rel.image_subset.description: This theorem states that the image of a relation forms a subset of itself under a specific condition regarding inclusion.

Rel.image_mono.code: Rel.image_mono.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : Monotone r.image

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

Rel.image_mono.description: This theorem establishes that the image of a relation is a monotone function.

Rel.image_inter.code:
Rel.image_inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) (s t : Set α) :
  r.image (s ∩ t) ⊆ r.image s ∩ r.image t

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Rel.image_inter.description: This theorem proves that the image of the intersection of two sets under a relation is contained within the intersection of their respective images.

Rel.image_union.code:
Rel.image_union.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) (s t : Set α) :
  r.image (s ∪ t) = r.image s ∪ r.image t

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Rel.image_union.description: This theorem states that the image of the union of two sets under a relation is equal to the union of the images of each set under that relation.

Rel.image_id.code: Rel.image_id.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : image Eq s = s

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Rel.image_id.description: This theorem asserts that the image of a set under the identity relation is equal to the original set itself.

Rel.image_comp.code:
Rel.image_comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} (r : Rel α β) (s : Rel β γ) (t : Set α) :
  (r • s).image t = s.image (r.image t)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

Rel.image_comp.description: This theorem asserts that the image of a set under the composition of two relations is equal to the image of that set under the first relation followed by the image under the second relation.

Rel.image_univ.code: Rel.image_univ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) : r.image Set.univ = r.codom

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.

Rel.image_univ.description: This theorem asserts that the image of the universal set under a relation is equal to the codomain of that relation.

Rel.preimage.code: Rel.preimage.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (r : Rel α β) (s : Set β) : Set α
Rel.preimage.comment: Preimage of a set under a relation `r`. Same as the image of `s` under `r.inv`

explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Set.preimage: The preimage of a set under a function consists of all elements that map into the set when the function is applied.

Rel.preimage.fullDefinition: def preimage (s : Set β) : Set α :=   r.inv.image s
Rel.preimage.description: This defines the preimage of a set under a relation as the set of all elements from the first type that relate to elements in the given set from the second type.

Rel.mem_preimage.code:

Sym2.lift₂.fullDefinition: def lift₂ :     { f : α → α → β → β → γ //         ∀ a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂, f a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ = f a₂ a₁ b₁ b₂ ∧ f a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ = f a₁ a₂ b₂ b₁ } ≃       (Sym2 α → Sym2 β → γ) where   toFun f :=     Quotient.lift₂ (s₁ := Sym2.Rel.setoid α) (s₂ := Sym2.Rel.setoid β)       (fun (a : α × α) (b : β × β) => f.1 a.1 a.2 b.1 b.2)       (by         rintro _ _ _ _ ⟨⟩ ⟨⟩         exacts [rfl, (f.2 _ _ _ _).2, (f.2 _ _ _ _).1, (f.2 _ _ _ _).1.trans (f.2 _ _ _ _).2])   invFun F :=     ⟨fun a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ => F s(a₁, a₂) s(b₁, b₂), fun a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ => by       constructor       exacts [congr_arg₂ F eq_swap rfl, congr_arg₂ F rfl eq_swap]⟩   left_inv f := Subtype.ext rfl   right_inv F := funext₂ fun a b => Sym2.inductionOn₂ a b fun _ _ _ _ => rfl

Sym.e1.code: Sym.e1 {n k : ℕ} : { s // 0 ∈ s } ≃ Sym (Fin n.succ) k
Sym.e1.comment:
Over `Fin (n + 1)`, the multisets of size `k + 1` containing `0` are equivalent to those of size
`k`, as demonstrated by respectively erasing or appending `0`.

explanatories.Nat.succ: This states the successor function for natural numbers, which yields the next integer by adding one to a given natural number.
explanatories.Sym.erase: The operation removes one occurrence of an element from a symmetric power if that element is present, effectively decreasing its multiplicity by one.
explanatories.Sym.cons: An element can be added to the symmetric power of a type, resulting in a new symmetric power that contains one additional element.
explanatories.Sym.mem_cons_self: An element is always a member of the symmetric power formed by including it in a collection alongside other elements.
explanatories.Bool.false: The boolean value false is a specific representation of the false state in boolean logic.

Sym.e1.fullDefinition: protected def e1 {n k : ℕ} : { s : Sym (Fin (n + 1)) (k + 1) // ↑0 ∈ s } ≃ Sym (Fin n.succ) k where   toFun s := s.1.erase 0 s.2   invFun s := ⟨cons 0 s, mem_cons_self 0 s⟩   left_inv s := by simp   right_inv s := by simp set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
Sym.e1.description: Multisets of a certain size containing a specific element are equivalently represented by multisets of a smaller size formed by either removing or adding that element.

Sym.e2.code: Sym.e2 {n k : ℕ} : { s // 0 ∉ s } ≃ Sym (Fin n.succ) k
Sym.e2.comment:
The multisets of size `k` over `Fin n+2` not containing `0`
are equivalent to those of size `k` over `Fin n+1`,
as demonstrated by respectively decrementing or incrementing every element of the multiset.

explanatories.Fin.succAbove: This definition describes a function that maps a finite number into a larger finite set while skipping over a specified element.
explanatories.mt: If a true implication leads to a false conclusion, then the antecedent must also be false.

explanatories.not_and: The theorem establishes that the negation of the conjunction of two propositions is equivalent to one of the propositions implying the negation of the other.
explanatories.Fin.succAbove_ne: This theorem states that when embedding a finite number into a larger finite set while skipping a specific element, the result will never be equal to the excluded element.
explanatories.Sym.map_map: Applying two functions in sequence to a symmetric power is equivalent to first mapping the composition of those functions over the symmetric power.
explanatories.Sym.map_congr: If two functions produce the same output for every element in a symmetric power, then mapping either function over that symmetric power yields the same result.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Sym.map_id': This theorem establishes that the application of the identity mapping to a symmetric power yields the original symmetric power unchanged.
explanatories.Fin.succAbove_predAbove: This theorem establishes that when moving between two finite sets by adjusting values relative to a specified element, the operation results in the original value when that element is excluded.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.Fin.castSucc_zero: The theorem states that the successor of zero in the context of finite numbers is still zero.
explanatories.Fin.predAbove_succAbove: This theorem states that applying a predecessor mapping to an element above a certain point in a finite set, after increasing the size of the set by adding a successor, retrieves the original element in the initial set.
explanatories.Equiv.trans: This definition establishes a method for composing two equivalence relations to create a new equivalence relation between the first and last types.
explanatories.Bool.false: The boolean value false is a specific representation of the false state in boolean logic.

Sym.e2.fullDefinition: protected def e2 {n k : ℕ} : { s : Sym (Fin n.succ.succ) k // ↑0 ∉ s } ≃ Sym (Fin n.succ) k where   toFun s := map (Fin.predAbove 0) s.1   invFun s :=     ⟨map (Fin.succAbove 0) s,       (mt mem_map.1) (not_exists.2 fun t => not_and.2 fun _ => Fin.succAbove_ne _ t)⟩   left_inv s := by     ext1     simp only [map_map]     refine (Sym.map_congr fun v hv ↦ ?_).trans (map_id' _)     exact Fin.succAbove_predAbove (ne_of_mem_of_not_mem hv s.2)   right_inv s := by     simp only [map_map, comp_apply, ← Fin.castSucc_zero, Fin.predAbove_succAbove, map_id'] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

PFun.fix.code: PFun.fix.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : α →. β ⊕ α) : α →. β
PFun.fix.comment:
First return map. Transforms a partial function `f : α →. β ⊕ α` into the partial function
`α →. β` which sends `a : α` to the first value in `β` it hits by iterating `f`, if such a value
exists. By abusing notation to illustrate, either `f a` is in the `β` part of `β ⊕ α` (in which
case `f.fix a` returns `f a`), or it is undefined (in which case `f.fix a` is undefined as well), or
it is in the `α` part of `β ⊕ α` (in which case we repeat the procedure, so `f.fix a` will return
`f.fix (f a)`).

FP.ofRat.fullDefinition: unsafe def ofRat : RMode → ℚ → Float   | RMode.NE, r =>     let low := ofRatDn r     let high := ofRatUp r     if hf : high.isFinite then       if r = toRat _ hf then high       else         if lf : low.isFinite then           if r - toRat _ lf > toRat _ hf - r then high           else             if r - toRat _ lf < toRat _ hf - r then low             else               match low, lf with               | Float.finite _ _ m _, _ => if 2 ∣ m then low else high         else Float.inf true     else Float.inf false

Finset.induction_on_union.comment:
To prove a relation on pairs of `Finset X`, it suffices to show that it is
* symmetric,
* it holds when one of the `Finset`s is empty,
* it holds for pairs of singletons,
* if it holds for `[a, c]` and for `[b, c]`, then it holds for `[a ∪ b, c]`.

Finset.disjiUnion.comment:
`disjiUnion s f h` is the set such that `a ∈ disjiUnion s f` iff `a ∈ f i` for some `i ∈ s`.
It is the same as `s.biUnion f`, but it does not require decidable equality on the type. The
hypothesis ensures that the sets are disjoint.

Finset.filterMap.comment:
`filterMap f s` is a combination filter/map operation on `s`.
The function `f : α → Option β` is applied to each element of `s`;
if `f a` is `some b` then `b` is included in the result, otherwise
`a` is excluded from the resulting finset.

In notation, `filterMap f s` is the finset `{b : β | ∃ a ∈ s , f a = some b}`.

Finset.fold_singleton.code:

Finset.fold_singleton.description: This theorem states that when folding a commutative and associative operation over a finite set containing only a single element, the result is the operation applied to that element's image and an initial value.

Finset.fold_map.code:
Finset.fold_map.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]

Finset.fold_image.description: This theorem states that when folding a commutative and associative operation over the images of a finite set transformed by a function, the result equals folding the operation over the original set by composing the two functions involved, provided that the transformation is injective.

Finset.fold.eq_1.code:
Finset.fold.eq_1.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (op : β → β → β) [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] (b : β) (f : α → β) (s : Finset α) :

Finset.fold.eq_1.description: This theorem establishes that folding a commutative and associative operation over a finite set is equivalent to folding the same operation over the image of that set's elements when treated as a multiset, starting from the same initial value.

Finset.fold_congr.code:
Finset.fold_congr.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] {f : α → β} {b : β} {s : Finset α} {g : α → β} (H : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = g x) :

Finset.fold_congr.description: This theorem asserts that if two functions agree on all elements of a finite set, then folding a commutative and associative operation using either function produces the same result.

Finset.fold_op_distrib.code:
Finset.fold_op_distrib.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] {s : Finset α} {f g : α → β} {b₁ b₂ : β} :
  fold op (op b₁ b₂) (fun x => op (f x) (g x)) s = op (fold op b₁ f s) (fold op b₂ g s)

explanatories.Multiset.fold: This defines a function that applies a commutative and associative operation to combine elements of a multiset starting from a given initial value.

Finset.fold_op_distrib.description: This theorem states that folding a commutative and associative operation over a finite set, where each element is transformed by combining two functions, results in applying the operation to the folds of each function separately, starting from their respective initial values.

Finset.fold_const.code:
Finset.fold_const.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] {b : β} {s : Finset α} [hd : Decidable (s = ∅)] (c : β) (h : op c (op b c) = op b c) :
  fold op b (fun x => c) s = if s = ∅ then b else op b c

explanatories.Multiset.fold: This defines a function that applies a commutative and associative operation to combine elements of a multiset starting from a given initial value.

Finset.fold_const.description: This theorem asserts that when folding a constant function over a finite set using a commutative and associative operation, the result is determined by whether the set is empty, ensuring that the operation applied with the constant and the starting value yields the same result as the initial value when the set is empty.

Finset.fold_hom.code:
Finset.fold_hom.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] {f : α → β} {b : β} {s : Finset α} {op' : γ → γ → γ} [Std.Commutative op']
  [Std.Associative op'] {m : β → γ} (hm : ∀ (x y : β), m (op x y) = op' (m x) (m y)) :
  fold op' (m b) (fun x => m (f x)) s = m (fold op b f s)

explanatories.Multiset.fold: This defines a function that applies a commutative and associative operation to combine elements of a multiset starting from a given initial value.
explanatories.Multiset.fold_hom: This theorem establishes that if a mapping commutes with respect to a commutative and associative operation, then folding the mapped values of a multiset produces the same result as mapping the fold of the original multiset.

Finset.fold_hom.description: This theorem establishes that when folding a value using a new operation on the images of a function applied to elements of a finite set, it is equivalent to applying the new operation to the result of folding the original function over the set, provided that the new operation maintains the same structure with respect to the original operation.

Finset.fold_disjUnion.code:
Finset.fold_disjUnion.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] {f : α → β} {s₁ s₂ : Finset α} {b₁ b₂ : β} (h : _root_.Disjoint s₁ s₂) :
  fold op (op b₁ b₂) f (s₁.disjUnion s₂ h) = op (fold op b₁ f s₁) (fold op b₂ f s₂)

explanatories.Finset.disjUnion: This definition describes a finite set formed by the union of two disjoint finite sets, ensuring that elements belong to either one set or the other.

Finset.fold_disjUnion.description: This theorem asserts that when folding a commutative and associative operation over the disjoint union of two finite sets, the result is the operation of the folds over each original set, combined with their respective initial values.

Finset.fold_disjiUnion.code:
Finset.fold_disjiUnion.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] {f : α → β} {ι : Type u_4} {s : Finset ι} {t : ι → Finset α} {b : ι → β} {b₀ : β}
  (h : (↑s).PairwiseDisjoint t) :
  fold op (fold op b₀ b s) f (s.disjiUnion t h) = fold op b₀ (fun i => fold op (b i) f (t i)) s

Finset.fold_disjiUnion.description: This theorem demonstrates that when combining elements from multiple disjoint sets using a commutative and associative operation, the result of folding the operation over the union of these sets is equivalent to folding over each individual set and then combining those results.

Finset.fold_union_inter.code:
Finset.fold_union_inter.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]

Finset.fold_insert_idem.code:

Finset.fold_ite'.code:
Finset.fold_ite'.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {op : β → β → β} [hc : Std.Commutative op]
  [ha : Std.Associative op] {f : α → β} {b : β} {s : Finset α} {g : α → β} (hb : op b b = b) (p : α → Prop)
  [DecidablePred p] :
  fold op b (fun i => if p i then f i else g i) s =
    op (fold op b f (filter p s)) (fold op b g (filter (fun i => ¬p i) s))
Finset.fold_ite'.comment:

Finset.fold_min_le.code:
Finset.fold_min_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {b : β} {s : Finset α} [LinearOrder β] (c : β) :

Finset.lt_fold_min.code:
Finset.lt_fold_min.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {b : β} {s : Finset α} [LinearOrder β] (c : β) :

Finset.fold_min_lt.code:
Finset.fold_min_lt.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {f : α → β} {b : β} {s : Finset α} [LinearOrder β] (c : β) :

Finset.fold_max_lt.description: This theorem states that the result of folding a maximum function over a finite set is less than a specified value if and only if the initial value is less than that value and every element in the set yields a function value that is also less than that specified value.

Finset.card_bij.code:
Finset.card_bij.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} (i : (a : α) → a ∈ s → β)
  (hi : ∀ (a : α) (ha : a ∈ s), i a ha ∈ t)
  (i_inj : ∀ (a₁ : α) (ha₁ : a₁ ∈ s) (a₂ : α) (ha₂ : a₂ ∈ s), i a₁ ha₁ = i a₂ ha₂ → a₁ = a₂)
  (i_surj : ∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a, ∃ (ha : a ∈ s), i a ha = b) : s.card = t.card
Finset.card_bij.comment:
Reorder a finset.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective injection,
rather than by an inverse function.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij` is that the bijection is allowed to use membership of the
domain, rather than being a non-dependent function.

  (j : (a : β) → a ∈ t → α) (hi : ∀ (a : α) (ha : a ∈ s), i a ha ∈ t) (hj : ∀ (a : β) (ha : a ∈ t), j a ha ∈ s)
  (left_inv : ∀ (a : α) (ha : a ∈ s), j (i a ha) ⋯ = a) (right_inv : ∀ (a : β) (ha : a ∈ t), i (j a ha) ⋯ = a) :
  s.card = t.card
Finset.card_bij'.comment:
Reorder a finset.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are allowed to use
membership of the domains, rather than being non-dependent functions.

Finset.card_bij'.description: This theorem asserts that if there exists a bijection between two finite sets, along with its inverse, then the cardinalities of these sets are equal.

Finset.card_nbij'.code:
Finset.card_nbij'.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} (i : α → β) (j : β → α)
  (hi : ∀ a ∈ s, i a ∈ t) (hj : ∀ a ∈ t, j a ∈ s) (left_inv : ∀ a ∈ s, j (i a) = a) (right_inv : ∀ a ∈ t, i (j a) = a) :
  s.card = t.card
Finset.card_nbij'.comment:
Reorder a finset.

The difference with `Finset.card_nbij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
than as a surjective injection.

The difference with `Finset.card_bij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are non-dependent
functions, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domains.

The difference with `Finset.card_equiv` is that bijectivity is only required to hold on the domains,
rather than on the entire types.

Finset.card_nbij'.description: This theorem establishes that if there exist two functions that serve as inverses for each other between two finite sets, ensuring elements from each set correspond uniquely to elements of the other, then these two sets have the same cardinality.
