Finset.strongInduction.code:
Finset.strongInduction.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {p : Finset α → Sort u_4}
  (H : (s : Finset α) → ((t : Finset α) → t ⊂ s → p t) → p s) (s : Finset α) : p s
Finset.strongInduction.comment:
Suppose that, given objects defined on all strict subsets of any finset `s`, one knows how to
define an object on `s`. Then one can inductively define an object on all finsets, starting from
the empty set and iterating. This can be used either to define data, or to prove properties.

explanatories.Multiset.card: This definition specifies a function that calculates the cardinality of a multiset by summing the counts of each element, effectively representing the total number of elements in the multiset.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.Multiset.card_lt_card: This theorem asserts that if one multiset is strictly smaller than another, then the number of elements in the first multiset is also strictly less than the number of elements in the second.
explanatories.Finset.card_lt_card: This theorem states that if one finite set is a proper subset of another, then its cardinality is strictly less than that of the larger set.

Finset.strongInduction.fullDefinition: def strongInduction {p : Finset α → Sort*} (H : ∀ s, (∀ t ⊂ s, p t) → p s) :     ∀ s : Finset α, p s   | s =>     H s fun t h =>       have : t.card < s.card := card_lt_card h       strongInduction H t   termination_by s => Finset.card s
Finset.strongInduction.description: This definition describes a method of strong induction applicable to finite sets, allowing for the establishment of properties or definitions for a set based on its strict subsets.

Finset.strongInduction.eq_1.code:
Finset.strongInduction.eq_1.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {p : Finset α → Sort u_4}
  (H : (s : Finset α) → ((t : Finset α) → t ⊂ s → p t) → p s) :
  ∀ (x : Finset α),
    strongInduction H x =
      H x fun t h =>
        let_fun this := ⋯;
        strongInduction H t

explanatories.Finset.toList.eq_1: This theorem establishes that the list representation of a finite set is equal to the list representation of its underlying values.
explanatories.Finset.image.eq_1: This theorem establishes that the image of a finite set under a function is equal to the finite set obtained by applying that function to each element of the underlying multiset.
explanatories.Multiset.toFinset.eq_1: This theorem demonstrates that the finite set representation of a multiset is equal to a set containing the unique elements of the multiset.
explanatories.Finset.Nontrivial.eq_1: This theorem states that a finite set is considered nontrivial if and only if its corresponding set of elements is also nontrivial.

Finset.strongInduction.eq_1.description: This theorem demonstrates that a strong induction hypothesis applied to a finite set can be expressed in terms of the hypothesis and the strong induction applied to its subsets.

Finset.strongInduction_eq.description: This theorem demonstrates that the strong induction principle for a property defined on finite sets can be expressed in terms of the induction hypothesis applied to a specific set, along with the properties of its subsets.

Finset.strongInductionOn.code:
Finset.strongInductionOn.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {p : Finset α → Sort u_4} (s : Finset α) :
  ((s : Finset α) → ((t : Finset α) → t ⊂ s → p t) → p s) → p s

Finset.strongDownwardInduction.comment:

`n`, one knows how to define `p s`. Then one can inductively define `p s` for all finsets `s` of
cardinality less than `n`, starting from finsets of card `n` and iterating. This
can be used either to define data, or to prove properties.

Finset.pi.comment:
Given a finset `s` of `α` and for all `a : α` a finset `t a` of `δ a`, then one can define the
finset `s.pi t` of all functions defined on elements of `s` taking values in `t a` for `a ∈ s`.
Note that the elements of `s.pi t` are only partially defined, on `s`.

Finset.Pi.cons.comment:

anyway.

explanatories.WithTop.map: This definition describes a way to extend a function mapping between two types to operate on values wrapped in an optional type that can also represent a top element.
explanatories.WithBot.map: This defines a function that applies a mapping to a type that includes a least element, transforming each element according to the specified function while preserving the structure of the original type.

Finset.inf'_map.description: This theorem states that the infimum of the image of a finite set under a mapping function can be expressed as the infimum of the original set under the composition of the mapping and another function, provided the image set is nonempty.

Finset.sup'_comp_eq_map.code:
Finset.sup'_comp_eq_map.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_4} [SemilatticeSup α] {s : Finset γ}
  {f : γ ↪ β} (g : β → α) (hs : s.Nonempty) : s.sup' hs (g ∘ ⇑f) = (map f s).sup' ⋯ g
Finset.sup'_comp_eq_map.comment:
A version of `Finset.sup'_map` with LHS and RHS reversed.
Also, this lemma assumes that `s` is nonempty instead of assuming that its image is nonempty.

explanatories.Multiset.map: This definition outlines a way to create a new multiset by applying a function to each element of an existing multiset, preserving the count of each element according to how many times the function produces the same output.
explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.

explanatories.WithTop.map: This definition describes a way to extend a function mapping between two types to operate on values wrapped in an optional type that can also represent a top element.
explanatories.WithBot.map: This defines a function that applies a mapping to a type that includes a least element, transforming each element according to the specified function while preserving the structure of the original type.

Finset.sup'_comp_eq_map.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum of a finite non-empty set of transformed elements, under a composition of functions, is equal to the supremum of the images of those elements under one function, followed by applying another function to the results.

Finset.inf'_mono.code:
Finset.inf'_mono.{u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [SemilatticeInf α] (f : β → α) {s₁ s₂ : Finset β}

Finset.inf'_mono.description: This theorem demonstrates that if one finite set is a subset of another and the first set is non-empty, then the infimum of a function over the larger set is less than or equal to the infimum over the smaller set.

Finset.sup'_eq_sup.description: For a non-empty finite set, the supremum of a function applied to the set's elements is equal to the supremum calculated using the same function directly on the set.

Finset.sup_apply.description: The supremum of a finite set applied to a function, evaluated at a specific element, is equal to the supremum of the function's outputs for that set at the same element.

Finset.sup'_apply.code:

Finset.sup'_apply.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a function applied to elements of a nonempty finite set, indexed by a specific element, is equivalent to applying the function to each element of the set with that index and then computing the supremum of the results.

Finset.inf'_apply.code:

Finset.inf'_apply.description: This theorem shows that the infimum of a function over a non-empty finite set can be computed by fixing an argument separately and applying the function to the elements of the set.

Finset.sup'_inf_distrib_left.code:
Finset.sup'_inf_distrib_left.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_5} [DistribLattice α] {s : Finset ι}

Finset.sup'_inf_distrib_left.description: This theorem establishes that the infimum of a fixed element combined with the supremum of a function's values over a nonempty finite set is equal to the supremum of the infimums of that fixed element and each value from the function.

Finset.sup'_inf_distrib_right.code:

Finset.sup'_inf_sup'.description: This theorem states that the infimum of the supremum values from two non-empty finite sets, evaluated through respective functions, is equal to the supremum of the joint product of those sets under the combined function that takes the infimum of the outputs from both functions.

Finset.inf'_sup_distrib_left.code:

Finset.inf'_sup_distrib_left.description: This theorem states that the supremum of a constant value with the infimum of a function over a nonempty finite set is equal to the infimum of the function adjusted by adding the constant to each output.

Finset.inf'_sup_distrib_right.code:

Finset.inf'_sup_distrib_right.description: This theorem shows that the infimum of the function over a non-empty finite set joined with a value is equal to the infimum of the same function joined with that value.

Finset.inf'_sup_inf'.description: The theorem states that the supremum of the infimums of two non-empty finite sets, when combined via their Cartesian product, equals the infimum of the supremum of the values derived from a function applied to pairs formed from the elements of those sets.

Finset.lt_sup'_iff.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between an element being less than the supremum of a function over a non-empty finite set and the existence of an element in that set for which the function's value exceeds the given element.

Finset.sup'_lt_iff.code:
Finset.sup'_lt_iff.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_5} [LinearOrder α] {s : Finset ι} (H : s.Nonempty) {f : ι → α}

Finset.sup'_lt_iff.description: This theorem establishes that the supremum of a function over a non-empty finite set being less than a given element is equivalent to all function values at the elements of the set being less than that element.

Finset.inf'_le_iff.description: The infimum of the images of a non-empty finite set under a function is less than or equal to a specified element if and only if there exists at least one image that is less than or equal to that element.

Finset.inf'_lt_iff.code:
Finset.inf'_lt_iff.{u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_5} [LinearOrder α] {s : Finset ι} (H : s.Nonempty) {f : ι → α}
  {a : α} : s.inf' H f < a ↔ ∃ i ∈ s, f i < a
Finset.inf'_lt_iff.description: The infimum of a function over a non-empty finite set is less than a value if and only if there exists an element in the set whose image under the function is also less than that value.

intersections of finite subfamilies. This version works for `ι : Sort*`. See also
`iInter_eq_iInter_finset` for a version that assumes `ι : Type*` but avoids `PLift`s in the right
hand side.
Set.iInter_eq_iInter_finset'.description: This theorem states that the intersection of a family of sets is equal to the intersection of the intersections of all possible finite subfamilies of that family.

Finset.induction_on_pi.comment:
Given a predicate on functions `∀ i, Finset (α i)` defined on a finite type, it is true on all
maps provided that it is true on `fun _ ↦ ∅` and for any function `g : ∀ i, Finset (α i)`, an index
`i : ι`, and `x ∉ g i`, `p g` implies `p (update g i (insert x (g i)))`.

See also `Finset.induction_on_pi_max` and `Finset.induction_on_pi_min` for specialized versions
that require `∀ i, LinearOrder (α i)`.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Finset.image₂_singleton_left: The image of a binary function applied to a singleton set and a finite set is equal to the image obtained by applying the function to the singleton and each element of the finite set.
explanatories.HasSubset.Subset.trans: A theorem indicating that this is an alternative name for the transitive property of set inclusion.
explanatories.Finset.Nonempty.image: This theorem asserts that if a finite set is non-empty, then the image of that set under any function will also be non-empty.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.Finset.image_id': This theorem states that the image of a finite set under the identity function is the set itself.
explanatories.Finset.image₂_assoc: The image created by applying one binary function to the result of applying another binary function to two finite sets and a third set is equal to applying a modified version of the first function to the original finite sets and the resulting image from the second function.
explanatories.MulAction.mul_smul: This theorem states that the action of multiplying two elements behaves associatively with respect to both multiplication and the action on another element.
explanatories.Function.Injective.mulAction: This definition describes a way to create a new multiplicative action on a type by pulling back through an injective function, ensuring that the action respects the original multiplicative structure.

Function.Injective.invOfMemRange.comment:

This is the computable version of `Function.invFun` that requires `Fintype α` and `DecidableEq β`,
or the function version of applying `(Equiv.ofInjective f hf).symm`.
This function should not usually be used for actual computation because for most cases,
an explicit inverse can be stated that has better computational properties.

`N = Fintype.card α`.

setFintype.description: This definition establishes that a set formed from a finite type is itself also finite when treated as a type, provided that the membership of elements in the set can be decided.

Fintype.finsetEquivSet.fullDefinition: noncomputable def finsetEquivSet : Finset α ≃ Set α where   toFun := (↑)   invFun := by classical exact fun s => s.toFinset   left_inv s := by convert Finset.toFinset_coe s   right_inv s := by classical exact s.coe_toFinset
Fintype.finsetEquivSet.description: This definition establishes a bijective equivalence between finite sets and finite subsets of a type that has a finite number of elements.

Quotient.fintype.fullDefinition: instance Quotient.fintype [Fintype α] (s : Setoid α) [DecidableRel ((· ≈ ·) : α → α → Prop)] :     Fintype (Quotient s) :=   Fintype.ofSurjective Quotient.mk'' Quotient.surjective_Quotient_mk''

PSigma.fintypePropLeft.fullDefinition: instance PSigma.fintypePropLeft {α : Prop} {β : α → Type*} [Decidable α] [∀ a, Fintype (β a)] :     Fintype (Σ'a, β a) :=   if h : α then Fintype.ofEquiv (β h) ⟨fun x => ⟨h, x⟩, PSigma.snd, fun _ => rfl, fun ⟨_, _⟩ => rfl⟩   else ⟨∅, fun x => (h x.1).elim⟩
PSigma.fintypePropLeft.description: This definition establishes that the type formed by pairs consisting of an element from a decidable proposition and a corresponding type derived from that proposition is also a finite type, provided that each type fulfils the finiteness condition.

PSigma.fintypePropRight.fullDefinition: instance PSigma.fintypePropRight {α : Type*} {β : α → Prop} [∀ a, Decidable (β a)] [Fintype α] :     Fintype (Σ'a, β a) :=   Fintype.ofEquiv { a // β a }     ⟨fun ⟨x, y⟩ => ⟨x, y⟩, fun ⟨x, y⟩ => ⟨x, y⟩, fun ⟨_, _⟩ => rfl, fun ⟨_, _⟩ => rfl⟩
PSigma.fintypePropRight.description: This definition asserts that a dependent sum type formed from a finite type and a decidable property of its elements is also finite.

PSigma.fintypePropProp.fullDefinition: instance PSigma.fintypePropProp {α : Prop} {β : α → Prop} [Decidable α] [∀ a, Decidable (β a)] :     Fintype (Σ'a, β a) :=   if h : ∃ a, β a then ⟨{⟨h.fst, h.snd⟩}, fun ⟨_, _⟩ => by simp⟩ else ⟨∅, fun ⟨x, y⟩ =>     (h ⟨x, y⟩).elim⟩

exists_seq_of_forall_finset_exists.code:
exists_seq_of_forall_finset_exists.{u_4} {α : Type u_4} (P : α → Prop) (r : α → α → Prop)
  (h : ∀ (s : Finset α), (∀ x ∈ s, P x) → ∃ y, P y ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, r x y) :
  ∃ f, (∀ (n : ℕ), P (f n)) ∧ ∀ (m n : ℕ), m < n → r (f m) (f n)
exists_seq_of_forall_finset_exists.comment:
Induction principle to build a sequence, by adding one point at a time satisfying a given
relation with respect to all the previously chosen points.

More precisely, Assume that, for any finite set `s`, one can find another point satisfying
some relation `r` with respect to all the points in `s`. Then one may construct a
function `f : ℕ → α` such that `r (f m) (f n)` holds whenever `m < n`.
We also ensure that all constructed points satisfy a given predicate `P`.
exists_seq_of_forall_finset_exists.description: This theorem demonstrates that if it is possible to find a point satisfying a certain property in relation to any finite set of points, then one can construct a sequence of points, each satisfying that property and the specified relation among them.

  (h : ∀ (s : Finset α), (∀ x ∈ s, P x) → ∃ y, P y ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, r x y) :
  ∃ f, (∀ (n : ℕ), P (f n)) ∧ Pairwise fun m n => r (f m) (f n)
exists_seq_of_forall_finset_exists'.comment:
Induction principle to build a sequence, by adding one point at a time satisfying a given
symmetric relation with respect to all the previously chosen points.

More precisely, Assume that, for any finite set `s`, one can find another point satisfying
some relation `r` with respect to all the points in `s`. Then one may construct a
function `f : ℕ → α` such that `r (f m) (f n)` holds whenever `m ≠ n`.
We also ensure that all constructed points satisfy a given predicate `P`.

exists_seq_of_forall_finset_exists'.description: This theorem guarantees the construction of a sequence such that all elements satisfy a specified property and maintain a symmetric relation with respect to each other, based on the ability to find such elements for any finite subset.

finsetStx.comment:
`finset% t` elaborates `t` as a `Finset`.
If `t` is a `Set`, then inserts `Set.toFinset`.
Does not make use of the expected type; useful for big operators over finsets.
```
#check finset% Finset.range 2 -- Finset Nat
#check finset% (Set.univ : Set Bool) -- Finset Bool
```

finsetStx.fullDefinition: elab (name := finsetStx) "finset% " t:term : term => do   let u ← mkFreshLevelMVar   let ty ← mkFreshExprMVar (mkSort (.succ u))   let x ← Elab.Term.elabTerm t (mkApp (.const ``Finset [u]) ty)   let xty ← whnfR (← inferType x)   if xty.isAppOfArity ``Set 1 then     Elab.Term.elabAppArgs (.const ``Set.toFinset [u]) #[] #[.expr x] none false false   else     return x
finsetStx.description: This definition introduces a parser for treating expressions as finite sets, converting sets into their finite set equivalents when necessary, and is particularly useful for handling large operations involving finite sets.

collection of setoids indexed by a type `ι`, a (finite) list `l` of
indices, and a function that for each `i ∈ l` gives a term of the
corresponding quotient type, then there is a corresponding term in the
quotient of the product of the setoids indexed by `l`.

Fintype.truncEquivFin.code: Fintype.truncEquivFin.{u_4} (α : Type u_4) [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] : Trunc (α ≃ Fin (card α))
Fintype.truncEquivFin.comment:
There is (computably) an equivalence between `α` and `Fin (card α)`.

Since it is not unique and depends on which permutation
of the universe list is used, the equivalence is wrapped in `Trunc` to
preserve computability.

See `Fintype.equivFin` for the noncomputable version,
and `Fintype.truncEquivFinOfCardEq` and `Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq`
for an equiv `α ≃ Fin n` given `Fintype.card α = n`.

See `Fintype.truncFinBijection` for a version without `[DecidableEq α]`.

    ∀ (α : Type u_4) [inst : Fintype α] [inst_1 : Nontrivial α],

Fintype.induction_subsingleton_or_nontri.comment:
A custom induction principle for fintypes. The base case is a subsingleton type,
and the induction step is for non-trivial types, and one can assume the hypothesis for
smaller types (via `Fintype.card`).

The major premise is `Fintype α`, so to use this with the `induction` tactic you have to give a name
to that instance and use that name.

Fintype.piFinset.comment:
Given for all `a : α` a finset `t a` of `δ a`, then one can define the
finset `Fintype.piFinset t` of all functions taking values in `t a` for all `a`. This is the
analogue of `Finset.pi` where the base finset is `univ` (but formally they are not the same, as
there is an additional condition `i ∈ Finset.univ` in the `Finset.pi` definition).

Fintype.truncRecEmptyOption.fullDefinition: def truncRecEmptyOption {P : Type u → Sort v} (of_equiv : ∀ {α β}, α ≃ β → P α → P β)     (h_empty : P PEmpty) (h_option : ∀ {α} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α], P α → P (Option α))     (α : Type u) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] : Trunc (P α) := by   suffices ∀ n : ℕ, Trunc (P (ULift <| Fin n)) by     apply Trunc.bind (this (Fintype.card α))     intro h     apply Trunc.map _ (Fintype.truncEquivFin α)     intro e     exact of_equiv (Equiv.ulift.trans e.symm) h   apply ind where     -- Porting note: do a manual recursion, instead of `induction` tactic,     -- to ensure the result is computable     /-- Internal induction hypothesis -/     ind : ∀ n : ℕ, Trunc (P (ULift <| Fin n))     | Nat.zero => by           have : card PEmpty = card (ULift (Fin 0)) := by simp only [card_fin, card_pempty,                                                                      card_ulift]           apply Trunc.bind (truncEquivOfCardEq this)           intro e           apply Trunc.mk           exact of_equiv e h_empty       | Nat.succ n => by           have : card (Option (ULift (Fin n))) = card (ULift (Fin n.succ)) := by             simp only [card_fin, card_option, card_ulift]           apply Trunc.bind (truncEquivOfCardEq this)           intro e           apply Trunc.map _ (ind n)           intro ih           exact of_equiv e (h_option ih)

Fintype.toCompleteLattice.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev toCompleteLattice [Lattice α] [BoundedOrder α] : CompleteLattice α where   __ := ‹Lattice α›   __ := ‹BoundedOrder α›   sSup := fun s => s.toFinset.sup id   sInf := fun s => s.toFinset.inf id   le_sSup := fun _ _ ha => Finset.le_sup (f := id) (Set.mem_toFinset.mpr ha)   sSup_le := fun s _ ha => Finset.sup_le fun b hb => ha _ <| Set.mem_toFinset.mp hb   sInf_le := fun _ _ ha => Finset.inf_le (Set.mem_toFinset.mpr ha)   le_sInf := fun s _ ha => Finset.le_inf fun b hb => ha _ <| Set.mem_toFinset.mp hb

Fintype.card_filter_piFinset_eq_of_mem.code:
Fintype.card_filter_piFinset_eq_of_mem.{u_4, u_6} {ι : Type u_4} {α : ι → Type u_6} [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι]
  [(i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)] (s : (i : ι) → Finset (α i)) (i : ι) {a : α i} (ha : a ∈ s i) :
  (filter (fun f => f i = a) (piFinset s)).card = ∏ j ∈ univ.erase i, (s j).card
Fintype.card_filter_piFinset_eq_of_mem.comment:
The number of dependent maps `f : Π j, s j` for which the `i` component is `a` is the product
over all `j ≠ i` of `(s j).card`.

Note that this is just a composition of easier lemmas, but there's some glue missing to make that
smooth enough not to need this lemma.

Fintype.prod_sum_type.code:

Fintype.prod_sum_type.description: This theorem states that the product of a function over the sum type formed by two finite types can be expressed as the product of the function values for each type separately.

Real.commRing.fullDefinition: instance commRing : CommRing ℝ where   natCast n := ⟨n⟩   intCast z := ⟨z⟩   zero := (0 : ℝ)   one := (1 : ℝ)   mul := (· * ·)   add := (· + ·)   neg := @Neg.neg ℝ _   sub := @Sub.sub ℝ _   npow := @npowRec ℝ ⟨1⟩ ⟨(· * ·)⟩   nsmul := @nsmulRec ℝ ⟨0⟩ ⟨(· + ·)⟩   zsmul := @zsmulRec ℝ ⟨0⟩ ⟨(· + ·)⟩ ⟨@Neg.neg ℝ _⟩ (@nsmulRec ℝ ⟨0⟩ ⟨(· + ·)⟩)   add_zero a := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_add, cauchy_zero]   zero_add a := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_add, cauchy_zero]   add_comm a b := by apply ext_cauchy; simp only [cauchy_add, add_comm]   add_assoc a b c := by apply ext_cauchy; simp only [cauchy_add, add_assoc]   mul_zero a := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_mul, cauchy_zero]   zero_mul a := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_mul, cauchy_zero]   mul_one a := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_mul, cauchy_one]   one_mul a := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_mul, cauchy_one]   mul_comm a b := by apply ext_cauchy; simp only [cauchy_mul, mul_comm]   mul_assoc a b c := by apply ext_cauchy; simp only [cauchy_mul, mul_assoc]   left_distrib a b c := by apply ext_cauchy; simp only [cauchy_add, cauchy_mul, mul_add]   right_distrib a b c := by apply ext_cauchy; simp only [cauchy_add, cauchy_mul, add_mul]   add_left_neg a := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_add, cauchy_neg, cauchy_zero]   natCast_zero := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_zero]   natCast_succ n := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_one, cauchy_add]   intCast_negSucc z := by apply ext_cauchy; simp [cauchy_neg, cauchy_natCast]

Real.«tacticPi_lower_bound[_,,]».comment:
Create a proof of `a < π` for a fixed rational number `a`, given a witness, which is a
sequence of rational numbers `√2 < r 1 < r 2 < ... < r n < 2` satisfying the property that
`√(2 + r i) ≤ r(i+1)`, where `r 0 = 0` and `√(2 - r n) ≥ a/2^(n+1)`.

Real.«tacticPi_lower_bound[_,,]».fullDefinition: elab "pi_lower_bound " "[" l:term,* "]" : tactic => do   let rat_sep := l.elemsAndSeps   let sep := rat_sep.getD 1 .missing   let ratStx := rat_sep.filter (· != sep)   let n := ← (toExpr ratStx.size).toSyntax   let els := (ratStx.map numDen).reduceOption   evalTactic (← `(tactic| apply pi_lower_bound_start $n))   let _ := ← els.mapM fun (x, y) => do       evalTactic (← `(tactic| apply sqrtTwoAddSeries_step_up $x $y))   evalTactic (← `(tactic| simp [sqrtTwoAddSeries]))   allGoals (evalTactic (← `(tactic| norm_num1)))

  (h₂ : 1 / 4 ^ n ≤ a) : π < a

Fin.instCommSemigroup.fullDefinition: instance instCommSemigroup (n : ℕ) : CommSemigroup (Fin n) :=   { inferInstanceAs (Mul (Fin n)) with     mul_assoc := fun ⟨a, ha⟩ ⟨b, hb⟩ ⟨c, hc⟩ =>       Fin.eq_of_val_eq <|         calc           a * b % n * c ≡ a * b * c [MOD n] := (Nat.mod_modEq _ _).mul_right _           _ ≡ a * (b * c) [MOD n] := by rw [mul_assoc]           _ ≡ a * (b * c % n) [MOD n] := (Nat.mod_modEq _ _).symm.mul_left _     mul_comm := Fin.mul_comm }

ZMod.chineseRemainder.fullDefinition: def chineseRemainder {m n : ℕ} (h : m.Coprime n) : ZMod (m * n) ≃+* ZMod m × ZMod n :=   let to_fun : ZMod (m * n) → ZMod m × ZMod n :=     ZMod.castHom (show m.lcm n ∣ m * n by simp [Nat.lcm_dvd_iff]) (ZMod m × ZMod n)   let inv_fun : ZMod m × ZMod n → ZMod (m * n) := fun x =>     if m * n = 0 then       if m = 1 then cast (RingHom.snd _ (ZMod n) x) else cast (RingHom.fst (ZMod m) _ x)     else Nat.chineseRemainder h x.1.val x.2.val   have inv : Function.LeftInverse inv_fun to_fun ∧ Function.RightInverse inv_fun to_fun :=     if hmn0 : m * n = 0 then by       rcases h.eq_of_mul_eq_zero hmn0 with (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)       · constructor         · intro x; rfl         · rintro ⟨x, y⟩           fin_cases y           simp [to_fun, inv_fun, castHom, Prod.ext_iff, eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton]       · constructor         · intro x; rfl         · rintro ⟨x, y⟩           fin_cases x           simp [to_fun, inv_fun, castHom, Prod.ext_iff, eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton]     else by       haveI : NeZero (m * n) := ⟨hmn0⟩       haveI : NeZero m := ⟨left_ne_zero_of_mul hmn0⟩       haveI : NeZero n := ⟨right_ne_zero_of_mul hmn0⟩       have left_inv : Function.LeftInverse inv_fun to_fun := by         intro x         dsimp only [to_fun, inv_fun, ZMod.castHom_apply]         conv_rhs => rw [← ZMod.natCast_zmod_val x]         rw [if_neg hmn0, ZMod.eq_iff_modEq_nat, ← Nat.modEq_and_modEq_iff_modEq_mul h,           Prod.fst_zmod_cast, Prod.snd_zmod_cast]         refine           ⟨(Nat.chineseRemainder h (cast x : ZMod m).val (cast x : ZMod n).val).2.left.trans ?_,             (Nat.chineseRemainder h (cast x : ZMod m).val (cast x : ZMod n).val).2.right.trans ?_⟩         · rw [← ZMod.eq_iff_modEq_nat, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val, ZMod.natCast_val]         · rw [← ZMod.eq_iff_modEq_nat, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val, ZMod.natCast_val]       exact ⟨left_inv, left_inv.rightInverse_of_card_le (by simp)⟩   { toFun := to_fun,     invFun := inv_fun,     map_mul' := RingHom.map_mul _     map_add' := RingHom.map_add _     left_inv := inv.1     right_inv := inv.2 }
ZMod.chineseRemainder.description: This definition establishes that for two coprime natural numbers, the structure formed by integers modulo their product is isomorphic to the direct product of the structures formed by integers modulo each of the two numbers individually.

zmod.chinese_remainder.comment:
The **Chinese remainder theorem**. For a pair of coprime natural numbers, `m` and `n`,
  the rings `ZMod (m * n)` and `ZMod m × ZMod n` are isomorphic.

See `Ideal.quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotient` for the Chinese remainder theorem for ideals in any
ring.

ZMod.unitsMap.description: This definition describes a group homomorphism that converts units from the modular arithmetic system of one integer to that of another, specifically when the first integer is divisible by the second.

AddCommMonoid.zmodModule.code:
AddCommMonoid.zmodModule.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [NeZero n] [AddCommMonoid M] (h : ∀ (x : M), n • x = 0) :

AddCommMonoid.zmodModule.comment:
The `ZMod n`-module structure on commutative monoids whose elements have order dividing `n ≠ 0`.
Also implies a group structure via `Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup`.
See note [reducible non-instances].

explanatories.mul_nsmul: This theorem establishes that in an additive monoid, scaling an element by the product of two natural numbers is equivalent to scaling it first by one number and then by the other.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.Nat.mod_add_div': The theorem states that for any natural number, the sum of its remainder when divided by another natural number and the quotient multiplied back by that natural number equals the original number.
explanatories.NeZero.ne: This theorem establishes that a non-zero element is not equal to zero.
explanatories.Fin.val: This defines how to extract the natural number represented by a finite index.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.one_nsmul: This theorem states that in an additive monoid, multiplying an element by one yields the element itself.
explanatories.mul_nsmul': This theorem shows that in an additive monoid, multiplying a scalar by an element can be expressed as the action of the scalar product of the two numbers on that element.
explanatories.nsmul_zero: This theorem states that in an additive monoid, multiplying the zero element by any natural number results in the zero element.
explanatories.nsmul_add: The scalar multiplication of a sum of two elements in an additive commutative monoid is equal to the sum of the scalar multiplications of each element.
explanatories.zero_nsmul: This theorem states that multiplying any element by zero in an additive monoid results in zero.

AddCommMonoid.zmodModule.fullDefinition: abbrev AddCommMonoid.zmodModule [NeZero n] [AddCommMonoid M] (h : ∀ (x : M), n • x = 0) :     Module (ZMod n) M := by   have h_mod (c : ℕ) (x : M) : (c % n) • x = c • x := by     suffices (c % n + c / n * n) • x = c • x by rwa [add_nsmul, mul_nsmul, h, add_zero] at this     rw [Nat.mod_add_div']   have := NeZero.ne n   match n with   | n + 1 => exact {     smul := fun (c : Fin _) x ↦ c.val • x     smul_zero := fun _ ↦ nsmul_zero _     zero_smul := fun _ ↦ zero_nsmul _     smul_add := fun _ _ _ ↦ nsmul_add _ _ _     one_smul := fun _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| one_nsmul _     add_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| add_nsmul _ _ _     mul_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| mul_nsmul' _ _ _   }
AddCommMonoid.zmodModule.description: This definition establishes a module structure over a commutative monoid in which the elements have an order that divides a non-zero integer, thus extending group properties within this framework.

ZMod.map_smul.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} {M₁ : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup M₁]
  [FunLike F M M₁] [AddMonoidHomClass F M M₁] [Module (ZMod n) M] [Module (ZMod n) M₁] (f : F) (c : ZMod n) (x : M) :

ZMod.map_smul.description: The theorem states that a linear transformation between two additive groups commutes with the action of scalar multiplication in the context of modular arithmetic.

AddAction.zmultiplesQuotientStabilizerEq.fullDefinition: noncomputable def zmultiplesQuotientStabilizerEquiv :     zmultiples a ⧸ stabilizer (zmultiples a) b ≃+ ZMod (minimalPeriod (a +ᵥ ·) b) :=   (ofBijective           (map _ (stabilizer (zmultiples a) b) (zmultiplesHom (zmultiples a) ⟨a, mem_zmultiples a⟩)             (by               rw [zmultiples_le, mem_comap, mem_stabilizer_iff, zmultiplesHom_apply, natCast_zsmul]               simp_rw [← vadd_iterate]               exact isPeriodicPt_minimalPeriod (a +ᵥ ·) b))           ⟨by             rw [← ker_eq_bot_iff, eq_bot_iff]             refine fun q => induction_on' q fun n hn => ?_             rw [mem_bot, eq_zero_iff, Int.mem_zmultiples_iff, ←               zsmul_vadd_eq_iff_minimalPeriod_dvd]             exact (eq_zero_iff _).mp hn, fun q =>             induction_on' q fun ⟨_, n, rfl⟩ => ⟨n, rfl⟩⟩).symm.trans     (Int.quotientZMultiplesNatEquivZMod (minimalPeriod (a +ᵥ ·) b))

explanatories.IsScalarTower.complexToReal: This definition establishes that the scalar action of real numbers on a complex module behaves as a scalar tower in conjunction with another scalar action if the complex scalar action demonstrates the same property.
explanatories.smul_one_smul: This theorem shows that multiplying an element by one and then applying scalar multiplication to another element is equivalent to directly applying the scalar multiplication of the first element to the second, demonstrating a specific property of scalar multiplication in the context of a scalar tower.
explanatories.StarModule.star_smul: This theorem asserts that in a star module, the star operation distributes over scalar multiplication, meaning the star of a scalar multiplied by a vector equals the product of the star of the scalar and the star of the vector.
explanatories.star_one: This theorem states that in a structure with multiplicative identity and a star multiplication operation, the star of the multiplicative identity equals the multiplicative identity itself.

Complex.liftAux.fullDefinition: def liftAux (I' : A) (hf : I' * I' = -1) : ℂ →ₐ[ℝ] A :=   AlgHom.ofLinearMap     ((Algebra.linearMap ℝ A).comp reLm + (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton _ _ I').comp imLm)     (show algebraMap ℝ A 1 + (0 : ℝ) • I' = 1 by rw [RingHom.map_one, zero_smul, add_zero])     fun ⟨x₁, y₁⟩ ⟨x₂, y₂⟩ =>     show       algebraMap ℝ A (x₁ * x₂ - y₁ * y₂) + (x₁ * y₂ + y₁ * x₂) • I' =         (algebraMap ℝ A x₁ + y₁ • I') * (algebraMap ℝ A x₂ + y₂ • I') by       rw [add_mul, mul_add, mul_add, add_comm _ (y₁ • I' * y₂ • I'), add_add_add_comm]       congr 1       -- equate "real" and "imaginary" parts       · let inst : SMulCommClass ℝ A A := by infer_instance  -- Porting note: added         rw [smul_mul_smul, hf, smul_neg, ← Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, ← sub_eq_add_neg, ←           RingHom.map_mul, ← RingHom.map_sub]       · rw [Algebra.smul_def, Algebra.smul_def, Algebra.smul_def, ← Algebra.right_comm _ x₂, ←           mul_assoc, ← add_mul, ← RingHom.map_mul, ← RingHom.map_mul, ← RingHom.map_add]
Complex.liftAux.description: This definition describes a homomorphism from the complex numbers to any real algebra that includes an element whose square is negative one.

explanatories.Complex.ext: This proves that if two complex numbers have equal real and imaginary parts, then they are equal to each other.
explanatories.SMulCommClass.smul_comm: This theorem states that in the presence of a commutative scalar multiplication structure, the order of multiplying two elements with a third remains unchanged when using scalar multiplication.

explanatories.Finsupp.ext: If two finitely supported functions yield the same value for every input, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.StarModule.star_smul: This theorem asserts that in a star module, the star operation distributes over scalar multiplication, meaning the star of a scalar multiplied by a vector equals the product of the star of the scalar and the star of the vector.
explanatories.OneHom.toFun: This definition describes the underlying function associated with a one homomorphism between two types that each have a one element.

explanatories.neg_neg: This theorem states that applying the negation operation twice on an element in a type with involutive negation returns the original element.
explanatories.AddSubgroup.coe_add: This theorem establishes that the image of the sum of two elements from an additive subgroup corresponds to the sum of their respective images in the additive group.
explanatories.AddMemClass.mk_add_mk: For two elements belonging to an additive substructure, their corresponding representations in the underlying set combine to yield the representation of their sum in the same substructure.
explanatories.skewAdjoint.val_smul: The scalar multiplication of an element from the skew adjoint set in a star module is preserved under the inclusion map.
explanatories.AddSubgroup.coe_mk: This theorem establishes that the natural representation of an element from an additive subgroup is equal to the original element itself.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.selfAdjoint.val_smul: The image of the scalar multiplication of a self-adjoint element is equal to the scalar multiplied by the image of the element.
explanatories.neg_inj: The negation of two elements in an involutive negation structure is equal if and only if the original elements are equal.
explanatories.Bool.false: The boolean value false is a specific representation of the false state in boolean logic.
explanatories.AddSubmonoid.coe_add: The addition operation in an additive submonoid is compatible with the addition operation in the larger additive structure.

realPart.comment:
The real part `ℜ a` of an element `a` of a star module over `ℂ`, as a linear map. This is just
`selfAdjointPart ℝ`, but we provide it as a separate definition in order to link it with lemmas
concerning the `imaginaryPart`, which doesn't exist in star modules over other rings.

  A →ₗ[ℝ] ↥(selfAdjoint A)
imaginaryPart.comment:
The imaginary part `ℑ a` of an element `a` of a star module over `ℂ`, as a linear map into the
self adjoint elements. In a general star module, we have a decomposition into the `selfAdjoint`
and `skewAdjoint` parts, but in a star module over `ℂ` we have
`realPart_add_I_smul_imaginaryPart`, which allows us to decompose into a linear combination of
`selfAdjoint`s.

explanatories.skewAdjoint.negISMul: This definition describes a linear map that transforms an element classified as skew-adjoint into a self-adjoint element by multiplying it with the scalar negative of the imaginary unit.

imaginaryPart.eq_1.description: This theorem states that the imaginary part of a vector space is equal to the composition of the negated scalar multiplication by the imaginary unit and the real skew-adjoint operator applied to the vector.

Complex.selfAdjointEquiv.fullDefinition: def Complex.selfAdjointEquiv : selfAdjoint ℂ ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℝ where   toFun := fun z ↦ (z : ℂ).re   invFun := fun x ↦ ⟨x, conj_ofReal x⟩   left_inv := fun z ↦ Subtype.ext <| conj_eq_iff_re.mp z.property.star_eq   right_inv := fun x ↦ rfl   map_add' := by simp   map_smul' := by simp
Complex.selfAdjointEquiv.description: This definition establishes a natural linear equivalence between the space of self-adjoint complex numbers and the real numbers.

Real.expNear.comment:
A finite initial segment of the exponential series, followed by an arbitrary tail.
For fixed `n` this is just a linear map wrt `r`, and each map is a simple linear function
of the previous (see `expNear_succ`), with `expNear n x r ⟶ exp x` as `n ⟶ ∞`,
for any `r`.

Real.expNear.fullDefinition: noncomputable def expNear (n : ℕ) (x r : ℝ) : ℝ :=   (∑ m ∈ range n, x ^ m / m.factorial) + x ^ n / n.factorial * r
Real.expNear.description: This definition describes a function that represents a finite segment of the exponential series along with an additional unbounded tail, showing linear behavior with respect to some variable while converging to the exponential function as the segment increases indefinitely.

Finmap.keysLookupEquiv.fullDefinition: def keysLookupEquiv :     Finmap β ≃ { f : Finset α × (∀ a, Option (β a)) // ∀ i, (f.2 i).isSome ↔ i ∈ f.1 } where   toFun s := ⟨(s.keys, fun i => s.lookup i), fun _ => lookup_isSome⟩   invFun f := mk (f.1.1.sigma fun i => (f.1.2 i).toFinset).val <| by     refine Multiset.nodup_keys.1 ((Finset.nodup _).map_on ?_)     simp only [Finset.mem_val, Finset.mem_sigma, Option.mem_toFinset, Option.mem_def]     rintro ⟨i, x⟩ ⟨_, hx⟩ ⟨j, y⟩ ⟨_, hy⟩ (rfl : i = j)     simpa using hx.symm.trans hy   left_inv f := ext <| by simp   right_inv := fun ⟨(s, f), hf⟩ => by     dsimp only at hf     ext     · simp [keys, Multiset.keys, ← hf, Option.isSome_iff_exists]     · simp (config := { contextual := true }) [lookup_eq_some_iff, ← hf]

MvPFunctor.wRec.fullDefinition: def wRec {α : TypeVec n} {C : Type*}     (g : ∀ a : P.A, P.drop.B a ⟹ α → (P.last.B a → P.W α) → (P.last.B a → C) → C) : P.W α → C   | ⟨a, f'⟩ =>     let g' (a : P.A) (f : P.last.B a → P.last.W) (h : P.WPath ⟨a, f⟩ ⟹ α)       (h' : P.last.B a → C) : C :=       g a (P.wPathDestLeft h) (fun i => ⟨f i, P.wPathDestRight h i⟩) h'     P.wpRec g' a f' set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
MvPFunctor.wRec.description: This definition introduces a recursion scheme for constructing results involving a well-founded type from a mutable vector functor by allowing evaluations based on the structure's elements and their associated mappings.

MvPFunctor.wRec.eq_1.code:
MvPFunctor.wRec.eq_1.{u, u_1} {n : ℕ} (P : MvPFunctor.{u} (n + 1)) {α : TypeVec.{u} n} {C : Type u_1}
  (g : (a : P.A) → P.drop.B a ⟹ α → (P.last.B a → P.W α) → (P.last.B a → C) → C) :
  ∀ (x : P.W α),
    P.wRec g x =
      match x with
      | ⟨a, f'⟩ =>
        let g' := fun a f h h' => g a (P.wPathDestLeft h) (fun i => ⟨f i, P.wPathDestRight h i⟩) h';
        P.wpRec g' a f'

MvPFunctor.M.corecContents.fullDefinition: def M.corecContents {α : TypeVec.{u} n}     {β : Type u}     (g₀ : β → P.A)     (g₁ : ∀ b : β, P.drop.B (g₀ b) ⟹ α)     (g₂ : ∀ b : β, P.last.B (g₀ b) → β)     (x : _)     (b : β)     (h : x = M.corecShape P g₀ g₂ b) :     M.Path P x ⟹ α   | _, M.Path.root x a f h' i c =>     have : a = g₀ b := by       rw [h, M.corecShape, PFunctor.M.dest_corec] at h'       cases h'       rfl     g₁ b i (P.castDropB this i c)   | _, M.Path.child x a f h' j i c =>     have h₀ : a = g₀ b := by       rw [h, M.corecShape, PFunctor.M.dest_corec] at h'       cases h'       rfl     have h₁ : f j = M.corecShape P g₀ g₂ (g₂ b (castLastB P h₀ j)) := by       rw [h, M.corecShape, PFunctor.M.dest_corec] at h'       cases h'       rfl     M.corecContents g₀ g₁ g₂ (f j) (g₂ b (P.castLastB h₀ j)) h₁ i c

Finsupp.update.comment:

Finsupp.mapRange.code:
Finsupp.mapRange.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} [Zero M] [Zero N] (f : M → N)
  (hf : f 0 = 0) (g : α →₀ M) : α →₀ N
Finsupp.mapRange.comment:
The composition of `f : M → N` and `g : α →₀ M` is `mapRange f hf g : α →₀ N`,
which is well-defined when `f 0 = 0`.

This preserves the structure on `f`, and exists in various bundled forms for when `f` is itself
bundled (defined in `Data/Finsupp/Basic`):

* `Finsupp.mapRange.equiv`
* `Finsupp.mapRange.zeroHom`
* `Finsupp.mapRange.addMonoidHom`
* `Finsupp.mapRange.addEquiv`
* `Finsupp.mapRange.linearMap`
* `Finsupp.mapRange.linearEquiv`

explanatories.Finsupp.support: This definition specifies the set of elements in a finitely supported function that have non-zero values.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_support_iff: This theorem states that an element belongs to the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluated at that element is non-zero.
explanatories.Function.support: This definition introduces the support of a function as the set of inputs for which the function does not map to the additive identity.
explanatories.Equiv.trans: This definition establishes a method for composing two equivalence relations to create a new equivalence relation between the first and last types.
explanatories.HasSubset.Subset.trans: A theorem indicating that this is an alternative name for the transitive property of set inclusion.
explanatories.Finsupp.onFinset: This definition establishes a finitely supported function based on a specified finite set of elements, ensuring that the function evaluates to zero outside of this set.
explanatories.not_imp_not: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the statement that the negation of a implies the negation of b and the statement that b implies a.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.

Finsupp.mapRange.fullDefinition: def mapRange (f : M → N) (hf : f 0 = 0) (g : α →₀ M) : α →₀ N :=   onFinset g.support (f ∘ g) fun a => by     rw [mem_support_iff, not_imp_not]; exact fun H => (congr_arg f H).trans hf
Finsupp.mapRange.description: This definition describes a method to transform a finitely supported function by mapping its values through another function, under the condition that the mapping preserves the zero value.

Finsupp.mapRange_apply.code:
Finsupp.mapRange_apply.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} [Zero M] [Zero N] {f : M → N}
  {hf : f 0 = 0} {g : α →₀ M} {a : α} : (mapRange f hf g) a = f (g a)
Finsupp.mapRange_apply.description: This theorem demonstrates that applying a function to the range of a finitely supported function yields the same result as applying the function to the value of that finitely supported function at a specific index.

Finsupp.mapRange_zero.code:
Finsupp.mapRange_zero.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} [Zero M] [Zero N] {f : M → N}
  {hf : f 0 = 0} : mapRange f hf 0 = 0
Finsupp.mapRange_zero.description: This theorem asserts that applying a function that maps zero to zero to the zero element in a finitely supported function results in zero.

Finsupp.mapRange_id.code: Finsupp.mapRange_id.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] (g : α →₀ M) : mapRange id ⋯ g = g
Finsupp.mapRange_id.description: This theorem asserts that applying the identity function through a range mapping to a finitely supported function results in the original function remaining unchanged.

Finsupp.mapRange_comp.code:
Finsupp.mapRange_comp.{u_1, u_5, u_7, u_8} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} {P : Type u_8} [Zero M] [Zero N]
  [Zero P] (f : N → P) (hf : f 0 = 0) (f₂ : M → N) (hf₂ : f₂ 0 = 0) (h : (f ∘ f₂) 0 = 0) (g : α →₀ M) :
  mapRange (f ∘ f₂) h g = mapRange f hf (mapRange f₂ hf₂ g)
Finsupp.mapRange_comp.description: The theorem establishes a relationship between the composition of two functions and their respective mappings in finitely supported functions, ensuring that the mapped output of their composition is equal to the sequential application of their mappings under certain conditions.

Finsupp.support_mapRange.code:
Finsupp.support_mapRange.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} [Zero M] [Zero N] {f : M → N}
  {hf : f 0 = 0} {g : α →₀ M} : (mapRange f hf g).support ⊆ g.support

explanatories.Finsupp.mapRange: This definition describes a method to transform a finitely supported function by mapping its values through another function, under the condition that the mapping preserves the zero value.

Finsupp.support_mapRange.description: This theorem states that the support of a function resulting from applying a specific transformation to a finitely supported function is contained within the support of the original function.

Finsupp.mapRange_single.code:
Finsupp.mapRange_single.{u_1, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} [Zero M] [Zero N] {f : M → N}

explanatories.Pi.single: This definition describes a way to create a function that assigns a specific value to one index while defaulting to zero for all other indices in the collection.
explanatories.Finsupp.single: This definition describes a finitely supported function that assigns a specific value to one input while being zero for all other inputs.

Finsupp.mapRange_single.description: This theorem states that applying a function to a finitely supported function that assigns a specific value results in a new finitely supported function with the same index but whose value is transformed by the function.

Finsupp.support_mapRange_of_injective.code:
Finsupp.support_mapRange_of_injective.{u_4, u_5, u_7} {ι : Type u_4} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} [Zero M] [Zero N]

explanatories.Function.support: This definition introduces the support of a function as the set of inputs for which the function does not map to the additive identity.
explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.Finsupp.mapRange: This definition describes a method to transform a finitely supported function by mapping its values through another function, under the condition that the mapping preserves the zero value.

Finsupp.support_mapRange_of_injective.description: This theorem states that the support of a finitely supported function remains unchanged when it is transformed through an injective mapping that preserves the zero element.

Finsupp.embDomain.code:
Finsupp.embDomain.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] (f : α ↪ β) (v : α →₀ M) :
  β →₀ M
Finsupp.embDomain.comment:
Given `f : α ↪ β` and `v : α →₀ M`, `Finsupp.embDomain f v : β →₀ M`
is the finitely supported function whose value at `f a : β` is `v a`.
For a `b : β` outside the range of `f`, it is zero.

explanatories.Membership.mem: The membership relation defines a property indicating that an element belongs to a set.
explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.Finsupp.support: This definition specifies the set of elements in a finitely supported function that have non-zero values.
explanatories.Finsupp.toFun: This definition describes the actual mapping function of a finitely supported function, which takes an input and returns its corresponding value in a specified type.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_support_toFun: This theorem states that an element is in the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluates to a non-zero value at that element.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Function.support: This definition introduces the support of a function as the set of inputs for which the function does not map to the additive identity.
explanatories.Finsupp.not_mem_support_iff: This theorem states that an element is not in the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluates to zero at that element.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Classical.decEq: This definition asserts that any type has a mechanism for determining equality between its elements in a classical framework.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Classical.not_not: The Double Negation Theorem states that the negation of the negation of a proposition is equivalent to the proposition itself.
explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.
explanatories.Finset.choose: This definition specifies a function that, given a finite set and a decidable predicate confirmed to have a unique satisfying element, returns that unique element from the finite set.
explanatories.Finset.mem_map: This theorem asserts that an element belongs to the finite set obtained by mapping through an injective function if and only if there exists an element in the original set that maps to it under that function.
explanatories.ExistsUnique.intro: Theorem asserting that if there exists an element satisfying a property and it is the only such element, then that existence is uniquely determined.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.injective: An embedding is shown to be injective, ensuring that different inputs yield different outputs when mapped to another set.
explanatories.true_iff_iff: Theorem stating that a biconditional between a truth value and a proposition is equivalent to the proposition itself.
explanatories.Finset.choose_mem: This theorem establishes that if there is a unique element in a finite set that satisfies a given property, then that element is indeed a member of the set.
explanatories.ne_self_iff_false: An element is not equal to itself if and only if a contradiction exists.
explanatories.not_true_eq_false: The theorem states that the negation of a true proposition is equivalent to a false proposition.

Finsupp.embDomain.fullDefinition: def embDomain (f : α ↪ β) (v : α →₀ M) : β →₀ M where   support := v.support.map f   toFun a₂ :=     haveI := Classical.decEq β     if h : a₂ ∈ v.support.map f then       v         (v.support.choose (fun a₁ => f a₁ = a₂)           (by             rcases Finset.mem_map.1 h with ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩             exact ExistsUnique.intro a ⟨ha, rfl⟩ fun b ⟨_, hb⟩ => f.injective hb))     else 0   mem_support_toFun a₂ := by     dsimp     split_ifs with h     · simp only [h, true_iff_iff, Ne]       rw [← not_mem_support_iff, not_not]       classical apply Finset.choose_mem     · simp only [h, Ne, ne_self_iff_false, not_true_eq_false]
Finsupp.embDomain.description: This definition describes a method for creating a finitely supported function whose values correspond to those of another function, while mapping inputs from one set to outputs in another and ensuring all other inputs outside this mapping are assigned a value of zero.

Finsupp.support_embDomain.code:

explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.
explanatories.Finsupp.embDomain: This definition describes a method for creating a finitely supported function whose values correspond to those of another function, while mapping inputs from one set to outputs in another and ensuring all other inputs outside this mapping are assigned a value of zero.

Finsupp.support_embDomain.description: This theorem asserts that the support of a finitely supported function, when transformed by an embedding from one domain to another, is equal to the image of the original support under that embedding.

Finsupp.embDomain_zero.code:
Finsupp.embDomain_zero.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] (f : α ↪ β) :
  embDomain f 0 = 0
Finsupp.embDomain_zero.description: This theorem states that embedding a function from one domain to another with a zero value results in the zero function.

Finsupp.embDomain_apply.code:
Finsupp.embDomain_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] (f : α ↪ β) (v : α →₀ M)
  (a : α) : (embDomain f v) (f a) = v a
Finsupp.embDomain_apply.description: This theorem demonstrates that applying an embedding to a finitely supported function at the image of an element produces the same result as applying the function directly to that element.

Finsupp.embDomain_notin_range.code:

explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

Finsupp.embDomain_notin_range.description: This theorem establishes that if a function does not map to a specific element, then the value of a finitely supported function extended to the domain of that mapping is zero at that element.

Finsupp.embDomain_injective.code:
Finsupp.embDomain_injective.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] (f : α ↪ β) :
  Injective (embDomain f)

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Finsupp.embDomain_injective.description: This theorem asserts that the process of embedding finitely supported functions from one set to another via an injective mapping preserves uniqueness, ensuring that different inputs in the original set yield distinct outputs in the target space.

Finsupp.embDomain_inj.code:
Finsupp.embDomain_inj.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] {f : α ↪ β}
  {l₁ l₂ : α →₀ M} : embDomain f l₁ = embDomain f l₂ ↔ l₁ = l₂
Finsupp.embDomain_inj.description: This theorem asserts that the embedding of two finitely supported functions is equal if and only if the original functions themselves are equal.

Finsupp.embDomain_eq_zero.code:
Finsupp.embDomain_eq_zero.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] {f : α ↪ β}
  {l : α →₀ M} : embDomain f l = 0 ↔ l = 0
Finsupp.embDomain_eq_zero.description: This theorem indicates that the embedding of a finitely supported function into another domain is zero if and only if the original function itself is zero.

Finsupp.embDomain_mapRange.code:
Finsupp.embDomain_mapRange.{u_1, u_2, u_5, u_7} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} [Zero M]

Finsupp.embDomain_mapRange.description: This theorem states that applying a function that embeds the domain of a finitely supported function followed by mapping its range yields the same result as first mapping the range and then embedding the domain.

explanatories.Finsupp.embDomain: This definition describes a method for creating a finitely supported function whose values correspond to those of another function, while mapping inputs from one set to outputs in another and ensuring all other inputs outside this mapping are assigned a value of zero.

Finsupp.single_of_embDomain_single.description: This theorem demonstrates that if a finitely supported function, when embedded via an injective map, matches a single element mapping, then there exists an original input that produces this mapping while maintaining the value associated with it.

Finsupp.embDomain_single.code:
Finsupp.embDomain_single.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {M : Type u_5} [Zero M] (f : α ↪ β) (a : α)
  (m : M) : embDomain f (single a m) = single (f a) m

explanatories.Finsupp.single: This definition describes a finitely supported function that assigns a specific value to one input while being zero for all other inputs.

Finsupp.embDomain_single.description: This theorem establishes that embedding a finitely supported function that assigns a value to a single input results in a function that assigns the same value to the image of that input under the embedding.

Finsupp.zipWith.code:
Finsupp.zipWith.{u_1, u_5, u_7, u_8} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} {P : Type u_8} [Zero M] [Zero N]

Finsupp.zipWith.comment:
Given finitely supported functions `g₁ : α →₀ M` and `g₂ : α →₀ N` and function `f : M → N → P`,
`Finsupp.zipWith f hf g₁ g₂` is the finitely supported function `α →₀ P` satisfying
`zipWith f hf g₁ g₂ a = f (g₁ a) (g₂ a)`, which is well-defined when `f 0 0 = 0`.

explanatories.Function.support: This definition introduces the support of a function as the set of inputs for which the function does not map to the additive identity.
explanatories.Classical.decEq: This definition asserts that any type has a mechanism for determining equality between its elements in a classical framework.
explanatories.Finsupp.onFinset: This definition establishes a finitely supported function based on a specified finite set of elements, ensuring that the function evaluates to zero outside of this set.
explanatories.Union.union: The union of two elements is defined as the combination of both elements into a single entity.

Finsupp.zipWith.fullDefinition: def zipWith (f : M → N → P) (hf : f 0 0 = 0) (g₁ : α →₀ M) (g₂ : α →₀ N) : α →₀ P :=   onFinset     (haveI := Classical.decEq α; g₁.support ∪ g₂.support)     (fun a => f (g₁ a) (g₂ a))     fun a (H : f _ _ ≠ 0) => by       classical       rw [mem_union, mem_support_iff, mem_support_iff, ← not_and_or]       rintro ⟨h₁, h₂⟩; rw [h₁, h₂] at H; exact H hf
Finsupp.zipWith.description: This definition introduces a method for combining two finitely supported functions into a new finitely supported function, where the values are determined by applying a binary function to the corresponding values of the original functions.

Finsupp.zipWith_apply.code:
Finsupp.zipWith_apply.{u_1, u_5, u_7, u_8} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} {P : Type u_8} [Zero M] [Zero N]
  [Zero P] {f : M → N → P} {hf : f 0 0 = 0} {g₁ : α →₀ M} {g₂ : α →₀ N} {a : α} :
  (zipWith f hf g₁ g₂) a = f (g₁ a) (g₂ a)
Finsupp.zipWith_apply.description: This theorem states that the result of applying a binary function to two finitely supported functions at a specific input is equal to the application of that function to the values of the two functions at that same input, given that the function maps zero inputs to zero outputs.

Finsupp.support_zipWith.code:
Finsupp.support_zipWith.{u_1, u_5, u_7, u_8} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} {N : Type u_7} {P : Type u_8} [Zero M]
  [Zero N] [Zero P] [D : DecidableEq α] {f : M → N → P} {hf : f 0 0 = 0} {g₁ : α →₀ M} {g₂ : α →₀ N} :
  (zipWith f hf g₁ g₂).support ⊆ g₁.support ∪ g₂.support

Finsupp.coe_add.code: Finsupp.coe_add.{u_1, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_5} [AddZeroClass M] (f g : α →₀ M) : ⇑(f + g) = ⇑f + ⇑g

Finsupp.add_apply.description: This theorem states that the value of the sum of two finitely supported functions at a specific input is equal to the sum of their individual values at that input.

Finsupp.zipWith_neLocus_eq_left.description: The set of indices where the results of two operations on finitely supported functions differ is equal to the set of indices where the second functions differ, when the operations satisfy specific injectivity and zero conditions.

Finsupp.zipWith_neLocus_eq_right.code:
Finsupp.zipWith_neLocus_eq_right.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {P : Type u_4}

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Finsupp.zipWith_neLocus_eq_right.description: The set of indices where the results of two finitely supported functions, obtained by applying a specified operation to a third function, differ is equal to the set of indices where the original functions differ.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Finsupp.mapRange_neLocus_eq.description: The set of indices where two finitely supported functions differ remains unchanged under a specific operation involving injective mappings and zero conditions.

Finsupp.neLocus_add_left.description: The set of indices where the sum of two finitely supported functions differs from the sum of another function is equal to the set of indices where the second function differs from the third function.

Finsupp.neLocus_add_right.code:

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_add_right.description: The set of indices where the sum of one finitely supported function differs from another, after adding the same third function, is equal to the set of indices where the first function differs from the second function.

Finsupp.neLocus_neg_neg.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_neg_neg.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_neg_neg.description: The set of indices where the negations of two finitely supported functions differ is equal to the set of indices where one function is positive while the other remains unchanged.

Finsupp.neLocus_neg.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_neg.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_neg.description: The set of indices where the negation of one finitely supported function differs from another is the same as the set of indices where the original function differs from the negation of the second function.

Finsupp.neLocus_eq_support_sub.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_eq_support_sub.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_eq_support_sub.description: The set of indices where two finitely supported functions differ is equal to the set of indices where the value of their difference is non-zero.

Finsupp.neLocus_sub_left.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_sub_left.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]
  (f g₁ g₂ : α →₀ N) : (f - g₁).neLocus (f - g₂) = g₁.neLocus g₂

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_sub_left.description: The set of indices where the differences of a function with two other functions are not equal corresponds to the set of indices where those two other functions differ.

Finsupp.neLocus_sub_right.code:
