explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_sub_right.description: The set of indices where the difference between one finitely supported function and another, after subtracting the same third function, differs is equal to the set of indices where the first two functions differ.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_add_right.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_self_add_right.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]
  (f g : α →₀ N) : f.neLocus (f + g) = g.support

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_add_right.description: The set of indices where a finitely supported function differs from the sum of itself and another function is exactly the support of the other function.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_add_left.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_self_add_left.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]
  (f g : α →₀ N) : (f + g).neLocus f = g.support

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_add_left.description: The set of indices where the sum of two finitely supported functions differs from one of them is equal to the support of the other function.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_sub_right.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_self_sub_right.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]
  (f g : α →₀ N) : f.neLocus (f - g) = g.support

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_sub_right.description: The set of indices where a finitely supported function differs from the result of subtracting another function from it is exactly the support of the other function.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_sub_left.code:
Finsupp.neLocus_self_sub_left.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {N : Type u_3} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq N] [AddGroup N]
  (f g : α →₀ N) : (f - g).neLocus f = g.support

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.neLocus_self_sub_left.description: The set of indices where the subtraction of one finitely supported function from another differs from the first function is equal to the support of the second function.

Finsupp.fintype.code:
Finsupp.fintype.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {π : Type u_2} [DecidableEq ι] [Zero π] [Fintype ι] [Fintype π] :
  Fintype (ι →₀ π)

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Fintype.ofEquiv: This definition states that if one type is finitely enumerable and there exists a bijection between it and another type, then the second type is also finitely enumerable.

Finsupp.fintype.fullDefinition: noncomputable instance Finsupp.fintype {ι π : Sort _} [DecidableEq ι] [Zero π] [Fintype ι]     [Fintype π] : Fintype (ι →₀ π) :=   Fintype.ofEquiv _ Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm
Finsupp.fintype.description: This definition establishes that the space of finitely supported functions from a finite type to another finite type is itself a finite type.

Finsupp.infinite_of_left.code:
Finsupp.infinite_of_left.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {π : Type u_2} [Nontrivial π] [Zero π] [Infinite ι] :
  Infinite (ι →₀ π)

explanatories.exists_ne: In a nontrivial type, for any chosen element, there exists at least one distinct element.
explanatories.Infinite.of_injective: This theorem states that if there exists an injective function from an infinite type to another type, then the codomain type must also be infinite.
explanatories.Finsupp.single_left_injective: This theorem establishes that the function which assigns a non-zero value to a specific input while defaulting to zero elsewhere is injective in the input variable.

Finsupp.infinite_of_left.fullDefinition: instance Finsupp.infinite_of_left {ι π : Sort _} [Nontrivial π] [Zero π] [Infinite ι] :     Infinite (ι →₀ π) :=   let ⟨_, hm⟩ := exists_ne (0 : π)   Infinite.of_injective _ <| Finsupp.single_left_injective hm
Finsupp.infinite_of_left.description: This definition asserts that the space of finitely supported functions from an infinite type to a nontrivial type is itself infinite.

Finsupp.infinite_of_right.code:
Finsupp.infinite_of_right.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {π : Type u_2} [Infinite π] [Zero π] [Nonempty ι] :
  Infinite (ι →₀ π)

explanatories.Infinite.of_injective: This theorem states that if there exists an injective function from an infinite type to another type, then the codomain type must also be infinite.
explanatories.Finsupp.single: This definition describes a finitely supported function that assigns a specific value to one input while being zero for all other inputs.
explanatories.Classical.arbitrary: A nonempty type can be represented by an arbitrary element chosen from it.
explanatories.Finsupp.single_injective: This theorem establishes that the finitely supported function that assigns a value to a specific input is injective with respect to that value.

Finsupp.infinite_of_right.fullDefinition: instance Finsupp.infinite_of_right {ι π : Sort _} [Infinite π] [Zero π] [Nonempty ι] :     Infinite (ι →₀ π) :=   Infinite.of_injective (fun i => Finsupp.single (Classical.arbitrary ι) i)     (Finsupp.single_injective (Classical.arbitrary ι))
Finsupp.infinite_of_right.description: This definition states that the space of finitely supported functions from a non-empty type to an infinite type is itself infinite.

Finsupp.tail.code: Finsupp.tail.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] (s : Fin (n + 1) →₀ M) : Fin n →₀ M
Finsupp.tail.comment: `tail` for maps `Fin (n + 1) →₀ M`. See `Fin.tail` for more details.

explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Fin.tail: This definition describes a function that retrieves the entry of a tuple corresponding to the successor of a given index from a tuple of length n+1.

Finsupp.tail.fullDefinition: def tail (s : Fin (n + 1) →₀ M) : Fin n →₀ M :=   Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm (Fin.tail s)
Finsupp.tail.description: This definition describes a function that returns the finitely supported function derived from an original function by omitting the last element.

Finsupp.cons.code: Finsupp.cons.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] (y : M) (s : Fin n →₀ M) : Fin (n + 1) →₀ M
Finsupp.cons.comment: `cons` for maps `Fin n →₀ M`. See `Fin.cons` for more details.

explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.

Finsupp.cons.fullDefinition: def cons (y : M) (s : Fin n →₀ M) : Fin (n + 1) →₀ M :=   Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm (Fin.cons y s : Fin (n + 1) → M)
Finsupp.cons.description: This definition describes a function that creates a finitely supported function by adding a new element at the front of an existing finitely supported function.

Finsupp.tail_apply.code: Finsupp.tail_apply.{u_1} {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] (t : Fin (n + 1) →₀ M) : t.tail i = t i.succ

explanatories.Fin.tail: This definition describes a function that retrieves the entry of a tuple corresponding to the successor of a given index from a tuple of length n+1.

Finsupp.tail_apply.description: This theorem states that the entry of a finitely supported function at an index corresponds to the entry at the successor of that index when the last element is omitted.

Finsupp.cons_zero.code: Finsupp.cons_zero.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] (y : M) (s : Fin n →₀ M) : (cons y s) 0 = y

explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.

Finsupp.cons_zero.description: This theorem states that the first entry of a finitely supported function created by adding a new element to the front of an existing function is equal to that new element.

Finsupp.cons_succ.code: Finsupp.cons_succ.{u_1} {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] (y : M) (s : Fin n →₀ M) : (cons y s) i.succ = s i

explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.
explanatories.Fin.succ: The successor of a finite number is produced by increasing its upper limit, resulting in a new finite number that is one greater.

Finsupp.cons_succ.description: This theorem states that for a finitely supported function created by adding a new element to the front, the entry at the index corresponding to the successor of an existing index is equal to the entry from the original function at that index.

Finsupp.tail_cons.code: Finsupp.tail_cons.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] (y : M) (s : Fin n →₀ M) : (cons y s).tail = s

explanatories.Fin.tail: This definition describes a function that retrieves the entry of a tuple corresponding to the successor of a given index from a tuple of length n+1.
explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.
explanatories.Finsupp.cons: This definition describes a function that creates a finitely supported function by adding a new element at the front of an existing finitely supported function.

Finsupp.tail_cons.description: This theorem states that the result of omitting the first element from a finitely supported function created by adding a new element to the front of an existing function is equal to the original function.

Finsupp.cons_tail.code: Finsupp.cons_tail.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] (t : Fin (n + 1) →₀ M) : cons (t 0) t.tail = t

explanatories.Fin.tail: This definition describes a function that retrieves the entry of a tuple corresponding to the successor of a given index from a tuple of length n+1.
explanatories.Finsupp.tail: This definition describes a function that returns the finitely supported function derived from an original function by omitting the last element.
explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.

Finsupp.cons_tail.description: This theorem states that a finitely supported function constructed by adding a new element at the front is equal to the original function when the first element is replaced by the first entry and the remainder of the entries is taken as the tail.

Finsupp.cons_zero_zero.code: Finsupp.cons_zero_zero.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] : cons 0 0 = 0

explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.

Finsupp.cons_zero_zero.description: This theorem states that when zero is added as the first element to another zero, the result is simply zero.

Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_of_left.code: Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_of_left.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] {y : M} {s : Fin n →₀ M} (h : y ≠ 0) : cons y s ≠ 0

explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.

Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_of_left.description: This theorem asserts that if the new element added to the front of a finitely supported function is non-zero, then the resulting function is also non-zero.

Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_of_right.code: Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_of_right.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] {y : M} {s : Fin n →₀ M} (h : s ≠ 0) : cons y s ≠ 0

explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.

Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_of_right.description: This theorem asserts that if a finitely supported function is non-zero, then adding a new element to the front results in another non-zero function.

Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_iff.code: Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_iff.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [Zero M] {y : M} {s : Fin n →₀ M} : cons y s ≠ 0 ↔ y ≠ 0 ∨ s ≠ 0

explanatories.Fin.cons: This definition describes a function that constructs an n+1-tuple by adding a new element at the beginning of an existing n-tuple.

Finsupp.cons_ne_zero_iff.description: This theorem establishes that a finitely supported function formed by adding a new element is non-zero if and only if either the new element or the original function is non-zero.

Finsupp.indicator.code: Finsupp.indicator.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] (s : Finset ι) (f : (i : ι) → i ∈ s → α) : ι →₀ α
Finsupp.indicator.comment: Create an element of `ι →₀ α` from a finset `s` and a function `f` defined on this finset.

explanatories.Classical.decEq: This definition asserts that any type has a mechanism for determining equality between its elements in a classical framework.
explanatories.Finset.filter: This definition describes a method for creating a new finite set that includes only the elements of an existing set that satisfy a given property.
explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.subtype: An embedding is defined that allows elements from a subtype, which satisfies a given property, to be associated with elements from the broader set while maintaining the injective nature of the mapping.
explanatories.Finsupp.support: This definition specifies the set of elements in a finitely supported function that have non-zero values.

Finsupp.indicator.fullDefinition: def indicator (s : Finset ι) (f : ∀ i ∈ s, α) : ι →₀ α where   toFun i :=     haveI := Classical.decEq ι     if H : i ∈ s then f i H else 0   support :=     haveI := Classical.decEq α     (s.attach.filter fun i : s => f i.1 i.2 ≠ 0).map (Embedding.subtype _)   mem_support_toFun i := by     classical simp
Finsupp.indicator.description: This definition describes a function that constructs a finitely supported function from a finite set and a specified function defined on that set.

Finsupp.indicator_of_mem.code:
Finsupp.indicator_of_mem.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] {s : Finset ι} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s)
  (f : (i : ι) → i ∈ s → α) : (indicator s f) i = f i hi
Finsupp.indicator_of_mem.description: If an element belongs to a given finite set, then the value of the finitely supported function at that element equals the value specified by the function defined on the set.

Finsupp.indicator_of_not_mem.code:
Finsupp.indicator_of_not_mem.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] {s : Finset ι} {i : ι} (hi : i ∉ s)
  (f : (i : ι) → i ∈ s → α) : (indicator s f) i = 0
Finsupp.indicator_of_not_mem.description: If an element does not belong to a given finite set, then the value of the finitely supported function at that element is zero.

Finsupp.indicator_apply.code:
Finsupp.indicator_apply.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] (s : Finset ι) (f : (i : ι) → i ∈ s → α)
  (i : ι) [DecidableEq ι] : (indicator s f) i = if hi : i ∈ s then f i hi else 0

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

Finsupp.indicator_apply.description: The theorem states that the value of the finitely supported function at a given element is determined by whether that element is in the finite set, yielding the corresponding function value or zero.

Finsupp.indicator_injective.code:
Finsupp.indicator_injective.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] (s : Finset ι) :
  Injective fun f => indicator s f

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Finsupp.indicator_injective.description: The theorem asserts that the construction of finitely supported functions from a finite set is injective, meaning different functions defined on the set yield different finitely supported functions.

Finsupp.support_indicator_subset.code:
Finsupp.support_indicator_subset.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] (s : Finset ι)
  (f : (i : ι) → i ∈ s → α) : ↑(indicator s f).support ⊆ ↑s

explanatories.Finsupp.indicator: This definition describes a function that constructs a finitely supported function from a finite set and a specified function defined on that set.

Finsupp.support_indicator_subset.description: The theorem confirms that the support of the finitely supported function constructed from a finite set is a subset of the original set.

Finsupp.single_eq_indicator.code:
Finsupp.single_eq_indicator.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [Zero α] (i : ι) (b : α) :
  single i b = indicator {i} fun x x => b

  (v : α →₀ M) : β →₀ M
Finsupp.mapDomain.comment:
Given `f : α → β` and `v : α →₀ M`, `mapDomain f v : β →₀ M`
is the finitely supported function whose value at `a : β` is the sum
of `v x` over all `x` such that `f x = a`.

explanatories.Finsupp.sum: This defines a function that computes the product of another function evaluated at elements supported by a given finitely supported function.

Finsupp.mapDomain.fullDefinition: def mapDomain (f : α → β) (v : α →₀ M) : β →₀ M :=   v.sum fun a => single (f a)
Finsupp.mapDomain.description: This definition constructs a finitely supported function in the target domain by summing the values of an original finitely supported function over all elements that map to the same target element through a given function.

explanatories.Finsupp.support: This definition specifies the set of elements in a finitely supported function that have non-zero values.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_support_iff: This theorem states that an element belongs to the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluated at that element is non-zero.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_support_toFun: This theorem states that an element is in the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluates to a non-zero value at that element.

explanatories.Finset.filter: This definition describes a method for creating a new finite set that includes only the elements of an existing set that satisfy a given property.
explanatories.Finset.mem_filter: This theorem states that an element belongs to the filtered version of a set if and only if it is in the original set and satisfies the filtering condition.

explanatories.Classical.em: Every proposition is either true or false, a principle known as the law of excluded middle.

explanatories.Classical.em: Every proposition is either true or false, a principle known as the law of excluded middle.
explanatories.Or.symm: The disjunction operation is symmetric, meaning that if one proposition is true or the other, then the order of these propositions can be reversed.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_support_iff: This theorem states that an element belongs to the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluated at that element is non-zero.

explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.DFinsupp.support: This definition describes the support of a finitely supported function as the finite set of indices for which the function takes non-zero values.
explanatories.Finsupp.mk: This theorem provides a construction method for creating a finitely supported function from a specified support set and a mapping function, ensuring the function's non-zero values correspond to the elements in the support.
explanatories.DFinsupp.mem_support_iff: This theorem states that an index belongs to the support of a finitely-supported function if and only if the function at that index is non-zero.
explanatories.Equiv.left_inv: This theorem asserts that the inverse function of an equivalence relation is a left inverse of the original function.
explanatories.Equiv.right_inv: This theorem states that the inverse function of an equivalence relation has a right inverse that retrieves the original function.
explanatories.Finsupp.split: The split function extracts the corresponding component of a finitely supported function that maps from a dependent type to another structure, based on a specified index.
explanatories.Finset.mem_def: This theorem states that an element belongs to a finite set if and only if it belongs to the underlying multiset representation of that set.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_splitSupport_iff_nonzero: An index is included in the support of a split function if and only if the result of splitting the original function at that index is non-zero.
explanatories.em: This theorem states that for any proposition, either it is true or its negation is true, reflecting the principle of excluded middle.
explanatories.Classical.decEq: This definition asserts that any type has a mechanism for determining equality between its elements in a classical framework.
explanatories.Finsupp.onFinset: This definition establishes a finitely supported function based on a specified finite set of elements, ensuring that the function evaluates to zero outside of this set.
explanatories.Finset.sigma: This definition establishes a finite set of dependent pairs formed by combining elements from a finite set of indices with their corresponding sets of values.
explanatories.Finset.mem_sigma: An element is part of the set of dependent pairs if and only if its first component belongs to the original set and its second component belongs to the corresponding set determined by the first component.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.DFinsupp.mem_support_toFun: This theorem states that an index is part of the support of a dependent function with finite support if and only if the value at that index is non-zero.
explanatories.Finsupp.coe_zero: The theorem asserts that the zero finitely supported function is equal to the zero function.
explanatories.Pi.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that for any element of a collection where each element is an instance of the "zero" type, the application of the "zero" value to that element yields the "zero" value.
explanatories.not_true: The negation of truth corresponds exactly to falsehood, establishing a logical equivalence between these two concepts.

Finsupp.toMultiset.code: Finsupp.toMultiset.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} : (α →₀ ℕ) →+ Multiset α
Finsupp.toMultiset.comment:
Given `f : α →₀ ℕ`, `f.toMultiset` is the multiset with multiplicities given by the values of
`f` on the elements of `α`. We define this function as an `AddMonoidHom`.

Under the additional assumption of `[DecidableEq α]`, this is available as
`Multiset.toFinsupp : Multiset α ≃+ (α →₀ ℕ)`; the two declarations are separate as this assumption
is only needed for one direction.

explanatories.Finsupp.sum: This defines a function that computes the product of another function evaluated at elements supported by a given finitely supported function.
explanatories.Finsupp.sum_zero_index: The product of a function evaluated at a finitely supported function with no non-zero values equals one.
explanatories.Finsupp.sum_add_index': The product of two finitely supported functions evaluated through an additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism equals the product of their individual evaluations under that homomorphism, provided certain conditions are met.
explanatories.zero_nsmul: This theorem states that multiplying any element by zero in an additive monoid results in zero.
explanatories.Finset.sum: This defines a function that computes the sum of a function's values at each element of a finite set.
explanatories.Multiset.sum: This defines a function that computes the sum of elements in a multiset based on a commutative additive monoid structure.

Finsupp.toMultiset.fullDefinition: def toMultiset : (α →₀ ℕ) →+ Multiset α where   toFun f := Finsupp.sum f fun a n => n • {a}   -- Porting note: times out if h is not specified   map_add' _f _g := sum_add_index' (h := fun a n => n • ({a} : Multiset α))     (fun _ ↦ zero_nsmul _) (fun _ ↦ add_nsmul _)   map_zero' := sum_zero_index
Finsupp.toMultiset.description: This definition establishes a way to construct a multiset from a finitely supported function, where the multiplicities of each element in the multiset correspond to the values assigned by the function.

explanatories.Finsupp.sum: This defines a function that computes the product of another function evaluated at elements supported by a given finitely supported function.
explanatories.Finsupp.toMultiset: This definition establishes a way to construct a multiset from a finitely supported function, where the multiplicities of each element in the multiset correspond to the values assigned by the function.
explanatories.Finsupp.toMultiset_apply: This theorem states that the multiset generated from a finitely supported function is equivalent to the sum of the individual contributions of each element weighted by their corresponding multiplicities.
explanatories.Finset.sum: This defines a function that computes the sum of a function's values at each element of a finite set.
explanatories.Multiset.toFinset: This definition describes a function that transforms a multiset into a finite set by eliminating any duplicate elements.
explanatories.Multiset.count: This definition describes a function that returns the number of times a specific element appears in a multiset.
explanatories.Multiset.count_nsmul: This theorem establishes that the count of a specific element in a scaled multiset is equal to the product of the scaling factor and the count of that element in the original multiset.
explanatories.Multiset.count_singleton: This theorem states that the count of an element in a singleton multiset is one if the element matches the singleton's value, and zero otherwise.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Finsupp.mem_support_iff: This theorem states that an element belongs to the support of a finitely supported function if and only if the function evaluated at that element is non-zero.
explanatories.Finsupp.coe_mk: The theorem states that a finitely supported function constructed from a given function and its support is equal to the original function if the support condition is satisfied.
explanatories.Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq: The sum of the counts of elements in a multiset, multiplied by their corresponding singleton sets, equals the original multiset itself.
explanatories.Finsupp.ext: If two finitely supported functions yield the same value for every input, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.Multiset.count_sum': The count of a particular element in the sum of multisets generated by a function over a finite set equals the sum of the counts of that element in each individual multiset.
explanatories.mul_boole: This theorem states that there is no specific mathematical assertion or property presented.
explanatories.Finset.sum_ite_eq: The theorem states that the sum of a function's values over a finite set, conditioned on a specific element, equals the function's value evaluated at that element if it belongs to the set, otherwise it is zero.
explanatories.ite_not: The result of a conditional expression with a negated condition is equivalent to swapping the outcomes for the original condition.
explanatories.ite_eq_right_iff: This theorem establishes that a conditional expression equaling the second option is equivalent to the condition implying that both options are equal.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Multiset.count_add: This theorem states that the count of a specific element in the union of two multisets is equal to the sum of its counts in each individual multiset.
explanatories.AddEquiv.symm: The definition states that the inverse of an additive isomorphism is also an additive isomorphism.
explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Multiset.sum: This defines a function that computes the sum of elements in a multiset based on a commutative additive monoid structure.

Multiset.toFinsupp.description: This definition establishes a bijective relationship between a multiset and a finitely supported function that counts the multiplicities of its elements.

Sym.equivNatSum.comment:
The `n`th symmetric power of a type `α` is naturally equivalent to the subtype of
finitely-supported maps `α →₀ ℕ` with total mass `n`.

See also `Sym.equivNatSumOfFintype` when `α` is finite.

Sym.equivNatSum.fullDefinition: def equivNatSum :     Sym α n ≃ {P : α →₀ ℕ // P.sum (fun _ ↦ id) = n} :=   Multiset.toFinsupp.toEquiv.subtypeEquiv <| by simp
Sym.equivNatSum.description: This definition establishes a natural equivalence between the n-th symmetric power of a type and the subtype of finitely supported functions that map elements of that type to natural numbers, ensuring the total sum equals n.

explanatories.Finsupp.sum_fintype: If the domain of a finitely supported function is finite and a certain property holds for every element in that domain, then the product of a function evaluated at the finitely supported function equals the product of the same function evaluated at each element in the domain.

Sym.equivNatSumOfFintype.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equivNatSumOfFintype [Fintype α] :     Sym α n ≃ {P : α → ℕ // ∑ i, P i = n} :=   (equivNatSum α n).trans <| Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.subtypeEquiv <| by simp [Finsupp.sum_fintype]
Sym.equivNatSumOfFintype.description: This definition establishes a natural equivalence between the nth symmetric power of a finite type and the subtype of functions from that type to the natural numbers that sum to a specified integer.

Finsupp.antidiagonal'.comment:
The `Finsupp` counterpart of `Multiset.antidiagonal`: the antidiagonal of
`s : α →₀ ℕ` consists of all pairs `(t₁, t₂) : (α →₀ ℕ) × (α →₀ ℕ)` such that `t₁ + t₂ = s`.
The finitely supported function `antidiagonal s` is equal to the multiplicities of these pairs.

explanatories.Multiset.map: This definition outlines a way to create a new multiset by applying a function to each element of an existing multiset, preserving the count of each element according to how many times the function produces the same output.
explanatories.Prod.map: A mapping function transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.
explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.

QPF.comp.fullDefinition: def comp : QPF (Functor.Comp F₂ F₁) where   P := PFunctor.comp q₂.P q₁.P   abs {α} := by     dsimp [Functor.Comp]     intro p     exact abs ⟨p.1.1, fun x => abs ⟨p.1.2 x, fun y => p.2 ⟨x, y⟩⟩⟩   repr {α} := by     dsimp [Functor.Comp]     intro y     refine ⟨⟨(repr y).1, fun u => (repr ((repr y).2 u)).1⟩, ?_⟩     dsimp [PFunctor.comp]     intro x     exact (repr ((repr y).2 x.1)).snd x.2   abs_repr {α} := by     dsimp [Functor.Comp]     intro x     conv =>       rhs       rw [← abs_repr x]     cases' repr x with a f     dsimp     congr with x     cases' h' : repr (f x) with b g     dsimp; rw [← h', abs_repr]   abs_map {α β} f := by     dsimp (config := { unfoldPartialApp := true }) [Functor.Comp, PFunctor.comp]     intro p     cases' p with a g; dsimp     cases' a with b h; dsimp     symm     trans     · symm       apply abs_map     congr     rw [PFunctor.map_eq]     dsimp [Function.comp_def]     congr     ext x     rw [← abs_map]     rfl
QPF.comp.description: The definition establishes that the composition of two quantitative polynomial functors results in another quantitative polynomial functor.

QPF.quotientQPF.code:
QPF.quotientQPF.{u} {F : Type u → Type u} [q : QPF F] {G : Type u → Type u} [Functor G]
  {FG_abs : {α : Type u} → F α → G α} {FG_repr : {α : Type u} → G α → F α}
  (FG_abs_repr : ∀ {α : Type u} (x : G α), FG_abs (FG_repr x) = x)
  (FG_abs_map : ∀ {α β : Type u} (f : α → β) (x : F α), FG_abs (f <$> x) = f <$> FG_abs x) : QPF G
QPF.quotientQPF.comment:
Given a qpf `F` and a well-behaved surjection `FG_abs` from `F α` to
functor `G α`, `G` is a qpf. We can consider `G` a quotient on `F` where
elements `x y : F α` are in the same equivalence class if
`FG_abs x = FG_abs y`.

explanatories.QPF.abs_map: This theorem establishes that the absolute value of a transformed element in a quantitative family, produced by applying a function, is equivalent to applying that function to the absolute value of the original element.
explanatories.QPF.abs: This definition specifies a function that converts an element from a particular structured type associated with a quantitative family into an element of that quantitative family itself.

QPF.quotientQPF.fullDefinition: def quotientQPF (FG_abs_repr : ∀ {α} (x : G α), FG_abs (FG_repr x) = x)     (FG_abs_map : ∀ {α β} (f : α → β) (x : F α), FG_abs (f <$> x) = f <$> FG_abs x) : QPF G where   P := q.P   abs {α} p := FG_abs (abs p)   repr {α} x := repr (FG_repr x)   abs_repr {α} x := by simp only; rw [abs_repr, FG_abs_repr]   abs_map {α β} f x := by simp only; rw [abs_map, FG_abs_map]
QPF.quotientQPF.description: This definition establishes that a type constructed from a quotient of a quantitative family is itself a quantitative family provided that there exists a surjective mapping that preserves structure between the original family and the new type.

MvQPF.quotientQPF.fullDefinition: def quotientQPF (FG_abs_repr : ∀ {α} (x : G α), FG_abs (FG_repr x) = x)     (FG_abs_map : ∀ {α β} (f : α ⟹ β) (x : F α), FG_abs (f <$$> x) = f <$$> FG_abs x) :     MvQPF G where   P := q.P   abs p := FG_abs (abs p)   repr x := repr (FG_repr x)   abs_repr x := by dsimp; rw [abs_repr, FG_abs_repr]   abs_map f p := by dsimp; rw [abs_map, FG_abs_map]

MvQPF.Cofix.map.fullDefinition: def Cofix.map {α β : TypeVec n} (g : α ⟹ β) : Cofix F α → Cofix F β :=   Quot.lift (fun x : q.P.M α => Quot.mk Mcongr (g <$$> x))     (by       rintro aa₁ aa₂ ⟨r, pr, ra₁a₂⟩; apply Quot.sound       let r' b₁ b₂ := ∃ a₁ a₂ : q.P.M α, r a₁ a₂ ∧ b₁ = g <$$> a₁ ∧ b₂ = g <$$> a₂       use r'; constructor       · show IsPrecongr r'         rintro b₁ b₂ ⟨a₁, a₂, ra₁a₂, b₁eq, b₂eq⟩         let u : Quot r → Quot r' :=           Quot.lift (fun x : q.P.M α => Quot.mk r' (g <$$> x))             (by               intro a₁ a₂ ra₁a₂               apply Quot.sound               exact ⟨a₁, a₂, ra₁a₂, rfl, rfl⟩)         have hu : (Quot.mk r' ∘ fun x : q.P.M α => g <$$> x) = u ∘ Quot.mk r := by           ext x           rfl         rw [b₁eq, b₂eq, M.dest_map, M.dest_map, ← q.P.comp_map, ← q.P.comp_map]         rw [← appendFun_comp, id_comp, hu, ← comp_id g, appendFun_comp]         rw [q.P.comp_map, q.P.comp_map, abs_map, pr ra₁a₂, ← abs_map]       show r' (g <$$> aa₁) (g <$$> aa₂); exact ⟨aa₁, aa₂, ra₁a₂, rfl, rfl⟩)

  (Q : β → Prop) (u v : β → Cofix F α)
  (h :
    ∀ (x : β),
      Q x →
        ∃ a f' f₀ f₁,
          (u x).dest = abs ⟨a, (P F).appendContents f' f₀⟩ ∧
            (v x).dest = abs ⟨a, (P F).appendContents f' f₁⟩ ∧
              ∀ (i : (P F).last.B a), ∃ x', Q x' ∧ f₀ i = u x' ∧ f₁ i = v x')
  (x : β) : Q x → u x = v x

left-hand side and right-hand side of the equality through functions `u v : β → Cofix F α`

MvQPF.WEquiv.recOn.{u} {n : ℕ} {F : TypeVec.{u} (n + 1) → Type u} [q : MvQPF F] {α : TypeVec.{u} n}
  {motive : (a a_1 : (P F).W α) → WEquiv a a_1 → Prop} :
  ∀ {a a_1 : (P F).W α} (t : WEquiv a a_1),
    (∀ (a : (P F).A) (f' : (P F).drop.B a ⟹ α) (f₀ f₁ : (P F).last.B a → (P F).W α)
        (a_2 : ∀ (x : (P F).last.B a), WEquiv (f₀ x) (f₁ x)),
        (∀ (x : (P F).last.B a), motive (f₀ x) (f₁ x) ⋯) → motive ((P F).wMk a f' f₀) ((P F).wMk a f' f₁) ⋯) →
      (∀ (a₀ : (P F).A) (f'₀ : (P F).drop.B a₀ ⟹ α) (f₀ : (P F).last.B a₀ → (P F).W α) (a₁ : (P F).A)
          (f'₁ : (P F).drop.B a₁ ⟹ α) (f₁ : (P F).last.B a₁ → (P F).W α)
          (a : abs ⟨a₀, (P F).appendContents f'₀ f₀⟩ = abs ⟨a₁, (P F).appendContents f'₁ f₁⟩),
          motive ((P F).wMk a₀ f'₀ f₀) ((P F).wMk a₁ f'₁ f₁) ⋯) →
        (∀ (u v w : (P F).W α) (a : WEquiv u v) (a_2 : WEquiv v w), motive u v a → motive v w a_2 → motive u w ⋯) →
          motive a a_1 t

MvQPF.WEquiv.recOn.fullDefinition: inductive WEquiv {α : TypeVec n} : q.P.W α → q.P.W α → Prop   | ind (a : q.P.A) (f' : q.P.drop.B a ⟹ α) (f₀ f₁ : q.P.last.B a → q.P.W α) :     (∀ x, WEquiv (f₀ x) (f₁ x)) → WEquiv (q.P.wMk a f' f₀) (q.P.wMk a f' f₁)   | abs (a₀ : q.P.A) (f'₀ : q.P.drop.B a₀ ⟹ α) (f₀ : q.P.last.B a₀ → q.P.W α) (a₁ : q.P.A)     (f'₁ : q.P.drop.B a₁ ⟹ α) (f₁ : q.P.last.B a₁ → q.P.W α) :     abs ⟨a₀, q.P.appendContents f'₀ f₀⟩ = abs ⟨a₁, q.P.appendContents f'₁ f₁⟩ →       WEquiv (q.P.wMk a₀ f'₀ f₀) (q.P.wMk a₁ f'₁ f₁)   | trans (u v w : q.P.W α) : WEquiv u v → WEquiv v w → WEquiv u w set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

MvQPF.Fix.comment:
Least fixed point of functor F. The result is a functor with one fewer parameters
than the input. For `F a b c` a ternary functor, `Fix F` is a binary functor such that

```lean
Fix F a b = F a b (Fix F a b)
```

explanatories.DFinsupp.filter: This definition specifies a function that filters a finitely supported function based on a predicate, returning the original values where the predicate is true and zero elsewhere.
explanatories.Multiset.filter: This definition outlines a function that creates a multiset containing only the elements from another multiset that satisfy a given condition, preserving their multiplicities.
explanatories.Multiset.attach: This definition describes a process that associates a proof of membership for each element in a multiset, resulting in a new multiset of elements that are accompanied by this membership proof.

explanatories.Multiset.mem_filter: This theorem states that an element is a member of a multiset filtered by a specific property if and only if it is a member of the original multiset and satisfies that property.
explanatories.Or.imp_left: The theorem shows that if one proposition implies another, then the disjunction of that proposition with a third proposition implies the disjunction of the second proposition with the same third proposition.
explanatories.Multiset.mem_map: This theorem states that an element is a member of the image of a multiset under a function if and only if there exists a corresponding element in the original multiset that maps to it.
explanatories.Multiset.mem_attach: This theorem asserts that if an element is a member of a multiset, then the associated attached form of that element is also a member of the multiset's attachment.
explanatories.Subtype.eta: For any element of a subtype, reconstructing that element from its underlying value and proof of property yields equality with the original element.
explanatories.Finset.filter: This definition describes a method for creating a new finite set that includes only the elements of an existing set that satisfy a given property.
explanatories.Finset.mem_filter: This theorem states that an element belongs to the filtered version of a set if and only if it is in the original set and satisfies the filtering condition.
explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.
explanatories.Sigma.eta: The equality shows that the dependent pair structure can be expressed in terms of its components.

DFinsupp.update.{u, v} {ι : Type u} {β : ι → Type v} [DecidableEq ι] [(i : ι) → Zero (β i)] (i : ι)
  (f : Π₀ (i : ι), β i) (b : β i) : Π₀ (i : ι), β i
DFinsupp.update.comment:
Replace the value of a `Π₀ i, β i` at a given point `i : ι` by a given value `b : β i`.
If `b = 0`, this amounts to removing `i` from the support.
Otherwise, `i` is added to it.

explanatories.DFinsupp.support': This definition describes a way to obtain the support set of a dependent function with finite support, which indicates where the function takes non-zero values.

explanatories.Or.imp_left: The theorem shows that if one proposition implies another, then the disjunction of that proposition with a third proposition implies the disjunction of the second proposition with the same third proposition.

explanatories.Eq.mpr: If there is a proof of equality between two types, then this definition provides a way to convert an element of one type to an element of the other type.
explanatories.Finset.preimage: This definition describes a function that computes the preimage of a finite set under an injective mapping, resulting in a finite set of the original elements.

explanatories.Finset.mem_preimage: An element is in the preimage of a finite set under an injective function if and only if its image under that function belongs to the original finite set.
explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.

DFinsupp.sumAddHom.fullDefinition: def sumAddHom [∀ i, AddZeroClass (β i)] [AddCommMonoid γ] (φ : ∀ i, β i →+ γ) :     (Π₀ i, β i) →+ γ where   toFun f :=     (f.support'.lift fun s => ∑ i ∈ Multiset.toFinset s.1, φ i (f i)) <| by       rintro ⟨sx, hx⟩ ⟨sy, hy⟩       dsimp only [Subtype.coe_mk, toFun_eq_coe] at *       have H1 : sx.toFinset ∩ sy.toFinset ⊆ sx.toFinset := Finset.inter_subset_left       have H2 : sx.toFinset ∩ sy.toFinset ⊆ sy.toFinset := Finset.inter_subset_right       refine         (Finset.sum_subset H1 ?_).symm.trans           ((Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_).trans (Finset.sum_subset H2 ?_))       · intro i H1 H2         rw [Finset.mem_inter] at H2         simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset] at H1 H2         convert AddMonoidHom.map_zero (φ i)         exact (hy i).resolve_left (mt (And.intro H1) H2)       · intro i _         rfl       · intro i H1 H2         rw [Finset.mem_inter] at H2         simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset] at H1 H2         convert AddMonoidHom.map_zero (φ i)         exact (hx i).resolve_left (mt (fun H3 => And.intro H3 H1) H2)   map_add' := by     rintro ⟨f, sf, hf⟩ ⟨g, sg, hg⟩     change (∑ i ∈ _, _) = (∑ i ∈ _, _) + ∑ i ∈ _, _     simp only [coe_add, coe_mk', Subtype.coe_mk, Pi.add_apply, map_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]     congr 1     · refine (Finset.sum_subset ?_ ?_).symm       · intro i         simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.mem_add]         exact Or.inl       · intro i _ H2         simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.mem_add] at H2         rw [(hf i).resolve_left H2, AddMonoidHom.map_zero]     · refine (Finset.sum_subset ?_ ?_).symm       · intro i         simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.mem_add]         exact Or.inr       · intro i _ H2         simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.mem_add] at H2         rw [(hg i).resolve_left H2, AddMonoidHom.map_zero]   map_zero' := by     simp only [toFun_eq_coe, coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply, map_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero]; rfl

  [(a : α) → Zero (N a)] (f g : Π₀ (a : α), N a) : Finset α
DFinsupp.neLocus.comment:
Given two finitely supported functions `f g : α →₀ N`, `Finsupp.neLocus f g` is the `Finset`
where `f` and `g` differ. This generalizes `(f - g).support` to situations without subtraction.

explanatories.DFinsupp.support: This definition describes the support of a finitely supported function as the finite set of indices for which the function takes non-zero values.
explanatories.Finset.filter: This definition describes a method for creating a new finite set that includes only the elements of an existing set that satisfy a given property.

DFinsupp.neLocus.fullDefinition: def neLocus (f g : Π₀ a, N a) : Finset α :=   (f.support ∪ g.support).filter fun x ↦ f x ≠ g x
DFinsupp.neLocus.description: This definition describes a finite set of elements where two finitely supported functions differ, serving as a generalization of the support of their difference without needing to perform explicit subtraction.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def lt_trichotomy_rec {P : Lex (Π₀ i, α i) → Lex (Π₀ i, α i) → Sort*}     (h_lt : ∀ {f g}, toLex f < toLex g → P (toLex f) (toLex g))     (h_eq : ∀ {f g}, toLex f = toLex g → P (toLex f) (toLex g))     (h_gt : ∀ {f g}, toLex g < toLex f → P (toLex f) (toLex g)) : ∀ f g, P f g :=   Lex.rec fun f ↦ Lex.rec fun g ↦ match (motive := ∀ y, (f.neLocus g).min = y → _) _, rfl with   | ⊤, h => h_eq (neLocus_eq_empty.mp <| Finset.min_eq_top.mp h)   | (wit : ι), h => by     apply (mem_neLocus.mp <| Finset.mem_of_min h).lt_or_lt.by_cases <;> intro hwit     · exact h_lt ⟨wit, fun j hj ↦ not_mem_neLocus.mp (Finset.not_mem_of_lt_min hj h), hwit⟩     · exact h_gt ⟨wit, fun j hj ↦         not_mem_neLocus.mp (Finset.not_mem_of_lt_min hj <| by rwa [neLocus_comm]), hwit⟩

DFinsupp.lex_fibration.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [(i : ι) → Zero (α i)] (r : ι → ι → Prop)
  (s : (i : ι) → α i → α i → Prop) [(i : ι) → (s : Set ι) → Decidable (i ∈ s)] :
  Fibration (InvImage (GameAdd (DFinsupp.Lex r s) (DFinsupp.Lex r s)) snd) (DFinsupp.Lex r s) fun x =>
    x.2.1.piecewise x.2.2 x.1
DFinsupp.lex_fibration.comment:
This key lemma says that if a finitely supported dependent function `x₀` is obtained by merging
two such functions `x₁` and `x₂`, and if we evolve `x₀` down the `DFinsupp.Lex` relation one
step and get `x`, we can always evolve one of `x₁` and `x₂` down the `DFinsupp.Lex` relation
one step while keeping the other unchanged, and merge them back (possibly in a different way)
to get back `x`. In other words, the two parts evolve essentially independently under
`DFinsupp.Lex`. This is used to show that a function `x` is accessible if
`DFinsupp.single i (x i)` is accessible for each `i` in the (finite) support of `x`
(`DFinsupp.Lex.acc_of_single`).

is required; consider ℂ with the order `z ≤ w` iff they have the same imaginary part and
`z - w ≤ 0` in the reals; then `1 + I` and `1 - I` are incomparable to zero, and thus we have:
`0 * 0 = SignType.sign (1 + I) * SignType.sign (1 - I) ≠ SignType.sign 2 = 1`.
(`Complex.orderedCommRing`)

  {f : Γ₀ →*₀ ℝ≥0} (hf : StrictMono ⇑f) {r : ℝ≥0} (hr : 0 < r) : ∃ d, f ↑d < r
NNReal.exists_lt_of_strictMono.comment:
If `Γ₀ˣ` is nontrivial and `f : Γ₀ →*₀ ℝ≥0` is strictly monotone, then for any positive
`r : ℝ≥0`, there exists `d : Γ₀ˣ` with `f d < r`.

explanatories.StrictMono: A function is considered strictly monotone if it maintains the order relationship such that whenever one input is strictly less than another, the output corresponding to the first input is also strictly less than the output corresponding to the second input.

NNReal.exists_lt_of_strictMono.description: This theorem asserts that in a nontrivial linear ordered group with zero, if a strictly monotonic function maps elements to nonnegative reals, then for any positive nonnegative real number, there exists an element in the group that is mapped to a value less than that number.

Matroid.ExchangeProperty.comment:

for all `X` and `Y` satisfying `P` and all `a ∈ X \ Y`, there exists `b ∈ Y \ X` so that
swapping `a` for `b` in `X` maintains `P`.

Matroid.Indep.fullDefinition: (Indep : Set α → Prop)   /-- The `Indep`endent sets are those contained in `Base`s. -/   (indep_iff' : ∀ ⦃I⦄, Indep I ↔ ∃ B, Base B ∧ I ⊆ B)   /-- There is at least one `Base`. -/   (exists_base : ∃ B, Base B)   /-- For any bases `B`, `B'` and `e ∈ B \ B'`, there is some `f ∈ B' \ B` for which `B-e+f`     is a base. -/   (base_exchange : Matroid.ExchangeProperty Base)   /-- Every independent subset `I` of a set `X` for is contained in a maximal independent     subset of `X`. -/   (maximality : ∀ X, X ⊆ E → Matroid.ExistsMaximalSubsetProperty Indep X)   /-- Every base is contained in the ground set. -/   (subset_ground : ∀ B, Base B → B ⊆ E)

IndepMatroid.ofBddAugment.fullDefinition: protected def ofBddAugment (E : Set α) (Indep : Set α → Prop)     (indep_empty : Indep ∅)     (indep_subset : ∀ ⦃I J⦄, Indep J → I ⊆ J → Indep I)     (indep_aug : ∀ ⦃I J⦄, Indep I → Indep J → I.encard < J.encard →       ∃ e ∈ J, e ∉ I ∧ Indep (insert e I))     (indep_bdd : ∃ (n : ℕ), ∀ I, Indep I → I.encard ≤ n )     (subset_ground : ∀ I, Indep I → I ⊆ E) : IndepMatroid α :=   IndepMatroid.ofBdd (E := E) (Indep := Indep)     (indep_empty := indep_empty)     (indep_subset := indep_subset)     (indep_aug := by       simp_rw [mem_maximals_setOf_iff, not_and, not_forall, exists_prop,  mem_diff,         and_imp, and_assoc]       rintro I B hI hImax hB hBmax       obtain ⟨J, hJ, hIJ, hne⟩ := hImax hI       obtain ⟨n, h_bdd⟩ := indep_bdd

IndepMatroid.ofFinite.fullDefinition: protected def ofFinite {E : Set α} (hE : E.Finite) (Indep : Set α → Prop)     (indep_empty : Indep ∅)     (indep_subset : ∀ ⦃I J⦄, Indep J → I ⊆ J → Indep I)     (indep_aug :       ∀ ⦃I J⦄, Indep I → Indep J → I.ncard < J.ncard → ∃ e ∈ J, e ∉ I ∧ Indep (insert e I))     (subset_ground : ∀ ⦃I⦄, Indep I → I ⊆ E) : IndepMatroid α :=   IndepMatroid.ofBddAugment (E := E) (Indep := Indep) (indep_empty := indep_empty)     (indep_subset := indep_subset)     (indep_aug := by       refine fun {I J} hI hJ hIJ ↦ indep_aug hI hJ ?_       rwa [← Nat.cast_lt (α := ℕ∞), (hE.subset (subset_ground hJ)).cast_ncard_eq,         (hE.subset (subset_ground hI)).cast_ncard_eq] )     (indep_bdd := ⟨E.ncard, fun I hI ↦ by       rw [hE.cast_ncard_eq]       exact encard_le_card <| subset_ground hI ⟩)     (subset_ground := subset_ground)

IndepMatroid.ofFinset.fullDefinition: protected def ofFinset [DecidableEq α] (E : Set α) (Indep : Finset α → Prop)     (indep_empty : Indep ∅)     (indep_subset : ∀ ⦃I J⦄, Indep J → I ⊆ J → Indep I)     (indep_aug : ∀ ⦃I J⦄, Indep I → Indep J → I.card < J.card → ∃ e ∈ J, e ∉ I ∧ Indep (insert e I))     (subset_ground : ∀ ⦃I⦄, Indep I → (I : Set α) ⊆ E) : IndepMatroid α :=   IndepMatroid.ofFinitary     (E := E)     (Indep := (fun I ↦ (∀ (J : Finset α), (J : Set α) ⊆ I → Indep J)))     (indep_empty := by simpa [subset_empty_iff])     (indep_subset := ( fun I J hJ hIJ K hKI ↦ hJ _ (hKI.trans hIJ) ))     (indep_aug := by       intro I J hI hIfin hJ hJfin hIJ       rw [ncard_eq_toFinset_card _ hIfin, ncard_eq_toFinset_card _ hJfin] at hIJ       have aug := indep_aug (hI _ (by simp [Subset.rfl])) (hJ _ (by simp [Subset.rfl])) hIJ       simp only [Finite.mem_toFinset] at aug       obtain ⟨e, heJ, heI, hi⟩ := aug       exact ⟨e, heJ, heI, fun K hK ↦ indep_subset hi <| Finset.coe_subset.1 (by simpa)⟩ )     (indep_compact := fun I h J hJ ↦ h _ hJ J.finite_toSet _ Subset.rfl )     (subset_ground := fun I hI x hxI ↦ by simpa using subset_ground <| hI {x} (by simpa) )

Matroid.comap.comment:
The pullback of a matroid on `β` by a function `f : α → β` to a matroid on `α`.
Elements with the same (nonloop) image are parallel and the ground set is `f ⁻¹' M.E`.
The matroids `M.comap f` and `M ↾ range f` have isomorphic simplifications;
the preimage of each nonloop of `M ↾ range f` is a parallel class.

explanatories.IndepMatroid.matroid: This definition constructs a matroid from an independent matroid by establishing that its bases are the maximal independent sets associated with it.
explanatories.Matroid.E: This definition specifies that a matroid has a ground set consisting of a certain collection of elements.

explanatories.Matroid.Indep.subset: This theorem states that if a set is independent in a matroid and another set contains it as a subset, then the first set is also independent in that matroid.
explanatories.Set.image_subset: The image of a subset under a function is contained within the image of the superset.
explanatories.Set.InjOn.mono: The theorem establishes that if a function is injective on a larger set, it remains injective when restricted to a smaller subset that is contained within the larger set.
explanatories.mem_maximals_iff: This theorem characterizes the elements in a set as maximal under a specific relation by stating that an element is maximal if it belongs to the set and is not less than any other element in the set according to that relation, meaning it is equal to any element it relates to.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.and_self: The theorem shows that the conjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the proposition itself.
explanatories.and_imp: The theorem states that the implication resulting from the conjunction of two propositions leading to a third proposition is equivalent to the scenario where each of the two propositions separately implies the third proposition.
explanatories.true_and: The theorem demonstrates that the conjunction of a true proposition and any other proposition is equivalent to the other proposition itself.
explanatories.Classical.not_forall: The equivalence between the negation of a universal statement and the existence of a counterexample is demonstrated by showing that not all elements satisfy the property if at least one element does not.
explanatories.exists_prop: The existence of an element satisfying one proposition implies both that proposition and another proposition are true.
explanatories.exists_and_left: The existence of an element that satisfies a property alongside a condition is equivalent to that condition being true and the existence of an element satisfying the property.
explanatories.Matroid.Basis.subset: This theorem states that if a set is a basis of a matroid, then it must be a subset of the set it is derived from.
explanatories.Set.MapsTo.image_subset: The theorem establishes that if a function maps a set into another set, then the image of the first set under the function is contained within the second set.
explanatories.Eq.subset: Equality of two sets implies that one set is a subset of the other.

Matroid.comap.fullDefinition: def comap (N : Matroid β) (f : α → β) : Matroid α :=   IndepMatroid.matroid <|   { E := f ⁻¹' N.E     Indep := fun I ↦ N.Indep (f '' I) ∧ InjOn f I     indep_empty := by simp     indep_subset := fun I J h hIJ ↦ ⟨h.1.subset (image_subset _ hIJ), InjOn.mono hIJ h.2⟩     indep_aug := by       rintro I B ⟨hI, hIinj⟩ hImax hBmax       simp only [mem_maximals_iff, mem_setOf_eq, hI, hIinj, and_self, and_imp,         true_and, not_forall, exists_prop, exists_and_left] at hImax hBmax
Matroid.comap.description: This definition describes the pullback of a matroid through a function, creating a new matroid where elements with the same image are treated as parallel, and the ground set consists of the preimage of the original matroid's ground set.

Matroid.mapSetEmbedding.fullDefinition: def mapSetEmbedding (M : Matroid α) (f : M.E ↪ β) : Matroid β := Matroid.ofExistsMatroid   (E := range f)   (Indep := fun I ↦ M.Indep ↑(f ⁻¹' I) ∧ I ⊆ range f)   (hM := by     classical     obtain (rfl | ⟨⟨e,he⟩⟩) := eq_emptyOn_or_nonempty M     · refine ⟨emptyOn β, ?_⟩       simp only [emptyOn_ground] at f       simp [range_eq_empty f, subset_empty_iff]     have _ : Nonempty M.E := ⟨⟨e,he⟩⟩     have _ : Nonempty α := ⟨e⟩     refine ⟨M.comapOn (range f) (fun x ↦ ↑(invFunOn f univ x)), rfl, ?_⟩     simp_rw [comapOn_indep_iff, ← and_assoc, and_congr_left_iff, subset_range_iff_exists_image_eq]     rintro _ ⟨I, rfl⟩     rw [← image_image, InjOn.invFunOn_image f.injective.injOn (subset_univ _),       preimage_image_eq _ f.injective, and_iff_left_iff_imp]     rintro - x hx y hy     simp only [EmbeddingLike.apply_eq_iff_eq, Subtype.val_inj]     exact (invFunOn_injOn_image f univ) (image_subset f (subset_univ I) hx)       (image_subset f (subset_univ I) hy) )

Given `M : Matroid α` and `X : Set α`, the restriction of `M` to `X`,
viewed as a matroid on type `X` with ground set `univ`.

Array.cyclicPermute!.code: Array.cyclicPermute!.{u} {α : Type u} [Inhabited α] : Array α → List Nat → Array α
Array.cyclicPermute!.comment:
Permute the array using a sequence of indices defining a cyclic permutation.
If the list of indices `l = [i₁, i₂, ..., iₙ]` are all distinct then
`(cyclicPermute! a l)[iₖ₊₁] = a[iₖ]` and `(cyclicPermute! a l)[i₀] = a[iₙ]`

explanatories.Array.set!: This defines a function that updates an element in an array at a specified index, raising an error if the index is invalid.
explanatories.Array.swapAt!: This defines a function that replaces an element at a specified index in an array with a new value and returns the updated array along with the original element that was replaced.

Array.cyclicPermute!.fullDefinition: def cyclicPermute! [Inhabited α] : Array α → List Nat → Array α   | a, []      => a   | a, i :: is => cyclicPermuteAux a is a[i]! i where cyclicPermuteAux : Array α → List Nat → α → Nat → Array α | a, [], x, i0 => a.set! i0 x | a, i :: is, x, i0 =>   let (y, a) := a.swapAt! i x   cyclicPermuteAux a is y i0
Array.cyclicPermute!.description: This definition describes a function that rearranges the elements of an array based on a specified sequence of distinct indices to achieve a cyclic permutation.

ByteSlice.forIn.loop.fullDefinition: def forIn.loop {m : Type u → Type v} {β : Type u} [Monad m] (f : UInt8 → β → m (ForInStep β))     (arr : ByteArray) (off _end : Nat) (i : Nat) (b : β) : m β :=   if h : i < _end then do     match ← f (arr.get! i) b with     | ForInStep.done b => pure b     | ForInStep.yield b => have := Nat.Up.next h; loop f arr off _end (i+1) b   else pure b termination_by _end - i
